verses.translation: When proceeding toward Vṛndāvana, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was overwhelmed with ecstatic love for Kṛṣṇa, and He lost all remembrance of the external world. In this way He traveled continuously for three days in Rāḍha-deśa, the country where the Ganges River does not flow.

verses.devanagari: নিত্যানন্দ প্রভু মহাপ্রভু ভুলাইয়া ।\\nগঙ্গাতীরে লঞা আইলা ‘যমুনা’ বলিয়া ॥৯৩॥
verses.transliteration: nityānanda prabhu mahāprabhu bhulāiyā\\ngaṅgā-tīre lañā āilā 'yamunā' baliyā
verses.translation: First of all, Lord Nityānanda bewildered Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu by bringing Him along the banks of the Ganges, saying that it was the river Yamunā.

verses.devanagari: শান্তিপুরে আচার্যের গৃহে আগমন ।\\nপ্রথম ভিক্ষা কৈল তাহাঁ, রাত্রে সংকীর্তন ॥৯৪॥
verses.transliteration: śāntipure ācāryera gṛhe āgamana\\nprathama bhikṣā kaila tāhāṅ, rātre saṅkīrtana
verses.translation: After three days, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu came to the house of Advaita Ācārya at Śāntipura and accepted alms there. This was His first acceptance of alms. At night He performed congregational chanting there.
verses.purport: PURPORT\nIt appears that in His transcendental ecstasy, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu forgot to eat for three continuous days. He was then misled by Nityānanda Prabhu, who said that the river Ganges was the Yamunā. Because the Lord was in the ecstasy of going to Vṛndāvana, He was engladdened to see the Yamunā, although in actuality the river was the Ganges. In this way the Lord was brought to the house of Advaita Prabhu at Śāntipura after three days, and He accepted food there. As long as the Lord remained there, He saw His mother, Śacīdevī, and every night executed congregational chanting with all the devotees.

verses.devanagari: মাতা ভক্তগণের তাহাঁ করিল মিলন ।\\nসর্ব সমাধান করি’ কৈল নীলাদ্রিগমন ॥৯৫॥
verses.transliteration: mātā bhakta-gaṇera tāhāṅ karila milana\\nsarva samādhāna kari' kaila nīlādri-gamana
verses.translation: At the house of Advaita Prabhu, He met His mother as well as all the devotees from Māyāpura. He adjusted everything and then went to Jagannātha Purī.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu knew very well that His acceptance of
sannyāsa
was a thunderbolt for His mother. He therefore called for His mother and the devotees from Māyāpura, and by the arrangement of Śrī Advaita Ācārya, He met them for the last time after His acceptance of
sannyāsa.
His mother was overwhelmed with grief when she saw that He was clean-shaven. There was no longer any beautiful hair on His head. Mother Śacī was pacified by all the devotees, and Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu asked her to cook for Him because He was very hungry, not having taken anything for three days. His mother immediately agreed, and forgetting everything else, she cooked for Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu during all the days she was at the house of Śrī Advaita Prabhu. Then, after a few days, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu requested His mother's permission to go to Jagannātha Purī. At His mother's request, He made Jagannātha Purī His headquarters after His acceptance of
sannyāsa.
Thus everything was adjusted, and with His mother's permission Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu proceeded toward Jagannātha Purī.

verses.devanagari: পথে নানা লীলারস, দেব-দরশন ।\\nমাধবপুরীর কথা, গোপাল-স্থাপন ॥৯৬॥
verses.transliteration: pathe nānā līlā-rasa, deva-daraśana\\nmādhava-purīra kathā, gopāla-sthāpana
verses.translation: On the way toward Jagannātha Purī, Caitanya Mahāprabhu performed many other pastimes. He visited various temples and heard the story about Mādhavendra Purī and the installation of Gopāla.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This Mādhava Purī is Mādhavendra Purī. Another Mādhava Purī is Mādhavācārya, who was the spiritual master of a devotee in the line of Gadādhara Paṇḍita and who wrote a book known as
Śrī Maṅgala-bhāṣya.
Mādhavācārya, however, is different from Mādhavendra Purī, who is mentioned in this verse.

verses.devanagari: ক্ষীর-চুরি-কথা, সাক্ষি-গোপাল-বিবরণ ।\\nনিত্যানন্দ কৈল প্রভুর দণ্ড-ভঞ্জন ॥৯৭॥
verses.transliteration: kṣīra-curi-kathā, sākṣi-gopāla-vivaraṇa\\nnityānanda kaila prabhura daṇḍa-bhañjana
verses.translation: From Nityānanda Prabhu, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu heard the story of Kṣīra-curī Gopinātha and of the witness Gopāla. Then Nityānanda Prabhu broke the sannyāsa rod belonging to Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
verses.purport: PURPORT\nThis Kṣīra-curī Gopinātha is situated about five miles away from the Bāleśvara station on the Northeastern Railway, formerly known as the Bengal Māyāpura Railway. This station is situated a few miles away from the famous Kargapura junction station. Sometimes the charge of the temple was given to Śyāmasundara Adhikārī from Gopīvallabhapura, which lies on the border of the district of Medinīpura. Śyāmasundara Adhikārī was a descendant of Rasikānanda Murāri, the chief disciple of Śyāmānanda Gosvāmī.\nA few miles before the Jagannātha Purī station is a small station called Sākṣi-gopāla. Near this station is a village named Satyavādī, where the temple of Sākṣi-gopāla is situated.

verses.devanagari: ক্রুদ্ধ হঞা একা গেলা জগন্নাথ দেখিতে ।\\nদেখিয়া মূর্চ্ছিত হঞা পড়িলা ভূমিতে ॥৯৮॥
verses.transliteration: kruddha hañā ekā gelā jagannātha dekhite\\ndekhiyā mūrcchita hañā paḍilā bhūmite
verses.translation: After His sannyāsa rod was broken by Nityānanda Prabhu, Caitanya Mahāprabhu apparently became very angry and left His company to travel alone to the Jagannātha temple. When Caitanya Mahāprabhu entered the Jagannātha temple and saw Lord Jagannātha, He immediately lost His senses and fell down on the ground.

verses.devanagari: সার্বভৌম লঞা গেলা আপন-ভবন ।\\nতৃতীয় প্রহরে প্রভুর হইল চেতন ॥৯৯॥
verses.transliteration: sārvabhauma lañā gelā āpana-bhavana\\ntṛtīya prahare prabhura ha-ila cetana
verses.translation: After Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu saw Lord Jagannātha in the temple and fell down unconscious, Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya took Him to his home. The Lord remained unconscious until the afternoon, when He finally regained His consciousness.

verses.devanagari: নিত্যানন্দ, জগদানন্দ, দামোদর, মুকুন্দ ।\\nপাছে আসি’ মিলি’ সবে পাইল আনন্দ ॥১০০॥
verses.transliteration: nityānanda, jagadānanda, dāmodara, mukunda\\npāche āsi' mili' sabe pāila ānanda
verses.translation: The Lord had left Nityānanda's company and had gone alone to the Jagannātha temple, but later Nityānanda, Jagadānanda, Dāmodara and Mukunda came to see Him, and after seeing Him they were very pleased.

verses.devanagari: তবে সার্বভৌমে প্রভু প্রসাদ করিল ।\\nআপন-ঈশ্বরমূর্তি তাঁরে দেখাইল ॥১০১॥
verses.transliteration: tabe sārvabhaume prabhu prasāda karila\\nāpana-īśvara-mūrti tāṅre dekhāila
verses.translation: After this incident, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu bestowed His mercy upon Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya by showing him His original form as the Lord.

verses.devanagari: তবে ত’ করিলা প্রভু দক্ষিণ গমন ।\\nকূর্মক্ষেত্রে কৈল বাসুদেব বিমোচন ॥১০২॥
verses.transliteration: tabe ta' karilā prabhu dakṣiṇa gamana\\nkūrma-kṣetre kaila vāsudeva vimocana
verses.translation: After bestowing mercy upon Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya, the Lord started for southern India. When He came to Kūrma-kṣetra, He delivered a person named Vāsudeva.

verses.devanagari: জিয়ড়-নৃসিংহে কৈল নৃসিংহ-স্তবন ।\\nপথে-পথে গ্রামে-গ্রামে নামপ্রবর্তন ॥১০৩॥
verses.transliteration: jiyaḍa-nṛsiṁhe kaila nṛsiṁha-stavana\\npathe-pathe grāme-grāme nāma-pravartana
verses.translation: After visiting Kūrma-kṣetra, the Lord visited the South Indian temple of Jiyaḍa-nṛsiṁha and offered His prayers to Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva. On His way, He introduced the chanting of the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra in every village.

verses.devanagari: গোদাবরীতীর-বনে বৃন্দাবন-ভ্রম ।\\nরামানন্দ রায় সহ তাহাঞি মিলন ॥১০৪॥
verses.transliteration: godāvarī-tīra-vane vṛndāvana-bhrama\\nrāmānanda rāya saha tāhāñi milana
verses.translation: Once the Lord mistook the forest on the bank of the river Godāvarī to be Vṛndāvana. In that place He happened to meet Rāmānanda Rāya.

verses.devanagari: ত্রিমল্ল-ত্রিপদী-স্থান কৈল দরশন ।\\nসর্বত্র করিল কৃষ্ণনাম প্রচারণ ॥১০৫॥
verses.transliteration: trimalla-tripadī-sthāna kaila daraśana\\nsarvatra karila kṛṣṇa-nāma pracāraṇa
verses.translation: He visited the place known as Trimalla, or Tirupati, and there He extensively preached the chanting of the Lord's holy name.
verses.purport: PURPORT\nThis holy place is situated in the district of Tāñjor, South India. The temple of Tripadī is situated in the valley of Veṅkaṭācala (Veṅkaṭa Mountain) and contains a Deity of Lord Rāmacandra. On top of Veṅkaṭācala is the famous temple of Bālājī.

verses.devanagari: তবে ত’ পাষণ্ডিগণে করিল দলন ।\\nঅহোবল-নৃসিংহাদি কৈল দরশন ॥১০৬॥
verses.transliteration: tabe ta' pāṣaṇḍī-gaṇe karila dalana\\nahovala-nṛsiṁhādi kaila daraśana
verses.translation: After visiting the temple of Trimalla, or Tripadī, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu had to subdue some atheists. He then visited the temple of Ahovala-nṛsiṁha.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This Ahovala temple is situated in Dākṣiṇātya, in the district of Karṇula, within the subdivision of Sārbela. Throughout the whole district this very famous temple is much appreciated by the people. There are nine other temples also, and all of them together are called the Nava-nṛsiṁha temples. There is much wonderful architecture and artistic engraving work in these temples. However, as stated in the local gazette, the
Karṇula Manual,
the work is not complete.

verses.devanagari: শ্রীরঙ্গক্ষেত্র আইলা কাবেরীর তীর ।\\nশ্রীরঙ্গ দেখিয়া প্রেমে হইলা অস্থির ॥১০৭॥
verses.transliteration: śrī-raṅga-kṣetra āilā kāverīra tīra\\nśrī-raṅga dekhiyā preme ha-ilā asthira
verses.translation: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu came to the land of Śrī Raṅga-kṣetra, on the bank of the Kāverī, He visited the temple of Śrī Raṅganātha and was there overwhelmed in the ecstasy of love of Godhead.

verses.devanagari: ত্রিমল্ল ভট্টের ঘরে কৈল প্রভু বাস ।\\nতাহাঞি রহিলা প্রভু বর্ষা চারি মাস ॥১০৮॥
verses.transliteration: trimalla bhaṭṭera ghare kaila prabhu vāsa\\ntāhāñi rahilā prabhu varṣā cāri māsa
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu lived at the house of Trimalla Bhaṭṭa for the four months of the rainy season.

verses.devanagari: শ্রীবৈষ্ণব ত্রিমল্লভট্ট — পরম পণ্ডিত ।\\nগোসাঞির পাণ্ডিত্য-প্রেমে হইলা বিস্মিত ॥১০৯॥
verses.transliteration: śrī-vaiṣṇava trimalla-bhaṭṭa—parama paṇḍita\\ngosāñira pāṇḍitya-preme ha-ilā vismita
verses.translation: Śrī Trimalla Bhaṭṭa was both a member of the Śrī Vaiṣṇava community and a learned scholar; therefore when he saw Caitanya Mahāprabhu, who was both a great scholar and a great devotee of the Lord, he was very much astonished.

verses.devanagari: চাতুর্মাস্য তাঁহা প্রভু শ্রীবৈষ্ণবের সনে ।\\nগোঙাইল নৃত্য-গীত-কৃষ্ণসংকীর্তনে ॥১১০॥
verses.transliteration: cāturmāsya tāṅhā prabhu śrī-vaiṣṇavera sane\\ngoṅāila nṛtya-gīta-kṛṣṇa-saṅkīrtane
verses.translation: Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu passed the Cāturmāsya months with the Śrī Vaiṣṇavas, dancing, singing and chanting the holy name of the Lord.

verses.devanagari: চাতুর্মাস্য-অন্তে পুনঃ দক্ষিণ গমন ।\\nপরমানন্দপুরী সহ তাহাঁঞি মিলন ॥১১১॥
verses.transliteration: cāturmāsya-ante punaḥ dakṣiṇa gamana\\nparamānanda-purī saha tāhāñi milana
verses.translation: After the end of Cāturmāsya, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu continued traveling throughout southern India. At that time He met Paramānanda Purī.

verses.devanagari: তবে ভট্টথারি হৈতে কৃষ্ণদাসের উদ্ধার ।\\nরামজপী বিপ্রমুখে কৃষ্ণনাম প্রচার ॥১১২॥
verses.transliteration: tabe bhaṭṭathāri haite kṛṣṇa-dāsera uddhāra\\nrāma-japī vipra-mukhe kṛṣṇa-nāma pracāra
verses.translation: After this, Kṛṣṇadāsa, the servant of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu, was delivered from the clutches of a Bhaṭṭathāri. Caitanya Mahāprabhu then preached that Lord Kṛṣṇa's name should also be chanted by brāhmaṇas who were accustomed to chanting Lord Rāma's name.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
In the Mālābāra district, a section of the
brāhmaṇas
are known as Nambudari
brāhmaṇas,
and the Bhaṭṭathāris are their priests. Bhaṭṭathāris know many tantric black arts, such as the art of killing a person, of bringing him under submission, and of destroying or devastating him. They are very expert in these black arts, and one such Bhaṭṭathāri bewildered the personal servant of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu while the servant accompanied the Lord in His travels through South India. Somehow or other Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu delivered this Kṛṣṇadāsa from the clutches of the Bhaṭṭathāri. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is well known as Patita-pāvana, the savior of all fallen souls, and He proved this in His behavior toward His personal servant, Kṛṣṇadāsa, whom He saved. Sometimes the word Bhaṭṭathāri is misspelled in Bengal as Bhaṭṭamāri.

verses.devanagari: শ্রীরঙ্গপুরী সহ তাহাঞি মিলন ।\\nরামদাস বিপ্রের কৈল দুঃখবিমোচন ॥১১৩॥
verses.transliteration: śrī-raṅga-purī saha tāhāñi milana\\nrāma-dāsa viprera kaila duḥkha-vimocana
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then met Śrī Raṅgapurī and mitigated all the sufferings of a brāhmaṇa named Rāmadāsa.

verses.devanagari: তত্ত্ববাদী সহ কৈল তত্ত্বের বিচার ।\\nআপনাকে হীনবুদ্ধি হৈল তাঁ-সবার ॥১১৪॥
verses.transliteration: tattva-vādī saha kaila tattvera vicāra\\nāpanāke hīna-buddhi haila tāṅ-sabāra
verses.translation: Caitanya Mahāprabhu also had a discussion with the Tattvavādī community, and the Tattvavādīs felt themselves to be inferior Vaiṣṇavas.
verses.purport: PURPORT\nThe Tattvavādī sect belongs to Madhvācārya's Vaiṣṇava community, but its behavior differs from the strict Madhvācārya Vaiṣṇava principles. There is one monastery named Uttararāḍhī, and its commander is named Raghuvarya Tīrtha Madhvācārya.

verses.devanagari: অনন্ত, পুরুষোত্তম, শ্রীজনার্দন ।\\nপদ্মনাভ, বাসুদেব কৈল দরশন ॥১১৫॥
verses.transliteration: ananta, puruṣottama, śrī-janārdana\\npadmanābha, vāsudeva kaila daraśana
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then visited the Viṣṇu temples of Anantadeva, Puruṣottama, Śrī Janārdana, Padmanābha and Vāsudeva.
verses.purport: PURPORT\nA temple of Ananta Padmanābha Viṣṇu is situated in the Trivandrum district. This temple is very famous in those quarters. Another Viṣṇu temple, named Śrī Janārdana, is situated about twenty-six miles north of the Trivandrum district, near the railway station called Varkālā.

verses.devanagari: তবে প্রভু কৈল সপ্ততাল বিমোচন ।\\nসেতুবন্ধে স্নান, রামেশ্বর দরশন ॥১১৬॥
verses.transliteration: tabe prabhu kaila sapta-tāla vimocana\\nsetubandhe snāna, rāmeśvara daraśana
verses.translation: After that, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu delivered the celebrated Saptatāla tree, took His bath at Setubandha Rāmeśvara and visited the temple of Lord Śiva known as Rāmeśvara.
verses.purport: PURPORT\nIt is said that the Saptatāla tree is a very old, massive palm tree. There was once a fight between Vāliand his brother Sugrīva, and Lord Rāmacandra took the side of Sugrīva and killed Vāli, keeping Himself behind this celebrated tree. When Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu toured south India, He embraced this tree, which was delivered and directly promoted to Vaikuṇṭha.

verses.devanagari: তাহাঞি করিল কূর্মপুরাণ শ্রবণ ।\\nমায়াসীতা নিলেক রাবণ, তাহাতে লিখন ॥১১৭॥
verses.transliteration: tāhāñi karila kūrma-purāṇa śravaṇa\\nmāyā-sītā nileka rāvaṇa, tāhāte likhana
verses.translation: At Rāmeśvara, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu had a chance to read the Kūrma Purāṇa, in which He discovered that the form of Sītā kidnapped by Rāvaṇa was not that of the real Sītā but a mere shadow representation.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
The
Kūrma Purāṇa
states that this shadowy Sītā was placed into a fire as a test of chastity. It was Māyā-sītā who entered the fire and the real Sītā who came out of the fire.

verses.devanagari: শুনিয়া প্রভুর আনন্দিত হৈল মন ।\\nরামদাস বিপ্রের কথা হইল স্মরণ ॥১১৮॥
verses.transliteration: śuniyā prabhura ānandita haila mana\\nrāma-dāsa viprera kathā ha-ila smaraṇa
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was very glad to read about the false Sītā, and He remembered His meeting with Rāmadāsa Vipra, who was very sorry that mother Sītā had been kidnapped by Rāvaṇa.

verses.devanagari: সেই পুরাতন পত্র আগ্রহ করি’ নিল ।\\nরামদাসে দেখাইয়া দুঃখ খণ্ডাইল ॥১১৯॥
verses.transliteration: sei purātana patra āgraha kari' nila\\nrāmadāse dekhāiyā duḥkha khaṇḍāila
verses.translation: Indeed, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu eagerly tore this page from the Kūrma Purāṇa, although the book was very old, and He later showed it to Rāmadāsa Vipra, whose unhappiness was mitigated.

verses.devanagari: ব্রহ্মসংহিতা, কর্ণামৃত, দুই পুঁথি পাঞা ।\\nদুই পুস্তক লঞা আইলা উত্তম জানিঞা ॥১২০॥
verses.transliteration: brahma-saṁhitā, karṇāmṛta, dui puṅthi pāñā\\ndui pustaka lañā āilā uttama jāniñā
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu also found two other books-namely, Brahma-saṁhitā and Kṛṣṇa-karṇāmṛta. Knowing these books to be excellent, He took them to present to His devotees.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
In the olden days there were no presses, and all the important scriptures were handwritten and kept in large temples. Caitanya Mahāprabhu found
Brahma-saṁhitā
and
Kṛṣṇa-karṇāmṛta
in handwritten texts, and knowing them to be very authoritative, He took them with Him to present to His devotees. Of course, He obtained the permission of the temple commander. Now both
Brahma-saṁhitā
and
Kṛṣṇa-karṇāmṛta
are available in print with commentaries by Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura.

verses.devanagari: পুনরপি নীলাচলে গমন করিল ।\\nভক্তগণে মেলিয়া স্নানযাত্রা দেখিল ॥১২১॥
verses.transliteration: punarapi nīlācale gamana karila\\nbhakta-gaṇe meliyā snāna-yātrā dekhila
verses.translation: After collecting these books, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu returned to Jagannātha Purī. At that time, the bathing ceremony of Jagannātha was taking place, and He saw it.

verses.devanagari: অনবসরে জগন্নাথের না পাঞা দরশন ।\\nবিরহে আলালনাথ করিলা গমন ॥১২২॥
verses.transliteration: anavasare jagannāthera nā pāñā daraśana\\nvirahe ālālanātha karilā gamana
verses.translation: When Jagannātha was absent from the temple, Caitanya Mahāprabhu, who could not see Him, felt separation and left Jagannātha Purī to go to a place known as Ālālanātha.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
Ālālanātha is also known as Brahmagiri. This place is about fourteen miles from Jagannātha Purī and is also on the beach. There is a temple of Jagannātha there. At the present moment a police station and post office are situated there because so many people come to see the temple.
The word
anavasara
is used when Śrī Jagannāthajī cannot be seen in the temple. After the bathing ceremony (
snāna-yātrā
), Lord Jagannātha is supposed to become sick. He is therefore removed to His private apartment, where no one can see Him. Actually, during this period renovations are made on the body of the Jagannātha Deity. This is called
nava-yauvana.
During the Ratha-yātrā ceremony, Lord Jagannātha once again comes before the public. Thus for fifteen days after the bathing ceremony, Lord Jagannātha is not visible to any visitors.

verses.devanagari: ভক্তসনে দিন কত তাহাঞি রহিলা ।\\nগৌড়ের ভক্ত আইসে, সমাচার পাইলা ॥১২৩॥
verses.transliteration: bhakta-sane dina kata tāhāñi rahilā\\ngauḍera bhakta āise, samācāra pāilā
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu remained for some days at Ālālanātha. In the meantime, Caitanya Mahāprabhu received news that all the devotees from Bengal were coming to Jagannātha Purī.

verses.devanagari: নিত্যানন্দ-সার্বভৌম আগ্রহ করিঞা ।\\nনীলাচলে আইলা মহাপ্রভুকে লইঞা ॥১২৪॥
verses.transliteration: nityānanda-sārvabhauma āgraha kariñā\\nnīlācale āilā mahāprabhuke la-iñā
verses.translation: When the devotees from Bengal arrived at Jagannātha Purī, both Nityānanda Prabhu and Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya greatly endeavored to take Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu back to Jagannātha Purī.

verses.devanagari: বিরহে বিহ্বল প্রভু না জানে রাত্রি-দিনে ।\\nহেনকালে আইলা গৌড়ের ভক্তগণে ॥১২৫॥
verses.transliteration: virahe vihvala prabhu nā jāne rātri-dine\\nhena-kāle āilā gauḍera bhakta-gaṇe
verses.translation: When Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu finally left Ālālanātha to return to Jagannātha Purī, He was overwhelmed both day and night due to separation from Jagannātha. His lamentation knew no bounds. During this time, all the devotees from different parts of Bengal, and especially from Navadvīpa, arrived in Jagannātha Purī.

verses.devanagari: সবে মিলি’ যুক্তি করি’ কীর্তন আরম্ভিল ।\\nকীর্তন-আবেশে প্রভুর মন স্থির হৈল ॥১২৬॥
verses.transliteration: sabe mili' yukti kari' kīrtana ārambhila\\nkīrtana-āveśe prabhura mana sthira haila
verses.translation: After due consideration, all the devotees began chanting the holy name congregationally. Lord Caitanya's mind was thus pacified by the ecstasy of the chanting.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
Being absolute, Lord Jagannātha is identical in person, form, picture,
kīrtana
and all other circumstances. Therefore when Caitanya Mahāprabhu heard the chanting of the holy name of the Lord, He was pacified. Previously, He had been feeling very morose due to separation from Jagannātha. The conclusion is that whenever a
kīrtana
of pure devotees takes place, the Lord is immediately present. By chanting the holy names of the Lord, we associate with the Lord personally.

verses.devanagari: পূর্বে যবে প্রভু রামানন্দেরে মিলিলা ।\\nনীলাচলে আসিবারে তাঁরে আজ্ঞা দিলা ॥১২৭॥
verses.transliteration: pūrve yabe prabhu rāmānandere mililā\\nnīlācale āsibāre tāṅre ājñā dilā
verses.translation: Previously, when Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu had been touring South India, He had met Rāmānanda Rāya on the banks of the Godāvarī. At that time it had been decided that Rāmānanda Rāya would resign from his post as governor and return to Jagannātha Purī to live with Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

verses.devanagari: রাজ-আজ্ঞা লঞা তেঁহো আইলা কত দিনে ।\\nরাত্রি-দিনে কৃষ্ণকথা রামানন্দসনে ॥১২৮॥
verses.transliteration: rāja-ājñā lañā teṅho āilā kata dine\\nrātri-dine kṛṣṇa-kathā rāmānanda-sane
verses.translation: Upon the order of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, Śrī Rāmānanda Rāya took leave of the King and returned to Jagannātha Purī. After he arrived, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu very much enjoyed talking with him both day and night about Lord Kṛṣṇa and His pastimes.

verses.devanagari: কাশীমিশ্রে কৃপা, প্রদ্যুম্ন মিশ্রাদি-মিলন ।\\nপরমানন্দপুরী-গোবিন্দ-কাশীশ্বরাগমন ॥১২৯॥
verses.transliteration: kāśī-miśre kṛpā, pradyumna miśrādi-milana\\nparamānanda-purī-govinda-kāśīśvarāgamana
verses.translation: After Rāmānanda Rāya's arrival, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu bestowed His mercy upon Kāśī Miśra and met Pradyumna Miśra and others. At that time three personalities-Paramānanda Purī, Govinda and Kāśīśvara-came to see Lord Caitanya at Jagannātha Purī.

verses.devanagari: দামোদরস্বরূপ-মিলনে পরম আনন্দ ।\\nশিখিমাহিতি-মিলন, রায় ভবানন্দ ॥১৩০॥
verses.transliteration: dāmodara-svarūpa-milane parama ānanda\\nśikhi-māhiti-milana, rāya bhavānanda
verses.translation: Eventually there was a meeting with Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī, and the Lord became very greatly pleased. Then there was a meeting with Śikhi Māhiti and with Bhavānanda Rāya, the father of Rāmānanda Rāya.

verses.devanagari: গৌড় হইতে সর্ব বৈষ্ণবের আগমন ।\\nকুলীনগ্রামবাসি-সঙ্গে প্রথম মিলন ॥১৩১॥
verses.transliteration: gauḍa ha-ite sarva vaiṣṇavera āgamana\\nkulīna-grāma-vāsi-saṅge prathama milana
verses.translation: All the devotees from Bengal gradually began arriving at Jagannātha Purī. At this time, the residents of Kulīna-grāma also came to see Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu for the first time.

verses.devanagari: নরহরি দাস আদি যত খণ্ডবাসী ।\\nশিবানন্দসেন-সঙ্গে মিলিলা সবে আসি’ ॥১৩২॥
verses.transliteration: narahari dāsa ādi yata khaṇḍa-vāsī\\nśivānanda-sena-saṅge mililā sabe āsi'
verses.translation: Eventually Narahari dāsa and other inhabitants of Khaṇḍa, along with Śivānanda Sena, all arrived, and Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu met them.

verses.devanagari: স্নানযাত্রা দেখি’ প্রভু সঙ্গে ভক্তগণ ।\\nসবা লঞা কৈলা প্রভু গুণ্ডিচা মার্জন ॥১৩৩॥
verses.transliteration: snāna-yātrā dekhi' prabhu saṅge bhakta-gaṇa\\nsabā lañā kailā prabhu guṇḍicā mārjana
verses.translation: After seeing the bathing ceremony of Lord Jagannātha, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu washed and cleaned Śrī Guṇḍicā temple with the assistance of many devotees.

verses.devanagari: সবা-সঙ্গে রথযাত্রা কৈল দরশন ।\\nরথ-অগ্রে নৃত্য করি’ উদ্যানে গমন ॥১৩৪॥
verses.transliteration: sabā-saṅge ratha-yātrā kaila daraśana\\nratha-agre nṛtya kari' udyāne gamana
verses.translation: After this, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu and all the devotees saw the Ratha-yātrā, the car festival ceremony. Caitanya Mahāprabhu Himself danced in front of the car, and after dancing He entered a garden.

verses.devanagari: প্ৰতাপরুদ্রেরে কৃপা কৈল সেই স্থানে ।\\nগৌড়ীয়াভক্তে আজ্ঞা দিল বিদায়ের দিনে ॥১৩৫॥
verses.transliteration: pratāparudrere kṛpā kaila sei sthāne\\ngauḍīyā-bhakte ājñā dila vidāyera dine
verses.translation: In that garden, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu bestowed His mercy upon King Pratāparudra. Afterwards, when the Bengali devotees were about to return home, the Lord gave separate orders to almost every one of them.

verses.devanagari: প্রত্যব্দ আসিবে রথযাত্রা-দরশনে ।\\nএই ছলে চাহে ভক্তগণের মিলনে ॥১৩৬॥
verses.transliteration: pratyabda āsibe ratha-yātrā-daraśane\\nei chale cāhe bhakta-gaṇera milane
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu desired to meet all the devotees of Bengal every year. Therefore He ordered them to come to see the Ratha-yātrā festival every year.

verses.devanagari: সার্বভৌম-ঘরে প্রভুর ভিক্ষা-পরিপাটী ।\\nষাঠীর মাতা কহে, যাতে রাণ্ডী হউক্ ষাঠী ॥১৩৭॥
verses.transliteration: sārvabhauma-ghare prabhura bhikṣā-paripāṭī\\nṣāṭhīra mātā kahe, yāte rāṇḍī ha-uk ṣāṭhī
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was invited to dine at the house of Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya. While He was eating sumptuously, the son-in-law of Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya [the husband of his daughter Ṣāṭhī] criticized Him. Because of this, Ṣāṭhī's mother cursed him by praying that Ṣāṭhī would become a widow. In other words, she cursed her son-in-law to die.

verses.devanagari: বর্ষান্তরে অদ্বৈতাদি ভক্তের আগমন ।\\nপ্ৰভুরে দেখিতে সবে করিলা গমন ॥১৩৮॥
verses.transliteration: varṣāntare advaitādi bhaktera āgamana\\nprabhure dekhite sabe karilā gamana
verses.translation: At the end of the year, all the devotees from Bengal, headed by Advaita Ācārya, again came to see the Lord. Indeed, there was a great rush of devotees to Jagannātha Purī.

verses.devanagari: আনন্দে সবারে নিয়া দেন বাসস্থান ।\\nশিবানন্দ সেন করে সবার পালন ॥১৩৯॥
verses.transliteration: ānande sabāre niyā dena vāsa-sthāna\\nśivānanda sena kare sabāra pālana
verses.translation: When all the devotees from Bengal arrived, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu allotted them residential quarters, and Śivānanda Sena was put in charge of their maintenance.

verses.devanagari: শিবানন্দের সঙ্গে আইলা কুক্কুর ভাগ্যবান্ ।\\nপ্রভুর চরণ দেখি’ কৈল অন্তর্ধান ॥১৪০॥
verses.transliteration: śivānandera saṅge āilā kukkura bhāgyavān\\nprabhura caraṇa dekhi' kaila antardhāna
verses.translation: A dog accompanied Śivānanda Sena and the devotees, and that dog was so fortunate that after seeing the lotus feet of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu, it was liberated and went back home, back to Godheand.

verses.devanagari: পথে সার্বভৌম সহ সবার মিলন ।\\nসার্বভৌম ভট্টাচার্যের কাশীতে গমন ॥১৪১॥
verses.transliteration: pathe sārvabhauma saha sabāra milana\\nsārvabhauma bhaṭṭācāryera kāśīte gamana
verses.translation: Everyone met Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya on his way to Vārāṇasī.

verses.devanagari: প্ৰভুরে মিলিলা সর্ব বৈষ্ণব আসিয়া ।\\nজলক্রীড়া কৈল প্রভু সবারে লইয়া ॥১৪২॥
verses.transliteration: prabhure mililā sarva vaiṣṇava āsiyā\\njala-krīḍā kaila prabhu sabāre la-iyā
verses.translation: After arriving at Jagannātha Purī, all the Vaiṣṇavas met with Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Later, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu sported in the water, taking all the devotees with Him.

verses.devanagari: সবা লঞা কৈল গুণ্ডিচা-গৃহ-সংমার্জন ।\\nরথযাত্রা-দরশনে প্রভুর নর্তন ॥১৪৩॥
verses.transliteration: sabā lañā kaila guṇḍicā-gṛha-sammārjana\\nratha-yātrā-daraśane prabhura nartana
verses.translation: First the Lord washed the temple of Guṇḍicā very thoroughly. Then everyone saw the Ratha-yātrā festival and the Lord's dancing before the car.

verses.devanagari: উপবনে কৈল প্রভু বিবিধ বিলাস ।\\nপ্ৰভুর অভিষেক কৈল বিপ্র কৃষ্ণদাস ॥১৪৪॥
verses.transliteration: upavane kaila prabhu vividha vilāsa\\nprabhura abhiṣeka kaila vipra kṛṣṇadāsa
verses.translation: In the forest along the road from the Jagannātha temple to Guṇḍicā, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu performed various pastimes. A brāhmaṇa named Kṛṣṇadāsa performed the bathing ceremony of Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

verses.devanagari: গুণ্ডিচাতে নৃত্য-অন্তে কৈল জলকেলি ।\\nহেরা-পঞ্চমীতে দেখিল লক্ষ্মীদেবীর কেলী ॥১৪৫॥
verses.transliteration: guṇḍicāte nṛtya-ante kaila jala-keli\\nherā-pañcamīte dekhila lakṣmī-devīra kelī
verses.translation: After dancing in the Guṇḍicā temple, the Lord sported in the water with His devotees, and on Herā-pañcamī day they all saw the activities of the goddess of fortune, Lakṣmīdevī.

verses.devanagari: কৃষ্ণজন্ম-যাত্রাতে প্রভু গোপবেশ হৈলা ।\\nদধিভার বহি’ তবে লগুড় ফিরাইলা ॥১৪৬॥
verses.transliteration: kṛṣṇa-janma-yātrāte prabhu gopa-veśa hailā\\ndadhi-bhāra vahi' tabe laguḍa phirāilā
verses.translation: On Janmāṣṭamī, Lord Kṛṣṇa's birthday, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu dressed Himself as a cowherd boy and, carrying a balance with pots of yogurt, encircled a log.

verses.devanagari: গৌড়ের ভক্তগণে তবে করিল বিদায় ।\\nসঙ্গের ভক্ত লঞা করে কীর্তন সদায় ॥১৪৭॥
verses.transliteration: gauḍera bhakta-gaṇe tabe karila vidāya\\nsaṅgera bhakta lañā kare kīrtana sadāya
verses.translation: After this, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu bade farewell to all the devotees from Gauḍa-deśa [Bengal] and continued chanting with His intimate devotees who constantly remained with Him.

verses.devanagari: বৃন্দাবন যাইতে কৈল গৌড়েরে গমন ।\\nপ্রতাপরুদ্র কৈল পথে বিবিধ সেবন ॥১৪৮॥
verses.transliteration: vṛndāvana yāite kaila gauḍere gamana\\npratāparudra kaila pathe vividha sevana
verses.translation: To visit Vṛndāvana, the Lord went to Gauḍa-deśa [Bengal]. On the way, King Pratāparudra performed a variety of service to please the Lord.

verses.devanagari: পুরীগোসাঞি-সঙ্গে বস্ত্রপ্রদান-প্রসঙ্গ ।\\nরামানন্দ রায় আইলা ভদ্রক পর্যন্ত ॥১৪৯॥
verses.transliteration: purī-gosāñi-saṅge vastra-pradāna-prasaṅga\\nrāmānanda rāya āilā bhadraka paryanta
verses.translation: On the way to Vṛndāvana via Bengal, there was an incident wherein some cloth was exchanged with Purī Gosāñi. Śrī Rāmānada Rāya accompanied the Lord as far as the city of Bhadraka.

verses.devanagari: আসি’ বিদ্যাবাচস্পতির গৃহেতে রহিলা ।\\nপ্রভুরে দেখিতে লোকসংঘট্ট হইলা ॥১৫০॥
verses.transliteration: āsi' vidyā-vācaspatira gṛhete rahilā\\nprabhure dekhite loka-saṅghaṭṭa ha-ilā
verses.translation: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu reached Vidyānagara, Bengal, on the way to Vṛndāvana, He stopped at the house of Vidyā-vācaspati, who was the brother of Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya. When Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu suddenly arrived at his house, great crowds of people gathered.

verses.devanagari: পঞ্চদিন দেখে লোক নাহিক বিশ্রাম ।\\nলোকভয়ে রাত্রে প্রভু আইলা কুলিয়া-গ্রাম ॥১৫১॥
verses.transliteration: pañca-dina dekhe loka nāhika viśrāma\\nloka-bhaye rātre prabhu āilā kuliyā-grāma
verses.translation: For five consecutive days all the people gathered to see the Lord, and still there was no rest. Out of fear of the crowd, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu left at night and went to the town of Kuliyā [present-day Navadvīpa].
verses.purport:
PURPORT
If one considers the statements of the
Caitanya-bhāgavata
along with the description by Locana dāsa Ṭhākura, it is clear that present-day Navadvīpa was formerly known as Kuliyā-grāma. While at Kuliyā-grāma, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu bestowed His favor upon Devānanda Paṇḍita and delivered Gopāla Cāpala and many others who had previously committed offenses at His lotus feet. At that time, to go from Vidyānagara to Kuliyā-grāma one had to cross a branch of the Ganges. All of those old places still exist. Cināḍāṅgā was formerly situated in Kuliyā-grāma, which is now known as Kolera Gañja.

verses.devanagari: কুলিয়া-গ্রামেতে প্রভুর শুনিয়া আগমন ।\\nকোটি কোটি লোক আসি’ কৈল দরশন ॥১৫২॥
verses.transliteration: kuliyā-grāmete prabhura śuniyā āgamana\\nkoṭi koṭi loka āsi' kaila daraśana
verses.translation: Hearing of the Lord's arrival in Kuliyā-grāma, may hundreds and thousands of people came to see Him.

verses.devanagari: কুলিয়া-গ্রামে কৈল দেবানন্দেরে প্রসাদ ।\\nগোপাল-বিপ্রেরে ক্ষমাইল শ্রীবাসাপরাধ ॥১৫৩॥
verses.transliteration: kuliyā-grāme kaila devānandere prasāda\\ngopāla-viprere kṣamāila śrīvāsāparādha
verses.translation: The specific acts performed by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu at this time were His showing favor upon Devānanda Paṇḍita and excusing the brāhmaṇa known as Gopāla Cāpala from the offense he had committed at the lotus feet of Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura.

verses.devanagari: পাষণ্ডী নিন্দক আসি’ পড়িলা চরণে ।\\nঅপরাধ ক্ষমি’ তারে দিল কৃষ্ণপ্রেমে ॥১৫৪॥
verses.transliteration: pāṣaṇḍī nindaka āsi' paḍilā caraṇe\\naparādha kṣami' tāre dila kṛṣṇa-preme
verses.translation: Many atheists and blasphemers came and fell at the lotus feet of the Lord, and the Lord in return excused them and gave them love of Kṛṣṇa.

verses.devanagari: বৃন্দাবন যাবেন প্রভু শুনি’ নৃসিংহানন্দ ।\\nপথ সাজাইল মনে পাইয়া আনন্দ ॥১৫৫॥
verses.transliteration: vṛndāvana yābena prabhu śuni' nṛsiṁhānanda\\npatha sājāila mane pāiyā ānanda
verses.translation: When Śrī Nṛsiṁhānanda Brahmacārī heard that Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu would go to Vṛndāvana, he became very pleased and mentally began decorating the way there.

verses.devanagari: কুলিয়া নগর হৈতে পথ রত্নে বান্ধাইল ।\\nনিবৃন্ত পুষ্পশয্যা উপরে পাতিল ॥১৫৬॥
verses.transliteration: kuliyā nagara haite patha ratne bāndhāila\\nnivṛnta puṣpa-śayyā upare pātila
verses.translation: First Nṛsiṁhānanda Brahmacārī contemplated a broad road starting from the city of Kuliyā. He bedecked the road with jewels, upon which he then laid a bed of stemless flowers.

verses.devanagari: পথে দুই দিকে পুষ্পবকুলের শ্রেণী ।\\nমধ্যে মধ্যে দুইপাশে দিব্য পুষ্করিণী ॥১৫৭॥
verses.transliteration: pathe dui dike puṣpa-bakulera śreṇī\\nmadhye madhye dui-pāśe divya puṣkariṇī
verses.translation: He mentally decorated both sides of the road with bakula flower trees, and at intervals on both sides he placed lakes of a transcendental nature.

verses.devanagari: রত্নবাঁধা ঘাট, তাহে প্রফুল্ল কমল ।\\nনানা পক্ষি-কোলাহল, সুধা-সম জল ॥১৫৮॥
verses.transliteration: ratna-bāṅdhā ghāṭa, tāhe praphulla kamala\\nnānā pakṣi-kolāhala, sudhā-sama jala
verses.translation: These lakes had bathing places constructed with jewels, and they were filled with blossoming lotus flowers. There were various birds chirping, and the water was exactly like nectar.

verses.devanagari: শীতল সমীর বহে নানা গন্ধ লঞা ।\\n‘কানাইর নাটশালা’ পর্যন্ত লইল বান্ধিঞা ॥১৫৯॥
verses.transliteration: śītala samīra vahe nānā gandha lañā\\n'kānāira nāṭaśālā' paryanta la-ila bāndhiñā
verses.translation: The entire road was surcharged with many cool breezes, which carried the fragrances from various flowers. He carried the construction of this road as far as Kānāi Nāṭaśālā.
verses.purport: PURPORT\nKānāi Nāṭaśālā is about 202 miles from Calcutta on the Loop line of the Eastern Railway. The railway station is named Tālajhāḍi, and after one gets off at that station, he has to go about two miles to find Kānāi Nāṭaśālā.

verses.devanagari: আগে মন নাহি চলে, না পারে বান্ধিতে ।\\nপথ বান্ধা না যায়, নৃসিংহ হৈলা বিস্মিতে ॥১৬০॥
verses.transliteration: āge mana nāhi cale, nā pāre bāndhite\\npatha-bāndhā nā yāya, nṛsiṁha hailā vismite
verses.translation: Within the mind of Nṛsiṁhānanda Brahmacārī, the road could not be constructed beyond Kānāi Nāṭaśālā. He could not understand why the road's construction could not be completed, and thus he was astonished.

verses.devanagari: নিশ্চয় করিয়া কহি, শুন, ভক্তগণ ।\\nএবার না যাবেন প্রভু শ্রীবৃন্দাবন ॥১৬১॥
verses.transliteration: niścaya kariyā kahi, śuna, bhakta-gaṇa\\nebāra nā yābena prabhu śrī-vṛndāvana
verses.translation: With great assurance he then told the devotees that Lord Caitanya would not go to Vṛndāvana at that time.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
Śrīla Nṛsiṁhānanda Brahmacārī was a great devotee of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu; therefore when he heard that from Kuliyā Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was going to Vṛndāvana, although he had no material wealth he began to construct within his mind a very attractive path or road for Caitanya Mahāprabhu to traverse. Some of the description of this path is given above. But even mentally he could not construct the road beyond Kānāi Nāṭaśālā. Therefore he concluded that Caitanya Mahāprabhu would not go to Vṛndāvana at that time.
For a pure devotee, it is the same whether he materially constructs a path or constructs one within his mind. This is because the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Janārdana, is
bhāva-grāhī,
or appreciative of the sentiment. For Him a path made with actual jewels and a path made of mental jewels are the same. Though subtle, mind is also matter, so any path-indeed, anything for the service of the Lord, whether in gross matter or in subtle matter-is accepted equally by the Supreme Personality of Godhead. The Lord accepts the attitude of His devotee and sees how much he is prepared to serve Him. The devotee is at liberty to serve the Lord either in gross matter or in subtle matter. The important point is that the service be in relation with the Supreme Personality of Godheand. This is confirmed in the
Bhagavad-gītā
(Bg. 9.26):
patraṁ puṣpaṁ phalaṁ toyaṁ
yo me bhaktyā prayacchati
tad ahaṁ bhakty-upahṛtam
aśnāmi prayatātmanaḥ
"If one offers Me with love and devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit or water, I will accept it." The real ingredient is
bhakti
(devotion). Pure devotion is uncontaminated by the modes of material nature.
Ahaituky apratihatā:
unconditional devotional service cannot be checked by any material condition. This means that one does not have to be very rich to serve the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Even the poorest man can equally serve the Supreme Personality of Godhead if he has pure devotion. If there is no ulterior motive, devotional service cannot be checked by any material condition.

verses.devanagari: ‘কানাঞির নাটশালা’ হৈতে আসিব ফিরিঞা ।\\nজানিবে পশ্চাৎ, কহিলু নিশ্চয় করিঞা ॥১৬২॥
verses.transliteration: 'kānāñira nāṭaśālā' haite āsiba phiriñā\\njānibe paścāt, kahilu niścaya kariñā
verses.translation: Nṛsiṁhānanda Brahmacārī said, "The Lord will go to Kānāi Nāṭaśālā and then will return. All of you will come to know of this later, but I now say this with great assurance."

verses.devanagari: গোসাঞি কুলিয়া হৈতে চলিলা বৃন্দাবন ।\\nসঙ্গে সহস্রেক লোক যত ভক্তগণ ॥১৬৩॥
verses.transliteration: gosāñi kuliyā haite calilā vṛndāvana\\nsaṅge sahasreka loka yata bhakta-gaṇa
verses.translation: When Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu began to proceed from Kuliyā toward Vṛndāvana, thousands of men were with Him, and all of them were devotees.

verses.devanagari: যাহাঁ যায় প্রভু, তাহাঁ কোটিসংখ্য লোক ।\\nদেখিতে আইসে, দেখি’ খণ্ডে দুঃখ-শোক ॥১৬৪॥
verses.transliteration: yāhāṅ yāya prabhu, tāhāṅ koṭi-saṅkhya loka\\ndekhite āise, dekhi' khaṇḍe duḥkha-śoka
verses.translation: Wherever the Lord visited, crowds of innumerable people came to see Him. When they saw Him, all their unhappiness and lamentation disappeared.

verses.devanagari: যাহাঁ যাহাঁ প্রভুর চরণ পড়য়ে চলিতে ।\\nসে মৃত্তিকা লয় লোক, গর্ত হয় পথে ॥১৬৫॥
verses.transliteration: yāhāṅ yāhāṅ prabhura caraṇa paḍaye calite\\nse mṛttikā laya loka, garta haya pathe
verses.translation: Wherever the Lord touched the ground with His lotus feet, people immediately came and gathered the dirt. Indeed, they gathered so much that many holes were created in the road.

verses.devanagari: ঐছে চলি, আইলা প্রভু ‘রামকেলি’ গ্রাম ।\\nগৌড়ের নিকট গ্রাম অতি অনুপাম ॥১৬৬॥
verses.transliteration: aiche cali, āilā prabhu 'rāmakeli' grāma\\ngauḍera nikaṭa grāma ati anupāma
verses.translation: Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu eventually arrived at a village named Rāmakeli. This village is situated on the border of Bengal and is very exquisite.
verses.purport: PURPORT\nRāmakeli-grāma is situated on the banks of the Ganges on the border of Bengal. Śrīla Rūpa and Sanātana Gosvāmīs had their residences in this village.

verses.devanagari: তাহাঁ নৃত্য করে প্রভু প্রেমে অচেতন ।\\nকোটি কোটি লোক আইসে দেখিতে চরণ ॥১৬৭॥
verses.transliteration: tāhāṅ nṛtya kare prabhu preme acetana\\nkoṭi koṭi loka āise dekhite caraṇa
verses.translation: While performing saṅkīrtana in Rāmakeli-grāma, the Lord danced and sometimes lost consciousness due to love of God. While at Rāmakeli-grāma, an unlimited number of people came to see His lotus feet.

verses.devanagari: গৌড়েশ্বর যবন-রাজা প্রভাব শুনিঞা ।\\nকহিতে লাগিল কিছু বিস্মিত হঞা ॥১৬৮॥
verses.transliteration: gauḍeśvara yavana-rājā prabhāva śuniñā\\nkahite lāgila kichu vismita hañā
verses.translation: When the Mohammedan King of Bengal heard of Caitanya Mahāprabhu's influence in attracting innumerable people, he became very astonished and began to speak as follows.
verses.purport: PURPORT\nAt that time the Mohammedan king of Bengal was Nawab Husen Sāhā Bādasāha.

verses.devanagari: বিনা দানে এত লোক যাঁর পাছে হয় ।\\nসেই ত’ গোসাঞা, ইহা জানিহ নিশ্চয় ॥১৬৯॥
verses.transliteration: vinā dāne eta loka yāṅra pāche haya\\nsei ta' gosāñā, ihā jāniha niścaya
verses.translation: "Such a person, who is followed by so many people without giving them charity, must be a prophet. I can surely understand this fact."

verses.devanagari: কাজী, যবন ইহার না করিহ হিংসন ।\\nআপন-ইচ্ছায় বুলুন, যাহাঁ উঁহার মন ॥১৭০॥
verses.transliteration: kājī, yavana ihāra nā kariha hiṁsana\\nāpana-icchāya buluna, yāhāṅ uṅhāra mana
verses.translation: The Mohammedan King ordered the magistrate, "Do not disturb this Hindu prophet out of jealousy. Let Him do His own will wherever He likes."
verses.purport: PURPORT\nEven a Mohammedan king could understand Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's transcendental position as a prophet; therefore he ordered the local magistrate not to disturb Him but to let Him do whatever He liked.

verses.devanagari: কেশব-ছত্রীরে রাজা বার্তা পুছিল ।\\nপ্রভুর মহিমা ছত্রী উড়াইয়া দিল ॥১৭১॥
verses.transliteration: keśava-chatrīre rājā vārtā puchila\\nprabhura mahimā chatrī uḍāiyā dila
verses.translation: When the Mohammedan King asked his assistant, Keśava Chatrī, for news of the influence of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, Keśava Chatrī, although knowing everything about Caitanya Mahāprabhu, tried to avoid the conversation by not giving any importance to Caitanya Mahāprabhu's activities.
verses.purport: PURPORT\nKeśava Chatrī became a diplomat when questioned about Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Although he knew everything about Him, he was afraid that the Mohammedan King might become His enemy. He gave no importance to the Lord's activities so that the Mohammedan King would take Him to be an ordinary man and would not give Him any trouble.

verses.devanagari: ভিখারী সন্ন্যাসী করে তীর্থ পর্যটন ।\\nতাঁরে দেখিবারে আইসে দুই চারি জন ॥১৭২॥
verses.transliteration: bhikhārī sannyāsī kare tīrtha paryaṭana\\ntāṅre dekhibāre āise dui cāri jana
verses.translation: Keśava Chatrī informed the Mohammedan King that Caitanya Mahāprabhu was a mendicant touring different places of pilgrimage and that, as such, only a few people came to see Him.

verses.devanagari: যবনে তোমার ঠাঞি করয়ে লাগানি ।\\nতাঁর হিংসায় লাভ নাহি, হয় আর হানি ॥১৭৩॥
verses.transliteration: yavane tomāra ṭhāñi karaye lāgāni\\ntāṅra hiṁsāya lābha nāhi, haya āra hāni
verses.translation: Keśava Chatrī said, "Out of jealousy your Mohammedan servant plots against Him. I think that you should not be very interested in Him, for there is no profit in it. Rather, there is simply loss."

verses.devanagari: রাজারে প্রবোধি’ কেশব ব্রাহ্মণ পাঠাঞা ।\\nচলিবার তরে প্রভুরে পাঠাইল কহিঞা ॥১৭৪॥
verses.transliteration: rājāre prabodhi' keśava brāhmaṇa pāṭhāñā\\ncalibāra tare prabhure pāṭhāila kahiñā
verses.translation: After pacifying the King in this way, Keśava Chatrī sent a brāhmaṇa messenger to Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu, requesting Him to leave without delay.

verses.devanagari: দবির খাসেরে রাজা পুছিল নিভৃতে ।\\nগোসাঞির মহিমা তেঁহো লাগিল কহিতে ॥১৭৫॥
verses.transliteration: dabira khāsere rājā puchila nibhṛte\\ngosāñira mahimā teṅho lāgila kahite
verses.translation: In private, the King inquired from Dabira Khāsa [Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī], who began to speak about the glories of the Lord.

verses.devanagari: যে তোমারে রাজ্য দিল, যে তোমার গোসাঞা ।\\nতোমার দেশে তোমার ভাগ্যে জন্মিলা আসিঞা ॥১৭৬॥
verses.transliteration: ye tomāre rājya dila, ye tomāra gosāñā\\ntomāra deśe tomāra bhāgye janmilā āsiñā
verses.translation: Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī said, "The Supreme Personality of Godhead, who gave you this kingdom and whom you accept as a prophet, has taken birth in your country due to your good fortune.

verses.devanagari: তোমার মঙ্গল বাঞ্ছে, কার্যসিদ্ধি হয় ।\\nইহার আশীর্বাদে তোমার সর্বত্রই জয় ॥১৭৭॥
verses.transliteration: tomāra maṅgala vāñche, kārya-siddhi haya\\nihāra āśīrvāde tomāra sarvatra-i jaya
verses.translation: "This prophet always desires your good fortune. By His grace, all your business is successful. By His blessings, you will attain victory everywhere.

verses.devanagari: মোরে কেন পুছ, তুমি পুছ আপন-মন ।\\nতুমি নরাধিপ হও বিষ্ণু-অংশ সম ॥১৭৮॥
verses.transliteration: more kena pucha, tumi pucha āpana-mana\\ntumi narādhipa hao viṣṇu-aṁśa sama
verses.translation: "Why are you questioning me? Better that you question your own mind. Because you are the King of the people, you are the representative of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Therefore you can understand this better than I."

verses.devanagari: তোমার চিত্তে চৈতন্যেরে কৈছে হয় জ্ঞান ।\\nতোমার চিত্তে যেই লয়, সেই ত’ প্রমাণ ॥১৭৯॥
verses.transliteration: tomāra citte caitanyere kaiche haya jñāna\\ntomāra citte yei laya, sei ta' pramāṇa
verses.translation: Thus Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī informed the King about his mind as a way of knowing Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. He assured the King that whatever occurred in his mind could be considered evidence.

verses.devanagari: রাজা কহে, শুন, মোর মনে যেই লয় ।\\nসাক্ষাৎ ঈশ্বর ইহঁ নাহিক সংশয় ॥১৮০॥
verses.transliteration: rājā kahe, śuna, mora mane yei laya\\nsākṣāt īśvara ihaṅ nāhika saṁśaya
verses.translation: The King replied, "I consider Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu to be the Supreme Personality of Godhead. There is no doubt about it."

verses.devanagari: এত কহি’ রাজা গেলা নিজ অভ্যন্তরে ।\\nতবে দবির খাস আইলা আপনার ঘরে ॥১৮১॥
verses.transliteration: eta kahi' rājā gelā nija abhyantare\\ntabe dabira khāsa āilā āpanāra ghare
verses.translation: After having this conversation with Rūpa Gosvāmī, the King entered his private house. Rūpa Gosvāmī, then known as Dabira Khāsa, also returned to his residence.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
A monarch is certainly a representative of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. As stated in
Bhagavad-gītā, sarva-loka-maheśvaram:
the Supreme Personality of Godhead is the proprietor of all planetary systems. In each and every planet there must be some king, governmental head or executive. Such a person is supposed to be the representative of Lord Viṣṇu. On behalf of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, he must see to the interests of all the people. Therefore Lord Viṣṇu, as Paramātmā, gives the king all intelligence to execute governmental affairs. Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī therefore asked the King what was in his mind concerning Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and indicated that whatever the King thought about Him was correct.

verses.devanagari: ঘরে আসি’ দুই ভাই যুকতি করিঞা ।\\nপ্রভু দেখিবারে চলে বেশ লুকাঞা ॥১৮২॥
verses.transliteration: ghare āsi' dui bhāi yukati kariñā\\nprabhu dekhibāre cale veśa lukāñā
verses.translation: After returning to his residence, Dabira Khāsa and his brother decided after much consideration to go see the Lord incognito.

verses.devanagari: অর্ধরাত্রে দুই ভাই আইলা প্রভু-স্থানে ।\\nপ্রথমে মিলিলা নিত্যানন্দ-হরিদাস সনে ॥১৮৩॥
verses.transliteration: ardha-rātre dui bhāi āilā prabhu-sthāne\\nprathame mililā nityānanda-haridāsa sane
verses.translation: Thus in the dead of night the two brothers, Dabira Khāsa and Sākara Mallika, went to see Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu incognito. First they met Nityānanda Prabhu and Haridāsa Ṭhākura.

verses.devanagari: তাঁরা দুইজন জানাইলা প্রভুর গোচরে ।\\nরূপ, সাকরমল্লিক আইলা তোমা’ দেখিবারে ॥১৮৪॥
verses.transliteration: tāṅrā dui-jana jānāilā prabhura gocare\\nrūpa, sākara-mallika āilā tomā' dekhibāre
verses.translation: Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu and Haridāsa Ṭhākura told Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu that two personalities-Śrī Rūpa and Sanātana-had come to see Him.
verses.purport: PURPORT\nSākara Mallika was the name of Sanātana Gosvāmī, and Dabira Khāsa was the name of Rūpa Gosvāmī. They were recognized by these names in the service of the Mohammedan King; therefore these are Mohammedan names. As officials, the brothers adopted all kinds of Mohammedan customs.

verses.devanagari: দুই গুচ্ছ তৃণ দুঁহে দশনে ধরিঞা ।\\nগলে বস্ত্র বান্ধি’ পড়ে দণ্ডবৎ হঞা ॥১৮৫॥
verses.transliteration: dui guccha tṛṇa duṅhe daśane dhariñā\\ngale vastra bāndhi' paḍe daṇḍavat hañā
verses.translation: In great humility, both brothers took bunches of straw between their teeth and, each binding a cloth around his neck, fell down like rods before the Lord.

verses.devanagari: দৈন্য রোদন করে, আনন্দে বিহ্বল ।\\nপ্রভু কহে, — উঠ, উঠ, হইল মঙ্গল ॥১৮৬॥
verses.transliteration: dainya rodana kare, ānande vihvala\\nprabhu kahe,—uṭha, uṭha, ha-ila maṅgala
verses.translation: Upon seeing Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the two brothers were overwhelmed with joy, and out of humility they began to cry. Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu asked them to get up and assured them of all good fortune.

verses.devanagari: উঠি’ দুই ভাই তবে দন্তে তৃণ ধরি’ ।\\nদৈন্য করি’ স্তুতি করে করযোড় করি ॥১৮৭॥
verses.transliteration: uṭhi' dui bhāi tabe dante tṛṇa dhari'\\ndainya kari' stuti kare karayoḍa kari
verses.translation: The two brothers got up, and again taking straw between their teeth, they humbly offered their prayers with folded hands.

verses.devanagari: জয় জয় শ্রীকৃষ্ণচৈতন্য দয়াময় ।\\nপতিতপাবন জয়, জয় মহাশয় ॥১৮৮॥
verses.transliteration: jaya jaya śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya dayā-maya\\npatita-pāvana jaya, jaya mahāśaya
verses.translation: "All glories to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the most merciful savior of the fallen souls! All glories to the Supreme Personality!

verses.devanagari: নীচ-জাতি, নীচ-সঙ্গী, করি নীচ কাজ ।\\nতোমার অগ্রেতে প্রভু কহিতে বাসি লাজ ॥১৮৯॥
verses.transliteration: nīca-jāti, nīca-saṅgī, kari nīca kāja\\ntomāra agrete prabhu kahite vāsi lāja
verses.translation: "Sir, we belong to the lowest class of men, and our associates and employment are also of the lowest type. Therefore we cannot introduce ourselves to You. We feel very much ashamed, standing here before You.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
Although the two brothers, Rūpa and Sanātana (at that time Dabira Khāsa and Sākara Mallika), presented themselves as being born in a low family, they nonetheless belonged to a most respectable
brāhmaṇa
family that was originally from Karṇāta. Thus they actually belonged to the
brāhmaṇa
caste. Unfortunately, because of being associated with the Mohammedan governmental service, their customs and behavior resembled those of the Mohammedans. Therefore they presented themselves as
nīca-jāti.
The word
jāti
means birth. According to
śāstra,
there are three kinds of birth. The first birth is from the womb of the mother, the second birth is the acceptance of the reformatory method, and the third birth is acceptance by the spiritual master (initiation). One becomes abominable by adopting an abominable profession or by associating with people who are naturally abominable. Rūpa and Sanātana, as Dabira Khāsa and Sākara Mallika, associated with Mohammedans, who were naturally opposed to brahminical culture and cow protection. In
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(Seventh Canto) it is stated that every person belongs to a certain classification. A person is identifiable by the special symptoms mentioned in the
śāstras.
By one's symptoms, one is known to belong to a certain caste. Both Dabira Khāsa and Sākara Mallika belonged to the
brāhmaṇa
caste, but because they were employed by Mohammedans, their original habits degenerated into those of the Mohammedan community. Since the symptoms of brahminical culture were almost nil, they identified themselves with the lowest caste. In the
Bhakti-ratnākara
it is clearly stated that because Sākara Mallika and Dabira Khāsa associated with lower-class men, they introduced themselves as belonging to the lower classes. Actually, however, they had been born in respectable
brāhmaṇa
families.

verses.devanagari: মত্তুল্যো নাস্তি পাপাত্মা নাপরাধী চ কশ্চন ।\\nপরিহারেঽপি লজ্জা মে কিং ব্রুবে পুরুষোত্তম ॥১৯০॥
verses.transliteration: mat-tulyo nāsti pāpātmā\\nnāparādhī ca kaścana\\nparihāre 'pi lajjā me\\nkiṁ bruve puruṣottama
verses.translation: "Dear Lord, let us inform you that no one is more sinful than us, nor is there any offender like us. Even if we wanted to mention our sinful activities, we would immediately become ashamed. And what to speak of giving them up!"
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This verse is from the
Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu
(1.2.154), by Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī.

verses.devanagari: পতিত-পাবন-হেতু তোমার অবতার ।\\nআমা-বই জগতে, পতিত নাহি আর ॥১৯১॥
verses.transliteration: patita-pāvana-hetu tomāra avatāra\\nāmā-ba-i jagate, patita nāhi āra
verses.translation: Both brothers submitted, "Dear Lord, You have incarnated to deliver the fallen souls. You should consider that in this world there is none so fallen as us.

verses.devanagari: জগাই-মাধাই দুই করিলে উদ্ধার ।\\nতাহাঁ উদ্ধারিতে শ্রম নহিল তোমার ॥১৯২॥
verses.transliteration: jagāi-mādhāi dui karile uddhāra\\ntāhāṅ uddhārite śrama nahila tomāra
verses.translation: "You have delivered the two brothers Jagāi and Mādhāi, but to deliver them You did not have to exert Yourself very much.

verses.devanagari: ব্রাহ্মণজাতি তারা, নবদ্বীপে ঘর ।\\nনীচ-সেবা নাহি করে, নহে নীচের কূর্পর ॥১৯৩॥
verses.transliteration: brāhmaṇa-jāti tārā, navadvīpe ghara\\nnīca-sevā nāhi kare, nahe nīcera kūrpara
verses.translation: "The brothers Jagāi and Mādhāi belonged to the brāhmaṇa caste, and their residence was in the holy place of Navadvīpa. They never served low-class persons, nor were they instruments to abominable activities.

verses.devanagari: সবে এক দোষ তার, হয় পাপাচার ।\\nপাপরাশি দহে নামাভাসেই তোমার ॥১৯৪॥
verses.transliteration: sabe eka doṣa tāra, haya pāpācāra\\npāpa-rāśi dahe nāmābhāsei tomāra
verses.translation: "Jagāi and Mādhāi had but one fault—they were addicted to sinful activity. However, volumes of sinful activity can be burned to ashes simply by a dim reflection of the chanting of Your holy name.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī and Sanātana Gosvāmī presented themselves as being lower than the two brothers Jagāi and Mādhāi, who were delivered by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. When Rūpa and Sanātana compared themselves to Jagāi and Mādhāi, they found themselves inferior because the Lord had no trouble in delivering two drunken brothers. This was so because, despite the fact that they were addicted to sinful activity, in other ways their life was brilliant. They belonged to the
brāhmaṇa
caste of Navadvīpa, and such
brāhmaṇas
were pious by nature. Although they had been addicted to some sinful activities due to bad association, those unwanted things could vanish simply because of the chanting of the holy name of the Lord. Another point for Jagāi and Mādhāi was that, as members of a
brāhmaṇa
family, they did not accept service under anyone. The
śāstras
strictly forbid a
brāhmaṇa
to accept service under anyone. The idea is that by accepting a master, one accepts the occupation of a dog. In other words, a dog cannot thrive without having a master, and for the sake of pleasing the master, dogs offend many people. They bark at innocent people just to please the master. Similarly, when one is a servant, he has to perform abominable activities according to the orders of the master. Therefore, when Dabira Khāsa and Sākara Mallika compared their position to that of Jagāi and Mādhāi, they found Jagāi and Mādhāi's position far better. Jagāi and Mādhāi never accepted the service of a low-class person; nor were they forced to execute abominable activities under the order of a low-class master. Jagāi and Mādhāi chanted the name of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu by way of blasphemy, but because they simply chanted His name, they immediately became free from the reactions of sinful activities. Thus later they were saved.

verses.devanagari: তোমার নাম লঞা তোমার করিল নিন্দন ।\\nসেই নাম হইল তার মুক্তির কারণ ॥১৯৫॥
verses.transliteration: tomāra nāma lañā tomāra karila nindana\\nsei nāma ha-ila tāra muktira kāraṇa
verses.translation: "Jagāi and Mādhāi uttered Your holy name by way of blaspheming You. Fortunately, that holy name became the cause of their deliverance.

verses.devanagari: জগাই-মাধাই হৈতে কোটী কোটী গুণ ।\\nঅধম পতিত পাপী আমি দুই জন ॥১৯৬॥
verses.transliteration: jagāi-mādhāi haite koṭī koṭī guṇa\\nadhama patita pāpī āmi dui jana
verses.translation: "We two are millions and millions of times inferior to Jagāi and Mādhāi. We are more degraded, fallen and sinful than they.

verses.devanagari: ম্লেচ্ছজাতি, ম্লেচ্ছসেবী, করি ম্লেচ্ছকর্ম ।\\nগো-ব্রাহ্মণ-দ্রোহি-সঙ্গে আমার সঙ্গম ॥১৯৭॥
verses.transliteration: mleccha-jāti, mleccha-sevī, kari mleccha-karma\\ngo-brāhmaṇa-drohi-saṅge āmāra saṅgama
verses.translation: "Actually we belong to the caste of meat-eaters because we are servants of meat-eaters. Indeed, our activities are exactly like those of the meat-eaters. Because we always associate with such people, we are inimical toward the cows and brāhmaṇas."
verses.purport:
PURPORT
There are two kinds of meat-eaters-one who is born in a family of meat-eaters and one who has learned to associate with meat-eaters. From Śrīla Rūpa and Sanātana Gosvāmīs (formerly Dabira Khāsa and Sākara Mallika) we can learn how one attains the character of a meat-eater simply by associating with meat-eaters. At the present moment in India the presidential offices are occupied by many so-called
brāhmaṇas,
but the state maintains slaughterhouses for killing cows and makes propaganda against Vedic civilization. The first principle of Vedic civilization is the avoidance of meat-eating and intoxication. Presently in India, intoxication and meat-eating are encouraged, and the so-called learned
brāhmaṇas
presiding over this state of affairs have certainly become degraded according to the standard given herein by Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī and Sanātana Gosvāmī. These so-called
brāhmaṇas
give sanction to slaughterhouses for the sake of a fat salary, and they do not protest these abominable activities. By deprecating the principles of Vedic civilization and supporting cow-killing, they are immediately degraded to the platform of
mlecchas
and
yavanas. A mleccha
is a meat-eater, and a
yavana
is one who has deviated from Vedic culture. Unfortunately, such
mlecchas
and
yavanas
are in executive power. How, then, can there be peace and prosperity in the state? The king or the president must be the representative of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. When Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira accepted the rule of Bhārata-varṣa (formerly this entire planet, including all the seas and land), he took sanction from authorities like Bhīṣmadeva and Lord Kṛṣṇa. He thus ruled the entire world according to religious principles. At the present moment, however, heads of state do not care for religious principles. If irreligious people vote on an issue, even though it be against the principles of the
śāstras,
the bills will be passed. The president and heads of state become sinful by agreeing to such abominable activities. Sanātana and Rūpa Gosvāmīs pleaded guilty to such activities; they therefore classified themselves among the
mlecchas,
although born in a
brāhmaṇa
family.

verses.devanagari: মোর কর্ম, মোর হাতে-গলায় বান্ধিয়া ।\\nকু-বিষয়-বিষ্ঠা-গর্তে দিয়াছে ফেলাইয়া ॥১৯৮॥
verses.transliteration: mora karma, mora hāte-galāya bāndhiyā\\nku-viṣaya-viṣṭhā-garte diyāche phelāiyā
verses.translation: The two brothers, Sākara Mallika and Dabira Khāsa, very humbly submitted that due to their abominable activities they were now bound by the neck and hands and had been thrown into a ditch filled with abominable stoollike objects of material sense enjoyment.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura has explained
ku-viṣaya garta
as follows: "Because of the activities of the senses, we become subjected to many sense gratificatory processes and are thus entangled by the laws of material nature. This entanglement is called
viṣaya.
When the sense gratificatory processes are executed by pious activity, they are called
su-viṣaya.
The word
su
means 'good,' and
viṣaya
means 'sense objects.' When the sense gratificatory activities are performed under sinful conditions, they are called
ku-viṣaya,
bad sense enjoyment. In either case, either
ku-viṣaya
or
su-viṣaya,
these are material activities. As such, they are compared to stool. In other words, such things are to be avoided. To become free from
su-viṣaya
and
ku-viṣaya,
one must engage himself in the transcendental loving service of Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead. The activities of devotional service are free from the contamination of material qualities. Therefore, to be free from the reactions of
su-viṣaya
and
ku-viṣaya,
one must take to Kṛṣṇa consciousness. In that way, one will save himself from contamination." In this connection, Śrīla Narottama dāsa Ṭhākura has sung:
karma-kāṇḍa, jñāna-kāṇḍa, kevala viṣera bhāṇḍa
amṛta baliyā yeba khāya
nānā yoni sadā phire, kadarya bhakṣaṇa kare
tāra janma adhaḥ-pāte yāya
Su-viṣaya and
ku-viṣaya
both fall under the category of
karma-kāṇḍa.
There is another
kāṇḍa
(platform of activity), called
jñāna-kāṇḍa,
or philosophical speculation about the effects of
ku-viṣaya
and
su-viṣaya
with the intention to find out the means of deliverance from material entanglement. On the platform of
jñāna-kāṇḍa,
one may give up the objects of
ku-viṣaya
and
su-viṣaya.
But that is not the perfection of life. Perfection is transcendental to both
jñāna-kāṇḍa
and
karma-kāṇḍa;
it is on the platform of devotional service. If we do not take to devotional service in Kṛṣṇa consciousness, we have to remain within this material world and endure the repetition of birth and death due to the effects of
jñāna-kāṇḍa
and
karma-kāṇḍa.
Therefore Narottama dāsa Ṭhākura says:
nānā yoni sadā phire, kadarya bhakṣaṇa kare
tāra janma adhaḥ-pāte yāya
"One travels throughout various species of life and eats all kinds of nonsense. Thus he spoils his existence." A man in material existence and attached to
ku-viṣaya
or
su-viṣaya
is in the same position as that of a worm in stool. After all, whether it be moist or dry, stool is stool. Similarly, material activities may be either pious or impious, but because they are all material, they are compared to stool. Worms cannot get out of stool by their own endeavor; similarly, those who are overly attached to material existence cannot get out of materialism and suddenly become Kṛṣṇa conscious. Attachment is there. As explained by Prahlāda Mahārāja in
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(7.5.30):
matir na kṛṣṇe parataḥ svato vā
mitho 'bhipadyeta gṛha-vratānām
adānta-gobhir viśatāṁ tamisraṁ
punaḥ-punaś-carvita-carvaṇānām
"Those who have made up their minds to remain in this material world and enjoy sense gratification cannot become Kṛṣṇa conscious. Because of their attachment to material activity, they cannot attain liberation, either by the instructions of superior persons or by their own endeavor or by passing resolutions in big conferences. Because their senses are uncontrolled, they gradually descend to the darkest regions of material existence to repeat the same process of birth and death in desirable or undesirable species of life."

verses.devanagari: আমা উদ্ধারিতে বলী নাহি ত্রিভুবনে ।\\nপতিতপাবন তুমি — সবে তোমা বিনে ॥১৯৯॥
verses.transliteration: āmā uddhārite balī nāhi tri-bhuvane\\npatita-pāvana tumi—sabe tomā vine
verses.translation: "No one within the three worlds is sufficiently powerful to deliver us. You are the only savior of the fallen souls; therefore there is no one but You.

verses.devanagari: আমা উদ্ধারিয়া যদি দেখাও নিজ-বল ।\\n‘পতিতপাবন’ নাম তবে সে সফল ॥২০০॥
verses.transliteration: āmā uddhāriyā yadi dekhāo nija-bala\\n'patita-pāvana' nāma tabe se saphala
verses.translation: "If You simply deliver us by Your transcendental strength, then certainly Your name will be known as Patita-pāvana, the savior of the fallen souls.

verses.devanagari: সত্য এক বাত কহোঁ, শুন, দয়াময় ।\\nমো-বিনু দয়ার পাত্র জগতে না হয় ॥২০১॥
verses.transliteration: satya eka bāta kahoṅ, śuna, dayā-maya\\nmo-vinu dayāra pātra jagate nā haya
verses.translation: "Let us speak one word that is very true. Plainly hear us, O merciful one. There is no other object of mercy within the three worlds but us.

verses.devanagari: মোরে দয়া করি’ কর স্বদয়া সফল ।\\nঅখিল ব্রহ্মাণ্ড দেখুক তোমার দয়া-বল ॥২০২॥
verses.transliteration: more dayā kari' kara sva-dayā saphala\\nakhila brahmāṇḍa dekhuka tomāra dayā-bala
verses.translation: "We are the most fallen; therefore by showing us Your mercy, Your mercy is most successful. Let the power of Your mercy be exhibited throughout the entire universe!

verses.devanagari: ন মৃষা পরমার্থমেব মে, শৃণু বিজ্ঞাপনমেকমগ্রতঃ ।\\nযদি মে ন দয়িষ্যসে তদা, দয়নীয়স্তব নাথ দুর্লভঃ ॥২০৩॥
verses.transliteration: na mṛṣā paramārtham eva me\\nśṛṇu vijñāpanam ekam agrataḥ\\nyadi me na dayiṣyase tadā\\ndayanīyas tava nātha durlabhaḥ
verses.translation: “ 'Let us submit one piece of information before You, dear Lord. It is not at all false but is full of meaning. It is this: If You are not merciful upon us, then it will be very, very difficult to find more suitable candidates for Your mercy.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This verse is from the
Stotra-ratna
(47), by Śrī Yāmunācārya.

verses.devanagari: আপনে অযোগ্য দেখি’ মনে পাঙ ক্ষোভ ।\\nতথাপি তোমার গুণে উপজয় লোভ ॥২০৪॥
verses.transliteration: āpane ayogya dekhi' mane pāṅ kṣobha\\ntathāpi tomāra guṇe upajaya lobha
verses.translation: "We are very depressed at being unfit candidates for Your mercy. Yet since we have heard of Your transcendental qualities, we are very much attracted to You.

verses.devanagari: বামন যৈছে চাঁদ ধরিতে চাহে করে ।\\nতৈছে এই বাঞ্ছা মোর উঠয়ে অন্তরে ॥২০৫॥
verses.transliteration: vāmana yaiche cāṅda dharite cāhe kare\\ntaiche ei vāñchā mora uṭhaye antare
verses.translation: "Indeed, we are like a dwarf who wants to capture the moon. Although we are completely unfit, a desire to receive Your mercy is awakening within our minds.

verses.devanagari: ভবন্তমেবানুচরন্নিরন্তরঃ\\nপ্রশান্তনিঃশেষমনোরথান্তরঃ ।\\nকদাহমৈকান্তিকনিত্যকিঙ্করঃ\\nপ্রহর্ষয়িষ্যামি সনাথজীবিতম্ ॥২০৬॥
verses.transliteration: bhavantam evānucaran nirantaraḥ\\npraśānta-niḥśeṣa-mano-rathāntaraḥ\\nkadāham aikāntika-nitya-kiṅkaraḥ\\npraharṣayiṣyāmi sanātha-jīvitam
verses.translation: “ 'By serving You constantly, one is freed from all material desires and is completely pacified. When shall I engage as Your permanent eternal servant and always feel joyful to have such a fitting master?' "
verses.purport:
PURPORT
In His teachings to Sanātana Gosvāmī, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu has declared every living entity to be an eternal servitor of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. This is the constitutional position of all living entities. Just as a dog or servant is very satisfied to get a competent, perfect master, or as a child is completely satisfied to possess a competent father, so the living entity is satisfied by completely engaging in the service of the Supreme Lord. He thereby knows that he has a competent master to save him from all kinds of danger. Unless the living entity comes to the guaranteed protection of the Supreme Lord, He is full of anxiety. This life of anxiety is called material existence. To be completely satisfied and devoid of anxiety, one must come to the position of eternally rendering service to the Supreme Lord. This verse is also from the
Stotra-ratna
(43) by Śrī Yāmunācārya.

verses.devanagari: শুনি’ মহাপ্রভু কহে, — শুন, দবির-খাস ।\\nতুমি দুই ভাই — মোর পুরাতন দাস ॥২০৭॥
verses.transliteration: śuni' mahāprabhu kahe,—śuna, dabira-khāsa\\ntumi dui bhāi—mora purātana dāsa
verses.translation: After hearing the prayer of Dabira Khāsa and Sākara Mallika, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "My dear Dabira Khāsa, you two brothers are My old servants.

verses.devanagari: আজি হৈতে দুঁহার নাম ‘রূপ’ ‘সনাতন’ ।\\nদৈন্য ছাড়, তোমার দৈন্যে ফাটে মোর মন ॥২০৮॥
verses.transliteration: āji haite duṅhāra nāma 'rūpa' 'sanātana'\\ndainya chāḍa, tomāra dainye phāṭe mora mana
verses.translation: "My dear Sākara Mallika, from this day your names will be changed to Śrīla Rūpa and Śrīla Sanātana. Now please abandon your humility, for My heart is breaking to see you so humble.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
Actually this is Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's initiation of Dabira Khāsa and Sākara Mallika. They approached the Lord with all humility, and the Lord accepted them as old servants, as eternal servants, and He changed their names. It is to be understood from this that it is essential for a disciple to change his name after initiation.
śaṅkha-cakrādy-ūrdhva-puṇḍra-
dhāraṇādy-ātma-lakṣaṇam
tan nāma-karaṇaṁ caiva
vaiṣṇavatvam ihocyate
"After initiation, the disciple's name must be changed to indicate that he is a servant of Lord Viṣṇu. The disciple should also immediately begin marking his body with
tilaka
(
ūrdhva-puṇḍra
), especially his forehead. These are spiritual marks, symptoms of a perfect Vaiṣṇava." This is a verse from the
Padma Purāṇa, Uttara-khaṇḍa.
A member of the
sahajiyā-sampradāya
does not change his name; therefore he cannot be accepted as a Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava. If a person does not change his name after initiation, it is to be understood that he will continue in his bodily conception of life.

verses.devanagari: দৈন্যপত্রী লিখি’ মোরে পাঠালে বার বার ।\\nসেই পত্রীদ্বারা জানি তোমার ব্যবহার ॥২০৯॥
verses.transliteration: dainya-patrī likhi' more pāṭhāle bāra bāra\\nsei patrī-dvārā jāni tomāra vyavahāra
verses.translation: "You have written several letters showing your humility. I can understand your behavior from those letters.

verses.devanagari: তোমার হৃদয় আমি জানি পত্রীদ্বারে ।\\nতোমা শিখাইতে শ্লোক পাঠাইল তোমারে ॥২১০॥
verses.transliteration: tomāra hṛdaya āmi jāni patrī-dvāre\\ntomā śikhāite śloka pāṭhāila tomāre
verses.translation: "By your letters, I could understand your heart. Therefore, in order to teach you, I sent you one verse, which reads as follows.

verses.devanagari: পরব্যসনিনী নারী ব্যগ্রাপি গৃহকর্মসু ।\\nতদেবাস্বাদয়ত্যন্তর্নবসঙ্গরসায়নম্ ॥২১১॥
verses.transliteration: para-vyasaninī nārī\\nvyagrāpi gṛha-karmasu\\ntad evāsvādayaty antar\\nnava-saṅga-rasāyanam
verses.translation: “ 'If a woman is attached to a man other than her husband, she will appear very busy in carrying out her household affairs, but within her heart she is always relishing feelings of association with her paramour.'

verses.devanagari: গৌড়-নিকট আসিতে নাহি মোর প্রয়োজন ।\\nতোমা-দুঁহা দেখিতে মোর ইহাঁ আগমন ॥২১২॥
verses.transliteration: gauḍa-nikaṭa āsite nāhi mora prayojana\\ntomā-duṅhā dekhite mora ihāṅ āgamana
verses.translation: "I really had no business in coming to Bengal, but I have come just to see you two brothers.

verses.devanagari: এই মোর মনের কথা কেহ নাহি জানে ।\\nসবে বলে, কেনে আইলা রামকেলি-গ্রামে ॥২১৩॥
verses.transliteration: ei mora manera kathā keha nāhi jāne\\nsabe bale, kene āilā rāma-keli-grāme
verses.translation: "Everyone is asking why I have come to this village of Rāmakeli. No one knows My intentions.

verses.devanagari: ভাল হৈল, দুই ভাই আইলা মোর স্থানে ।\\nঘরে যাহ, ভয় কিছু না করিহ মনে ॥২১৪॥
verses.transliteration: bhāla haila, dui bhāi āilā mora sthāne\\nghare yāha, bhaya kichu nā kariha mane
verses.translation: "It is very good that you two brothers have come to see Me. Now you can go home. Do not fear anything.

verses.devanagari: জন্মে জন্মে তুমি দুই — কিঙ্কর আমার ।\\nঅচিরাতে কৃষ্ণ তোমায় করিবে উদ্ধার ॥২১৫॥
verses.transliteration: janme janme tumi dui—kiṅkara āmāra\\nacirāte kṛṣṇa tomāya karibe uddhāra
verses.translation: "Birth after birth you have been My eternal servants. I am sure that Kṛṣṇa will deliver you very soon."

verses.devanagari: এত বলি দুঁহার শিরে ধরিল দুই হাতে ।\\nদুই ভাই প্রভু-পদ নিল নিজ মাথে ॥২১৬॥
verses.transliteration: eta bali duṅhāra śire dharila dui hāte\\ndui bhāi prabhu-pada nila nija māthe
verses.translation: The Lord then placed His two hands on the heads of both of them, and in return they immediately placed the lotus feet of the Lord on their heads.

verses.devanagari: দোঁহা আলিঙ্গিয়া প্রভু বলিল ভক্তগণে ।\\nসবে কৃপা করি’ উদ্ধারহ দুই জনে ॥২১৭॥
verses.transliteration: doṅhā āliṅgiyā prabhu balila bhakta-gaṇe\\nsabe kṛpā kari' uddhāraha dui jane
verses.translation: After this, the Lord embraced both of them and requested all of the devotees present to be merciful upon them and deliver them.

verses.devanagari: দুই জনে প্ৰভুর কৃপা দেখি’ ভক্তগণে ।\\n‘হরি’ ‘হরি’ বলে সবে আনন্দিত-মনে ॥২১৮॥
verses.transliteration: dui jane prabhura kṛpā dekhi' bhakta-gaṇe\\n'hari' 'hari' bale sabe ānandita-mane
verses.translation: When all of the devotees saw the mercy of the Lord upon the two brothers, they were very gladdened, and they began to chant the holy name of the Lord, "Hari! Hari!"
verses.purport:
PURPORT
Śrīla Narottama dāsa Ṭhākura says,
chāḍiyā vaiṣṇava sevā nistāra pāyeche kebā:
unless one serves a Vaiṣṇava, he cannot be delivered. The spiritual master initiates the disciple to deliver him, and if the disciple executes the order of the spiritual master and does not offend other Vaiṣṇavas, his path is clear. Consequently Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu requested all the Vaiṣṇavas present to show mercy toward the two brothers, Rūpa and Sanātana, who had just been initiated by the Lord. When a Vaiṣṇava sees that another Vaiṣṇava is a recipient of the Lord's mercy, he becomes very happy. Vaiṣṇavas are not envious. If a Vaiṣṇava, by the mercy of the Lord, is empowered by Him to distribute the Lord's holy name all over the world, other Vaiṣṇavas become very joyful—that is, if they are truly Vaiṣṇavas. One who is envious of the success of a Vaiṣṇava is certainly not a Vaiṣṇava himself, but an ordinary mundane man. Envy and jealousy are manifested by mundane people, not by Vaiṣṇavas. Why should a Vaiṣṇava be envious of another Vaiṣṇava who is successful in spreading the holy name of the Lord? An actual Vaiṣṇava is very pleased to accept another Vaiṣṇava who is bestowing the Lord's mercy. A mundane person in the dress of a Vaiṣṇava should not be respected but rejected. This is enjoined in the
śāstra
(
upekṣā
). The word
upekṣā
means neglect. One should neglect an envious person. A preacher's duty is to love the Supreme Personality of Godhead, make friendships with Vaiṣṇavas, show mercy to the innocent and reject or neglect those who are envious or jealous. There are many jealous people in the dress of Vaiṣṇavas in this Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement, and they should be completely neglected. There is no need to serve a jealous person who is in the dress of a Vaiṣṇava. When Narottama dāsa Ṭhākura says
chāḍiyā vaiṣṇava sevā nistāra payeche kebā,
he is indicating an actual Vaiṣṇava, not an envious or jealous person in the dress of a Vaiṣṇava.

verses.devanagari: নিত্যানন্দ, হরিদাস, শ্রীবাস, গদাধর ।\\nমুকুন্দ, জগদানন্দ, মুরারি, বক্রেশ্বর ॥২১৯॥
verses.transliteration: nityānanda, haridāsa, śrīvāsa, gadādhara\\nmukunda, jagadānanda, murāri, vakreśvara
verses.translation: All the Vaiṣṇava associates of the Lord were present, including Nityānanda, Haridāsa Ṭhākura, Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura, Gadādhara Paṇḍita, Mukunda, Jagadānanda, Murāri and Vakreśvara.

verses.devanagari: সবার চরণে ধরি, পড়ে দুই ভাই ।\\nসবে বলে, — ধন্য তুমি, পাইলে গোসাঞি ॥২২০॥
verses.transliteration: sabāra caraṇe dhari, paḍe dui bhāi\\nsabe bale,—dhanya tumi, pāile gosāñi
verses.translation: In accordance with the instructions of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the two brothers, Rūpa and Sanātana, immediately touched the lotus feet of these Vaiṣṇavas, who all became very happy and congratulated the two brothers for having received the mercy of the Lord.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This behavior is indicative of real Vaiṣṇavas. When they saw that Rūpa and Sanātana were fortunate enough to receive the mercy of the Lord, they were so pleased that they all congratulated the two brothers. A jealous person in the dress of a Vaiṣṇava is not at all happy to see the success of another Vaiṣṇava in receiving the Lord's mercy. Unfortunately in this Age of Kali there are many mundane persons in the dress of Vaiṣṇavas, and Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura has described them as disciples of Kali. He says,
kali-celā.
He indicates that there is another Vaiṣṇava, a pseudoVaiṣṇava with
tilaka
on his nose and
kaṇṭhī
beads around his neck. Such a pseudoVaiṣṇava associates with money and women and is jealous of successful Vaiṣṇavas. Although passing for a Vaiṣṇava, his only business is earning money in the dress of a Vaiṣṇava. Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura therefore says that such a pseudoVaiṣṇava is not a Vaiṣṇava at all but a disciple of Kali-yuga. A disciple of Kali cannot become an
ācārya
by the decision of some high court. Mundane votes have no jurisdiction to elect a Vaiṣṇava
ācārya.
A Vaiṣṇava
ācārya
is self-effulgent, and there is no need for any court judgment. A false
ācārya
may try to override a Vaiṣṇava by a high-court decision, but Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura says that he is nothing but a disciple of Kali-yuga.

verses.devanagari: সবা-পাশ আজ্ঞা মাগি’ চলন-সময় ।\\nপ্রভু-পদে কহে কিছু করিয়া বিনয় ॥২২১॥
verses.transliteration: sabā-pāśa ājñā māgi' calana-samaya\\nprabhu-pade kahe kichu kariyā vinaya
verses.translation: After begging the permission of all the Vaiṣṇavas present, the two brothers, at the time of their departure, humbly submitted something at the lotus feet of the Lord.

verses.devanagari: ইহাঁ হৈতে চল, প্রভু, ইহাঁ নাহি কায ।\\nযদ্যপি তোমারে ভক্তি করে গৌড়রাজ ॥২২২॥
verses.transliteration: ihāṅ haite cala, prabhu, ihāṅ nāhi kāya\\nyadyapi tomāre bhakti kare gauḍa-rāja
verses.translation: They said, "Dear Lord, although the King of Bengal, Nawab Husena Sāhā, is very respectful toward You, You have no other business here. Kindly depart from this place.

verses.devanagari: তথাপি যবন জাতি, না করি প্রতীতি ।\\nতীর্থযাত্রায় এত সংঘট্ট ভাল নহে রীতি ॥২২৩॥
verses.transliteration: tathāpi yavana jāti, nā kari pratīti\\ntīrtha-yātrāya eta saṅghaṭṭa bhāla nahe rīti
verses.translation: "Although the King is respectful toward You, he still belongs to the yavana class and should not be believed. We think that there is no need for such a great crowd to accompany You on Your pilgrimage to Vṛndāvana.

verses.devanagari: যার সঙ্গে চলে এই লোক লক্ষকোটি ।\\nবৃন্দাবন-যাত্রার এ নহে পরিপাটী ॥২২৪॥
verses.transliteration: yāra saṅge cale ei loka lakṣa-koṭi\\nvṛndāvana-yātrāra e nahe paripāṭī
verses.translation: "Dear Lord, You are going to Vṛndāvana with hundreds and thousands of people following You, and this is not a fitting way to go on a pilgrimage."
verses.purport: PURPORT\nSometimes, for business purposes, large crowds of men are taken to different places of pilgrimage, and money is collected from them. That is a very lucrative business, but Rūpa and Sanātana Gosvāmīs, expressing their opinion in the presence of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu, disapproved of such crowded pilgrimages. Actually when Lord Caitanya visited Vṛndāvana, He visited it alone and accepted a servant only at His devotees' request. He never visited Vṛndāvana with crowds of people for a commercial purpose.

verses.devanagari: যদ্যপি বস্তুতঃ প্রভুর কিছু নাহি ভয় ।\\nতথাপি লৌকিকলীলা, লোক-চেষ্টাময় ॥২২৫॥
verses.transliteration: yadyapi vastutaḥ prabhura kichu nāhi bhaya\\ntathāpi laukika-līlā, loka-ceṣṭā-maya
