verses.translation: "We want to submit before You something that may or may not be befitting. The matter is this: unless he sees You, the King of Orissa will become a mendicant."

verses.devanagari: কাণে মুদ্রা লই’ মুঞি হইব ভিখারী ।\\nরাজ্যভোগ নহে চিত্তে বিনা গৌরহরি ॥২০॥
verses.transliteration: kāṇe mudrā la-i' muñi ha-iba bhikhārī\\nrājya-bhoga nahe citte vinā gaurahari
verses.translation: Nityānanda Prabhu continued, "The King has decided to become a mendicant and accept the sign of a mendicant by wearing an ivory earring. He does not want to enjoy his kingdom without seeing the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu."
verses.purport:
PURPORT
In India there is still a class of professional mendicants who are very much like the gypsies of Western countries. They know some magical art and mystical processes, and their business is to beg from door to door, sometimes pleading and sometimes threatening. Such mendicants are sometimes called
yogīs
and sometimes
kāṇaphāṭā yogīs.
The word
kāṇaphāṭā
refers to one who has put a hole in his ear to wear an earring made of ivory. Mahārāja Pratāparudra was so depressed by not getting to see Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu that he decided to become such a
yogī.
Ordinary men think that a
yogī
must have an ivory earring in his ear, but this is not the sign of a real
yogī.
Mahārāja Pratāparudra also thought that to become a mendicant
yogī,
one must wear such an earring.

verses.devanagari: দেখিব সে মুখচন্দ্র নয়ন ভরিয়া ।\\nধরিব সে পাদপদ্ম হৃদয়ে তুলিয়া ॥২১॥
verses.transliteration: dekhiba se mukha-candra nayana bhariyā\\ndhariba se pāda-padma hṛdaye tuliyā
verses.translation: Nityānanda Prabhu continued, "The King also expressed his desire to see the moonlike face of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu to his eye's full satisfaction. He would like to raise the lotus feet of the Lord to his heart."

verses.devanagari: যদ্যপি শুনিয়া প্ৰভুর কোমল হয় মন  ।\\nতথাপি বাহিরে কহে নিষ্ঠুর বচন ॥২২॥
verses.transliteration: yadyapi śuniyā prabhura komala haya mana\\ntathāpi bāhire kahe niṣṭhura vacana
verses.translation: Hearing all these statements, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's mind was certainly softened, but externally He wished to speak some harsh words.

verses.devanagari: তোমা-সবার ইচ্ছা, — এই আমারে লঞা  ।\\nরাজাকে মিলহ ইহঁ কটকেতে গিয়া ॥২৩॥
verses.transliteration: tomā-sabāra icchā,-ei āmāre lañā\\nrājāke milaha ihaṅ kaṭakete giyā
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "I can understand that you all desire to take Me to Kaṭaka to see the King."
verses.purport: PURPORT\nŚrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is naturally the reservoir of all kindness, and as soon as He heard the statement made by the King, His heart immediately softened. Thus the Lord was ready to go see the King even at Kaṭaka. He did not even consider allowing the King to come from Kaṭaka to Jagannātha Purī to see Him. It is significant that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was so kind that He was ready to go see the King at Kaṭaka. Apparently it was never expected that the King wanted to see the Lord at His place, but by way of being externally harsh, the Lord indicated that if all the devotees so desired, He would go to Kaṭaka to see the King.

verses.devanagari: পরমার্থ থাকুক — লোকে করিবে নিন্দন  ।\\nলোকে রহু — দামোদর করিবে ভর্ত্সন ॥২৪॥
verses.transliteration: paramārtha thākuka-loke karibe nindana\\nloke rahu-dāmodara karibe bhartsana
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu continued, "What to speak of spiritual advancement-all the people will blaspheme Me. And what to speak of all the people-Dāmodara would chastise Me.

verses.devanagari: তোমা-সবার আজ্ঞায় আমি না মিলি রাজারে  ।\\nদামোদর কহে যবে, মিলি তবে তাঁরে ॥২৫॥
verses.transliteration: tomā-sabāra ājñāya āmi nā mili rājāre\\ndāmodara kahe yabe, mili tabe tāṅre
verses.translation: "I shall not meet the King at the request of all the devotees, but I shall do so if Dāmodara will give his permission."
verses.purport:
PURPORT
From the spiritual point of view, a
sannyāsī
is strictly forbidden to see materialistic people, especially a king who is always engaged in counting pounds, shillings and pence. Indeed, the meeting between a
sannyāsī
and a king is always considered abominable. A
sannyāsī
is always subjected to public criticism, and a small fault on his part is taken seriously by the public. People actually expect a
sannyāsī
to preach and not take part in any social or political matters. If a
sannyāsī
is subject to public criticism, his preaching will not be fruitful. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu specifically wanted to avoid such criticism so that His preaching work would not be hampered. It so happened that while the Lord was talking to His disciples at that time, the devotee Dāmodara Paṇḍita was present. This Dāmodara Paṇḍita was a very faithful devotee and a staunch lover of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Whenever there was anything that might touch or taint the character of the Lord, Dāmodara Paṇḍita would immediately point it out, not even considering the exalted position of the Lord. It is sometimes said that fools rush in where angels dare not, and Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu wanted to point out Dāmodara Paṇḍita's foolishness in coming forward to criticize the Lord. Thus the Lord indirectly hinted that if Dāmodara Paṇḍita would give Him permission, He would go to see the King. There was deep meaning in this statement, for it is a warning that Dāmodara should not dare criticize the Lord any more, for it was not befitting his position as a devotee. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was considered the guide and spiritual master of all the devotees living with Him. Dāmodara Paṇḍita was one of them, and the Lord rendered Dāmodara Paṇḍita a special favor by warning him to avoid criticizing Him any further. A devotee or a disciple should never attempt to criticize the Lord or His representative, the spiritual master.

verses.devanagari: দামোদর কহে, — তুমি স্বতন্ত্র ঈশ্বর ।\\nকর্তব্যাকর্তব্য সব তোমার গোচর ॥২৬॥
verses.transliteration: dāmodara kahe,-tumi svatantra īśvara\\nkartavyākartavya saba tomāra gocara
verses.translation: Dāmodara immediately replied, "My Lord, You are the fully independent Supreme Personality of Godhead. Since everything is known to You, You know what is permissible and what is not permissible.

verses.devanagari: আমি কোন্ ক্ষুদ্রজীব, তোমাকে বিধি দিব ?\\nআপনি মিলিবে তাঁরে, তাহাও দেখিব ॥২৭॥
verses.transliteration: āmi kon kṣudra-jīva, tomāke vidhi diba?\\nāpani milibe tāṅre, tāhāo dekhiba
verses.translation: "I am merely an insignificant jīva, so what power do I have to give directions to You? By Your own personal choice You will meet with the King. I shall see it.

verses.devanagari: রাজা তোমারে স্নেহ করে, তুমি — স্নেহবশ ।\\nতাঁর স্নেহে করাবে তাঁরে তোমার পরশ ॥২৮॥
verses.transliteration: rājā tomāre sneha kare, tumi-sneha-vaśa\\ntāṅra snehe karābe tāṅre tomāra paraśa
verses.translation: "The King is very much attached to You, and You are feeling affection and love toward him. Thus I can understand that by virtue of the King's affection for You, You will touch him.

verses.devanagari: যদ্যপি ঈশ্বর তুমি পরম স্বতন্ত্র ।\\nতথাপি স্বভাবে হও প্রেম-পরতন্ত্র ॥২৯॥
verses.transliteration: yadyapi īśvara tumi parama svatantra\\ntathāpi svabhāve hao prema-paratantra
verses.translation: "Although You are the Supreme Personality of Godhead and are completely independent, still You are dependent on the love and affection of Your devotees. That is Your nature."

verses.devanagari: নিত্যানন্দ কহে — ঐছে হয় কোন্ জন ।\\nযে তোমারে কহে, ‘কর রাজদরশন’ ॥৩০॥
verses.transliteration: nityānanda kahe-aiche haya kon jana\\nye tomāre kahe, 'kara rāja-daraśana'
verses.translation: Nityānanda Prabhu then said, "Who is there in the three worlds who can ask You to see the King?

verses.devanagari: কিন্তু অনুরাগী লোকের স্বভাব এক হয় ।\\nইষ্ট না পাইলে নিজ প্রাণ সে ছাড়য় ॥৩১॥
verses.transliteration: kintu anurāgī lokera svabhāva eka haya\\niṣṭa nā pāile nija prāṇa se chāḍaya
verses.translation: "Still, isn't it the nature of an attached man to give up his life if he does not attain his desired object?

verses.devanagari: যাজ্ঞিক-ব্রাহ্মণী সব তাহাতে প্রমাণ ।\\nকৃষ্ণ লাগি’ পতি-আগে ছাড়িলেক প্রাণ ॥৩২॥
verses.transliteration: yājñika-brāhmaṇī saba tāhāte pramāṇa\\nkṛṣṇa lāgi' pati-āge chāḍileka prāṇa
verses.translation: "For instance, some of the wives of the\nbrāhmaṇas\nwho were performing sacrifices gave up their lives in the presence of their husbands for the sake of Kṛṣṇa."
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This refers to the day Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa and His cowherd boys and flocks of animals were present on the pasturing grounds near Mathurā. At that time the cowherd boys, being a little hungry, requested food, and Lord Kṛṣṇa asked them to go to the
brāhmaṇas
who were engaged nearby in performing
yajña,
or sacrifice, and to get some food from that
yajña.
Being so ordered by the Lord, all the cowherd boys went to the
brāhmaṇas
and asked them for food, but they were denied. After this, the cowherd boys begged food from the wives of the
brāhmaṇas.
All these wives were very much devoted to Lord Kṛṣṇa in spontaneous love, and as soon as they heard the request of the cowherd boys and understood that Kṛṣṇa wanted some food, they immediately left the place of sacrifice. They were very much chastised for this by their husbands, and they were ready to give up their lives. It is the nature of a pure devotee to sacrifice his life for the transcendental loving service of the Lord.

verses.devanagari: এক যুক্তি আছে, যদি কর অবধান  ।\\nতুমি না মিলিলেহ তাঁরে, রহে তাঁর প্রাণ ॥৩৩॥
verses.transliteration: eka yukti āche, yadi kara avadhāna\\ntumi nā milileha tāṅre, rahe tāṅra prāṇa
verses.translation: Nityānanda Prabhu then submitted one suggestion for the Lord's consideration. "There is a way," He suggested, "by which You need not meet the King but which would enable the King to continue living.

verses.devanagari: এক বহির্বাস যদি দেহ’ কৃপা করি’  ।\\nতাহা পাঞা প্রাণ রাখে তোমার আশা ধরি’ ॥৩৪॥
verses.transliteration: eka bahirvāsa yadi deha' kṛpā kari'\\ntāhā pāñā prāṇa rākhe tomāra āśā dhari'
verses.translation: "If You, out of Your mercy, send one of Your outward garments to the King, the King would live hoping to see You some time in the future."
verses.purport: PURPORT\nŚrī Nityānanda Prabhu was thus very tactfully suggesting that Caitanya Mahāprabhu give a piece of His old clothing to the King. Even though the King was not to meet the Lord, the King would then be pacified by receiving such a cloth. The King was very anxious to see the Lord, yet it was not possible for the Lord to see him. Just to resolve the situation, Nityānanda Prabhu suggested that the Lord send an old piece of clothing. Thus the King would understand that the Lord was showing mercy to him. The King would then not do anything drastic like giving up his life or becoming a mendicant.

verses.devanagari: প্রভু কহে, — তুমি-সব পরম বিদ্বান্ ।\\nযেই ভাল হয়, সেই কর সমাধান ॥৩৫॥
verses.transliteration: prabhu kahe,-tumi-saba parama vidvān\\nyei bhāla haya, sei kara samādhāna
verses.translation: The Lord said, "Since you are all very learned personalities, whatever you decide I shall accept."

verses.devanagari: তবে নিত্যানন্দ-গোসাঞি গোবিন্দের পাশ ।\\nমাগিয়া লইল প্রভুর এক বহির্বাস ॥৩৬॥
verses.transliteration: tabe nityānanda-gosāñi govindera pāśa\\nmāgiyā la-ila prabhura eka bahirvāsa
verses.translation: Lord Nityānanda Prabhu then obtained an external garment used by the Lord by requesting it from Govinda.

verses.devanagari: সেই বহির্বাস সার্বভৌমপাশ দিল ।\\nসার্বভৌম সেই বস্ত্র রাজারে পাঠা’ল ॥৩৭॥
verses.transliteration: sei bahirvāsa sārvabhauma-pāśa dila\\nsārvabhauma sei vastra rājāre pāṭhā'la
verses.translation: Thus Nityānanda Prabhu delivered the old cloth to the care of Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya, and Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya sent it to the King.

verses.devanagari: বস্ত্র পাঞা রাজার হৈল আনন্দিত মন ।\\nপ্রভুরূপ করি’ করে বস্ত্রের পূজন ॥৩৮॥
verses.transliteration: vastra pāñā rājāra haila ānandita mana\\nprabhu-rūpa kari' kare vastrera pūjana
verses.translation: When the King received the old cloth, he began to worship it exactly as he would worship the Lord personally.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is also the conclusion of the Vedic injunctions. Since the Supreme Personality of Godhead is the Absolute Truth, everything in relation to Him is also on the same platform. The King had great affection for Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and although he did not see the Lord, he had nonetheless already attained the conclusion of devotional service. Immediately upon receiving the cloth from Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya, the King began to worship it, accepting it as Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. The Lord's clothing, bedding, slippers and everything required as an ordinary necessity are all transformations of Śeṣa, Viṣṇu, the expansion of Śrī Baladeva. Thus the cloth and other paraphernalia of the Supreme Personality of Godhead are but other forms of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Everything connected to the Lord is worshipable. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu instructs us that just as Kṛṣṇa is worshipable, Kṛṣṇa's place, Vṛndāvana, is also worshipable. And as Vṛndāvana is worshipable, similarly the paraphernalia in Vṛndāvana—the trees, roads, river, everything-is worshipable. A pure devotee thus sings,
jaya jaya vṛndāvana-vāsī yata jana:
"All glories to the residents of Vṛndāvana." If a devotee has a staunch devotional attitude, all these conclusions will be awakened or revealed within the heart.
yasya deve parā bhaktir
yathā deve tathā gurau
tasyaite kathitā hy arthāḥ
prakāśante mahātmanaḥ
"Only unto those great souls who have implicit faith in both the Lord and the spiritual master are all the imports of Vedic knowledge automatically revealed." (
Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad
6.23)
Thus following in the footsteps of Mahārāja Pratāparudra and other devotees, we should learn to worship everything belonging to the Supreme Personality of Godhead. This is referred to by Lord Śiva as
tadīyānām.
In the
Padma Purāṇa
it is said:
ārādhanānāṁ sarveṣāṁ
viṣṇor ārādhanaṁ param
tasmāt parataraṁ devi
tadīyānāṁ samarcanam
"O Devī, the most exalted system of worship is the worship of Lord Viṣṇu. Greater than that is the worship of
tadīya,
or anything belonging to Viṣṇu." Śrī Viṣṇu is
sac-cid-ānanda-vigraha.
Similarly, the most confidential servant of Kṛṣṇa, the spiritual master, and all devotees of Viṣṇu are
tadīya.
The
sac-cid-ānanda-vigraha, guru,
Vaiṣṇavas, and things used by them must be considered
tadīya
and without a doubt worshipable by all living beings.

verses.devanagari: রামানন্দ রায় যবে ‘দক্ষিণ’ হৈতে আইলা ।\\nপ্রভুসঙ্গে রহিতে রাজাকে নিবেদিলা ॥৩৯॥
verses.transliteration: rāmānanda rāya yabe 'dakṣiṇa' haite āilā\\nprabhu-saṅge rahite rājāke nivedilā
verses.translation: After returning from his service in South India, Rāmānanda Rāya requested the King to allow him to remain with Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

verses.devanagari: তবে রাজা সন্তোষে তাঁহারে আজ্ঞা দিলা ।\\nআপনি মিলন লাগি’ সাধিতে লাগিলা ॥৪০॥
verses.transliteration: tabe rājā santoṣe tāṅhāre ājñā dilā\\nāpani milana lāgi' sādhite lāgilā
verses.translation: When Rāmānanda Rāya requested the King to allow him to stay with the Lord, the King immediately gave him permission with great satisfaction. As for the King himself, he began to solicit Rāmānanda Rāya to make a meeting arrangement.

verses.devanagari: মহাপ্রভু মহাকৃপা করেন তোমারে ।\\nমোরে মিলিবারে অবশ্য সাধিবে তাঁহারে ॥৪১॥
verses.transliteration: mahāprabhu mahā-kṛpā karena tomāre\\nmore milibāre avaśya sādhibe tāṅhāre
verses.translation: The King told Rāmānanda Rāya, "Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is very, very merciful to you. Therefore please solicit my meeting with Him without fail."

verses.devanagari: একসঙ্গে দুই জন ক্ষেত্রে যবে আইলা ।\\nরামানন্দ রায় তবে প্ৰভুরে মিলিলা ॥৪২॥
verses.transliteration: eka-saṅge dui jana kṣetre yabe āilā\\nrāmānanda rāya tabe prabhure mililā
verses.translation: The King and Rāmānanda Rāya returned together to Jagannātha-kṣetra [Purī], and Śrī Rāmānanda Rāya met Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

verses.devanagari: প্রভুপদে প্রেমভক্তি জানাইল রাজার ।\\nপ্রসঙ্গ পাঞা ঐছে কহে বারবার ॥৪৩॥
verses.transliteration: prabhu-pade prema-bhakti jānāila rājāra\\nprasaṅga pāñā aiche kahe bāra-bāra
verses.translation: At that time, Rāmānanda Rāya informed Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu about the ecstatic love of the King. Indeed, as soon as there was some opportunity, he repeatedly informed the Lord about the King.

verses.devanagari: রাজমন্ত্রী রামানন্দ — ব্যবহারে নিপুণ ।\\nরাজপ্রীতি কহি’ দ্রবাইল প্ৰভুর মন ॥৪৪॥
verses.transliteration: rāja-mantrī rāmānanda-vyavahāre nipuṇa\\nrāja-prīti kahi' dravāila prabhura mana
verses.translation: Śrī Rāmānanda Rāya was indeed a diplomatic minister for the King. His general behavior was very expert, and simply by describing the King's love for Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, he gradually softened the Lord's mind.
verses.purport: PURPORT\nA diplomat in the material world knows how to deal with people, especially in political affairs. Some of the great devotees of the Lord-like Rāmānanda Rāya, Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī, Sanātana Gosvāmī and Rūpa Gosvāmī-were government officers and had a background of very opulent householder life. Consequently they knew how to deal with people. In many instances we have seen the diplomacy of Rūpa Gosvāmī, Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī and Rāmānanda Rāya employed in the service of the Lord. When Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī's father and uncle were to be arrested by government officials, Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī hid them and personally met the government officers and settled the affair diplomatically. This is but one instance. Similarly, Sanātana Gosvāmī, after resigning his ministership, was thrown in jail, and he bribed the attendant of the jail so he could leave the clutches of the Nawab and live with Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Now we see Rāmānanda Rāya, a most confidential devotee of the Lord, diplomatically soften the heart of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, despite the fact that the Lord definitely decided not to meet the King. The diplomacy of Rāmānanda Rāya and entreaties of Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya and all the other great devotees succeeded. The conclusion is that diplomacy used for the service of the Lord is a form of devotional service.

verses.devanagari: উত্কণ্ঠাতে প্ৰতাপরুদ্র নারে রহিবারে ।\\nরামানন্দ সাধিলেন প্ৰভুরে মিলিবারে ॥৪৫॥
verses.transliteration: utkaṇṭhāte pratāparudra nāre rahibāre\\nrāmānanda sādhilena prabhure milibāre
verses.translation: Mahārāja Pratāparudra, in great anxiety, could not endure not seeing the Lord; therefore Śrī Rāmānanda Rāya, by his diplomacy, arranged a meeting with the Lord for the King.

verses.devanagari: রামানন্দ প্ৰভু-পায় কৈল নিবেদন ।\\nএকবার প্রতাপরুদ্রে দেখাহ চরণ ॥৪৬॥
verses.transliteration: rāmānanda prabhu-pāya kaila nivedana\\neka-bāra pratāparudre dekhāha caraṇa
verses.translation: Śrī Rāmānanda Rāya frankly requested Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, "Please show Your lotus feet to the King at least once."

verses.devanagari: প্রভু কহে, — রামানন্দ, কহ বিচারিয়া ।\\nরাজাকে মিলিতে যুয়ায় সন্ন্যাসী হঞা ? ॥ ৪৭ ॥
verses.transliteration: prabhu kahe,-rāmānanda, kaha vicāriyā\\nrājāke milite yuyāya sannyāsī hañā?
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu replied, "My dear Rāmānanda, you should make this request after duly considering whether it is befitting for a sannyāsī to meet a king.

verses.devanagari: রাজার মিলনে ভিক্ষুকের দুই লোক নাশ ।\\nপরলোক রহু, লোকে করে উপহাস ॥৪৮॥
verses.transliteration: rājāra milane bhikṣukera dui loka nāśa\\nparaloka rahu, loke kare upahāsa
verses.translation: "If a mendicant meets a king, this world and the next world are both destroyed for the mendicant. Indeed, what is there to say of the next world? In this world, people will joke if a sannyāsī meets a king."

verses.devanagari: রামানন্দ কহে, — তুমি ঈশ্বর স্বতন্ত্র ।\\nকারে তোমার ভয়, তুমি নহ পরতন্ত্র ॥৪৯॥
verses.transliteration: rāmānanda kahe,-tumi īśvara svatantra\\nkāre tomāra bhaya, tumi naha paratantra
verses.translation: Rāmānanda Rāya replied, "My Lord, You are the supreme independent personality. You have nothing to fear from anyone because You are not dependent on anyone."

verses.devanagari: প্রভু কহে, — আমি মনুষ্য আশ্রমে সন্ন্যাসী ।\\nকায়মনোবাক্যে ব্যবহারে ভয় বাসি ॥৫০॥
verses.transliteration: prabhu kahe,-āmi manuṣya āśrame sannyāsī\\nkāya-mano-vākye vyavahāre bhaya vāsi
verses.translation: When Rāmānanda Rāya addressed Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu as the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Caitanya Mahāprabhu objected, saying, "I am not the Supreme Personality of Godhead but an ordinary human being. Therefore I must fear public opinion in three ways-with My body, mind and words.

verses.devanagari: শুক্লবস্ত্রে মসি-বিন্দু যৈছে না লুকায় ।\\nসন্ন্যাসীর অল্প ছিদ্র সর্বলোকে গায় ॥৫১॥
verses.transliteration: śukla-vastre masi-bindu yaiche nā lukāya\\nsannyāsīra alpa chidra sarva-loke gāya
verses.translation: "As soon as the general public finds a little fault in the behavior of a sannyāsī, they advertise it like wildfire. A black spot of ink cannot be hidden on a white cloth. It is always very prominent."

verses.devanagari: রায় কহে, — কত পাপীর করিয়াছ অব্যাহতি ।\\nঈশ্বর-সেবক তোমার ভক্ত গজপতি ॥৫২॥
verses.transliteration: rāya kahe,-kata pāpīra kariyācha avyāhati\\nīśvara-sevaka tomāra bhakta gajapati
verses.translation: Rāmānanda Rāya replied, "My dear Lord, You have delivered so many sinful people. This King Pratāparudra, the King of Orissa, is actually a servitor of the Lord and Your devotee."

verses.devanagari: প্রভু কহে, — পূর্ণ যৈছে দুগ্ধের কলস  ।\\nসুরাবিন্দু-পাতে কেহ না করে পরশ ॥৫৩॥
verses.transliteration: prabhu kahe,-pūrṇa yaiche dugdhera kalasa\\nsurā-bindu-pāte keha nā kare paraśa
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then said, "There may be much milk in a big pot, but if it is contaminated by a drop of liquor, it is untouchable.

verses.devanagari: যদ্যপি প্রতাপরুদ্র — সর্বগুণবান্  ।\\nতাঁহারে মলিন কৈল এক ‘রাজা’-নাম ॥৫৪॥
verses.transliteration: yadyapi pratāparudra-sarva-guṇavān\\ntāṅhāre malina kaila eka 'rājā'-nāma
verses.translation: "The King certainly possesses all good qualities, but simply by taking up the name 'king,' he has infected everything.

verses.devanagari: তথাপি তোমার যদি মহাগ্রহ হয় ।\\nতবে আনি’ মিলাহ তুমি তাঁহার তনয় ॥৫৫॥
verses.transliteration: tathāpi tomāra yadi mahāgraha haya\\ntabe āni' milāha tumi tāṅhāra tanaya
verses.translation: "But if you are still very eager for the King to meet with Me, please first bring his son to meet Me.

verses.devanagari: “আত্মা বৈ জায়তে পুত্রঃ” — এই শাস্ত্রবাণী ।\\nপুত্রের মিলনে যেন মিলিবে আপনি ॥৫৬॥
verses.transliteration: ''ātmā vai jāyate putraḥ''-ei śāstra-vāṇī\\nputrera milane yena milibe āpani
verses.translation: "It is indicated in the revealed scriptures that the son represents the father; therefore the son's meeting with Me would be just as good as the King's meeting with Me."
verses.purport:
PURPORT
In
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(10.78.36) it is said:
ātmā vai putra utpanna iti vedānuśāsanam.
The
Vedas
enjoin that one is born as his own son. The son is nondifferent from the father, and this is admitted in every revealed scripture. In Christian theology it is believed that Christ, the son of God, is also God. Both of them are identical.

verses.devanagari: তবে রায় যাই’ সব রাজারে কহিলা ।\\nপ্রভুর আজ্ঞায় তাঁর পুত্র লঞা আইলা ॥৫৭॥
verses.transliteration: tabe rāya yāi' saba rājāre kahilā\\nprabhura ājñāya tāṅra putra lañā āilā
verses.translation: Rāmānanda Rāya then went to inform the King about his talks with Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and, following the Lord's orders, brought the King's son to see Him.

verses.devanagari: সুন্দর, রাজার পুত্র — শ্যামল-বরণ ।\\nকিশোর বয়স, দীর্ঘ কমলনয়ন ॥৫৮॥
verses.transliteration: sundara, rājāra putra-śyāmala-varaṇa\\nkiśora vayasa, dīrgha kamala-nayana
verses.translation: The prince, just entering upon his youth, was very beautiful. He was blackish in complexion and had large lotus eyes.

verses.devanagari: পীতাম্বর, ধরে অঙ্গে রত্ন-আভরণ  ।\\nশ্রীকৃষ্ণ-স্মরণে তেঁহ হৈলা ‘উদ্দীপন’ ॥৫৯॥
verses.transliteration: pītāmbara, dhare aṅge ratna-ābharaṇa\\nśrī-kṛṣṇa-smaraṇe teṅha hailā 'uddīpana'
verses.translation: The prince was dressed in yellow cloth, and there were jeweled ornaments decorating his body. Therefore anyone who saw him would remember Lord Kṛṣṇa.

verses.devanagari: তাঁরে দেখি, মহাপ্রভুর কৃষ্ণস্মৃতি হৈল  ।\\nপ্রেমাবেশে তাঁরে মিলি’ কহিতে লাগিল ॥৬০॥
verses.transliteration: tāṅre dekhi, mahāprabhura kṛṣṇa-smṛti haila\\npremāveśe tāṅre mili' kahite lāgila
verses.translation: Seeing the boy, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu immediately remembered Kṛṣṇa. Meeting the boy in ecstatic love, the Lord began to speak.

verses.devanagari: এই — মহাভাগবত, যাঁহার দর্শনে  ।\\nব্রজেন্দ্রনন্দন-স্মৃতি হয় সর্বজনে ॥৬১॥
verses.transliteration: ei-mahā-bhāgavata, yāṅhāra darśane\\nvrajendra-nandana-smṛti haya sarva-jane
verses.translation: "Here is a great devotee," Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said. "Upon seeing him, everyone can remember the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa, son of Mahārāja Nanda."
verses.purport:
PURPORT
On his
Anubhāṣya,
Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura states that a materialist mistakenly accepts the body and mind as the source of material enjoyment. In other words, a materialist accepts the bodily conception of life. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu did not regard the son of Mahārāja Pratāparudra with the idea that he was a materialist, being the son of a materialist. Nor did He consider Himself the enjoyer. Māyāvādī philosophers make a great mistake by assuming that the
sac-cid-ānanda-vigraha,
the transcendental form of the Lord, is like a material body. However, there is no material contamination in transcendence, nor is there any possibility of imagining a spirituality in matter. One cannot accept matter as spirit. As indicated by the technical words
bhauma ijya-dhīḥ
(
Bhāg.
10.84.13), materialistic Māyāvādīs imagine the form of God in matter, although according to their imagination, God is unlimitedly formless. This is simply mental speculation. Even though Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is the Supreme Personality of Godhead, He placed Himself in the position of a
gopī.
He also accepted the King's son directly as the son of Mahārāja Nanda, Vrajendra-nandana Hari. This is perfect vision according to the direction of the Vedic culture, as confirmed in
Śrīmad Bhagavad-gītā
(
paṇḍitāḥ sama-darśinaḥ
). Such acceptance of the Absolute Truth according to Vaiṣṇava philosophy is explained in both the
Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad
(3.2.3) and the
Kaṭha Upaniṣad
(1.2.23) in the following words:
nāyam ātmā pravacanena labhyo
na medhayā na bahunā śrutena
yam evaiṣa vṛṇute tena labhyas
tasyaiṣa ātmā vivṛṇute tanūṁ svām
"The Supreme Lord is not obtained by expert explanations, by vast intelligence, nor even by much hearing. He is obtained only by one whom He Himself chooses. To such a person He manifests His own form."
The living entity is entangled in material existence due to his lack of such spiritual vision. Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura has sung in his
Kalyāṇa-kalpataru: saṁsāre āsiyā prakṛti bhajiyā 'puruṣa' abhimāne mari.
When the living entity comes to the material world, he thinks himself the enjoyer. Thus he becomes more and more entangled.

verses.devanagari: কৃতার্থ হইলাঙ আমি ইঁহার দরশনে ।\\nএত বলি’ পুনঃ তারে কৈল আলিঙ্গনে ॥৬২॥
verses.transliteration: kṛtārtha ha-ilāṅa āmi iṅhāra daraśane\\neta bali' punaḥ tāre kaila āliṅgane
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu continued, "I have become very much obligated just by seeing this boy." After saying this, the Lord again embraced the prince.

verses.devanagari: প্রভুস্পর্শে রাজপুত্রের হৈল প্রেমাবেশ ।\\nস্বেদ, কম্প, অশ্রু, স্তম্ভ, পুলক বিশেষ ॥৬৩॥
verses.transliteration: prabhu-sparśe rāja-putrera haila premāveśa\\nsveda, kampa, aśru, stambha, pulaka viśeṣa
verses.translation: As soon as the prince was touched by Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, symptoms of ecstatic love immediately manifested themselves in his body. These symptoms included perspiration, trembling, tears, being stunned and jubilation.

verses.devanagari: ‘কৃষ্ণ’ ‘কৃষ্ণ’ কহে, নাচে, করয়ে রোদন ।\\nতাঁর ভাগ্য দেখি’ শ্লাঘা করে ভক্তগণ ॥৬৪॥
verses.transliteration: 'kṛṣṇa' 'kṛṣṇa' kahe, nāce, karaye rodana\\ntāṅra bhāgya dekhi' ślāghā kare bhakta-gaṇa
verses.translation: The boy began to cry and dance, and he chanted, "Kṛṣṇa! Kṛṣṇa!" Upon seeing his bodily symptoms and his chanting and dancing, all the devotees praised him for his great spiritual fortune.

verses.devanagari: তবে মহাপ্রভু তাঁরে ধৈর্য করাইল ।\\nনিত্য আসি’ আমায় মিলিহ — এই আজ্ঞা দিল ॥৬৫॥
verses.transliteration: tabe mahāprabhu tāṅre dhairya karāila\\nnitya āsi' āmāya miliha-ei ājñā dila
verses.translation: At that time, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu calmed the youth and ordered him to come there daily to meet Him.

verses.devanagari: বিদায় হঞা রায় আইল রাজপুত্রে লঞা ।\\nরাজা সুখ পাইল পুত্রের চেষ্টা দেখিয়া ॥৬৬॥
verses.transliteration: vidāya hañā rāya āila rāja-putre lañā\\nrājā sukha pāila putrera ceṣṭā dekhiyā
verses.translation: They then departed from Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and Rāmānanda Rāya took the boy back to the King's palace. The King was very happy when he heard of his son's activities.

verses.devanagari: পুত্রে আলিঙ্গন করি’ প্রেমাবিষ্ট হৈলা ।\\nসাক্ষাৎ পরশ যেন মহাপ্রভুর পাইলা ॥৬৭॥
verses.transliteration: putre āliṅgana kari' premāviṣṭa hailā\\nsākṣāt paraśa yena mahāprabhura pāilā
verses.translation: Just by embracing his son, the King was filled with ecstatic love, just as if he had touched Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu directly.

verses.devanagari: সেই হৈতে ভাগ্যবান্ রাজার নন্দন ।\\nপ্রভুভক্তগণ-মধ্যে হৈলা একজন ॥৬৮॥
verses.transliteration: sei haite bhāgyavān rājāra nandana\\nprabhu-bhakta-gaṇa-madhye hailā eka-jana
verses.translation: Since then, the fortunate prince was one of the most intimate devotees of the Lord.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
In this regard, Śrīla Prabodhānanda Sarasvatī writes:
yat-kāruṇya-kaṭākṣa-vaibhava-vatām.
If Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu simply glanced at someone for a moment, that person immediately turned into one of the most confidential devotees of the Lord. The prince came to see the Lord for the first time, but by the Lord's mercy the boy immediately became a topmost devotee. This was not in theory but in practice. We cannot apply the
nagna-mātṛkā-nyāya
formula. This states that if one's mother was naked in her childhood, she should continue to remain naked, even though she has become a mother of so many children. If a person is actually blessed by the mercy of the Lord, he can immediately become a topmost devotee of the Lord. The logic of
nagna-mātṛkā
states that if a person is not elevated on such and such a date, he cannot become an exalted devotee overnight, as it were. This particular instance offers evidence to contradict that theory. On the previous day, the boy was simply an ordinary prince, and the next day he was counted as one of the topmost devotees of the Lord. This was all made possible by the causeless mercy of the Lord. The Lord is omnipotent, all-powerful and almighty, and He can act as He likes.

verses.devanagari: এইমত মহাপ্রভু ভক্তগণ-সঙ্গে ।\\nনিরন্তর ক্রীড়া করে সংকীর্তন-রঙ্গে ॥৬৯॥
verses.transliteration: ei-mata mahāprabhu bhakta-gaṇa-saṅge\\nnirantara krīḍā kare saṅkīrtana-raṅge
verses.translation: Thus Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu acts in the society of His pure devotees, performing His pastimes and spreading the saṅkīrtana movement.

verses.devanagari: আচার্যাদি ভক্ত করে প্রভুরে নিমন্ত্রণ ।\\nতাহাঁ তাহাঁ ভিক্ষা করে লঞা ভক্তগণ ॥৭০॥
verses.transliteration: ācāryādi bhakta kare prabhure nimantraṇa\\ntāhāṅ tāhāṅ bhikṣā kare lañā bhakta-gaṇa
verses.translation: Some of the prominent devotees like Advaita Ācārya used to invite Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu to take His meals at their homes. The Lord accepted such invitations accompanied by His devotees.

verses.devanagari: এইমত নানা রঙ্গে দিন কত গেল ।\\nজগন্নাথের রথযাত্রা নিকট হইল ॥৭১॥
verses.transliteration: ei-mata nānā raṅge dina kata gela\\njagannāthera ratha-yātrā nikaṭa ha-ila
verses.translation: In this way, the Lord passed some days in great jubilation. Then the car festival of Lord Jagannātha approached.

verses.devanagari: প্রথমেই কাশীমিশ্রে প্রভু বোলাইল ।\\nপড়িছা-পাত্র, সার্বভৌমে বোলাঞা আনিল ॥৭২॥
verses.transliteration: prathamei kāśī-miśre prabhu bolāila\\npaḍichā-pātra, sārvabhaume bolāñā ānila
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu first of all called for Kāśī Miśra, then for the superintendent of the temple, then for Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya.

verses.devanagari: তিনজন-পাশে প্রভু হাসিয়া কহিল ।\\nগুণ্ডিচা-মন্দির-মার্জন-সেবা মাগি’ নিল ॥৭৩॥
verses.transliteration: tina-jana-pāśe prabhu hāsiyā kahila\\nguṇḍicā-mandira-mārjana-sevā māgi' nila
verses.translation: When these three people came before the Lord, He begged them for permission to wash the temple known as Guṇḍicā.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
The Guṇḍicā temple is situated two miles northeast of the Jagannātha temple. At the time of the Ratha-yātrā festival, Lord Jagannātha goes to the Guṇḍicā temple from His original temple and stays there for one week. After one week, He returns to His original temple. It is understood by hearsay that the wife of Indradyumna, the King who established the Jagannātha temple, was known as Guṇḍicā. There is also mention of the name of the Guṇḍicā temple in authoritative scripture. The area of the Guṇḍicā temple is estimated to be 288 cubits by 215 cubits. The main temple inside is about 36 cubits by 30 cubits, and the
kīrtana
hall is 32 cubits by 30 cubits.

verses.devanagari: পড়িছা কহে, — আমি-সব সেবক তোমার ।\\nযে তোমার ইচ্ছা সেই কর্তব্য আমার ॥৭৪॥
verses.transliteration: paḍichā kahe,-āmi-saba sevaka tomāra\\nye tomāra icchā sei kartavya āmāra
verses.translation: Upon hearing the Lord's request for them to wash the Guṇḍicā temple, the paḍichā, the superintendent of the temple, said, "My dear sir, we are all Your servants. Whatever You desire is our duty to perform.

verses.devanagari: বিশেষে রাজার আজ্ঞা হঞাছে আমারে ।\\nপ্রভুর আজ্ঞা যেই, সেই শীঘ্র করিবারে ॥৭৫॥
verses.transliteration: viśeṣe rājāra ājñā hañāche āmāre\\nprabhura ājñā yei, sei śīghra karibāre
verses.translation: "The King gave a special order for me to do without delay whatever Your Lordship orders.

verses.devanagari: তোমার যোগ্য সেবা নহে মন্দির-মার্জন ।\\nএই এক লীলা কর, যে তোমার মন ॥৭৬॥
verses.transliteration: tomāra yogya sevā nahe mandira-mārjana\\nei eka līlā kara, ye tomāra mana
verses.translation: "My dear Lord, washing the temple is not service befitting You. Nonetheless, if You wish to do so, it is to be accepted as one of Your pastimes.

verses.devanagari: কিন্তু ঘট, সংমার্জনী বহুত চাহিয়ে ।\\nআজ্ঞা দেহ — আজি সব ইহাঁ আনি দিয়ে ॥৭৭॥
verses.transliteration: kintu ghaṭa, sammārjanī bahuta cāhiye\\nājñā deha-āji saba ihāṅ āni diye
verses.translation: "To wash the temple, You need many waterpots and brooms. Therefore order me. I can immediately bring all these things to You."

verses.devanagari: নূতন একশত ঘট, শত সংমার্জনী ।\\nপড়িছা আনিয়া দিল প্রভুর ইচ্ছা জানি’ ॥৭৮॥
verses.transliteration: nūtana eka-śata ghaṭa, śata sammārjanī\\npaḍichā āniyā dila prabhura icchā jāni'
verses.translation: As soon as the superintendent understood the desire of the Lord, he immediately delivered a hundred new waterpots and a hundred brooms for sweeping the temple.

verses.devanagari: আর দিনে প্রভাতে লঞা নিজগণ  ।\\nশ্রীহস্তে সবার অঙ্গে লেপিয়া চন্দন ॥৭৯॥
verses.transliteration: āra dine prabhāte lañā nija-gaṇa\\nśrī-haste sabāra aṅge lepilā candana
verses.translation: The next day, early in the morning, the Lord took His personal associates with Him and, with His own hand, smeared sandalwood pulp on their bodies.

verses.devanagari: শ্রীহস্তে দিল সবারে এক এক মার্জনী  ।\\nসবগণ লঞা প্রভু চলিলা আপনি ॥৮০॥
verses.transliteration: śrī-haste dila sabāre eka eka mārjanī\\nsaba-gaṇa lañā prabhu calilā āpani
verses.translation: He then gave each devotee a broom with His own hand, and taking all of them personally with Him, the Lord went to Guṇḍicā.

verses.devanagari: গুণ্ডিচা মন্দিরে গেলা করিতে মার্জন ।\\nপ্রথমে মার্জনী লঞা করিল শোধন ॥৮১॥
verses.transliteration: guṇḍicā-mandire gelā karite mārjana\\nprathame mārjanī lañā karila śodhana
verses.translation: In this way the Lord and His associates went to cleanse the Guṇḍicā temple. At first they cleansed the temple with the brooms.

verses.devanagari: ভিতর মন্দির উপর, — সকল মাজিল ।\\nসিংহাসন মাজি’ পুনঃ স্থাপন করিল ॥৮২॥
verses.transliteration: bhitara mandira upara,-sakala mājila\\nsiṁhāsana māji' punaḥ sthāpana karila
verses.translation: The Lord cleansed everything inside the temple very nicely, including the ceiling. He then took up the sitting place [siṁhāsana], cleansed it and again put it in its original place.

verses.devanagari: ছোট-বড়-মন্দির কৈল মার্জন-শোধন ।\\nপাছে তৈছে শোধিল শ্রীজগমোহন ॥৮৩॥
verses.transliteration: choṭa-baḍa-mandira kaila mārjana-śodhana\\npāche taiche śodhila śrī-jagamohana
verses.translation: Thus the Lord and His companions cleansed and swept all the temple's buildings, big and small, and finally cleansed the area between the temple and the meeting place.

verses.devanagari: চারিদিকে শত ভক্ত সংমার্জনী করে ।\\nআপনি শোধেন প্রভু, শিখা’ন সবারে ॥৮৪॥
verses.transliteration: cāri-dike śata bhakta sammārjanī-kare\\nāpani śodhena prabhu, śikhā'na sabāre
verses.translation: Indeed, hundreds of devotees were engaged in cleansing all around the temple, and Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was personally carrying out the operation just to instruct others.

verses.devanagari: প্রেমোল্লাসে শোধেন, লয়েন কৃষ্ণনাম ।\\nভক্তগণ ‘কৃষ্ণ’ কহে, করে নিজ-কাম ॥৮৫॥
verses.transliteration: premollāse śodhena, layena kṛṣṇa-nāma\\nbhakta-gaṇa 'kṛṣṇa' kahe, kare nija-kāma
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu washed and cleansed the temple in great jubilation, chanting the holy name of Lord Kṛṣṇa all the time. Similarly, all the devotees were also chanting and at the same time performing their respective duties.

verses.devanagari: ধূলি-ধূসর তনু দেখিতে শোভন ।\\nকাহাঁ কাহাঁ অশ্রুজলে করে সংমার্জন ॥৮৬॥
verses.transliteration: dhūli-dhūsara tanu dekhite śobhana\\nkāhāṅ kāhāṅ aśru-jale kare sammārjana
verses.translation: The entire beautiful body of the Lord was covered with dust and dirt. In this way it became transcendentally beautiful. At times, when cleansing the temple, the Lord shed tears, and in some places He even cleansed with those tears.

verses.devanagari: ভোগমন্দির শোধন করি’ শোধিল প্রাঙ্গন ।\\nসকল আবাস ক্রমে করিল শোধন ॥৮৭॥
verses.transliteration: bhoga-mandira śodhana kari' śodhila prāṅgaṇa\\nsakala āvāsa krame karila śodhana
verses.translation: After this, the place where the Deity's food was kept [bhoga-mandira] was cleansed. Then the yard was cleansed, and then all the residential quarters, one after the other.

verses.devanagari: তৃণ, ধূলি, ঝিঁকুর, সব একত্র করিয়া ।\\nবহির্বাসে লঞা ফেলায় বাহির করিয়া ॥৮৮॥
verses.transliteration: tṛṇa, dhūli, jhiṅkura, saba ekatra kariyā\\nbahirvāse lañā phelāya bāhira kariyā
verses.translation: After Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu collected all the straw, dust and grains of sand in one place, He gathered it all in His cloth and threw it outside.

verses.devanagari: এইমত ভক্তগণ করি’ নিজ বাসে ।\\nতৃণ, ধূলি বাহিরে ফেলায় পরম হরিষে ॥৮৯॥
verses.transliteration: ei-mata bhakta-gaṇa kari' nija-vāse\\ntṛṇa, dhūli bāhire phelāya parama hariṣe
verses.translation: Following the example of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, all the devotees, in great jubilation, began to gather straws and dust with their own cloths and throw them outside the temple.

verses.devanagari: প্রভু কহে, — কে কত করিয়াছ সংমার্জন ।\\nতৃণ, ধূলি দেখিলেই জানিব পরিশ্রম ॥৯০॥
verses.transliteration: prabhu kahe,-ke kata kariyācha sammārjana\\ntṛṇa, dhūli dekhilei jāniba pariśrama
verses.translation: The Lord then told the devotees, "I can tell how much you have labored and how well you have cleansed the temple simply by seeing all the straw and dust you have collected outside."

verses.devanagari: সবার ঝ্যাঁটান বোঝা একত্র করিল ।\\nসবা হৈতে প্রভুর বোঝা অধিক হইল ॥৯১॥
verses.transliteration: sabāra jhyāṅṭāna bojhā ekatra karila\\nsabā haite prabhura bojhā adhika ha-ila
verses.translation: Even though all the devotees collected dirt in one pile, the dirt collected by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was much greater.

verses.devanagari: এইমত অভ্যন্তর করিল মার্জন ।\\nপুনঃ সবাকারে দিল করিয়া বণ্টন ॥৯২॥
verses.transliteration: ei-mata abhyantara karila mārjana\\npunaḥ sabākāre dila kariyā vaṇṭana
verses.translation: After the inside of the temple was cleansed, the Lord again allotted areas for the devotees to cleanse.

verses.devanagari: সূক্ষ্ম ধূলি, তৃণ, কাঁকর, সব করহ দূর ।\\nভালমতে শোধন করহ প্রভুর অন্তঃপুর ॥৯৩॥
verses.transliteration: sūkṣma dhūli, tṛṇa, kāṅkara, saba karaha dūra\\nbhāla-mate śodhana karaha prabhura antaḥpura
verses.translation: The Lord then ordered everyone to cleanse the inside of the temple very perfectly by taking finer dust, straws and grains of sand and throwing them outside.

verses.devanagari: সব বৈষ্ণব লঞা যবে দুইবার শোধিল ।\\nদেখি’ মহাপ্রভুর মনে সন্তোষ হইল ॥৯৪॥
verses.transliteration: saba vaiṣṇava lañā yabe dui-bāra śodhila\\ndekhi' mahāprabhura mane santoṣa ha-ila
verses.translation: After Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and all the Vaiṣṇavas cleansed the temple for the second time, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was very happy to see the cleansing work.

verses.devanagari: আর শত জন শত ঘটে জল ভরি’ ।\\nপ্রথমেই লঞা আছে কাল অপেক্ষা করি’ ॥৯৫॥
verses.transliteration: āra śata jana śata ghaṭe jala bhari'\\nprathamei lañā āche kāla apekṣā kari'
verses.translation: While the temple was being swept, about a hundred men stood ready with filled waterpots, and they simply awaited the Lord's order to throw the water from them.

verses.devanagari: ‘জল আন’ বলি’ যবে মহাপ্রভু কহিল ।\\nতবে শত ঘট আনি’ প্রভু-আগে দিল ॥৯৬॥
verses.transliteration: 'jala āna' bali' yabe mahāprabhu kahila\\ntabe śata ghaṭa āni' prabhu-āge dila
verses.translation: As soon as Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu called for water, all the men immediately brought the hundred waterpots, which were completely filled, and delivered them before the Lord.

verses.devanagari: প্রথমে করিল প্রভু মন্দির প্রক্ষালন ।\\nঊর্ধ্ব-অধো ভিত্তি, গৃহ-মধ্য, সিংহাসন ॥৯৭॥
verses.transliteration: prathame karila prabhu mandira prakṣālana\\nūrdhva-adho bhitti, gṛha-madhya, siṁhāsana
verses.translation: In this way, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu first washed the main temple and then thoroughly washed the ceiling, the walls, the floor, the sitting place [siṁhāsana] and everything else within the room.

verses.devanagari: খাপরা ভরিয়া জল ঊর্ধ্বে চালাইল ।\\nসেই জলে ঊর্ধ্ব শোধি ভিত্তি প্রক্ষালিল ॥৯৮॥
verses.transliteration: khāparā bhariyā jala ūrdhve cālāila\\nsei jale ūrdhva śodhi bhitti prakṣālila
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu Himself and His devotees began to throw water onto the ceiling. When this water fell, it washed the walls and floor.

verses.devanagari: শ্রীহস্তে করেন সিংহাসনের মার্জন ।\\nপ্রভু আগে জল আনি’ দেয় ভক্তগণ ॥৯৯॥
verses.transliteration: śrī-haste karena siṁhāsanera mārjana\\nprabhu āge jala āni' deya bhakta-gaṇa
verses.translation: Then Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu began to wash the sitting place of Lord Jagannātha with His own hands, and all the devotees began to bring water to the Lord.

verses.devanagari: ভক্তগণ করে গৃহ-মধ্য প্রক্ষালন ।\\nনিজ নিজ হস্তে করে মন্দির মার্জন ॥১০০॥
verses.transliteration: bhakta-gaṇa kare gṛha-madhya prakṣālana\\nnija nija haste kare mandira mārjana
verses.translation: All the devotees within the temple began to wash. Each one had a broom in his hand, and in this way they cleansed the temple of the Lord.

verses.devanagari: কেহ জল আনি’ দেয় মহাপ্রভুর করে ।\\nকেহ জল দেয় তাঁর চরণ-উপরে ॥১০১॥
verses.transliteration: keha jala āni' deya mahāprabhura kare\\nkeha jala deya tāṅra caraṇa-upare
verses.translation: Someone brought water to pour into the hands of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and someone poured water on His lotus feet.

verses.devanagari: কেহ লুকাঞা করে সেই জল পান ।\\nকেহ মাগি’ লয়, কেহ অন্যে করে দান ॥১০২॥
verses.transliteration: keha lukāñā kare sei jala pāna\\nkeha māgi' laya, keha anye kare dāna
verses.translation: The water that fell from the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was drunk by someone who hid himself. Someone else begged for that water, and another person was giving that water in charity.

verses.devanagari: ঘর ধুই’ প্রণালিকায় জল ছাড়ি’ দিল ।\\nসেই জলে প্রাঙ্গণ সব ভরিয়া রহিল ॥১০৩॥
verses.transliteration: ghara dhui' praṇālikāya jala chāḍi' dila\\nsei jale prāṅgaṇa saba bhariyā rahila
verses.translation: After the room was washed, the water was let out through an outlet, and it then flowed and filled the yard outside.

verses.devanagari: নিজ-বস্ত্রে কৈল প্রভু গৃহ সংমার্জন ।\\nমহাপ্রভু নিজ-বস্ত্রে মাজিল সিংহাসন ॥১০৪॥
verses.transliteration: nija-vastre kaila prabhu gṛha sammārjana\\nmahāprabhu nija-vastre mājila siṁhāsana
verses.translation: The Lord mopped the rooms with His own clothes, and He polished the throne with them also.

verses.devanagari: শত ঘট জলে হৈল মন্দির মার্জন  ।\\nমন্দির শোধিয়া কৈল — যেন নিজ মন ॥১০৫॥
verses.transliteration: śata ghaṭa jale haila mandira mārjana\\nmandira śodhiyā kaila-yena nija mana
verses.translation: In this way all the rooms were cleansed with a hundred waterpots. After the rooms had been cleansed, the minds of the devotees were as clean as the rooms.

verses.devanagari: নির্মল, শীতল, স্নিগ্ধ করিল মন্দিরে  ।\\nআপন-হৃদয় যেন ধরিল বাহিরে ॥১০৬॥
verses.transliteration: nirmala, śītala, snigdha karila mandire\\nāpana-hṛdaya yena dharila bāhire
verses.translation: When the temple was cleansed, it was purified, cool and pleasing, just as if the Lord's own pure mind had appeared.

verses.devanagari: শত শত জন জল ভরে সরোবরে ।\\nঘাটে স্থান নাহি, কেহ কূপে জল ভরে ॥১০৭॥
verses.transliteration: śata śata jana jala bhare sarovare\\nghāṭe sthāna nāhi, keha kūpe jala bhare
verses.translation: Since hundreds of men were engaged in bringing water from the lake, there was no place to stand on the banks. Consequently someone began to draw water from a well.

verses.devanagari: পূর্ণ কুম্ভ লঞা আইসে শত ভক্তগণ ।\\nশূন্য ঘট লঞা যায় আর শত জন ॥১০৮॥
verses.transliteration: pūrṇa kumbha lañā āise śata bhakta-gaṇa\\nśūnya ghaṭa lañā yāya āra śata jana
verses.translation: Hundreds of devotees brought water in the pots, and hundreds took the empty pots away to fill them up again.

verses.devanagari: নিত্যানন্দ, অদ্বৈত, স্বরূপ, ভারতী, পুরী ।\\nইঁহা বিনু আর সব আনে জল ভরি’ ॥১০৯॥
verses.transliteration: nityānanda, advaita, svarūpa, bhāratī, purī\\niṅhā vinu āra saba āne jala bhari'
verses.translation: With the exception of Nityānanda Prabhu, Advaita Ācārya, Svarūpa Dāmodara, Brahmānanda Bhāratī and Paramānanda Purī, everyone was engaged in filling the waterpots and bringing them there.

verses.devanagari: ঘটে ঘটে ঠেকি’ কত ঘট ভাঙ্গি’ গেল ।\\nশত শত ঘট লোক তাহাঁ লঞা আইল ॥১১০॥
verses.transliteration: ghaṭe ghaṭe ṭheki' kata ghaṭa bhāṅgi' gela\\nśata śata ghaṭa loka tāhāṅ lañā āila
verses.translation: Many of the waterpots were broken when people collided with one another, and hundreds of men had to bring new waterpots to fill.

verses.devanagari: জল ভরে, ঘর ধোয়, করে হরিধ্বনি ।\\n‘কৃষ্ণ’ ‘হরি’ ধ্বনি বিনা আর নাহি শুনি ॥১১১॥
verses.transliteration: jala bhare, ghara dhoya, kare hari-dhvani\\n'kṛṣṇa' 'hari' dhvani vinā āra nāhi śuni
verses.translation: Some people were filling the pots, and others were washing the rooms, but everyone was engaged in chanting the holy name of Kṛṣṇa and Hari.

verses.devanagari: ‘কৃষ্ণ’ ‘কৃষ্ণ’ কহি’ করে ঘটের প্রার্থন ।\\n‘কৃষ্ণ’ ‘কৃষ্ণ’ কহি’ করে ঘট সমর্পণ ॥১১২॥
verses.transliteration: 'kṛṣṇa' 'kṛṣṇa' kahi' kare ghaṭera prārthana\\n'kṛṣṇa' 'kṛṣṇa' kahi' kare ghaṭa samarpaṇa
verses.translation: One person begged for a waterpot by chanting the holy names "Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa," and another delivered a pot while chanting "Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa."

verses.devanagari: যেই যেই কহে, সেই কহে কৃষ্ণনামে ।\\nকৃষ্ণনাম হইল সঙ্কেত সব-কামে ॥১১৩॥
verses.transliteration: yei yei kahe, sei kahe kṛṣṇa-nāme\\nkṛṣṇa-nāma ha-ila saṅketa saba-kāme
verses.translation: Whenever anyone had to speak, he did so by uttering the holy name of Kṛṣṇa. Consequently, the holy name of Kṛṣṇa became an indication for everyone who wanted something.

verses.devanagari: প্রেমাবেশে প্রভু কহে ‘কৃষ্ণ’ ‘কৃষ্ণ’-নাম ।\\nএকলে প্রেমাবেশে করে শতজনের কাম ॥১১৪॥
verses.transliteration: premāveśe prabhu kahe 'kṛṣṇa' 'kṛṣṇa'-nāma\\nekale premāveśe kare śata-janera kāma
verses.translation: As Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was vibrating the holy name of Kṛṣṇa in ecstatic love, He Himself was performing the work of hundreds of men.

verses.devanagari: শত-হস্তে করেন যেন ক্ষালন-মার্জন ।\\nপ্রতিজন-পাশে যাই’ করান শিক্ষণ ॥১১৫॥
verses.transliteration: śata-haste karena yena kṣālana-mārjana\\npratijana-pāśe yāi' karāna śikṣana
verses.translation: It appeared as though Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu were cleansing and washing with a hundred hands. He approached everyone just to teach him how to work.

verses.devanagari: ভাল কর্ম দেখি’ তারে করে প্রসংশন ।\\nমনে না মিলিলে করে পবিত্র ভর্ত্সন ॥১১৬॥
verses.transliteration: bhāla karma dekhi' tāre kare prasaṁśana\\nmane nā milile kare pavitra bhartsana
verses.translation: When He saw someone doing nicely, the Lord praised him, but if He saw that someone was not working to His satisfaction, He immediately chastised that person, not bearing him any grudge.

verses.devanagari: তুমি ভাল করিয়াছ, শিখাহ অন্যেরে ।\\nএইমত ভাল কর্ম সেহো যেন করে ॥১১৭॥
verses.transliteration: tumi bhāla kariyācha, śikhāha anyere\\nei-mata bhāla karma seho yena kare
verses.translation: The Lord would say, "You have done well. Please teach this to others so that they may act in the same way."

verses.devanagari: এ-কথা শুনিয়া সবে সঙ্কুচিত হঞা ।\\nভাল-মতে-কর্ম করে সবে মন দিয়া ॥১১৮॥
verses.transliteration: e-kathā śuniyā sabe saṅkucita hañā\\nbhāla-mate karma kare sabe mana diyā
verses.translation: As soon as they heard Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu say this, everyone became ashamed. Thus they began to work with great attention.

verses.devanagari: তবে প্রক্ষালন কৈল শ্রীজগমোহন ।\\nভোগমন্দির-আদি তবে কৈল প্রক্ষালন ॥১১৯॥
verses.transliteration: tabe prakṣālana kaila śrī-jagamohana\\nbhoga-mandira-ādi tabe kaila prakṣālana
verses.translation: They washed the Jagamohana area and then the place where food was kept. All other places were also washed.

verses.devanagari: নাটশালা-ধুই’ ধুইল চত্বর-প্রাঙ্গণ ।\\nপাকশালা-আদি করি’ করিল প্রক্ষালন ॥১২০॥
verses.transliteration: nāṭaśālā dhui' dhuila catvara-prāṅgaṇa\\npākaśālā-ādi kari' karila prakṣālana
verses.translation: In this way the meeting place was washed, the entire yard, the raised sitting places, the kitchen and every other room.

verses.devanagari: মন্দিরের চতুর্দিক্ প্রক্ষালন কৈল ।\\nসব অন্তঃপুর ভালমতে ধোয়াইল ॥১২১॥
verses.transliteration: mandirera catur-dik prakṣālana kaila\\nsaba antaḥpura bhāla-mate dhoyāila
verses.translation: Thus all places around the temple were thoroughly washed within and without.

verses.devanagari: হেনকালে গৌড়ীয়া এক সুবুদ্ধি সরল  ।\\nপ্রভুর চরণ-যুগে দিল ঘট-জল ॥১২২॥
verses.transliteration: hena-kāle gauḍīyā eka subuddhi sarala\\nprabhura caraṇa-yuge dila ghaṭa-jala
verses.translation: After everything was thoroughly washed, a Vaiṣṇava from Bengal, who was very intelligent and simple, came and poured water on the lotus feet of the Lord.

verses.devanagari: সেই জল লঞা আপনে পান কৈল  ।\\nতাহা দেখি’ প্রভুর মনে দুঃখ রোষ হৈল ॥১২৩॥
verses.transliteration: sei jala lañā āpane pāna kaila\\ntāhā dekhi' prabhura mane duḥkha roṣa haila
verses.translation: The Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava then took that water and drank it himself. Seeing that, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu felt a little unhappy and was also outwardly angry.

verses.devanagari: যদ্যপি গোসাঞি তারে হঞাছে সন্তোষ ।\\nধর্মসংস্থাপন লাগি’ বাহিরে মহারোষ ॥১২৪॥
verses.transliteration: yadyapi gosāñi tāre hañāche santoṣa\\ndharma-saṁsthāpana lāgi' bāhire mahā-roṣa
verses.translation: Although the Lord was certainly satisfied with him, He became angry externally in order to establish the etiquette of religious principles.

verses.devanagari: শিক্ষা লাগি’ স্বরূপে ডাকি’ কহিল তাঁহারে  ।\\nএই দেখ তোমার ‘গৌড়ীয়া’র ব্যবহারে ॥১২৫॥
verses.transliteration: śikṣā lāgi' svarūpe ḍāki' kahila tāṅhāre\\nei dekha tomāra 'gauḍīyā'ra vyavahāre
verses.translation: The Lord then called for Svarūpa Dāmodara and told him, "Just see the behavior of your Bengali Vaiṣṇava.

verses.devanagari: ঈশ্বরমন্দিরে মোর পদ ধোয়াইল  ।\\nসেই জল আপনি লঞা পান কৈল ॥১২৬॥
verses.transliteration: īśvara-mandire mora pada dhoyāila\\nsei jala āpani lañā pāna kaila
verses.translation: "This person from Bengal has washed My feet within the temple of the Personality of Godhead. Not only that, but he has drunk the water himself.

verses.devanagari: এই অপরাধে মোর কাহাঁ হবে গতি ।\\nতোমার ‘গৌড়ীয়া’ করে এতেক ফৈজতি ! ॥ ১২৭ ॥
verses.transliteration: ei aparādhe mora kāhāṅ habe gati\\ntomāra 'gauḍīyā' kare eteka phaijati!
verses.translation: "I now do not know what My destination is because of this offense. Indeed, your Bengali Vaiṣṇava has greatly implicated Me."
verses.purport:
PURPORT
It is significant that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu told Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī that the Bengali Vaiṣṇava was "your Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava." This means that all Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇavas who are followers of the Caitanya cult are subordinate to Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī. The
paramparā
system is very strictly observed by Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇavas. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's personal secretary was Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī. The next group of devotees was the six Gosvāmīs, then Kavirāja Gosvāmī. It is necessary to observe the
paramparā
system of the Caitanya cult. There are many offenses one can commit while serving the Lord, and these are described in the
Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu, Hari-bhakti-vilāsa
and other books. According to the rules and regulations, no one should accept obeisances in the temple of the Lord before the Deity. Nor is it proper for a devotee to offer obeisances and touch the feet of the spiritual master before the Deity. This is considered an offense. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu Himself was personally the Supreme Personality of Godhead; therefore it was not actually offensive to wash His lotus feet in the temple. However, because He was playing the part of an
ācārya,
the Lord considered Himself an ordinary human being. He also wanted to give instructions to ordinary human beings. The point is that even though one plays the part of a spiritual master, he should not accept obeisances or permit a disciple to wash his feet before the Deity. This is a matter of etiquette.

verses.devanagari: তবে স্বরূপ গোসাঞি তার ঘাড়ে হাত দিয়া ।\\nঢেকা মারি’ পুরীর বাহির রাখিলেন লঞা ॥১২৮॥
verses.transliteration: tabe svarūpa gosāñi tāra ghāḍe hāta diyā\\nḍhekā māri' purīra bāhira rākhilena lañā
verses.translation: At this point Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī caught the Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava by the neck and, giving him a little push, ejected him from the Guṇḍicā Purī temple and made him stay outside.

verses.devanagari: পুনঃ আসি’ প্রভু পায় করিল বিনয় ।\\n‘অজ্ঞ-অপরাধ’ ক্ষমা করিতে যুয়ায় ॥১২৯॥
verses.transliteration: punaḥ āsi' prabhu pāya karila vinaya\\n'ajña-aparādha' kṣamā karite yuyāya
verses.translation: After Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī returned within the temple, he requested Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu to excuse that innocent person.

verses.devanagari: তবে মহাপ্রভুর মনে সন্তোষ হইলা  ।\\nসারি করি’ দুই পাশে সবারে বসাইলা ॥১৩০॥
verses.transliteration: tabe mahāprabhura mane santoṣa ha-ilā\\nsāri kari' dui pāśe sabāre vasāilā
verses.translation: After this incident, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was very satisfied. He then asked all of the devotees to sit down in two lines on both sides.

verses.devanagari: আপনে বসিয়া মাঝে, আপনার হাতে  ।\\nতৃণ, কাঁকর, কুটা লাগিলা কুড়াইতে ॥১৩১॥
verses.transliteration: āpane vasiyā mājhe, āpanāra hāte\\ntṛṇa, kāṅkara, kuṭā lāgilā kuḍāite
verses.translation: The Lord then personally sat down in the middle and picked up all kinds of straw, grains of sand and dirty things.

verses.devanagari: কে কত কুড়ায়, সব একত্র করিব ।\\nযার অল্প, তার ঠাঞি পিঠা-পানা লইব ॥১৩২॥
verses.transliteration: ke kata kuḍāya, saba ekatra kariba\\nyāra alpa, tāra ṭhāñi piṭhā-pānā la-iba
verses.translation: While Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was picking up the straws and grains of sand, He said, "I shall gather everyone's collection, and I shall ask whoever has collected less than all the others to pay a fine of sweet cakes and sweet rice."

verses.devanagari: এই মত সব পুরী করিল শোধন ।\\nশীতল, নির্মল কৈল — যেন নিজ-মন ॥১৩৩॥
verses.transliteration: ei mata saba purī karila śodhana\\nśītala, nirmala kaila-yena nija-mana
verses.translation: In this way all the quarters of the Guṇḍicā temple were completely cleansed and cleared. All quarters were cool and spotless, like one's cleansed and pacified mind.

verses.devanagari: প্রণালিকা ছাড়ি’ যদি পানি বহাইল ।\\nনূতন নদী যেন সমুদ্রে মিলিল ॥১৩৪॥
verses.transliteration: praṇālikā chāḍi' yadi pāni vahāila\\nnūtana nadī yena samudre milila
verses.translation: When the water from the different rooms was finally let out through the halls, it appeared as if new rivers were rushing out to meet the waters of the ocean.

verses.devanagari: এইমত পুরদ্বার-আগে পথ যত ।\\nসকল শোধিল, তাহা কে বর্ণিবে কত ॥১৩৫॥
verses.transliteration: ei-mata puradvāra-āge patha yata\\nsakala śodhila, tāhā ke varṇibe kata
verses.translation: Outside the gateway of the temple, all the roads were also cleansed, and no one could tell exactly how this was done.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
In commenting on the cleansing of the Guṇḍicā temple, Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura says that Śrī Caitanya Mahaprabhu was personally giving instructions on how one should receive Lord Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, within one's cleansed and pacified heart. If one wants to see Kṛṣṇa seated in his heart, he must first cleanse the heart, as prescribed by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu in His
Śikṣāṣṭaka: ceto-darpaṇa-mārjanam.
In this age, everyone's heart is unclean, as confirmed in
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam: hṛdy antaḥ-stho hy abhadrāṇi.
To wash all dirty things accumulated within the heart, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu advised everyone to chant the Hare Kṛṣṇa
mantra.
The first result will be that the heart is cleansed (
ceto-darpaṇa-mārjanam
). Similarly,
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(1.2.17) confirms this statement:
śṛṇvatāṁ sva-kathāḥ kṛṣṇaḥ
puṇya-śravaṇa-kīrtanaḥ
hṛdy antaḥ-stho hy abhadrāṇi
vidhunoti suhṛt satām
"Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Personality of Godhead, who is the Paramātmā [Supersoul] in everyone's heart and the benefactor of the truthful devotee, cleanses desire for material enjoyment from the heart of the devotee who relishes His messages, which are in themselves virtuous when properly heard and chanted."
If a devotee at all wants to cleanse his heart, he must chant and hear the glories of the Lord, Śrī Kṛṣṇa (
śṛṇvatāṁ sva-kathāḥ kṛṣṇaḥ
). This is a simple process. Kṛṣṇa Himself will help cleanse the heart because He is already seated there. Kṛṣṇa wants to continue living within the heart, and the Lord wants to give directions, but one has to keep his heart as clean as Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu kept the Guṇḍicā temple. The devotee therefore has to cleanse his heart just as the Lord cleansed the Guṇḍicā temple. In this way one can be pacified and enriched in devotional service. If the heart is filled with straw, grains of sand, weeds or dust (in other words,
anyābhilāṣa-pūrṇa
), one cannot enthrone the Supreme Personality of Godhead there. The heart must be cleansed of all material motives brought about through fruitive work, speculative knowledge, the mystic
yoga
system and so many other forms of so-called meditation. The heart must be cleansed without ulterior motive. As Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī says:
anyābhilāṣitā-śūnyaṁ jñāna-karmādy-anāvṛtam.
In other words, there should not be any external motive. One should not attempt material upliftment, understanding the Supreme by speculative knowledge, fruitive activity, severe austerity and penance, and so on. All these activities are against the natural growth of spontaneous love of Godhead. As soon as these are present within the heart, the heart should be understood to be unclean and therefore unfit to serve as Kṛṣṇa's sitting place. We cannot perceive the Lord's presence in our hearts unless our hearts are cleansed.
A material desire is explained as a desire to enjoy the material world to its fullest extent. In modern language, this is called economic development. An inordinate desire for economic development is considered to be like straws and grains of sand within the heart. If one is overly engaged in material activity, the heart will always remain disturbed. As stated by Narottama dāsa Ṭhākura:
saṁsāra viṣānale,     divā-niśi hiyā jvale,
juḍāite nā kainu upāya
In other words, endeavor for material opulence is against the principle of devotional service. Material enjoyment includes activities such as great sacrifices for auspicious activity, charity, austerity, elevation to the higher planetary system, and even living happily within the material world.
Modernized material benefits are like the dust of material contamination. When this dust is agitated by the whirlwind of fruitive activity, it overcomes the heart. Thus the mirror of the heart is covered with dust. There are many desires for performing auspicious and inauspicious activities, but people do not know how life after life they are keeping their hearts unclean. One who cannot give up the desire for fruitive activity is understood to be covered by the dust of material contamination.
Karmīs
generally think that the interaction of fruitive activities can be counteracted by another
karma,
or fruitive activity. This is certainly a mistaken conception. If one is deluded by such a conception, he is cheated by his own activity. Such activities have been compared to an elephant's bathing. An elephant may bathe very thoroughly, but as soon as it comes out of the river, it immediately takes some sand from the land and throws it all over its body. If one suffers due to his past fruitive activities, he cannot counteract his suffering by performing auspicious activities. The sufferings of human society cannot be counteracted by material plans. The only way suffering can be mitigated is by Kṛṣṇa consciousness. When one takes to Kṛṣṇa consciousness and engages himself in the devotional service of the Lord-beginning with chanting and hearing the glories of the Lord—the cleansing of the heart begins. When the heart is actually cleansed, one can clearly see the Lord sitting there without any disturbance. In
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(9.4.68) the Lord confirms that He sits within the heart of the pure devotee:
sādhavo hṛdayaṁ mahyaṁ sādhūnāṁ hṛdayaṁ tv aham.
Impersonal speculation, monism (merging into the existence of the Supreme), speculative knowledge, mystic
yoga
and meditation are all compared to grains of sand. They simply cause irritation to the heart. No one can satisfy the Supreme Personality of Godhead by such activities, nor do we give the Lord a chance to sit in our hearts peacefully. Rather, the Lord is simply disturbed by them. Sometimes
yogīs
and
jñānīs
in the beginning take to the chanting of the Hare Kṛṣṇa
mahā-mantra
as a way to begin their various practices. However, when they falsely think that they have attained release from the bondage of material existence, they give up chanting. They do not consider that the ultimate goal is the form of the Lord or the name of the Lord. Such unfortunate creatures are never favored by the Supreme Personality of Godhead, for they do not know what devotional service is. Lord Kṛṣṇa describes them in the
Bhagavad-gītā
in this way:
tān ahaṁ dviṣataḥ krūrān
saṁsāreṣu narādhamān
kṣipāmy ajasram aśubhān
āsurīṣv eva yoniṣu
"Those who are envious and mischievous, who are the lowest among men, I perpetually cast into the ocean of material existence, into various demoniac species of life." (Bg. 16.19)
By His practical example, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu has shown us that all the grains of sand must be picked up thoroughly and thrown outside. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu also cleansed the outside of the temple, fearing that the grains of sand would again come within. Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura explains that even though one may become free from the desire for fruitive activity, sometimes the subtle desire for fruitive activity comes into being within the heart. One often thinks of conducting business to improve devotional activity. However, the contamination is so strong that it may later develop into misunderstanding, described as
kuṭi-nāṭi
(faultfinding) and
pratiṣṭhāśā
(the desire for name and fame and for high position),
jīva-hiṁsā
(envy of other living entities),
niṣiddhācāra
(accepting things forbidden in the
śāstra
),
kāma
(desire for material gain) and
pūjā
(hankering for popularity). The word
kuṭi-nāṭi
means "duplicity." As an example, one may attempt to imitate Śrīla Haridāsa Ṭhākura by living in a solitary place. One's real desire may be for name and fame-in other words, one thinks that fools will accept one to be as good as Haridāsa Ṭhākura just because one lives in a solitary place. These are all material desires. A neophyte devotee is certain to be attacked by other material desires as well, women and money. In this way the heart is again filled with dirty things and becomes harder and harder, like that of a materialist. Gradually one desires to become a reputed devotee or an
avatāra
(incarnation).
The word
jīva-hiṁsā
(envy of other living entities) actually means stopping the preaching of Kṛṣṇa consciousness. Preaching work is described as
paropakāra,
welfare activity for others. Those who are ignorant of the benefits of devotional service must be educated by preaching. If one stops preaching and simply sits down in a solitary place, he is engaging in material activity. If one desires to make a compromise with the Māyāvādīs, he is also engaged in material activity. A devotee should never make compromises with nondevotees. By acting as a professional
guru,
mystic
yogī
or miracle man, one may cheat and bluff the general public and gain fame as a wonderful mystic, but all this is considered to be dust, straw and grains of sand within the heart. In addition, one should follow the regulative principles and not desire illicit sex, gambling, intoxicants or meat.
To give us practical instructions, Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu cleansed the temple twice. His second cleansing was more thorough. The idea was to throw away all the stumbling blocks on the path of devotional service. He cleansed the temple with firm conviction, as is evident from His using His own personal garments for cleaning. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu wanted to see personally that the temple was thoroughly cleansed to the standard of clean marble. Clean marble gives a cooling effect. Devotional service means attaining peace from all disturbances caused by material contamination. In other words, it is the process by which the mind is cooled. The mind can be peaceful and thoroughly cleansed when one no longer desires anything but devotional service.
Even though all dirty things may be cleansed away, sometimes subtle desires remain in the mind for impersonalism, monism, success and the four principles of religious activity (
dharma, artha, kāma
and
mokṣa
). All these are like spots on clean cloth. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu also wanted to cleanse all these away.
By His practical activity, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu informed us how to cleanse our hearts. Once the heart is cleansed, we should invite Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa to sit down, and we should observe the festival by distributing
prasāda
and chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa
mahā-mantra.
Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu used to teach every devotee by His personal behavior. Everyone who spreads the cult of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu accepts a similar responsibility. The Lord was personally chastising and praising individuals in the course of the cleaning, and those who are engaged as
ācāryas
must learn from Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu how to train devotees by personal example. The Lord was very pleased with those who could cleanse the temple by taking out undesirable things accumulated within. This is called
anartha-nivṛtti,
cleansing the heart of all unwanted things. Thus the cleansing of the Guṇḍicā-mandira was conducted by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu to let us know how the heart should be cleansed and soothed to receive Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa and enable Him to sit within the heart without disturbance.

verses.devanagari: নৃসিংহ মন্দির-ভিতর-বাহির শোধিল ।\\nক্ষণেক বিশ্রাম করি’ নৃত্য আরম্ভিল ॥১৩৬॥
verses.transliteration: nṛsiṁha-mandira-bhitara-bāhira śodhila\\nkṣaṇeka viśrāma kari' nṛtya ārambhila
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu also cleansed the Nṛsiṁha temple inside and outside. Finally, He rested a few minutes and then began dancing.
verses.purport: PURPORT\nThe Nṛsiṁha temple is a nice temple just outside the Guṇḍicā temple. In this temple there is a great festival on the day of Nṛsiṁha-caturdaśī. There is also a Nṛsiṁha temple at Navadvīpa where the same festival is observed, as described by Murāri Gupta in his book\nCaitanya-carita.

verses.devanagari: চারিদিকে ভক্তগণ করেন কীর্তন ।\\nমধ্যে নৃত্য করেন প্রভু মত্তসিংহ-সম ॥১৩৭॥
verses.transliteration: cāri-dike bhakta-gaṇa karena kīrtana\\nmadhye nṛtya karena prabhu matta-siṁha-sama
verses.translation: All around Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu all the devotees performed congregational chanting. The Lord, just like a maddened lion, danced in the middle.

verses.devanagari: স্বেদ, কম্প, বৈবর্ণ্যাশ্রু পুলক, হুঙ্কার ।\\nনিজ অঙ্গ ধুই’ আগে চলে অশ্রুধার ॥১৩৮॥
verses.transliteration: sveda, kampa, vaivarṇyāśru pulaka, huṅkāra\\nnija-aṅga dhui' āge cale aśru-dhāra
verses.translation: As usual, when Caitanya Mahāprabhu danced, there were perspiration, trembling, fading, tears, jubilation and roaring. Indeed, the tears from His eyes washed His body and those before Him.

verses.devanagari: চারিদিকে ভক্ত-অঙ্গ কৈল প্রক্ষালন ।\\nশ্রাবণের মেঘ যেন করে বরিষণ ॥১৩৯॥
verses.transliteration: cāri-dike bhakta-aṅga kaila prakṣālana\\nśrāvaṇera megha yena kare variṣaṇa
verses.translation: In this way Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu washed the bodies of all the devotees with the tears from His eyes. The tears poured like rains in the month of Śrāvaṇa.

verses.devanagari: মহা-উচ্চসংকীর্তনে আকাশ ভরিল ।\\nপ্রভুর উদ্দণ্ড-নৃত্যে ভূমিকম্প হৈল ॥১৪০॥
verses.transliteration: mahā-ucca-saṅkīrtane ākāśa bharila\\nprabhura uddaṇḍa-nṛtye bhūmi-kampa haila
verses.translation: The sky was filled with the great and loud chanting of saṅkīrtana, and the earth shook from the jumping and dancing of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

verses.devanagari: স্বরূপের উচ্চ-গান প্রভুরে সদা ভায় ।\\nআনন্দে উদ্দণ্ড নৃত্য করে গৌররায় ॥১৪১॥
verses.transliteration: svarūpera ucca-gāna prabhure sadā bhāya\\nānande uddaṇḍa nṛtya kare gaurarāya
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu always liked the loud chanting of Svarūpa Dāmodara. Therefore when Svarūpa Dāmodara sang, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu danced and jumped high in jubilation.

verses.devanagari: এইমত কতক্ষণ নৃত্য যে করিয়া ।\\nবিশ্রাম করিলা প্রভু সময় বুঝিয়া ॥১৪২॥
verses.transliteration: ei-mata kata-kṣaṇa nṛtya ye kariyā\\nviśrāma karilā prabhu samaya bujhiyā
verses.translation: The Lord thus chanted and danced for some time. Finally, understanding the circumstances, He stopped.

verses.devanagari: আচার্য-গোসাঞির পুত্র শ্রীগোপাল-নাম ।\\nনৃত্য করিতে তাঁরে আজ্ঞা দিল গৌরধাম ॥১৪৩॥
verses.transliteration: ācārya-gosāñira putra śrī-gopāla-nāma\\nnṛtya karite tāṅre ājñā dila gauradhāma
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then ordered Śrī Gopāla, the son of Advaita Ācārya, to dance.

verses.devanagari: প্রেমাবেশে নৃত্য করি’ হইলা মূর্চ্ছিতে ।\\nঅচেতন হঞা তেঁহ পড়িলা ভূমিতে ॥১৪৪॥
verses.transliteration: premāveśe nṛtya kari' ha-ilā mūrcchite\\nacetana hañā teṅha paḍilā bhūmite
verses.translation: While dancing in ecstatic love, Śrī Gopāla fainted and fell to the ground unconscious.

verses.devanagari: আস্তে-ব্যস্তে আচার্য তাঁরে কৈল কোলে ।\\nশ্বাস-রহিত দেখি’ আচার্য হৈলা বিকলে ॥১৪৫॥
verses.transliteration: āste-vyaste ācārya tāṅre kaila kole\\nśvāsa-rahita dekhi' ācārya hailā vikale
verses.translation: When Śrī Gopāla fainted, Advaita Ācārya hastily took him upon His lap. Seeing that he was not breathing, He became very much agitated.

verses.devanagari: নৃসিংহের মন্ত্র পড়ি’ মারে জল-ছাঁটি ।\\nহুঙ্কারের শব্দে ব্রহ্মাণ্ড যায় ফাটি’ ॥১৪৬॥
verses.transliteration: nṛsiṁhera mantra paḍi' māre jala-chāṅṭi\\nhuṅkārera śabde brahmāṇḍa yāya phāṭi'
verses.translation: Advaita Ācārya and others began to chant the holy name of Lord Nṛsiṁha and sprinkle water. The roaring of the chant was so great that it seemed to shake the entire universe.

verses.devanagari: অনেক করিল, তবু না হয় চেতন ।\\nআচার্য কান্দেন, কান্দে সব ভক্তগণ ॥১৪৭॥
verses.transliteration: aneka karila, tabu nā haya cetana\\nācārya kāndena, kānde saba bhakta-gaṇa
verses.translation: When the boy did not regain consciousness after some time, Advaita Ācārya and the other devotees began to cry.

verses.devanagari: তবে মহাপ্রভু তাঁর বুকে হস্ত দিল ।\\n‘উঠহ গোপাল’ বলি’ উচ্চৈঃস্বরে কহিল ॥১৪৮॥
verses.transliteration: tabe mahāprabhu tāṅra buke hasta dila\\n'uṭhaha gopāla' bali' uccaiḥsvare kahila
verses.translation: Then Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu placed His hand on the chest of Śrī Gopāla and said loudly, "Gopāla, stand up."

verses.devanagari: শুনিতেই গোপালের হইল চেতন ।\\n‘হরি’ বলি’ নৃত্য করে সর্বভক্তগণ ॥১৪৯॥
verses.transliteration: śunitei gopālera ha-ila cetana\\n'hari' bali' nṛtya kare sarva-bhakta-gaṇa
verses.translation: As soon as Gopāla heard the voice of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, he immediately came to his senses. All the devotees then began to dance, chanting the holy name of Hari.

verses.devanagari: এই লীলা বর্ণিয়াছেন দাস বৃন্দাবন ।\\nঅতএব সংক্ষেপ করি’ করিলুঁ বর্ণন ॥১৫০॥
verses.transliteration: ei līlā varṇiyāchena dāsa vṛndāvana\\nataeva saṅkṣepa kari' kariluṅ varṇana
verses.translation: This incident has been described in detail by Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura. Therefore I have described it only in brief.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a matter of etiquette. If a previous
ācārya
has already written about something, there is no need to repeat it for personal sense gratification or to outdo the previous
ācārya.
Unless there is some definite improvement, one should not repeat.

verses.devanagari: তবে মহাপ্রভু ক্ষণেক বিশ্রাম করিয়া ।\\nস্নান করিবারে গেলা ভক্তগণ লঞা ॥১৫১॥
verses.transliteration: tabe mahāprabhu kṣaṇeka viśrāma kariyā\\nsnāna karibāre gelā bhakta-gaṇa lañā
verses.translation: After taking rest, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and all the devotees departed to take their baths.

verses.devanagari: তীরে উঠি’ পরেন প্রভু শুষ্ক বসন ।\\nনৃসিংহ-দেবে নমস্করি’ গেলা উপবন ॥১৫২॥
verses.transliteration: tīre uṭhi' parena prabhu śuṣka vasana\\nnṛsiṁha-deve namaskari' gelā upavana
verses.translation: After bathing, the Lord stood on the bank of the lake and put on dry garments. After offering obeisances to Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva, whose temple was nearby, the Lord entered a garden.

verses.devanagari: উদ্যানে বসিলা প্রভু ভক্তগণ লঞা ।\\nতবে বাণীনাথ আইলা মহাপ্রসাদ লঞা ॥১৫৩॥
verses.transliteration: udyāne vasilā prabhu bhakta-gaṇa lañā\\ntabe vāṇīnātha āilā mahā-prasāda lañā
verses.translation: In the garden, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu sat down with the other devotees. Vāṇīnātha Rāya then came and brought all kinds of mahā-prasāda.

verses.devanagari: কাশীমিশ্র, তুলসী-পড়িছা — দুই জন ।\\nপঞ্চশত লোক যত করয়ে ভোজন ॥১৫৪॥\\nতত অন্ন-পিঠা-পানা সব পাঠাইল ।\\nদেখি’ মহাপ্রভুর মনে সন্তোষ হইল ॥১৫৫॥
verses.transliteration: tata anna-piṭhā-pānā saba pāṭhāila\\ndekhi' mahāprabhura mane saṅkoca ha-ila
verses.translation: Kāśī Miśra and Tulasī, the superintendent of the temple, brought as much prasāda as five hundred men could eat. Seeing the large quantity of prasāda, which consisted of rice, cakes, sweet rice and a variety of vegetables, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was very much satisfied.

verses.devanagari: পুরী-গোসাঞি, মহাপ্রভু, ভারতী ব্রহ্মানন্দ  ।\\nঅদ্বৈত-আচার্য, আর প্রভু-নিত্যানন্দ ॥১৫৬॥
verses.transliteration: purī-gosāñi, mahāprabhu, bhāratī brahmānanda\\nadvaita-ācārya, āra prabhu-nityānanda
verses.translation: Among the devotees present with Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu were Paramānanda Purī, Brahmānanda Bhāratī, Advaita Ācārya and Nityānanda Prabhu.

verses.devanagari: আচার্যরত্ন, আচার্যনিধি, শ্রীবাস, গদাধর  ।\\nশঙ্কর, নন্দনাচার্য, আর রাঘব, বক্রেশ্বর ॥১৫৭॥
verses.transliteration: ācāryaratna, ācāryanidhi, śrīvāsa, gadādhara\\nśaṅkara, nandanācārya, āra rāghava, vakreśvara
verses.translation: Ācāryaratna, Ācāryanidhi, Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura, Gadādhara Paṇḍita, Śaṅkara, Nandanācārya, Rāghava Paṇḍita and Vakreśvara were also present.

verses.devanagari: প্রভু-আজ্ঞা পাঞা বৈসে আপনে সার্বভৌম ।\\nপিণ্ডার উপরে প্রভু বৈসে লঞা ভক্তগণ ॥১৫৮॥
verses.transliteration: prabhu-ājñā pāñā vaise āpane sārvabhauma\\npiṇḍāra upare prabhu vaise lañā bhakta-gaṇa
verses.translation: Receiving the permission of the Lord, Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya sat down. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and all His devotees sat on raised wooden seats.

verses.devanagari: তার তলে, তার তলে করি’ অনুক্রম ।\\nউদ্যান ভরি’ বৈসে ভক্ত করিতে ভোজন ॥১৫৯॥
verses.transliteration: tāra tale, tāra tale kari' anukrama\\nudyāna bhari' vaise bhakta karite bhojana
verses.translation: In this way all the devotees sat down to take their lunch in consecutive lines, one beside the other.

verses.devanagari: ‘হরিদাস’ বলি’ প্রভু ডাকে ঘনে ঘন  ।\\nদূরে রহি’ হরিদাস করে নিবেদন ॥১৬০॥
verses.transliteration: 'haridāsa' bali' prabhu ḍāke ghane ghana\\ndūre rahi' haridāsa kare nivedana
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was repeatedly calling, "Haridāsa, Haridāsa," and at that time Haridāsa, standing at a distance, spoke as follows.

verses.devanagari: ভক্ত-সঙ্গে প্রভু করুন প্রসাদ অঙ্গীকার  ।\\nএ-সঙ্গে বসিতে যোগ্য নহি মুঞি ছার ॥১৬১॥
verses.transliteration: bhakta-saṅge prabhu karuna prasāda aṅgīkāra\\ne-saṅge vasite yogya nahi muñi chāra
verses.translation: Haridāsa Ṭhākura said, "Let Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu take His lunch with the devotees. Since I am abominable, I cannot sit down among you.

verses.devanagari: পাছে মোরে প্রসাদ গোবিন্দ দিবে বহির্দ্বারে  ।\\nমন জানি’ প্রভু পুনঃ না বলিল তাঁরে ॥১৬২॥
verses.transliteration: pāche more prasāda govinda dibe bahirdvāre\\nmana jāni' prabhu punaḥ nā balila tāṅre
verses.translation: "Govinda will give me prasāda later, outside the door." Understanding his mind, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu did not call him again.

verses.devanagari: স্বরূপ-গোসাঞি, জগদানন্দ, দামোদর ।\\nকাশীশ্বর, গোপীনাথ, বাণীনাথ, শঙ্কর ॥১৬৩॥\\nপরিবেশন করে তাহাঁ এই সাতজন ।\\nমধ্যে মধ্যে হরিধ্বনি করে ভক্তগণ ॥১৬৪॥
verses.transliteration: pariveśana kare tāhāṅ ei sāta-jana\\nmadhye madhye hari-dhvani kare bhakta-gaṇa
verses.translation: Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī, Jagadānanda, Dāmodara Paṇḍita, Kāśīśvara, Gopīnātha, Vāṇīnātha and Śaṅkara distributed prasāda, and the devotees chanted the holy names at intervals.

verses.devanagari: পুলিন-ভোজন কৃষ্ণ পূর্বে যৈছে কৈল ।\\nসেই লীলা মহাপ্রভুর মনে স্মৃতি হৈল ॥১৬৫॥
verses.transliteration: pulina-bhojana kṛṣṇa pūrve yaiche kaila\\nsei līlā mahāprabhura mane smṛti haila
verses.translation: Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa had previously taken His lunch in the forest, and that very pastime was remembered by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

verses.devanagari: যদ্যপি প্রেমাবেশে প্রভু হৈলা অস্থির ।\\nসময় বুঝিয়া প্রভু হৈলা কিছু ধীর ॥১৬৬॥
verses.transliteration: yadyapi premāveśe prabhu hailā asthira\\nsamaya bujhiyā prabhu hailā kichu dhīra
verses.translation: Just by remembering the pastimes of Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was agitated by ecstatic love. However, considering the time and circumstance, He remained somewhat patient.

verses.devanagari: প্রভু কহে, — মোরে দেহ’ লাফ্রা-ব্যঞ্জনে ।\\nপিঠা-পানা, অমৃত-গুটিকা দেহ’ ভক্তগণে ॥১৬৭॥
verses.transliteration: prabhu kahe,-more deha' lāphrā-vyañjane\\npiṭhā-pānā, amṛta-guṭikā deha' bhakta-gaṇe
