is understood in different ways by different religionists. Mundaners also come up with their different angles of vision. For the conditioned soul busy in sense gratification, a
mahājana
is recognized according to the proportion of sense gratification he offers. For instance, a businessman may consider a certain banker to be a
mahājana,
and
karmīs
desiring material enjoyment may consider philosophers like Jaimini to be
mahājanas.
There are many
yogīs
who want to control the senses, and for them Patañjali Rṣi is a
mahā-jana.
For the
jñānīs,
the atheist Kapila, Vaśiṣṭha, Durvāsā, Dattātreya and other impersonalist philosophers are
mahājanas.
For the demons, Hiraṇyākṣa, Hiraṇyakaśipu, Rāvaṇa, Rāvaṇa's son Meghanāda, Jarāsandha and others are accepted as
mahājanas.
For materialistic anthropologists speculating on the evolution of the body, a person like Darwin is a
mahājana.
The scientists who are bewildered by Kṛṣṇa's external energy have no relationship with the Supreme Personality of Godhead, yet they are accepted by some as
mahājanas.
Similarly, philosophers, historians, literary men, public speakers and social and political leaders are sometimes accepted as
mahājanas.
Such
mahājanas
are respected by certain men who have been described in
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(2.3.19):
śva-viḍ-varāhoṣṭra-kharaiḥ
saṁstutaḥ puruṣaḥ paśuḥ
na yat-karṇa-pathopeto
jātu nāma gadāgrajaḥ
"Men who are like dogs, hogs, camels and asses praise those men who never listen to the transcendental pastimes of Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the deliverer from evils."
Thus on the material platform animalistic leaders are worshiped by animals. Sometimes physicians, psychiatrists and social workers try to mitigate bodily pain, distress and fear, but they have no knowledge of spiritual identity and are bereft of a relationship with God. Yet they are considered
mahājanas
by the illusioned. Self-deceived persons sometimes accept leaders or spiritual masters from a priestly order that has been officially appointed by the codes of material life. In this way, they are deceived by official priests. Sometimes people accept as
mahā-janas
those who have been designated by Śrīla Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura as
ḍhaṅga-vipras
(imposter
brāhmaṇas).
Such imposters imitate the characteristics of Śrīla Haridāsa Ṭhākura, and they envy Haridāsa Ṭhākura, who was certainly a
mahājana.
They make great artificial endeavors, advertising themselves as great devotees of the Lord or as mystic hypnotists knowledgeable in witchcraft, hypnotism and miracles. Sometimes people accept demons like Pūtanā, Tṛṇāvarta, Vatsa, Baka, Aghāsura and Dhenuka, Kālīya and Pralamba. Some people accept imitators and adversaries of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, such as Pauṇḍraka, Śṛgāla Vāsudeva, the spiritual master of the demons (Śukrācārya), or atheists like Cārvāka, King Vena, Sugata and Arhat. Such people have no faith in Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu as the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Rather, they accept godless cheaters who present themselves as incarnations of God and cheat foolish people within the material world by word jugglery. Thus many rascals are accepted as
mahājanas.
In this material world a person may be famous as a
karma-vīra,
a successful fruitive worker, or one may be very successful in performing religious duties, or he may be known as a hero in mental speculation (
jñāna-vīra),
or he may be a very famous renunciant. In any case,
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(3.23.56) gives the following opinion in this matter.
neha yat karma dharmāya
na virāgāya kalpate
na tīrtha-pada-sevāyai
jīvann api mṛto hi saḥ
"Anyone whose work is not meant to elevate him to religious life, anyone whose religious ritualistic performances do not raise him to renunciation, and anyone situated in renunciation that does not lead him to devotional service to the Supreme Personality of Godhead must be considered dead, although he is breathing."
The conclusion is that all pious activity, fruitive activity, religious principles and renunciation must ultimately lead to devotional service. There are different types of processes for rendering service. One may serve his country, people, society, the
varṇāśrama-dharma,
the sick, the poor, the rich, women, demigods and so on. All this comes under the heading of sense gratification, or enjoyment in the material world. It is most unfortunate that people are more or less attracted by such material activity and that the leaders of these activities are accepted as
mahājanas,
great ideal leaders. Actually they are only misleaders, but an ordinary man cannot understand how he is being misled.
Narottama dāsa Ṭhākura says:
sādhu-śāstra-guru-vākya, cittete kariyā aikya. A sādhu
is a great personality like Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. The
śāstras
are the injunctions of revealed scriptures. Those who are devoid of devotional service sometimes mistake those who have mundane motives for
mahājanas.
The only motive must be
kṛṣṇa-bhakti,
devotional service to the Lord. Sometimes fruitive workers, dry philosophers, nondevotees, mystic
yogīs
and persons attached to material opulence, women and money are considered
mahājanas.
However,
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(6.3.25) gives the following statements about such unauthorized
mahājanas:
prāyeṇa veda tad idaṁ na mahājano 'yaṁ
devyā vimohita-matir bata māyayālam
trayyāṁ jaḍī-kṛta-matir madhu-puṣpitāyāṁ
vaitānike mahati karmaṇi yujyamānaḥ
In this material world,
karmīs
(fruitive actors) are accepted as
mahājanas
by foolish people who do not know the value of devotional service. Their mundane intelligence and mental speculative methods are under the control of the three modes of material nature. Consequently they cannot understand unalloyed devotional service. They are attracted by material activities, and they become worshipers of material nature. Thus they are known as fruitive actors. They even become entangled in material activities disguised as spiritual activities. In
Bhagavad-gītā,
such people are described as
veda-vāda-ratā.
They do not understand the real purpose of the
Vedas,
yet they think of themselves as Vedic authorities. People versed in Vedic knowledge must know Kṛṣṇa as the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
Vedaiś ca sarvair aham eva vedyaḥ.
(Bg. 15.15)
A man covered by illusion cannot understand the proper way; therefore Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu says:
dharma-sthāpana-hetu sādhura vyavahāra.
The behavior of a devotee is the criterion for all other behavior. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu Himself followed the devotional principles and taught others to follow them.
Purī-gosāñira ye ācaraṇa, sei dharma sāra.
Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu personally followed the behavior of Mādhavendra Purī and advised others to follow his principles. Unfortunately, people have been attracted to the material body since time immemorial.
yasyātma-buddhiḥ kuṇape tridhātuke
sva-dhīḥ kalatrādiṣu bhauma ijya-dhīḥ
yat-tīrtha-buddhiḥ salile na karhicij
janeṣv abhijñeṣu sa eva go-kharaḥ
"A human being who identifies this body made of three elements with his self, who considers the by-products of the body to be his kinsmen, who considers the land of birth worshipable, and who goes to the place of pilgrimage simply to take a bath rather than meet men of transcendental knowledge there is to be considered like an ass or a cow." (
Bhāg.
10.84.13) Those who accept the logic of
gaḍ-ḍalikā-pravāha
and follow in the footsteps of pseudo-
mahājanas
are carried away by the waves of
māyā.
Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura therefore warns:
miche māyāra vaśe, yāccha bhese',
khāccha hābuḍubu, bhāi
jīva kṛṣṇa-dāsa, e viśvāsa,
ka'rle ta' āra duḥkha nāi
"Don't be carried away by the waves of
māyā.
Just surrender to the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa, and all miseries will end." Those who follow social customs and behavior forget to follow the path chalked out by the
mahājanas;
thus they are offenders at the feet of the
mahājanas.
Sometimes they consider such
mahājanas
very conservative, or they create their own
mahājanas.
In this way they ignore the principles of the
paramparā
system. This is a great misfortune for everyone. If one does not follow in the footsteps of a real
mahājana,
one's plans for happiness will be frustrated. This is elaborately explained in
Madhya-līlā
(Chapter Twenty-five, verses 55, 56 and 58). It is there stated:
parama kāraṇa īśvare keha nāhi māne
sva-sva-mata sthāpe para-matera khaṇḍane
tāte chaya darśana haite 'tattva' nāhi jāni
'mahājana' yei kahe, sei 'satya' māni
śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya-vāṇī—amṛtera dhāra
tiṅho ye kahaye vastu, sei 'tattva'—sāra
People are so unfortunate that they do not accept the instructions of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Instead, they want to be supported by so-called
mahājanas,
authorities.
Tāte chaya darśana haite 'tattva' nāhi jāni:
we cannot ascertain the real truth simply by following speculators. We have to follow the footsteps of the
mahājanas
in the disciplic succession. Then our attempt will be successful.
Śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya-vāṇī-amṛtera dhāra:
"Whatever is spoken by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is an incessant flow of nectar." Whoever accepts His words as reality can understand the essence of the Absolute Truth. No one can ascertain the Absolute Truth by following the philosophy of Sāṅkhya or Patañjali, for the followers of Sāṅkhya or Patañjali do not accept Lord Viṣṇu as the Supreme Personality of Godhead (
na te viduḥ svārtha-gatiṁ hi viṣṇum).
The ambition of such people is never fulfilled; therefore they are attracted by the external energy. Although mental speculators may be renowned all over the world as great authorities, actually they are not. Such leaders are themselves conservative and not at all liberal. However, if we preach this philosophy, people will consider Vaiṣṇavas very sectarian. Śrīla Mādhavendra Purī was a real
mahājana,
but misguided people cannot distinguish the real from the unreal. However, a person who is awakened to Kṛṣṇa consciousness can understand the real religious path chalked out by the Lord and His pure devotees. Śrī Mādhavendra Purī was a real
mahājana
because he understood the Absolute Truth properly and throughout his life behaved like a pure devotee. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu approved the method of Śrī Mādhavendra Purī. Therefore, although from the material viewpoint the Sanoḍiyā
brāhmaṇa
was on a lower platform, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu considered him situated on the highest platform of spiritual realization.
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (6.3.20) states that there are twelve
mahājanas:
Brahmā, Nārada, Śambhu, Kumāra, Kapila, Manu, Prahlāda, Janaka, Bhīṣma, Bali, Śukadeva and Yamarāja.
To select our
mahājanas
in the Gauḍīya-sampradāya, we have to follow in the footsteps of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and His representatives. His next representative is Śrī Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī, and the next are the six Gosvāmīs-Śrī Rūpa, Śrī Sanātana, Bhaṭṭa Raghunātha, Śrī Jīva, Gopāla Bhaṭṭa and Dāsa Raghunātha. The follower of Viṣṇusvāmī was Śrīdhara Svāmī, the most well known commentator on
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam.
He was also a
mahājana.
Similarly, Caṇḍīdāsa, Vidyāpati and Jayadeva were all
mahājanas.
One who tries to imitate the
mahājanas
just to become an imitative spiritual master is certainly far away from following in the footsteps of the
mahājanas.
Sometimes people cannot actually understand how a
mahājana
follows other
mahājanas.
In this way people are inclined to fall from devotional service.

verses.devanagari: তর্কোঽপ্রতিষ্ঠঃ শ্রুতয়ো বিভিন্না\\nনাসাবৃষির্যস্য মতং ন ভিন্নম্ ।\\nধর্মস্য তত্ত্বং নিহিতং গুহায়াং\\nমহাজনো যেন গতঃ স পন্থাঃ ॥১৮৬॥
verses.transliteration: tarko 'pratiṣṭhaḥ śrutayo vibhinnā\\nnāsāv ṛṣir yasya mataṁ na bhinnam\\ndharmasya tattvaṁ nihitaṁ guhāyāṁ\\nmahājano yena gataḥ sa panthāḥ
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu continued," 'Dry arguments are inconclusive. A great personality whose opinion does not differ from others is not considered a great sage. Simply by studying the Vedas, which are variegated, one cannot come to the right path by which religious principles are understood. The solid truth of religious principles is hidden in the heart of an unadulterated self-realized person. Consequently, as the śāstras confirm, one should accept whatever progressive path the mahājanas advocate.' "
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a verse spoken by Yudhiṣṭhira Mahārāja in the
Mahābhārata, Vana-parva
(313.117).

verses.devanagari: তবে সেই বিপ্র প্রভুকে ভিক্ষা করাইল ।\\nমধুপুরীর লোক সব প্রভুকে দেখিতে আইল ॥১৮৭॥
verses.transliteration: tabe sei vipra prabhuke bhikṣā karāila\\nmadhu-purīra loka saba prabhuke dekhite āila
verses.translation: After this discussion, the brāhmaṇa gave lunch to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Then all the people residing in Mathurā came to see the Lord.

verses.devanagari: লক্ষ-সংখ্য লোক আইসে, নাহিক গণন ।\\nবাহির হঞা প্রভু দিল দরশন ॥১৮৮॥
verses.transliteration: lakṣa-saṅkhya loka āise, nāhika gaṇana\\nbāhira hañā prabhu dila daraśana
verses.translation: People came by hundreds of thousands, and no one could count them. Therefore Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu came out of the house to give audience to the people.

verses.devanagari: বাহু তুলি’ বলে প্রভু ‘হরিবোল’-ধ্বনি ।\\nপ্রেমে মত্ত নাচে লোক করি’ হরিধ্বনি ॥১৮৯॥
verses.transliteration: bāhu tuli' bale prabhu 'hari-bola'-dhvani\\npreme matta nāce loka kari' hari-dhvani
verses.translation: When the people assembled, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu raised His arms and said very loudly, "Hari bol!" The people responded to the Lord and became ecstatic. As if mad, they began to dance and vibrate the transcendental sound, "Hari!"

verses.devanagari: যমুনার ‘চব্বিশ ঘাটে’ প্রভু কৈল স্নান ।\\nসেই বিপ্র প্রভুকে দেখায় তীর্থস্থান ॥১৯০॥
verses.transliteration: yamunāra 'cabbiśa ghāṭe' prabhu kaila snāna\\nsei vipra prabhuke dekhāya tīrtha-sthāna
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu bathed in twenty-four ghats along the banks of the Yamunā, and the brāhmaṇa showed Him all the places of pilgrimage.
verses.purport: PURPORT\nThe twenty-four ghats (bathing places) along the Yamunā are (1) Avimukta, (2) Adhirūḍha, (3) Guhya-tīrtha, (4) Prayāga-tīrtha, (5) Kanakhala-tīrtha, (6) Tinduka, (7) Sūrya-tīrtha, (8) Vaṭasvāmī, (9) Dhruva-ghāṭa, (10) Ṛṣi-tīrtha, (11) Mokṣa-tīrtha, (12) Bodha-tīrtha, (13) Gokarṇa, (14) Kṛṣṇagaṅgā, (15) Vaikuṇṭha, (16) Asi-kuṇḍa, (17) Catuḥ-sāmudrika-kūpa, (18) Akrūra-tīrtha, (19) Yājñika-vipra-sthāna, (20) Kubjā-kūpa, (21) Raṅga-sthala, (22) Mañca-sthala, (23) Mallayuddha-sthāna and (24) Daśāśvamedha.

verses.devanagari: স্বয়ম্ভু, বিশ্রাম, দীর্ঘবিষ্ণু, ভূতেশ্বর ।\\nমহাবিদ্যা, গোকর্ণাদি দেখিলা বিস্তর ॥১৯১॥
verses.transliteration: svayambhu, viśrāma, dīrgha-viṣṇu, bhūteśvara\\nmahāvidyā, gokarṇādi dekhilā vistara
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu visited all the holy places on the banks of the Yamunā, including Svayambhu, Viśrāma-ghāṭa, Dīrgha Viṣṇu, Bhūteśvara, Mahāvidyā and Gokarṇa.

verses.devanagari: ‘বন’ দেখিবারে যদি প্রভুর মন হৈল ।\\nসেইত ব্রাহ্মণে প্রভু সঙ্গেতে লইল ॥১৯২॥
verses.transliteration: 'vana' dekhibāre yadi prabhura mana haila\\nsei ta brāhmaṇe prabhu saṅgete la-ila
verses.translation: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu wanted to see the various forests of Vṛndāvana, He took the brāhmaṇa with Him.

verses.devanagari: মধুবন, তাল, কুমুদ, বহুলা-বন গেলা ।\\nতাহাঁ তাহাঁ স্নান করি’ প্রেমাবিষ্ট হৈলা ॥১৯৩॥
verses.transliteration: madhu-vana, tāla, kumuda, bahulā-vana gelā\\ntāhāṅ tāhāṅ snāna kari' premāviṣṭa hailā
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu visited the different forests, including Madhuvana, Tālavana, Kumudavana and Bahulāvana. Wherever He went, He took His bath with great ecstatic love.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
The word
vana
means "forest." Vṛndāvana is the name given to the forest where Śrīmatī Vṛndādevī (Tulasīdevī) grows profusely. Actually it is not a forest as we ordinarily consider a forest because it is very thick with green vegetation. There are twelve such
vanas
in Vṛndāvana. Some are located on the western side of the Yamunā and others on the eastern side. The forests situated on the eastern side are Bhadravana, Bilvavana, Lauhavana, Bhāṇḍīravana and Mahāvana. On the western side are Madhuvana, Tālavana, Kumudavana, Bahulāvana, Kāmyavana, Khadiravana and Vṛndāvana. These are the twelve forests of the Vṛndāvana area.

verses.devanagari: পথে গাভীঘটা চরে প্রভুরে দেখিয়া ।\\nপ্রভুকে বেড়য় আসি’ হুঙ্কার করিয়া ॥১৯৪॥
verses.transliteration: pathe gābhī-ghaṭā care prabhure dekhiyā\\nprabhuke beḍaya āsi' huṅkāra kariyā
verses.translation: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu passed through Vṛndāvana, herds of grazing cows saw Him pass and, immediately surrounding Him, began to moo very loudly.

verses.devanagari: গাভী দেখি’ স্তব্ধ প্রভু প্রেমের তরঙ্গে ।\\nবাৎসল্যে গাভী প্রভুর চাটে সব-অঙ্গে ॥১৯৫॥
verses.transliteration: gābhī dekhi' stabdha prabhu premera taraṅge\\nvātsalye gābhī prabhura cāṭe saba-aṅge
verses.translation: Seeing the herds approach Him, the Lord was stunned with ecstatic love. The cows then began to lick His body in great affection.

verses.devanagari: সুস্থ হঞা প্রভু করে অঙ্গ-কণ্ডূয়ন ।\\nপ্রভু-সঙ্গে চলে, নাহি ছাড়ে ধেনুগণ ॥১৯৬॥
verses.transliteration: sustha hañā prabhu kare aṅga-kaṇḍūyana\\nprabhu-saṅge cale, nāhi chāḍe dhenu-gaṇa
verses.translation: Becoming pacified, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu began to caress the cows, and the cows, being unable to give up His company, went with Him.

verses.devanagari: কষ্টেসৃষ্ট্যে ধেনু সব রাখিল গোয়াল ।\\nপ্রভুকণ্ঠধ্বনি শুনি’ আইসে মৃগীপাল ॥১৯৭॥
verses.transliteration: kaṣṭe-sṛṣṭye dhenu saba rākhila goyāla\\nprabhu-kaṇṭha-dhvani śuni' āise mṛgī-pāla
verses.translation: It was with great difficulty that the cowherd men were able to keep the cows back. Then when the Lord chanted, all the deer heard His sweet voice and approached Him.

verses.devanagari: মৃগ-মৃগী মুখ দেখি’ প্রভু-অঙ্গ চাটে ।\\nভয় নাহি করে, সঙ্গে যায় বাটে-বাটে ॥১৯৮॥
verses.transliteration: mṛga-mṛgī mukha dekhi' prabhu-aṅga cāṭe\\nbhaya nāhi kare, saṅge yāya vāṭe-vāṭe
verses.translation: When the does and bucks came and saw the Lord's face, they began to lick His body. Not being at all afraid of Him, they accompanied Him along the path.

verses.devanagari: শুক, পিক, ভৃঙ্গ প্রভুরে দেখি’ ‘পঞ্চম’ গায় ।\\nশিখিগণ নৃত্য করি’ প্রভু-আগে যায় ॥১৯৯॥
verses.transliteration: śuka, pika, bhṛṅga prabhure dekhi' 'pañcama' gāya\\nśikhi-gaṇa nṛtya kari' prabhu-āge yāya
verses.translation: Bumblebees and birds like the parrot and cuckoo all began to sing loudly on the fifth note, and the peacocks began to dance in front of the Lord.

verses.devanagari: প্রভু দেখি’ বৃন্দাবনের বৃক্ষ-লতাগণে ।\\nঅঙ্কুর-পুলক, মধু-অশ্রু বরিষণে ॥২০০॥
verses.transliteration: prabhu dekhi' vṛndāvanera vṛkṣa-latā-gaṇe\\naṅkura pulaka, madhu-aśru variṣaṇe
verses.translation: Upon seeing Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the trees and creepers of Vṛndāvana became jubilant. Their twigs stood up, and they began to shed tears of ecstasy in the form of honey.

verses.devanagari: ফুল-ফল ভরি’ ডাল পড়ে প্রভু-পায় ।\\nবন্ধু দেখি’ বন্ধু যেন ‘ভেট’ লঞা যায় ॥২০১॥
verses.transliteration: phula-phala bhari' ḍāla paḍe prabhu-pāya\\nbandhu dekhi' bandhu yena'bheṭa' lañā yāya
verses.translation: The trees and creepers, overloaded with fruits and flowers, fell down at the lotus feet of the Lord and greeted Him with various presentations as if they were friends.

verses.devanagari: প্রভু দেখি’ বৃন্দাবনের স্থাবর-জঙ্গম ।\\nআনন্দিত — বন্ধু যেন দেখে বন্ধুগণ ॥২০২॥
verses.transliteration: prabhu dekhi' vṛndāvanera sthāvara-jaṅgama\\nānandita—bandhu yena dekhe bandhu-gaṇa
verses.translation: Thus all the moving and nonmoving living entities of Vṛndāvana became very jubilant to see the Lord. It was as if friends were made happy by seeing another friend.

verses.devanagari: তা-সবার প্রীতি দেখি’ প্রভু ভাবাবেশে ।\\nসবা-সনে ক্রীড়া করে হঞা তার বশে ॥২০৩॥
verses.transliteration: tā-sabāra prīti dekhi' prabhu bhāvāveśe\\nsabā-sane krīḍā kare hañā tāra vaśe
verses.translation: Seeing their affection, the Lord was moved by ecstatic love. He began to sport with them exactly as a friend sports with another friend. Thus He voluntarily came under the control of His friends.

verses.devanagari: প্রতি বৃক্ষ-লতা প্রভু করেন আলিঙ্গন ।\\nপুষ্পাদি ধ্যানে করেন কৃষ্ণে সমর্পণ ॥২০৪॥
verses.transliteration: prati vṛkṣa-latā prabhu karena āliṅgana\\npuṣpādi dhyāne karena kṛṣṇe samarpaṇa
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu began to embrace each and every tree and creeper, and they began to offer their fruits and flowers as if in meditation.

verses.devanagari: অশ্রু-কম্প-পুলক-প্রেমে শরীর অস্থিরে ।\\n‘কৃষ্ণ’ বল, ‘কৃষ্ণ’ বল — বলে উচ্চৈঃস্বরে ॥২০৫॥
verses.transliteration: aśru-kampa-pulaka-preme śarīra asthire\\n'kṛṣṇa' bala, 'kṛṣṇa' bala—bale uccaiḥsvare
verses.translation: The Lord's body was restless, and tears, trembling and jubilation were manifest. He said very loudly, "Chant Kṛṣṇa! Chant Kṛṣṇa!"

verses.devanagari: স্থাবর-জঙ্গম মিলি’ করে কৃষ্ণধ্বনি । \\nপ্রভুর গম্ভীর-স্বরে যেন প্রতিধ্বনি ॥২০৬॥
verses.transliteration: sthāvara-jaṅgama mili' kare kṛṣṇa-dhvani\\nprabhura gambhīra-svare yena prati-dhvani
verses.translation: All moving and nonmoving creatures then began to vibrate the transcendental sound of Hare Kṛṣṇa, as if they were echoing the deep sound of Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

verses.devanagari: মৃগের গলা ধরি’ প্রভু করেন রোদনে ।\\nমৃগের পুলক অঙ্গে, অশ্রু নয়নে ॥২০৭॥
verses.transliteration: mṛgera galā dhari' prabhu karena rodane\\nmṛgera pulaka aṅge, aśru nayane
verses.translation: The Lord then clasped the necks of the deer and began to cry. There was jubilation manifest in the bodies of the deer, and tears were in their eyes.

verses.devanagari: বৃক্ষডালে শুক-শারী দিল দরশন ।\\nতাহা দেখি’ প্রভুর কিছু শুনিতে হৈল মন ॥২০৮॥
verses.transliteration: vṛkṣa-ḍāle śuka-śārī dila daraśana\\ntāhā dekhi' prabhura kichu śunite haila mana
verses.translation: When a male and female parrot appeared on the branches of a tree, the Lord saw them and wanted to hear them speak.

verses.devanagari: শুক-শারিকা প্রভুর হাতে উড়ি’ পড়ে ।\\nপ্রভুকে শুনাঞা কৃষ্ণের গুণ-শ্লোক পড়ে ॥২০৯॥
verses.transliteration: śuka-śārikā prabhura hāte uḍi' paḍe\\nprabhuke śunāñā kṛṣṇera guṇa-śloka paḍe
verses.translation: Both parrots flew onto the hand of the Lord and began to chant the transcendental qualities of Kṛṣṇa, and the Lord listened to them.

verses.devanagari: সৌন্দর্যং ললনালিধৈর্যদলনং লীলা রমাস্তম্ভিনী ।\\nবীর্যং কন্দুকিতাদ্রিবর্যমমলাঃ পারে-পরার্ধং গুণাঃ ।\\nশীলং সর্বজনানুরঞ্জনমহো যস্যায়মস্মৎপ্রভু-\\nর্বিশ্বং বিশ্বজনীনকীর্তিরবতাৎ কৃষ্ণো জগন্মোহনঃ ॥২১০॥
verses.transliteration: saundaryaṁ lalanāli-dhairya-dalanaṁ līlā ramā-stambhinī\\nvīryaṁ kandukitādri-varyam amalāḥ pāre-parārdhaṁ guṇāḥ\\nśīlaṁ sarva-janānurañjanam aho yasyāyam asmat-prabhur\\nviśvaṁ viśva-janīna-kīrtir avatāt kṛṣṇo jagan-mohanaḥ
verses.translation: The male parrot sang: "The glorification of Lord Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, is beneficial to everyone in the universe. His beauty is victorious over the gopīs of Vṛndāvana, and it subdues their patience. His pastimes astound the goddess of fortune, and His bodily strength turns Govardhana Hill into a small toy like a ball. His spotless qualities are unlimited, and His behavior satisfies everyone. Lord Kṛṣṇa is attractive to everyone. Oh, may our Lord maintain the whole universe!"
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This verse is found in the
Govinda-līlāmṛta
(13.29).

verses.devanagari: শুক-মুখে শুনি’ তবে কৃষ্ণের বর্ণন ।\\nশারিকা পড়য়ে তবে রাধিকা-বর্ণন ॥২১১॥
verses.transliteration: śuka-mukhe śuni' tabe kṛṣṇera varṇana\\nśārikā paḍaye tabe rādhikā-varṇana
verses.translation: After hearing this description of Lord Kṛṣṇa from the male parrot, the female parrot began to recite a description of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī.

verses.devanagari: শ্রীরাধিকায়াঃ প্রিয়তা সুরূপতা\\nসুশীলতা নর্তনগানচাতুরী ।\\nগুণালিসম্পৎ কবিতা চ রাজতে\\nজগন্মনোমোহন-চিত্তমোহিনী ॥২১২॥
verses.transliteration: śrī-rādhikāyāḥ priyatā surūpatā\\nsuśīlatā nartana-gāna-cāturī\\nguṇāli-sampat kavitā ca rājate\\njagan-mano-mohana-citta-mohinī
verses.translation: The female parrot said: "Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī's affection, Her exquisite beauty and good behavior, Her artistic dancing and chanting and Her poetic compositions are all so attractive that they attract the mind of Kṛṣṇa, who attracts the mind of everyone in the universe."
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This verse is found in the
Govinda-līlāmṛta
(13.30).

verses.devanagari: পুনঃ শুক কহে, — কৃষ্ণ ‘মদনমোহন’ ।\\nতবে আর শ্লোক শুক করিল পঠন ॥২১৩॥
verses.transliteration: punaḥ śuka kahe,—kṛṣṇa 'madana-mohana'\\ntabe āra śloka śuka karila paṭhana
verses.translation: Thereafter the male parrot said, "Kṛṣṇa is the enchanter of the mind of Cupid." He then began to recite another verse.

verses.devanagari: বংশীধারী জগন্নারী-চিত্তহারী স শারিকে ।\\nবিহারী গোপনারীভির্জীয়ান্মদনমোহনঃ ॥২১৪॥
verses.transliteration: vamśī-dhārī jagan-nāri-\\ncitta-hārī sa śārike\\nvihārī gopa-nārībhir\\njīyān madana-mohanaḥ
verses.translation: The parrot then said, "My dear śārī [female parrot], Śrī Kṛṣṇa carries a flute and enchants the hearts of all women throughout the universe. He is specifically the enjoyer of beautiful gopīs, and He is the enchanter of Cupid also. Let Him be glorified!"
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This verse is also found in the
Govinda-līlāmṛta
(13.31).

verses.devanagari: পুনঃ শারী কহে শুকে করি’ পরিহাস ।\\nতাহা শুনি’ প্রভুর হৈল বিস্ময়-প্রেমোল্লাস ॥২১৫॥
verses.transliteration: punaḥ śārī kahe śuke kari' parihāsa\\ntāhā śuni' prabhura haila vismaya-premollāsa
verses.translation: Then the female parrot began to speak jokingly to śuka, and Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was struck with wonderful ecstatic love to hear her speak.

verses.devanagari: রাধা-সঙ্গে যদা ভাতি তদা ‘মদনমোহনঃ’ ।\\nঅন্যথা বিশ্বমোহোঽপি স্বয়ং ‘মদনমোহিতঃ’ ॥২১৬॥
verses.transliteration: rādhā-saṅge yadā bhāti\\ntadā 'madana-mohanaḥ'\\nanyathā viśva-moho 'pi\\nsvayaṁ 'madana-mohitaḥ'
verses.translation: The parrot śārī said, "When Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa is with Rādhārāṇī, He is the enchanter of Cupid; otherwise, when He is alone, He Himself is enchanted by erotic feelings even though He enchants the whole universe."
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is another verse from the
Govinda-līlāmṛta
(13.32).

verses.devanagari: শুক-শারী উড়ি’ পুনঃ গেল বৃক্ষডালে ।\\nময়ূরের নৃত্য প্রভু দেখে কুতূহলে ॥২১৭॥
verses.transliteration: śuka-śārī uḍi' punaḥ gela vṛkṣa-ḍāle\\nmayūrera nṛtya prabhu dekhe kutūhale
verses.translation: Both parrots then flew onto a tree branch, and Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu began to watch the dancing of peacocks with curiosity.

verses.devanagari: ময়ূরের কণ্ঠ দেখি’ প্রভুর কৃষ্ণস্মৃতি হৈল ।\\nপ্রেমাবেশে মহাপ্ৰভু ভূমিতে পড়িল ॥২১৮॥
verses.transliteration: mayūrera kaṇṭha dekhi' prabhura kṛṣṇa-smṛti haila\\npremāveśe mahāprabhu bhūmite paḍila
verses.translation: When the Lord saw the bluish necks of the peacocks, His remembrance of Kṛṣṇa immediately awakened, and He fell to the ground in ecstatic love.

verses.devanagari: প্রভুরে মূর্ছিত দেখি’ সেই ত ব্রাহ্মণ ।\\nভট্টাচার্য-সঙ্গে করে প্রভুর সন্তর্পণ ॥২১৯॥
verses.transliteration: prabhure mūrcchita dekhi' sei ta brāhmaṇa\\nbhaṭṭācārya-saṅge kare prabhura santarpaṇa
verses.translation: When the brāhmaṇa saw that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was unconscious, he and Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya took care of Him.

verses.devanagari: আস্তে-ব্যস্তে মহাপ্রভুর লঞা বহিৰ্বাস ।\\nজলসেক করে অঙ্গে, বস্ত্রের বাতাস ॥২২০॥
verses.transliteration: āste-vyaste mahāprabhura lañā bahirvāsa\\njala-seka kare aṅge, vastrera vātāsa
verses.translation: They hastily sprinkled water over the Lord's body. Then they took up His cloth and began to fan Him with it.

verses.devanagari: প্রভু-কর্ণে কৃষ্ণনাম কহে উচ্চ করি’ ।\\nচেতন পাঞা প্রভু যা’ন গড়াগড়ি ॥২২১॥
verses.transliteration: prabhu-karṇe kṛṣṇa-nāma kahe ucca kari'\\ncetana pāñā prabhu yā'na gaḍāgaḍi
verses.translation: They then began to chant the holy name of Kṛṣṇa into the Lord's ear. When the Lord regained consciousness, He began rolling on the ground.

verses.devanagari: কণ্টক-দুর্গম বনে অঙ্গ ক্ষত হৈল ।\\nভট্টাচার্য কোলে করি’ প্রভুরে সুস্থ কৈল ॥২২২॥
verses.transliteration: kaṇṭaka-durgama vane aṅga kṣata haila\\nbhaṭṭācārya kole kari' prabhure sustha kaila
verses.translation: When the Lord rolled on the ground, sharp thorns injured His body. Taking Him on his lap, Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya pacified Him.

verses.devanagari: কৃষ্ণাবেশে প্ৰভুর প্রেমে গরগর মন ।\\n‘বোল্’ ‘বোল্’ করি’ উঠি’ করেন নর্তন ॥২২৩॥
verses.transliteration: kṛṣṇāveśe prabhura preme garagara mana\\n'bol' 'bol' kari' uṭhi' karena nartana
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's mind wandered in ecstatic love of Kṛṣṇa. He immediately stood up and said, "Chant! Chant!" Then He Himself began to dance.

verses.devanagari: ভট্টাচার্য, সেই বিপ্র ‘কৃষ্ণনাম’ গায় ।\\nনাচিতে নাচিতে পথে প্রভু চলি’ যায় ॥২২৪॥
verses.transliteration: bhaṭṭācārya, sei vipra 'kṛṣṇa-nāma' gāya\\nnācite nācite pathe prabhu cali' yāya
verses.translation: Being thus ordered by the Lord, both Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya and the brāhmaṇa began to chant the holy name of Kṛṣṇa. Then the Lord, dancing and dancing, proceeded along the path.

verses.devanagari: প্ৰভুর প্রেমাবেশ দেখি’ ব্রাহ্মণ — বিস্মিত ।\\nপ্রভুর রক্ষা লাগি’ বিপ্র হইলা চিন্তিত ॥২২৫॥
verses.transliteration: prabhura premāveśa dekhi' brāhmaṇa—vismita\\nprabhura rakṣā lāgi' vipra ha-ilā cintita
verses.translation: The brāhmaṇa was astounded to see the symptoms of ecstatic love exhibited by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. He then became anxious to give the Lord protection.

verses.devanagari: নীলাচলে ছিলা যৈছে প্রেমাবেশ মন ।\\nবৃন্দাবন যাইতে পথে হৈল শত-গুণ ॥২২৬॥
verses.transliteration: nīlācale chilā yaiche premāveśa mana\\nvṛndāvana yāite pathe haila śata-guṇa
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's mind was absorbed in ecstatic love at Jagannātha Purī, but when He passed along the road on the way to Vṛndāvana, that love increased a hundred times.

verses.devanagari: সহস্রগুণ প্রেম বাড়ে মথুরা দরশনে ।\\nলক্ষগুণ প্রেম বাড়ে, ভ্রমেন যবে বনে ॥২২৭॥
verses.transliteration: sahasra-guṇa prema bāḍe mathurā daraśane\\nlakṣa-guṇa prema bāḍe, bhramena yabe vane
verses.translation: The Lord's ecstatic love increased a thousand times when He visited Mathurā, but it increased a hundred thousand times when He wandered in the forests of Vṛndāvana.

verses.devanagari: অন্য-দেশ প্রেম উছলে ‘বৃন্দাবন’ নামে ।\\nসাক্ষাৎ ভ্রময়ে এবে সেই বৃন্দাবনে ॥২২৮॥\\nপ্রেমে গরগর মন রাত্রি-দিবসে ।\\nস্নান-ভিক্ষাদি-নির্বাহ করেন অভ্যাসে ॥২২৯॥
verses.transliteration: preme garagara mana rātri-divase\\nsnāna-bhikṣādi-nirvāha karena abhyāse
verses.translation: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was elsewhere, the very name of Vṛndāvana was sufficient to increase His ecstatic love. Now, when He was actually traveling in the Vṛndāvana forest, His mind was absorbed in great ecstatic love day and night. He ate and bathed simply out of habit.

verses.devanagari: এইমত প্রেম — যাবৎ ভ্রমিল ‘বার’ বন ।\\nএকত্র লিখিলুঁ, সর্বত্র না যায় বর্ণন ॥২৩০॥
verses.transliteration: ei-mata prema—yāvat bhramila 'bāra' vana\\nekatra likhiluṅ, sarvatra nā yāya varṇana
verses.translation: Thus I have written a description of the ecstatic love Lord Caitanya manifested while He walked through the twelve forests of Vṛndāvana. To describe it all would be impossible.

verses.devanagari: বৃন্দাবনে হৈল প্রভুর যতেক প্রেমের বিকার ।\\nকোটি-গ্রন্থে ‘অনন্ত’ লিখেন তাহার বিস্তার ॥২৩১॥
verses.transliteration: vṛndāvane haila prabhura yateka premera vikāra\\nkoṭi-granthe 'ananta' likhena tāhāra vistāra
verses.translation: Lord Ananta writes millions of books elaborately describing the transformations of ecstatic love experienced by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu in Vṛndāvana.

verses.devanagari: তবু লিখিবারে নারে তার এক কণ ।\\nউদ্দেশ করিতে করি দিগ্দরশন ॥২৩২॥
verses.transliteration: tabu likhibāre nāre tāra eka kaṇa\\nuddeśa karite kari dig-daraśana
verses.translation: Since Lord Ananta Himself cannot describe even a fragment of these pastimes, I am simply pointing out the direction.

verses.devanagari: জগৎ ভাসিল চৈতন্যলীলার পাথারে ।\\nযাঁর যত শক্তি তত পাথারে সাঁতারে ॥২৩৩॥
verses.transliteration: jagat bhāsila caitanya-līlāra pāthāre\\nyāṅra yata śakti tata pāthāre sāṅtāre
verses.translation: The whole world became merged in the inundation of the pastimes of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. One can swim in that water to the extent that he has the strength.

verses.devanagari: শ্রীরূপ-রঘুনাথ-পদে যার আশ ।\\nচৈতন্যচরিতামৃত কহে কৃষ্ণদাস ॥২৩৪॥
verses.transliteration: śrī-rūpa-raghunātha-pade yāra āśa\\ncaitanya-caritāmṛta kahe kṛṣṇadāsa
verses.translation: Praying at the lotus feet of Śrī Rūpa and Śrī Raghunātha, always desiring their mercy, I, Kṛṣṇadāsa, narrate Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, following in their footsteps.
verses.purport: PURPORT\nThus end the Bhaktivedanta purports to Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā,  Seventeenth Chapter, describing the Lord's traveling to Vṛndāvana.

sections.title: Chapter 18: Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's Visit to Śrī Vṛndāvana

verses.devanagari: বৃন্দাবনে স্থিরচরান্নন্দয়ন্ স্বাবলোকনৈঃ ।\\nআত্মানঞ্চ তদালোকাদ্গৌরাঙ্গঃ পরিতোঽভ্রমৎ ॥১॥
verses.transliteration: vṛndāvane sthira-carān\\nnandayan svāvalokanaiḥ\\nātmānaṁ ca tad-ālokād\\ngaurāṅgaḥ parito 'bhramat
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu traveled all over Vṛndāvana and pleased all living entities, moving and nonmoving, with His glances. The Lord took much personal pleasure in seeing everyone. In this way Lord Gaurāṅga traveled in Vṛndāvana.

verses.devanagari: জয় জয় গৌরচন্দ্র জয় নিত্যানন্দ ।\\nজয়াদ্বৈতচন্দ্র জয় গৌরভক্তবৃন্দ ॥২॥
verses.transliteration: jaya jaya gauracandra jaya nityānanda\\njayādvaita-candra jaya gaura-bhakta-vṛnda
verses.translation: All glories to Lord Gauracandra! All glories to Nityānanda Prabhu! All glories to Advaita Prabhu! And all glories to the devotees of Lord Caitanya headed by Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura!

verses.devanagari: এইমত মহাপ্রভু নাচিতে নাচিতে ।\\n‘আরিট্’-গ্রামে আসি’ ‘বাহ্য’ হৈল আচম্বিতে ॥৩॥
verses.transliteration: ei-mata mahāprabhu nācite nācite\\n'āriṭ'-grāme āsi' 'bāhya' haila ācambite
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu danced in ecstasy, but when He arrived at Āriṭgrāma, His sense perception was awakened.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
Āriṭ-grāma is also called Ariṣṭa-grāma. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu understood that in that village, Ariṣṭāsura was killed by Śrī Kṛṣṇa. While there, He inquired about Rādhā-kuṇḍa, but no one could tell Him where it was. The
brāhmaṇa
accompanying Him could also not ascertain its whereabouts. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu could then understand that the holy places known as Rādhā-kuṇḍa and Śyāma-kuṇḍa were at that time lost to everyone's vision. He therefore discovered Rādhā-kuṇḍa and Śyāma-kuṇḍa, which were two reservoirs of water in two paddy fields. Although there was very little water, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was omniscient and could understand that formerly these two ponds were called Śrī Rādhā-kuṇḍa and Śyāma-kuṇḍa. In this way Rādhā-kuṇḍa and Śyāma-kuṇḍa were discovered.

verses.devanagari: আরিটে রাধাকুণ্ড-বার্তা পুছে লোক-স্থানে ।\\nকেহ নাহি কহে, সঙ্গের ব্রাহ্মণ না জানে ॥৪॥
verses.transliteration: āriṭe rādhā-kuṇḍa-vārtā puche loka-sthāne\\nkeha nāhi kahe, saṅgera brāhmaṇa nā jāne
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu asked the local people, "Where is Rādhā-kunda?" No one could inform Him, and the brāhmaṇa accompanying Him did not know either.

verses.devanagari: তীর্থ ‘লুপ্ত’ জানি’ প্রভু সর্বজ্ঞ ভগবান্ ।\\nদুই ধান্যক্ষেত্রে অল্পজলে কৈলা স্নান ॥৫॥
verses.transliteration: tīrtha 'lupta' jāni' prabhu sarvajña bhagavān\\ndui dhānya-kṣetre alpa-jale kailā snāna
verses.translation: The Lord then understood that the holy place called Rādhā-kuṇḍa was no longer visible. However, being the omniscient Supreme Personality of Godhead, He discovered Rādhā-kuṇḍa and Śyāma-kuṇḍa in two paddy fields. There was only a little water, but He took His bath there.

verses.devanagari: দেখি’ সব গ্রাম্য-লোকের বিস্ময় হৈল মন ।\\nপ্রেমে প্রভু করে রাধাকুণ্ডের স্তবন ॥৬॥
verses.transliteration: dekhi' saba grāmya-lokera vismaya haila mana\\npreme prabhu kare rādhā-kuṇḍera stavana
verses.translation: When the people of the village saw Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu taking His bath in those two ponds in the middle of the paddy fields, they were very astonished. The Lord then offered His prayers to Śrī Rādhā-kuṇḍa.

verses.devanagari: সব গোপী হৈতে রাধা কৃষ্ণের প্রেয়সী ।\\nতৈছে রাধাকুণ্ড প্রিয় ‘প্রিয়ার সরসী’ ॥৭॥
verses.transliteration: saba gopī haite rādhā kṛṣṇera preyasī\\ntaiche rādhā-kuṇḍa priya 'priyāra sarasi'
verses.translation: "Of all the gopīs, Rādhārāṇī is the dearmost. Similarly, the lake known as Rādhā-kuṇḍa is very dear to the Lord because it is very dear to Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī.

verses.devanagari: যথা রাধা প্রিয়া বিষ্ণোস্তস্যাঃ কুণ্ডং প্রিয়ং তথা ।\\nসর্বগোপীষু সৈবৈকা বিষ্ণোরত্যন্তবল্লভা ॥৮॥
verses.transliteration: yathā rādhā priyā viṣṇos\\ntasyāḥ kuṇḍaṁ priyaṁ tathā\\nsarva-gopīṣu saivaikā\\nviṣṇor atyanta-vallabhā
verses.translation: “ 'Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī is most dear to Lord Kṛṣṇa, and Her lake known as Rādhā-kuṇḍa is also very dear to Him. Of all the gopīs, Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī is certainly the most beloved.'
verses.purport: PURPORT\nThis is a verse from the\nPadma Purāṇa.

verses.devanagari: যেই কুণ্ডে নিত্য কৃষ্ণ রাধিকার সঙ্গে ।\\nজলে জলকেলি করে, তীরে রাস-রঙ্গে ॥৯॥
verses.transliteration: yei kuṇḍe nitya kṛṣṇa rādhikāra saṅge\\njale jala-keli kare, tīre rāsa-raṅge
verses.translation: "In that lake, Lord Kṛṣṇa and Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī used to sport daily in the water and have a rāsa dance on the bank.

verses.devanagari: সেই কুণ্ডে যেই একবার করে স্নান ।\\nতাঁরে রাধা-সম ‘প্রেম’ কৃষ্ণ করে দান ॥১০॥
verses.transliteration: sei kuṇḍe yei eka-bāra kare snāna\\ntāṅre rādhā-sama 'prema' kṛṣṇa kare dāna
verses.translation: "Indeed, Lord Kṛṣṇa gives ecstatic love like that of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī to whoever bathes in that lake even once in his life.

verses.devanagari: কুণ্ডের ‘মাধুরী’ — যেন রাধার ‘মধুরিমা’ ।\\nকুণ্ডের ‘মহিমা’ — যেন রাধার ‘মহিমা’ ॥১১॥
verses.transliteration: kuṇḍera 'mādhurī'—yena rādhāra 'madhurimā'\\nkuṇḍera 'mahimā'—yena rādhāra 'mahimā'
verses.translation: "The attraction of Rādhā-kuṇḍa is as sweet as that of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī. Similarly, the glories of the kuṇḍa [lake] are as glorious as Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī.

verses.devanagari: শ্রীরাধেব হরেস্তদীয়সরসী প্রেষ্ঠাদ্ভুতৈঃ স্বৈর্গুণৈ-\\nর্যস্যাং শ্রীযুত-মাধববেন্দুরনিশং প্রীত্যা তয়া ক্রীড়তি ।\\nপ্রেমাস্মিন্ বত রাধিকেব লভতে যস্যাং সকৃৎ স্নানকৃৎ\\nতস্যা বৈ মহিমা তথা মধুরিমা কেনাস্তু বর্ণ্যঃ ক্ষিতৌ ॥১২॥
verses.transliteration: śrī-rādheva hares tadīya-sarasī preṣṭhādbhutaiḥ svair guṇair\\nyasyāṁ śrī-yuta-mādhavendur aniśaṁ prītyā tayā krīḍati\\npremāsmin bata rādhikeva labhate yasyāṁ sakṛt snāna-kṛt\\ntasyā vai mahimā tathā madhurimā kenāstu varṇyaḥ kṣitau
verses.translation: “ 'Because of its wonderful transcendental qualities, Rādhā-kuṇḍa is as dear to Kṛṣṇa as Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī. It was in that lake that the all-opulent Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa performed His pastimes with Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī with great pleasure and transcendental bliss. Whoever bathes just once in Rādhā-kuṇḍa attains Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī's loving attraction for Śrī Kṛṣṇa. Who within this world can describe the glories and sweetness of Śrī Rādhā-kuṇḍa?' "
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This verse is found in the
Govinda-līlāmṛta
(7.102).

verses.devanagari: এইমত স্তুতি করে প্রেমাবিষ্ট হঞা ।\\nতীরে নৃত্য করে কুণ্ডলীলা সঙরিয়া ॥১৩॥
verses.transliteration: ei-mata stuti kare premāviṣṭa hañā\\ntīre nṛtya kare kuṇḍa-līlā saṅariyā
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu thus offered prayers to Rādhā-kuṇḍa. Overwhelmed by ecstatic love, He danced on the bank, remembering the pastimes Lord Kṛṣṇa performed on the bank of Rādhā-kuṇḍa.

verses.devanagari: কুণ্ডের মৃত্তিকা লঞা তিলক করিল ।\\nভট্টাচার্য-দ্বারা মৃত্তিকা সঙ্গে করি’ লৈল ॥১৪॥
verses.transliteration: kuṇḍera mṛttikā lañā tilaka karila\\nbhaṭṭācārya-dvārā mṛttikā saṅge kari' laila
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then marked His body with tilaka made from the mud of Rādhā-kuṇḍa, and with the help of Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya, He collected some of the mud and took it with Him.

verses.devanagari: তবে চলি’ আইলা প্রভু ‘সুমনঃ-সরোবর’ ।\\nতাহাঁ ‘গোবর্ধন’ দেখি’ হইলা বিহ্বল ॥১৫॥
verses.transliteration: tabe cali' āilā prabhu 'sumanaḥ-sarovara'\\ntāhāṅ 'govardhana' dekhi' ha-ilā vihvala
verses.translation: From Rādhā-kuṇḍa, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu went to Sumanaḥ Lake. When He saw Govardhana Hill from there, He was overwhelmed by joy.

verses.devanagari: গোবর্ধন দেখি’ প্রভু হইলা দণ্ডবৎ ।\\n‘এক শিলা’ আলিঙ্গিয়া হইলা উন্মত্ত ॥১৬॥
verses.transliteration: govardhana dekhi' prabhu ha-ilā daṇḍavat\\n'eka śilā' āliṅgiyā ha-ilā unmatta
verses.translation: When the Lord saw Govardhana Hill, He immediately offered obeisances, falling down on the ground like a rod. He embraced one piece of rock from Govardhana Hill and became mad.

verses.devanagari: প্রেমে মত্ত চলি’ আইলা গোবর্ধন-গ্রাম ।\\n‘হরিদেব’ দেখি’ তাহাঁ হইলা প্রণাম ॥১৭॥
verses.transliteration: preme matta cali' āilā govardhana-grāma\\n'harideva' dekhi' tāhāṅ ha-ilā praṇāma
verses.translation: Mad with ecstatic love, the Lord came to the village known as Govardhana. It was there that He saw the Deity Harideva and offered His obeisances unto Him.

verses.devanagari: ‘মথুরা’-পদ্মের পশ্চিমদলে যাঁর বাস ।\\n‘হরিদেব’ নারায়ণ — আদি পরকাশ ॥১৮॥
verses.transliteration: 'mathurā'-padmera paścima-dale yāṅra vāsa\\n'harideva' nārāyaṇa—ādi parakāśa
verses.translation: Harideva is an incarnation of Nārāyaṇa, and His residence is on the western petal of the lotus of Mathurā.

verses.devanagari: হরিদেব-আগে নাচে প্রেমে মত্ত হঞা ।\\nসব লোক দেখিতে আইল আশ্চর্য শুনিয়া ॥১৯॥
verses.transliteration: harideva-āge nāce preme matta hañā\\nsaba loka dekhite āila āścarya śuniyā
verses.translation: Mad with ecstatic love, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu began to dance before the Harideva Deity. Hearing of the Lord's wonderful activities, all the people came to see Him.

verses.devanagari: প্রভু-প্রেম-সৌন্দর্য দেখি’ লোকে চমৎকার ।\\nহরিদেবের ভৃত্য প্ৰভুর করিল সত্কার ॥২০॥
verses.transliteration: prabhu-prema-saundarya dekhi' loke camatkāra\\nharidevera bhṛtya prabhura karila satkāra
verses.translation: The people were astonished when they saw Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's ecstatic love and personal beauty. The priests who served the Harideva Deity offered the Lord a good reception.

verses.devanagari: ভট্টাচার্য ‘ব্রহ্মকুণ্ডে’ পাক যাঞা কৈল ।\\nব্রহ্মকুণ্ডে স্নান করি’ প্রভু ভিক্ষা কৈল ॥২১॥
verses.transliteration: bhaṭṭācārya 'brahma-kuṇḍe' pāka yāñā kaila\\nbrahma-kuṇḍe snāna kari' prabhu bhikṣā kaila
verses.translation: At Brahma-kuṇḍa, Bhaṭṭācārya cooked food, and the Lord, after taking His bath at Brahma-kuṇḍa, accepted His lunch.

verses.devanagari: সে-রাত্রি রহিলা হরিদেবের মন্দিরে  ।\\nরাত্রে মহাপ্রভু করে মনেতে বিচারে ॥২২॥
verses.transliteration: se-rātri rahilā haridevera maṇḍire\\nrātre mahāprabhu kare manete vicāre
verses.translation: That night the Lord stayed at the temple of Harideva, and during the night He began to reflect.

verses.devanagari: ‘গোবর্ধন-উপরে আমি কভু না চড়িব  ।\\nগোপাল-রায়ের দরশন কেমনে পাইব ?’ ২৩ ॥২৩॥
verses.transliteration: 'govardhana-upare āmi kabhu nā caḍiba\\ngopāla-rāyera daraśana kemane pāiba?'
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu thought, "Since I shall not at any time climb Govardhana Hill, how shall I be able to see Gopāla Rāya?"

verses.devanagari: এত মনে করি’ প্রভু মৌন করি’ রহিলা ।\\nজানিয়া গোপাল কিছু ভঙ্গী উঠাইলা ॥২৪॥
verses.transliteration: eta mane kari' prabhu mauna kari' rahilā\\njāniyā gopāla kichu bhaṅgī uṭhāilā
verses.translation: Thinking in this way, the Lord remained silent, and Lord Gopāla, knowing His contemplation, played a trick.

verses.devanagari: অনারুরুক্ষবে শৈলং স্বস্মৈ ভক্তাভিমানিনে ।\\nঅবরুহ্য গিরেঃ কৃষ্ণো গৌরায় স্বমদর্শয়ৎ ॥২৫॥
verses.transliteration: anārurukṣave śailaṁ\\nsvasmai bhaktābhimānine\\navaruhya gireḥ kṛṣṇo\\ngaurāya svam adarśayat
verses.translation: Coming down from Govardhana Hill, Lord Gopāla granted an interview to Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, who was unwilling to climb the hill, thinking Himself a devotee of Lord Kṛṣṇa.

verses.devanagari: ‘অন্নকূট’-নামে গ্রামে গোপালের স্থিতি ।\\nরাজপুত-লোকের সেই গ্রামে বসতি ॥২৬॥
verses.transliteration: 'annakūṭa'-nāme grāme gopālera sthiti\\nrāja-puta-lokera sei grāme vasati
verses.translation: Gopāla stayed in a village called Annakūṭa-grāma on Govardhana Hill. The villagers who lived in that village were mainly from Rajasthan.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
The village named Annakūṭa-grāma is referred to in
Bhakti-ratnākara
(Fifth Wave):
gopa-gopī bhuñjāyena kautuka apāra
ei hetu 'āniyora' nāma se ihāra
annakūṭa-sthāna ei dekha śrīnivāsa
e-sthāna darśane haya pūrṇa abhilāṣa
"It is here that all the
gopīs
and the
gopas
enjoyed wonderful pastimes with Śrī Kṛṣṇa. Therefore this place is also called Āniyora. The Annakūṭa ceremony was celebrated here. O Śrīnivāsa, whoever sees this place has all his desires fulfilled." It is also stated:
kuṇḍera nikaṭa dekha niviḍa-kānana
ethāi 'gopāla' chilā hañā saṅgopana
"Look at the dense forest near the
kuṇḍa.
It was there that Gopāla was concealed." Also, the
Stavāvalī
(8.75) by Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī states:
vrajendra-varyārpita-bhogam uccair
dhṛtvā bṛhat-kāyam aghārir utkaḥ
vareṇa rādhāṁ chalayan vibhuṅkte
yatrānna-kūṭaṁ tad ahaṁ prapadye

verses.devanagari: একজন আসি’ রাত্রে গ্রামীকে বলিল ।\\n‘তোমার গ্রাম মারিতে তুরুক-ধারী সাজিল ॥২৭॥
verses.transliteration: eka-jana āsi' rātre grāmīke balila\\n'tomāra grāma mārite turuka-dhārī sājila
verses.translation: One person who came to the village informed the inhabitants, "The Turkish soldiers are now preparing to attack your village.

verses.devanagari: আজি রাত্র্যে পলাহ, না রহিহ একজন ।\\nঠাকুর লঞা ভাগ’, আসিবে কালি যবন ।।’ ॥ ২৮ ॥
verses.transliteration: āji rātrye palāha, nā rahiha eka-jana\\nṭhākura lañā bhāga', āsibe kāli yavana'
verses.translation: "Flee this village tonight, and do not allow one person to remain. Take the Deity with you and leave, for the Mohammedan soldiers will come tomorrow."

verses.devanagari: শুনিয়া গ্রামের লোক চিন্তিত হইল ।\\nপ্রথমে গোপাল লঞা গাঁঠুলি-গ্রামে খুইল ॥২৯॥
verses.transliteration: śuniyā grāmera loka cintita ha-ila\\nprathame gopāla lañā gāṅṭhuli-grāme khuila
verses.translation: Hearing this, all the villagers became very anxious. They first took Gopāla and moved Him to a village known as Gāṅṭhuli.

verses.devanagari: বিপ্রগৃহে গোপালের নিভৃতে সেবন ।\\nগ্রাম উজাড় হৈল, পলাইল সর্বজন ॥৩০॥
verses.transliteration: vipra-gṛhe gopālera nibhṛte sevana\\ngrāma ujāḍa haila, palāila sarva-jana
verses.translation: The Gopāla Deity was kept in the house of a brāhmaṇa, and His worship was conducted secretly. Everyone fled, and thus the village of Annakūṭa was deserted.

verses.devanagari: ঐছে ম্লেচ্ছভয়ে গোপাল ভাগে বারে-বারে ।\\nমন্দির ছাড়ি’ কুঞ্জে রহে, কিবা গ্রামান্তরে ॥৩১॥
verses.transliteration: aiche mleccha-bhaye gopāla bhāge bāre-bāre\\nmandira chāḍi' kuñje rahe, kibā grāmāntare
verses.translation: Due to fear of the Mohammedans, the Gopāla Deity was moved from one place to another again and again. Thus giving up His temple, Lord Gopāla would sometimes live in a bush and sometimes in one village after another.

verses.devanagari: প্রাতঃকালে প্রভু ‘মানসগঙ্গা’য় করি’ স্নান ।\\nগোবর্ধন-পরিক্রমায় করিলা প্ৰয়াণ ॥৩২॥
verses.transliteration: prātaḥ-kāle prabhu 'mānasa-gaṅgā'ya kari' snāna\\ngovardhana-parikramāya karilā prayāṇa
verses.translation: In the morning, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu took His bath in a lake called Mānasa-gaṅgā. He then circumambulated Govardhana Hill.

verses.devanagari: গোবর্ধন দেখি’ প্রভু প্রেমাবিষ্ট হঞা ।\\nনাচিতে নাচিতে চলিলা শ্লোক পড়িয়া ॥৩৩॥
verses.transliteration: govardhana dekhi' prabhu premāviṣṭa hañā\\nnācite nācite calilā śloka paḍiyā
verses.translation: Just by seeing Govardhana Hill, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu became ecstatic with love of Kṛṣṇa. While dancing and dancing, He recited the following verse.

verses.devanagari: হন্তায়মদ্রিরবলা হরিদাসবর্যো\\nযদ্রামকৃষ্ণচরণস্পরশপ্রমোদঃ ।\\nমানং তনোতি সহ-গোগণয়োস্তয়োর্যৎ\\nপানীয়-সুযবস-কন্দর-কন্দমূলৈঃ ॥৩৪॥
verses.transliteration: hantāyam adrir abalā haridāsa-varyo\\nyad rāma-kṛṣṇa-caraṇa-sparaśa-pramodaḥ\\nmānaṁ tanoti saha-go-gaṇayos tayor yat\\npānīya-sūyavasa-kandara-kanda-mūlaiḥ
verses.translation: "Of all the devotees, this Govardhana Hill is the best! O My friends, this hill supplies Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma, as well as Their calves, cows and cowherd friends, with all kinds of necessities-water for drinking, very soft grass, caves, fruits, flowers and vegetables. In this way the hill offers respect to the Lord. Being touched by the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma, Govardhana Hill appears very jubilant. "
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a quotation from
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(10.21.18). It was spoken by the
gopīs
when Lord Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma entered the forest in the autumn. The
gopīs
spoke among themselves and glorified Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma for Their pastimes.

verses.devanagari: ‘গোবিন্দকুণ্ডাদি’ তীর্থে প্রভু কৈলা স্নান ।\\nতাহাঁ শুনিলা — গোপাল গেল গাঁঠুলি গ্রাম ॥৩৫॥
verses.transliteration: 'govinda-kuṇḍādi' tīrthe prabhu kailā snāna\\ntāhāṅ śunilā—gopāla gela gāṅṭhuli grāma
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then took His bath in a lake called Govinda-kuṇḍa, and while He was there, He heard that the Deity Gopāla had already gone to Gāṅṭhuli-grāma.

verses.devanagari: সেই গ্রামে গিয়া কৈল গোপাল-দরশন ।\\nপ্রেমাবেশে প্রভু করে কীর্তন-নর্তন ॥৩৬॥
verses.transliteration: sei grāme giyā kaila gopāla-daraśana\\npremāveśe prabhu kare kīrtana-nartana
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then went to the village of Gāṅṭhuli-grāma and saw the Lord Gopāla Deity. Overwhelmed by ecstatic love, He began to chant and dance.

verses.devanagari: গোপালের সৌন্দর্য দেখি’ প্রভুর আবেশ ।\\nএই শ্লোক পড়ি’ নাচে, হৈল দিন-শেষ ॥৩৭॥
verses.transliteration: gopālera saundarya dekhi' prabhura āveśa\\nei śloka paḍi' nāce, haila dina-śeṣa
verses.translation: As soon as the Lord saw the beauty of the Gopāla Deity, He was immediately overwhelmed by ecstatic love, and He recited the following verse. He then chanted and danced until the day ended.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura gives the following information about Govinda-kuṇḍa. There is a village named Āniyora on Govardhana Hill, a little distance from the village of Paiṭhā. Govinda-kuṇḍa is situated near here, and there are two temples to Govinda and Baladeva there. According to some, Queen Padmāvatī excavated this lake. In the
Bhakti-ratnākara
(Fifth Wave), the following statement is found:
ei śrī-govinda-kuṇḍa-mahimā aneka
ethā indra kaila govindera abhiṣeka
"Govinda-kuṇḍa is exalted for its many spiritual activities. It was here that Indra was defeated by Lord Kṛṣṇa, and Indra offered his prayers and bathed Lord Govinda." In the book
Stavāvalī
(
Vraja-vilāsa-stava
74) the following verse is found:
nīcaiḥ prauḍha-bhayāt svayaṁ surapatiḥ pādau vidhṛtyeha yaiḥ
svar-gaṅgā-salilaiś cakāra surabhi-dvārābhiṣekotsavam
govindasya navaṁ gavām adhipatā rājye sphuṭaṁ kautukāt
tair yat prādurabhūt sadā sphuratu tad govinda-kuṇḍaṁ dṛśoḥ
In the
Mathurā-khaṇḍa
it is also stated:
yatrābhiṣikto bhagavān
maghonā yadu-vairiṇā
govinda-kuṇḍaṁ taj-jātaṁ
snāna-mātreṇa mokṣadam
"Simply by bathing in Govinda-kuṇḍa, one is awarded liberation. This lake was produced when Bhagavān Śrī Kṛṣṇa was bathed by Lord Indra."
Gāṅṭhuli-grāma is situated near the two villages Bilachu and Gopāla-pura. According to hearsay, Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa first met here. In the
Bhakti-ratnākara
(Fifth Wave), it is stated:
sakhī duṅha vastre gāṅṭhi dila saṅgopane.
It is also stated:
phāguyā laiyā keha gāṅṭhi khuli' dilā.
For this reason the village is known as Gāṅṭhuli.

verses.devanagari: বামস্তামরসাক্ষস্য ভুজদণ্ডঃ স পাতু বঃ ।\\nক্রীড়াকন্দুকতাং যেন নীতো গোবর্ধনো গিরিঃ ॥৩৮॥
verses.transliteration: vāmas tāmarasākṣasya\\nbhuja-daṇḍaḥ sa pātu vaḥ\\nkrīḍā-kandukatāṁ yena\\nnīto govardhano giriḥ
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, " 'May the left arm of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, whose eyes are like the petals of a lotus flower, always protect you. With His left arm He raised Govardhana Hill as if it were a toy.' "
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This verse is found in
Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu
(2.1.62).

verses.devanagari: এইমত তিনদিন গোপালে দেখিলা ।\\nচতুর্থ-দিবসে গোপাল স্বমন্দিরে গেলা ॥৩৯॥
verses.transliteration: ei-mata tina-dina gopāle dekhilā\\ncaturtha-divase gopāla svamandire gelā
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu saw the Gopāla Deity for three days. On the fourth day, the Deity returned to His own temple.

verses.devanagari: গোপাল সঙ্গে চলি’ আইলা নৃত্য-গীত করি ।\\nআনন্দ-কোলাহলে লোক বলে ‘হরি’ ‘হরি’ ॥৪০॥
verses.transliteration: gopāla saṅge cali' āilā nṛtya-gīta kari\\nānanda-kolāhale loka bale 'hari' 'hari'
verses.translation: Caitanya Mahāprabhu walked with the Deity of Gopāla, and He chanted and danced. A large and jubilant crowd of people also chanted the transcendental name of Kṛṣṇa, "Hari! Hari!"

verses.devanagari: গোপাল মন্দিরে গেলা, প্রভু রহিলা তলে ।\\nপ্রভুর বাঞ্ছা পূর্ণ সব করিল গোপালে ॥৪১॥
verses.transliteration: gopāla mandire gelā, prabhu rahilā tale\\nprabhura vāñchā pūrṇa saba karila gopāle
verses.translation: The Deity Gopāla then returned to His own temple, and Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu remained at the bottom of the hill. Thus all the desires of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu were satisfied by the Deity Gopāla.

verses.devanagari: এইমত গোপালের করুণ স্বভাব ।\\nযেই ভক্ত জনের দেখিতে হয় ‘ভাব’ ॥৪২॥
verses.transliteration: ei-mata gopālera karuṇa svabhāva\\nyei bhakta janera dekhite haya 'bhāva'
verses.translation: This is the way of Lord Gopāla's kind behavior to His devotees. Seeing this, the devotees were overwhelmed by ecstatic love.

verses.devanagari: দেখিতে উৎকণ্ঠা হয়, না চড়ে গোবর্ধনে ।\\nকোন ছলে গোপাল আসি’ উতরে আপনে ॥৪৩॥
verses.transliteration: dekhite utkaṇṭhā haya, nā caḍe govardhane\\nkona chale gopāla āsi' utare āpane
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was very anxious to see Gopāla, but He did not want to climb Govardhana Hill. Therefore by some trick the Deity Gopāla personally descended.

verses.devanagari: কভু কুঞ্জে রহে, কভু রহে গ্রামান্তরে ।\\nসেই ভক্ত, তাহাঁ আসি’ দেখয়ে তাঁহারে ॥৪৪॥
verses.transliteration: kabhu kuñje rahe, kabhu rahe grāmāntare\\nsei bhakta, tāhāṅ āsi' dekhaye tāṅhāre
verses.translation: In this way, giving some excuse, Gopāla sometimes remains in the bushes of the forest, and sometimes He stays in a village. One who is a devotee comes to see the Deity.

verses.devanagari: পর্বতে না চড়ে দুই — রূপ-সনাতন ।\\nএইরূপে তাঁ-সবারে দিয়াছেন দরশন ॥৪৫॥
verses.transliteration: parvate nā caḍe dui—rūpa-sanātana\\nei-rūpe tāṅ-sabāre diyāchena daraśana
verses.translation: The two brothers Rūpa and Sanātana did not climb the hill. To them also Lord Gopāla granted an interview.

verses.devanagari: বৃদ্ধকালে রূপ-গোসাঞি না পারে যাইতে  ।\\nবাঞ্ছা হৈল গোপালের সৌন্দর্য দেখিতে ॥৪৬॥
verses.transliteration: vṛddha-kāle rūpa-gosāñi nā pāre yāite\\nvāñchā haila gopālera saundarya dekhite
verses.translation: In ripe old age, Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī could not go there, but he had a desire to see the beauty of Gopāla.

verses.devanagari: ম্লেচ্ছভয়ে আইলা গোপাল মথুরা-নগরে  ।\\nএকমাস রহিল বিঠ্ঠলেশ্বর-ঘরে ॥৪৭॥
verses.transliteration: mleccha-bhaye āilā gopāla mathurā-nagare\\neka-māsa rahila viṭhṭhaleśvara-ghare
verses.translation: Due to fear of the Mohammedans, Gopāla went to Mathurā, where He remained in the temple of Viṭhṭhaleśvara for one full month.
verses.purport: PURPORT\nWhen the two brothers Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī and Sanātana Gosvāmī went to Vṛndāvana, they decided to live there. Following Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's example, they did not climb the hill because they considered it nondifferent from Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead. On some pretext, the Gopāla Deity granted Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu an audience beneath the hill, and Gopāla similarly favored Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī and Sanātana Gosvāmī. During his ripe old age, when Rūpa Gosvāmī could not go to Govardhana Hill because of invalidity, Gopāla kindly went to Mathurā and remained at the temple of Viṭhṭhaleśvara for one month. It was then that Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī could see Gopāla's beauty to his heart's content.

verses.devanagari: তবে রূপ গোসাঞি সব নিজগণ লঞা ।\\nএকমাস দরশন কৈলা মথুরায় রহিয়া ॥৪৮॥
verses.transliteration: tabe rūpa gosāñi saba nija-gaṇa lañā\\neka-māsa daraśana kailā mathurāya rahiyā
verses.translation: Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī and his associates stayed in Mathurā for one month and saw the Deity Gopāla.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
The following description of the temple of Viṭhṭhaleśvara is given in
Bhakti-ratnākara
(Fifth Wave):
viṭhṭhalera sevā kṛṣṇa-caitanya-vigraha
tāhāra darśane haila parama āgraha
śrī-viṭhṭhalanātha—bhaṭṭa-vallabha-tanaya
karilā yateka prīti kahile nā haya
gāṭholi-grāme gopāla āilā 'chala' kari'
tāṅre dekhi' nṛtya-gīte magna gaurahari
śrī-dāsa-gosvāmī ādi parāmarśa kari'
śrī-viṭhṭhaleśvare kailā sevā-adhikārī
pitā śrī-vallabha-bhaṭṭa tāṅra adarśane
kata-dina mathurāya chilena nirjane
Śrī Vallabha Bhaṭṭa had two sons. The elder, Gopīnātha, was born in 1432 Śakābda Era, and the younger, Viṭhṭhalanātha, was born in 1437 and died in 1507. Viṭhṭhala had seven sons: Giridhara, Govinda, Bālakṛṣṇa, Gokuleśa, Raghunātha, Yadunātha and Ghanaśyāma. Viṭhṭhala completed many of his father's unfinished books, including his commentary on
Vedānta-sūtra,
the
Subodhinī
commentary on
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, Vidvan-maṇḍana, Śṛṅgāra-rasa-maṇḍana
and
Nyāsādeśa-vivaraṇa.
Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu went to Vṛndāvana before the birth of Viṭhṭhala. Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī was very old at the time Gopāla stayed at the house of Viṭhṭhalanātha.

verses.devanagari: সঙ্গে গোপাল-ভট্ট, দাস-রঘুনাথ ।\\nরঘুনাথ-ভট্টগোসাঞি, আর লোকনাথ ॥৪৯॥
verses.transliteration: saṅge gopāla-bhaṭṭa, dāsa-raghunātha\\nraghunātha-bhaṭṭa-gosāñi, āra lokanātha
verses.translation: When Rūpa Gosvāmī stayed at Mathurā, he was accompanied by Gopāla Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī, Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī, Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī and Lokanātha dāsa Gosvāmī.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
Śrī Lokanātha Gosvāmī was a personal associate of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and a great devotee of the Lord. He was a resident of a village named Tālakhaḍi in the district of Yaśohara in Bengal. Previously he lived in Kācnāpāḍā. His father's name was Padmanābha, and his only younger brother was Pragalbha. Following the orders of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, Śrī Lokanātha went to Vṛndāvana to live. He established a temple named Gokulānanda. Śrīla Narottama dāsa Ṭhākura selected Lokanātha dāsa Gosvāmī to be his spiritual master, and he was his only disciple. Because Lokanātha dāsa Gosvāmī did not want his name mentioned in
Caitanya-caritāmṛta,
we do not often see it in this celebrated book. On the E.B.R. Railroad, the Yaśohara station is located in Bangladesh. From the railway station one has to go by bus to the village of Sonākhāli and from there to Khejurā. From there one has to walk, or, during the rainy season, go by boat to the village of Tālakhaḍi. In this village there are still descendants of Lokanātha Gosvāmī's younger brother.

verses.devanagari: ভূগর্ভ-গোসাঞি, আর শ্রীজীব-গোসাঞি ।\\nশ্রীযাদব-আচার্য, আর গোবিন্দ গোসাঞি ॥৫০॥
verses.transliteration: bhūgarbha-gosāñi, āra śrī-jīva-gosāñi\\nśrī-yādava-ācārya, āra govinda gosāñi
verses.translation: Bhūgarbha Gosvāmī, Śrī Jīva Gosvāmī, Śrī Yādava Ācārya and Govinda Gosvāmī also accompanied Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī.

verses.devanagari: শ্রীউদ্ধব-দাস, আর মাধব — দুইজন ।\\nশ্রীগোপাল-দাস, আর দাস-নারায়ণ ॥৫১॥
verses.transliteration: śrī-uddhava-dāsa, āra mādhava—dui-jana\\nśrī-gopāla-dāsa, āra dāsa-nārāyaṇa
verses.translation: He was also accompanied by Śrī Uddhava dāsa, Mādhava, Śrī Gopāla dāsa and Nārāyaṇa dāsa.

verses.devanagari: ‘গোবিন্দ’ ভক্ত, আর বাণী-কৃষ্ণদাস ।\\nপুণ্ডরীকাক্ষ, ঈশান, আর লঘু-হরিদাস ॥৫২॥
verses.transliteration: 'govinda' bhakta, āra vāṇī-kṛṣṇadāsa\\npuṇḍarīkākṣa, īśāna, āra laghu-haridāsa
verses.translation: The great devotee Govinda, Vāṇī Kṛṣṇadāsa, Puṇḍarīkākṣa, Īśāna and Laghu Haridāsa also accompanied him.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
Laghu Haridāsa should not be confused with Junior Haridāsa, who committed suicide at Prayāga. Generally a devotee is called Haridāsa, and consequently there are many Haridāsas. The chief was Ṭhākura Haridāsa. There was also a Madhyama Haridāsa.
In
Bhakti-ratnākara
(Sixth Wave), there is a list of many of the chief devotees who accompanied Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī.
gosvāmī gopāla-bhaṭṭa ati dayāmaya
bhūgarbha, śrī-lokanātha—guṇera ālaya
śrī-mādhava, śrī-paramānanda-bhaṭṭācārya
śrī-madhu-paṇḍita—yāṅra caritra āścarya
premī kṛṣṇadāsa kṛṣṇadāsa brahmacārī
yādava ācārya, nārāyaṇa kṛpāvān
śrī-puṇḍarīkākṣa-gosāñi, govinda, īśāna
śrī-govinda vāṇī-kṛṣṇadāsa aty-udāra
śrī-uddhava—madhye-madhye gauḍe gati yāṅra
dvija-haridāsa kṛṣṇadāsa kavirāja
śrī-gopāla-dāsa yāṅra alaukika kāya
śrī-gopāla, mādhavādi yateka vaiṣṇava
"The following Vaiṣṇavas were present with Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī: the merciful Gopāla Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī; Bhūgarbha Gosvāmī; Śrī Lokanātha dāsa Gosvāmī, a reservoir of good qualities; Śrī Mādhava; Śrī Paramānanda Bhaṭṭācārya; Śrī Madhu Paṇḍita, whose characteristics are all wonderful; Premī Kṛṣṇadāsa; Kṛṣṇadāsa Brahmacārī; Yādava Ācārya; the merciful Nārāyaṇa; Śrī Puṇḍarīkākṣa Gosvāmī; Govinda; Īśāna; Śrī Govinda; the magnanimous Vāṇī Kṛṣṇadāsa; Śrī Uddhava, who occasionally visited Bengal; Dvija Haridāsa; Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja; Śrī Gopāla dāsa, whose body is completely spiritual; Śrī Gopāla; Mādhava; and many others."

verses.devanagari: এই সব মুখ্যভক্ত লঞা নিজ-সঙ্গে ।\\nশ্রীগোপাল দরশন কৈলা বহু-রঙ্গে ॥৫৩॥
verses.transliteration: ei saba mukhya-bhakta lañā nija-saṅge\\nśrī-gopāla daraśana kailā bahu-raṅge
verses.translation: It was with great jubilation that Rūpa Gosvāmī visited Lord Gopāla accompanied by all these devotees.

verses.devanagari: একমাস রহি’ গোপাল গেলা নিজ-স্থানে ।\\nশ্রীরূপ-গোসাঞি আইলা শ্ৰীবৃন্দাবনে ॥৫৪॥
verses.transliteration: eka-māsa rahi' gopāla gelā nija-sthāne\\nśrī-rūpa-gosāñi āilā śrī-vṛndāvane
verses.translation: After staying at Mathurā for one month, the Deity Gopāla returned to His own place, and Śrī Rūpa Gosvāmī returned to Vṛndāvana.

verses.devanagari: প্রস্তাবে কহিলুঁ গোপাল-কৃপার আখ্যান ।\\nতবে মহাপ্ৰভু গেলা ‘শ্রীকাম্যবন’ ॥৫৫॥
verses.transliteration: prastāve kahiluṅ gopāla-kṛpāra ākhyāna\\ntabe mahāprabhu gelā 'śrī-kāmyavana'
verses.translation: In the course of this story, I have given a description of Lord Gopāla's mercy. After seeing the Gopāla Deity, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu went to Śrī Kāmyavana.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
Kāmyavana is mentioned in the
Ādi-varāha Purāṇa:
caturthaṁ kāmyaka-vanaṁ
vanānāṁ vanam uttamam
tatra gatvā naro devi
mama loke mahīyate
In the
Bhakti-ratnākara
(Fifth Wave) it is also said:
ei kāmyavane kṛṣṇa-līlā manohara
karibe darśana sthāna kuṇḍa bahutara
kāmyavane yata tīrtha lekhā nāhi tāra

verses.devanagari: প্রভুর গমন-রীতি পূর্বে যে লিখিল ।\\nসেইমত বৃন্দাবনে তাবৎ দেখিল ॥৫৬॥
verses.transliteration: prabhura gamana-rīti pūrve ye likhila\\nsei-mata vṛndāvane tāvat dekhila
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's touring Vṛndāvana has been previously described. In the same ecstatic way, He traveled all over Vṛndāvana.

verses.devanagari: তাহাঁ লীলাস্থলী দেখি’ গেলা ‘নন্দীশ্বর’ ।\\n‘নন্দীশ্বর’ দেখি’ প্রেমে হইলা বিহ্বল ॥৫৭॥
verses.transliteration: tāhāṅ līlā-sthalī dekhi' gelā 'nandīśvara'\\n'nandīśvara' dekhi' preme ha-ilā vihvala
verses.translation: After visiting the places of Kṛṣṇa's pastimes at Kāmyavana, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu went to Nandīśvara. While there, He was overwhelmed with ecstatic love.
verses.purport: PURPORT\nNandīśvara is the house of Mahārāja Nanda.

verses.devanagari: ‘পাবনাদি’ সব কুণ্ডে স্নান করিয়া ।\\nলোকেরে পুছিল, পর্বত-উপরে যাঞা ॥৫৮॥
verses.transliteration: 'pāvanādi' saba kuṇḍe snāna kariyā\\nlokere puchila, parvata-upare yāñā
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu bathed in all the celebrated lakes, beginning with Lake Pāvana. Thereafter He climbed a hill and spoke to the people.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
The Pāvana-sarovara is described in the
Mathurā-māhātmya:
pāvane sarasi snātvā
kṛṣṇaṁ nandīśvare girau
dṛṣṭvā nandaṁ yaśodāṁ ca
sarvābhīṣṭam avāpnuyāt

verses.devanagari: কিছু দেবমূর্তি হয় পর্বত-উপরে ?\\nলোক কহে, — মূর্তি হয় গোফার ভিতরে ॥৫৯॥
verses.transliteration: kichu deva-mūrti haya parvata-upare?\\nloka kahe,—mūrti haya gophāra bhitare
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu asked, "Are there any deities on top of this hill?" The local people replied, "There are deities on this hill, but they are located within a cave.

verses.devanagari: দুইদিকে মাতা-পিতা পুষ্ট কলেবর ।\\nমধ্যে এক ‘শিশু’ হয় ত্রিভঙ্গ-সুন্দর ॥৬০॥
verses.transliteration: dui-dike mātā-pitā puṣṭa kalevara\\nmadhye eka 'śiśu' haya tribhaṅga-sundara
verses.translation: "There is a father and mother with well-built bodies, and between them is a very beautiful child who is curved in three places."

verses.devanagari: শুনি’ মহাপ্রভু মনে আনন্দ পাঞা ।\\n‘তিন’ মূর্তি দেখিলা সেই গোফা উঘাড়িয়া ॥৬১॥
verses.transliteration: śuni' mahāprabhu mane ānanda pāñā\\n'tina' mūrti dekhilā sei gophā ughāḍiyā
verses.translation: Hearing this, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu became very happy. After excavating the cave, He saw the three deities.

verses.devanagari: ব্রজেন্দ্র-ব্রজেশ্বরীর কৈল চরণ বন্দন ।\\nপ্রেমাবেশে কৃষ্ণের কৈল সর্বাঙ্গ-স্পর্শন ॥৬২॥
verses.transliteration: vrajendra-vrajeśvarīra kaila caraṇa vandana\\npremāveśe kṛṣṇera kaila sarvāṅga-sparśana
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu offered His respects to Nanda Mahārāja and mother Yaśodā, and with great ecstatic love He touched the body of Lord Kṛṣṇa.

verses.devanagari: সব দিন প্রেমাবেশে নৃত্য-গীত কৈলা ।\\nতাহাঁ হৈতে মহাপ্রভু ‘খদির-বন’ আইলা ॥৬৩॥
verses.transliteration: saba dina premāveśe nṛtya-gīta kailā\\ntāhāṅ haite mahāprabhu 'khadira-vana, āilā
verses.translation: Every day the Lord chanted and danced in ecstatic love. Finally He went to Khadiravana.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
Khadiravana is described in the
Bhakti-ratnākara
(Fifth Wave):
dekhaha khadira-vana vidita jagate
viṣṇu-loka-prāpti ethā gamana-mātrete
"Behold the forest named Khadiravana, renowned throughout the universe. If one comes to Khadiravana, he can immediately be elevated to Viṣṇuloka."

verses.devanagari: লীলাস্থল দেখি’ তাহাঁ গেলা ‘শেষশায়ী’ ।\\n‘লক্ষ্মী’ দেখি’ এই শ্লোক পড়েন গোসাঞি ॥৬৪॥
verses.transliteration: līlā-sthala dekhi' tāhāṅ gelā 'śeṣaśāyī'\\n'lakṣmī' dekhi' ei śloka paḍena gosāñi
verses.translation: After seeing the places of Lord Kṛṣṇa's pastimes, Śrī Caitanya went to Śeṣaśāyī, where He saw Lakṣmī and recited the following verse.

verses.devanagari: যত্তে সুজাতচরণাম্বুরুহং স্তনেষু\\nভীতাঃ শনৈঃ প্রিয় দধিমহি কর্কশেষু ।\\nতেনাটবীমটসি তদ্ব্যথতে ন কিংস্বিৎ\\nকূর্পাদিভির্ভ্রমতি ধীর্ভবদায়ুষাং নঃ ॥৬৫॥
verses.transliteration: yat te sujāta-caraṇāmburuhaṁ staneṣu\\nbhītāḥ śanaiḥ priya dadhīmahi karkaśeṣu\\ntenāṭavīm aṭasi tad vyathate na kiṁ svit\\nkūrpādibhir bhramati dhīr bhavad-āyuṣāṁ naḥ
verses.translation: "O dearly beloved! Your lotus feet are so soft that we place them gently on our breasts, fearing that Your feet will be hurt. Our life rests only in You. Our minds, therefore, are filled with anxiety that Your tender feet might be wounded by pebbles as You roam about on the forest path."
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a verse from
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(10.31.19) spoken by the
gopīs
when Kṛṣṇa left them in the midst of the
rāsa-līlā.

verses.devanagari: তবে ‘খেলা-তীর্থ’ দেখি’ ‘ভাণ্ডীরবন’ আইলা ।\\nযমুনা পার হঞা ‘ভদ্র-বন’ গেলা ॥৬৬॥
verses.transliteration: tabe 'khelā-tīrtha' dekhi' 'bhāṇḍīravana, āilā\\nyamunā pāra hañā 'bhadra-vana' gelā
verses.translation: Afterwards, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu saw Khelā-tīrtha and then went to Bhāṇḍīravana. Crossing the Yamunā River, He went to Bhadravana.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
In the
Bhakti-ratnākara
it is said that Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma used to play at Khelā-tīrtha with the cowherd boys during the entire day. Mother Yaśodā had to call Them to take Their baths and eat Their lunch.

verses.devanagari: ‘শ্রীবন’ দেখি’ পুনঃ গেলা ‘লোহ-বন’ ।\\n‘মহাবন’ গিয়া কৈলা জন্মস্থান-দরশন ॥৬৭॥
verses.transliteration: 'śrīvana' dekhi' punaḥ gelā 'loha-vana'\\n'mahāvana' giyā kailā janma-sthāna-daraśana
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then visited Śrīvana and Lohavana. He then went to Mahāvana and saw Gokula, the place of Lord Kṛṣṇa's early childhood pastimes.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
Of Śrīvana (also called Bilvavana), the
Bhakti-ratnākara
states,
devatā-pūjita bilvavana śobhāmaya:
"The beautiful forest of Bilvavana is worshiped by all the demigods."
About Lohavana,
Bhakti-ratnākara
(Fifth Wave) states:
lohavane kṛṣṇera adbhuta go-cāraṇa
ethā loha-jaṅghāsure vadhe bhagavān
"At Lohavana, Lord Kṛṣṇa used to tend cows. The demon named Lohajaṅgha was killed at this place."
Mahāvana is described as follows in
Bhakti-ratnākara
(Fifth Wave):
dekha nanda-yaśodā-ālaya mahāvane
ei dekha śrī-kṛṣṇa-candrera janma sthala
śrī-gokula, mahāvana—dui 'eka' haya
"Behold the house of Nanda and Yaśodā in Mahāvana. See the birthplace of Lord Kṛṣṇa. Mahāvana and the birthplace of Lord Kṛṣṇa, Gokula, are one and the same."

verses.devanagari: যমলার্জুনভঙ্গাদি দেখিল সেই স্থল ।\\nপ্রেমাবেশে প্রভুর মন হৈল টলমল ॥৬৮॥
verses.transliteration: yamalārjuna-bhaṅgādi dekhila sei sthala\\npremāveśe prabhura mana haila ṭalamala
verses.translation: Upon seeing the place where the twin arjuna trees were broken by Śrī Kṛṣṇa, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was moved to great ecstatic love.

verses.devanagari: ‘গোকুল’ দেখিয়া আইলা ‘মথুরা’-নগরে ।\\n‘জন্মস্থান’ দেখি’ রহে সেই বিপ্র-ঘরে ॥৬৯॥
verses.transliteration: 'gokula' dekhiyā āilā 'mathurā'-nagare\\njanma-sthāna' dekhi' rahe sei vipra-ghare
verses.translation: After seeing Gokula, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu returned to Mathurā, where He saw the birthplace of the Lord. While there, He stayed at the house of the Sanoḍiyā brāhmaṇa.

verses.devanagari: লোকের সংঘট্ট দেখি মথুরা ছাড়িয়া ।\\nএকান্তে ‘অক্রূর তীর্থে’ রহিলা আসিয়া ॥৭০॥
verses.transliteration: lokera saṅghaṭṭa dekhi mathurā chāḍiyā\\nekānte 'akrūra-tīrthe' rahilā āsiyā
verses.translation: Seeing a great crowd assemble at Mathurā, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu left and went to Akrūra-tīrtha. He remained there in a solitary place.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
Akrūra-tīrtha is also mentioned in the
Bhakti-ratnākara
(Fifth Wave):
dekha, śrīnivāsa, ei akrūra grāmete
śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya-prabhu chilena nibhṛte
"Śrīnivāsa, look at this village of Akrūra. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu stayed there in a solitary place."

verses.devanagari: আর দিন আইলা প্রভু দেখিতে ‘বৃন্দাবন’ ।\\n‘কালীয়-হ্রদে’ স্নান কৈলা আর প্রস্কন্দন ॥৭১॥
verses.transliteration: āra dina āilā prabhu dekhite 'vṛndāvana'\\n'kālīya-hrade' snāna kailā āra praskandana
verses.translation: The next day, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu went to Vṛndāvana and took His bath at the Kālīya Lake and Praskandana.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
Kālīya-hrada is mentioned in
Bhakti-ratnākara
(Fifth Wave):
e kālīya-tīrtha pāpa vināśaya
kālīya-tīrtha-sthāne bahu-kārya-siddhi haya
"When one takes a bath in Kālīya-hrada, he is freed from all sinful activities. One can also be successful in business by bathing in Kālīya-hrada."

verses.devanagari: ‘দ্বাদশ-আদিত্য’ হৈতে ‘কেশীতীর্থে’ আইলা ।\\nরাস-স্থলী দেখি’ প্রেমে মূর্চ্ছিত হইলা ॥৭২॥
verses.transliteration: 'dvādaśa-āditya' haite 'keśī-tīrthe' āilā\\nrāsa-sthalī dekhi' preme mūrcchita ha-ilā
verses.translation: After seeing the holy place called Praskandana, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu went to Dvādaśāditya. From there He went to Keśī-tīrtha, and when He saw the place where the rāsa dance had taken place, He immediately lost consciousness due to ecstatic love.

verses.devanagari: চেতন পাঞা পুনঃ গড়াগড়ি যায় ।\\nহাসে, কান্দে, নাচে, পড়ে, উচ্চৈঃস্বরে গায় ॥৭৩॥
verses.transliteration: cetana pāñā punaḥ gaḍāgaḍi yāya\\nhāse, kānde, nāce, paḍe, uccaiḥ-svare gāya
verses.translation: When the Lord regained His senses, He began to roll on the ground. He would sometimes laugh, cry, dance and fall down. He would also chant very loudly.

verses.devanagari: এইরঙ্গে সেইদিন তথা গোঙাইলা ।\\nসন্ধ্যাকালে অক্রূরে আসি’ ভিক্ষা নিৰ্বাহিলা ॥৭৪॥
verses.transliteration: ei-raṅge sei-dina tathā goṅāilā\\nsandhyā-kāle akrūre āsi' bhikṣā nirvāhilā
verses.translation: Being thus transcendentally amused, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu passed that day happily at Keśī-tīrtha. In the evening He returned to Akrūra-tīrtha, where He took His meal.

verses.devanagari: প্রাতে বৃন্দাবনে কৈলা ‘চীরঘাটে’ স্নান ।\\nতেঁতুলী-তলাতে আসি’ করিলা বিশ্রাম ॥৭৫॥
verses.transliteration: prāte vṛndāvane kailā 'cīra-ghāṭe' snāna\\nteṅtulī-talāte āsi' karilā viśrāma
verses.translation: The next morning Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu returned to Vṛndāvana and took His bath at Cīra-ghāṭa. He then went to Teṅtulī-talā, where He took rest.

verses.devanagari: কৃষ্ণলীলা-কালের সেই বৃক্ষ পুরাতন ।\\nতার তলে পিঁড়ি-বান্ধা পরম চিক্কণ ॥৭৬॥
verses.transliteration: kṛṣṇa-līlā-kālera sei vṛkṣa purātana\\ntāra tale piṅḍi-bāndhā parama-cikkaṇa
verses.translation: The tamarind tree named Teṅtulī-talā was very old, having been there since the time of Lord Kṛṣṇa's pastimes. Beneath the tree was a very shiny platform.

verses.devanagari: নিকটে যমুনা বহে শীতল সমীর ।\\nবৃন্দাবন-শোভা দেখে যমুনার নীর ॥৭৭॥
verses.transliteration: nikaṭe yamunā vahe śītala samīra\\nvṛndāvana-śobhā dekhe yamunāra nīra
verses.translation: Since the River Yamunā flowed near Teṅtulī-talā, a very cool breeze blew there. While there, the Lord saw the beauty of Vṛndāvana and the water of the River Yamunā.

verses.devanagari: তেঁতুল-তলে বসি’ করে নাম সংকীর্তন ।\\nমধ্যাহ্ন করি’ আসি’ করে ‘অক্রূরে’ ভোজন ॥৭৮॥
verses.transliteration: teṅtula-tale vasi' kare nāma-saṅkīrtana\\nmadhyāhna kari' āsi' kare 'akrūre' bhojana
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu used to sit beneath the old tamarind tree and chant the holy name of the Lord. At noon He would return to Akrūra-tīrtha to take lunch.

verses.devanagari: অক্রূরের লোক আইসে প্রভুরে দেখিতে । লোক-ভিড়ে স্বচ্ছন্দে নারে ‘কীর্তন’ করিতে ॥৭৯॥
verses.transliteration: akrūrera loka āise prabhure dekhite\\nloka-bhiḍe svacchande nāre 'kīrtana' karite
verses.translation: All the people who lived near Akrūra-tīrtha came to see Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and due to the large crowds, the Lord could not peacefully chant the holy name.

verses.devanagari: বৃন্দাবনে আসি’ প্রভু বসিয়া একান্ত  ।\\nনামসংকীর্তন করে মধ্যাহ্ন-পর্যন্ত ॥৮০॥
verses.transliteration: vṛndāvane āsi' prabhu vasiyā ekānta\\nnāma-saṅkīrtana kare madhyāhna-paryanta
verses.translation: Therefore Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu would go to Vṛndāvana and sit in a solitary place. It was there that He chanted the holy name until noon.

verses.devanagari: তৃতীয় প্রহরে লোক পায় দরশন ।\\nসবারে-উপদেশ করে ‘নামসংকীর্তন’ ॥৮১॥
verses.transliteration: tṛtīya-prahare loka pāya daraśana\\nsabāre upadeśa kare 'nāma-saṅkīrtana'
verses.translation: In the afternoon, people were able to speak to Him. The Lord told everyone of the importance of chanting the holy name.

verses.devanagari: হেনকালে আইলা বৈষ্ণব ‘কৃষ্ণদাস’ নাম ।\\nরাজপুত-জাতি, গৃহস্থ, যমুনা-পারে গ্রাম ॥৮২॥
verses.transliteration: hena-kāle āila vaiṣṇava 'kṛṣṇadāsa' nāma\\nrājaputa-jāti,—gṛhastha, yamunā-pāre grāma
verses.translation: During this time, a Vaiṣṇava named Kṛṣṇadāsa came to see Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. He was a householder belonging to the kṣatriya caste, and his house was located on the other side of the Yamunā.

verses.devanagari: ‘কেশী’ স্নান করি’ সেই ‘কালীয়দহ’ যাইতে ।\\nআম্লি-তলায় গোসাঞিরে দেখে আচম্বিতে ॥৮৩॥
verses.transliteration: 'keśī' snāna kari' sei 'kālīya-daha' yāite\\nāmli-talāya gosāñire dekhe ācambite
verses.translation: After bathing at Keśī-tīrtha, Kṛṣṇadāsa went toward Kālīya-daha and suddenly saw Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu sitting at Āmli-talā [Teṅtulī-talā].

verses.devanagari: প্ৰভুর রূপ-প্রেম দেখি’ হইল চমৎকার ।\\nপ্রেমাবেশে প্ৰভুরে করেন নমস্কার ॥৮৪॥
verses.transliteration: prabhura rūpa-prema dekhi' ha-ila camatkāra\\npremāveśe prabhure karena namaskāra
verses.translation: Upon seeing the Lord's personal beauty and ecstatic love, Kṛṣṇadāsa was very astonished. Out of ecstatic love, he offered his respectful obeisances unto the Lord.

verses.devanagari: প্রভু কহে, — কে তুমি, কাহাঁ তোমার ঘর ?\\nকৃষ্ণদাস কহে, — মুঞি গৃহস্থ পামর ॥৮৫॥
verses.transliteration: prabhu kahe,—ke tumi, kāhāṅ tomāra ghara?\\nkṛṣṇadāsa kahe,—mui gṛhastha pāmara
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu asked Kṛṣṇadāsa, "Who are you? Where is your home?" Kṛṣṇadāsa replied, "I am a most fallen householder.

verses.devanagari: রাজপুত-জাতি মুঞি, ও-পারে মোর ঘর ।\\nমোর ইচ্ছা হয় — ‘হঙ বৈষ্ণব-কিঙ্কর’ ॥৮৬॥
verses.transliteration: rājaputa-jāti muñi, o-pāre mora ghara\\nmora icchā haya—'haṅa vaiṣṇava-kiṅkara'
verses.translation: "I belong to the Rājaputa caste, and my home is just on the other side of the River Yamunā. However, I wish to be the servant of a Vaiṣṇava.

verses.devanagari: কিন্তু আজি এক মুঞি ‘স্বপ্ন’ দেখিনু ।\\nসেই স্বপ্ন পরতেক তোমা আসি’ পাইনু ॥৮৭॥
verses.transliteration: kintu āji eka muñi 'svapna' dekhinu\\nsei svapna parateka tomā āsi' pāinu
verses.translation: "Today I have had a dream, and according to that dream I have come here and found You."

verses.devanagari: প্রভু তাঁরে কৃপা কৈলা আলিঙ্গন করি ।\\nপ্রেমে মত্ত কৈল সেই নাচে, বলে ‘হরি’ ॥৮৮॥
verses.transliteration: prabhu tāṅre kṛpā kailā āliṅgana kari\\npreme matta haila sei nāce, bale 'hari'
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then bestowed upon Kṛṣṇadāsa His causeless mercy by embracing him. Kṛṣṇadāsa became mad with ecstatic love and began to dance and chant the holy name of Hari.

verses.devanagari: প্রভু-সঙ্গে মধ্যাহ্নে অক্রূর তীর্থে আইলা ।\\nপ্ৰভুর অবশিষ্টপাত্র-প্রসাদ পাইলা ॥৮৯॥
verses.transliteration: prabhu-saṅge madhyāhne akrūra tīrthe āilā\\nprabhura avaśiṣṭa-pātra-prasāda pāilā
verses.translation: Kṛṣṇadāsa returned to Akrūra-tīrtha with the Lord, and remnants of the Lord's food were given to him.

verses.devanagari: প্রাতে প্ৰভু-সঙ্গে আইলা জলপাত্র লঞা ।\\nপ্ৰভু-সঙ্গে রহে গৃহ-স্ত্রী-পুত্র ছাড়িয়া ॥৯০॥
verses.transliteration: prāte prabhu-saṅge āilā jala-pātra lañā\\nprabhu-saṅge rahe gṛha-strī-putra chāḍiyā
verses.translation: The next morning, Kṛṣṇadāsa went with Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu to Vṛndāvana and carried His waterpot. Kṛṣṇadāsa thus left his wife, home and children in order to remain with Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

verses.devanagari: বৃন্দাবনে পুনঃ ‘কৃষ্ণ’ প্রকট হইল ।\\nযাহাঁ তাহাঁ লোক সব কহিতে লাগিল ॥৯১॥
verses.transliteration: vṛndāvane punaḥ 'kṛṣṇa' prakaṭa ha-ila\\nyāhāṅ tāhāṅ loka saba kahite lāgila
verses.translation: Everywhere the Lord went, all the people said, "Kṛṣṇa has again manifest at Vṛndāvana."

verses.devanagari: একদিন অক্রূরেতে লোক প্রাতঃকালে ।\\nবৃন্দাবন হৈতে আইসে করি’ কোলাহলে ॥৯২॥
verses.transliteration: eka-dina akrūrete loka prātaḥ-kāle\\nvṛndāvana haite āise kari' kolāhale
verses.translation: One morning many people came to Akrūra-tīrtha. As they came from Vṛndāvana, they made a tumultuous sound.

verses.devanagari: প্রভু দেখি’ করিল লোক চরণ বন্দন ।\\nপ্রভু কহে, — কাহাঁ হৈতে করিলা আগমন ? ॥ ৯৩ ॥
verses.transliteration: prabhu dekhi' karila loka caraṇa vandana\\nprabhu kahe,—kāhāṅ haite karilā āgamana?
verses.translation: Upon seeing Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, all the people offered respects at His lotus feet. The Lord then asked them, "Where are you all coming from?"

verses.devanagari: লোকে কহে, — কৃষ্ণ প্ৰকট কালীয়দহের জলে !\\nকালীয়-শিরে নৃত্য করে, ফণা-রত্ন জ্বলে ॥৯৪॥
verses.transliteration: loke kahe,—kṛṣṇa prakaṭa kālīya-dahera jale!\\nkālīya-śire nṛtya kare, phaṇā-ratna jvale
verses.translation: The people replied, "Kṛṣṇa has again manifest Himself on the waters of the Kālīya Lake. He dances on the hoods of the serpent Kālīya, and the jewels on those hoods are blazing.

verses.devanagari: সাক্ষাৎ দেখিল লোক — নাহিক সংশয় ।\\nশুনি’ হাসি’ কহে প্রভু, — সব ‘সত্য’ হয় ॥৯৫॥
verses.transliteration: sākṣāt dekhila loka—nāhika saṁśaya\\nśuni' hāsi' kahe prabhu,—saba 'satya' haya
verses.translation: "Everyone has seen Lord Kṛṣṇa Himself. There is no doubt about it." Hearing this, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu began to laugh. He then said, "Everything is correct."
