verses.devanagari: এইমত তিন-রাত্রি লোকের গমন ।\\nসবে আসি’ কহে, — কৃষ্ণ পাইলুঁ দরশন ॥৯৬॥
verses.transliteration: ei-mata tina-rātri lokera gamana\\nsabe āsi' kahe,—kṛṣṇa pāiluṅ daraśana
verses.translation: For three successive nights people went to Kālīya-daha to see Kṛṣṇa, and everyone returned saying, "Now we have seen Kṛṣṇa Himself."

verses.devanagari: প্রভু-আগে কহে লোক, — শ্রীকৃষ্ণ দেখিল ।\\n‘সরস্বতী’ এই বাক্যে ‘সত্য’ কহাইল ॥৯৭॥
verses.transliteration: prabhu-āge kahe loka,—śrī-kṛṣṇa dekhila\\n'sarasvatī' ei vākye 'satya' kahāila
verses.translation: Everyone came before Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and said, "Now we have directly seen Lord Kṛṣṇa." Thus by the mercy of the goddess of learning they were made to speak the truth.

verses.devanagari: মহাপ্রভু দেখি’ ‘সত্য’ কৃষ্ণ-দরশন ।\\nনিজাজ্ঞানে সত্য ছাড়ি’ ‘অসত্যে সত্য-ভ্রম’ ॥৯৮॥
verses.transliteration: mahāprabhu dekhi' 'satya' kṛṣṇa-daraśana\\nnijājñāne satya chāḍi' 'asatye satya-bhrama'
verses.translation: When the people saw Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, they actually saw Kṛṣṇa, but because they were following their own imperfect knowledge, they accepted the wrong thing as Kṛṣṇa.

verses.devanagari: ভট্টাচার্য তবে কহে প্রভুর চরণে ।\\n‘আজ্ঞা দেহ’, যাই’ করি কৃষ্ণ দরশনে !’ ॥ ৯৯ ॥
verses.transliteration: bhaṭṭācārya tabe kahe prabhura caraṇe\\n'ājñā deha', yāi' kari kṛṣṇa daraśane!'
verses.translation: At that time Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya placed a request at the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. He said, "Please give me permission to go see Lord Kṛṣṇa directly."
verses.purport: PURPORT\nThe puzzled people who visited Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu were actually seeing Lord Kṛṣṇa, but they were mistaken in thinking that Lord Kṛṣṇa had come to Kālīya Lake. They all said that they had seen Kṛṣṇa directly performing His pastimes on the hood of the serpent Kālīya and that the jewels on Kālīya's hoods were blazing brilliantly. Because they were speculating with their imperfect knowledge, they saw Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu as an ordinary human being and a boatman's light in the lake as Kṛṣṇa. One must see things as they are through the mercy of a spiritual master; otherwise if one tries to see Kṛṣṇa directly, he may mistake an ordinary man for Kṛṣṇa or Kṛṣṇa for an ordinary man. Everyone has to see Kṛṣṇa according to the verdict of Vedic literatures presented by the self-realized spiritual master. A sincere person is able to see Kṛṣṇa through the transparent via medium of Śrī Gurudeva, the spiritual master. Unless one is enlightened by the knowledge given by the spiritual master, he cannot see things as they are, even though he remains constantly with the spiritual master. This incident at Kālīya-daha is very instructive for those eager to advance in Kṛṣṇa consciousness.

verses.devanagari: তবে তাঁরে কহে প্রভু চাপড় মারিয়া ।\\n“মূর্খের বাক্যে ‘মূর্খ’ হৈলা পণ্ডিত হঞা ॥১০০॥
verses.transliteration: tabe tāṅre kahe prabhu cāpaḍa māriyā\\n"mūrkhera vākye 'mūrkha' hailā paṇḍita hañā
verses.translation: When Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya asked to see Kṛṣṇa at Kālīya-daha, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu mercifully slapped him, saying, "You are a learned scholar, but you have become a fool influenced by the statements of other fools.
verses.purport: PURPORT\nMāyā is so strong that even a person like Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya, who was constantly staying with Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, was influenced by the words of fools. He wanted to see Kṛṣṇa directly by going to Kālīya-daha, but Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, being the original spiritual master, would not allow His servant to fall into such foolishness. He therefore chastised him, slapping him just to bring him to a real sense of Kṛṣṇa consciousness.

verses.devanagari: কৃষ্ণ কেনে দরশন দিবে কলিকালে ?\\nনিজ-ভ্রমে মূর্খ লোক করে কোলাহলে ॥১০১॥
verses.transliteration: kṛṣṇa kene daraśana dibe kali-kāle?\\nnija-bhrame mūrkha-loka kare kolāhale
verses.translation: "Why will Kṛṣṇa appear in the Age of Kali? Foolish people who are mistaken are simply causing agitation and making a tumult.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's first statement (
kṛṣṇa kene daraśana dibe kali-kāle
) refers to the scriptures. According to scripture, Kṛṣṇa appears in Dvāpara-yuga, but He never appears as Himself in Kali-yuga. Rather, He appears in Kali-yuga in a covered form. As stated in
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(11.5.32):
kṛṣṇa-varṇaṁ tviṣākṛṣṇaṁ sāṅgopāṅgāstra-pārṣadam.
Kṛṣṇa appears in the Age of Kali in the garb of a devotee, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, who always associates with His internal soldiers-Śrī Advaita Prabhu, Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu, Śrīvāsa Prabhu and Gadādhara Prabhu. Although Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya was personally serving Lord Kṛṣṇa in His role as a devotee (Caitanya Mahāprabhu), he mistook Lord Kṛṣṇa for an ordinary man and an ordinary man for Lord Kṛṣṇa because he did not follow the rules set down by
śāstra
and
guru.

verses.devanagari: ‘বাতুল’ না হইও, ঘরে রহত বসিয়া ।\\n‘কৃষ্ণ’ দরশন করিহ কালি রাত্র্যে যাঞা ।।” ॥১০২॥
verses.transliteration: 'vātula' nā ha-io, ghare rahata vasiyā\\n'kṛṣṇa' daraśana kariha kāli rātrye yāñā"
verses.translation: "Do not become mad. Simply sit down here, and tomorrow night you will go see Kṛṣṇa."

verses.devanagari: প্রাতঃকালে ভব্য-লোক প্রভু-স্থানে আইলা ।\\n‘কৃষ্ণ দেখি’ আইলা?’ — প্ৰভু তাঁহারে পুছিলা ॥১০৩॥
verses.transliteration: prātaḥ-kāle bhavya-loka prabhu-sthāne āilā\\n'kṛṣṇa dekhi' āilā?'—prabhu tāṅhāre puchilā
verses.translation: The next morning some respectable gentlemen came to see Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and the Lord asked them, "Have you seen Kṛṣṇa?"

verses.devanagari: লোক কহে, — রাত্র্যে কৈবর্ত্য নৌকাতে চড়িয়া  ।\\nকালীয়দহে মৎস্য মারে, দেউটী জ্বালিয়া ॥১০৪॥
verses.transliteration: loka kahe,—rātrye kaivartya naukāte caḍiyā\\nkālīya-dahe matsya māre, deuṭī jvāliyā
verses.translation: These respectable gentlemen replied, "At night in the Kālīya Lake a fisherman lighting a torch in his boat catches many fish.

verses.devanagari: দূর হৈতে তাহা দেখি’ লোকের হয় ‘ভ্রম’  ।\\n‘কালীয়ের শরীরে কৃষ্ণ করিছে নর্তন’ ! ১০৫ ॥১০৫॥
verses.transliteration: dūra haite tāhā dekhi' lokera haya 'bhrama'\\n'kālīyera śarīre kṛṣṇa kariche nartana'!
verses.translation: "From a distance, people mistakenly think that they are seeing Kṛṣṇa dancing on the body of the Kālīya serpent.

verses.devanagari: নৌকাতে কালীয়-জ্ঞান, দীপে রত্ন-জ্ঞানে !\\nজালিয়ারে মূঢ়-লোক ‘কৃষ্ণ’ করি’ মানে ! ॥ ১০৬ ॥
verses.transliteration: naukāte kālīya-jñāna, dīpe ratna-jñāne!\\njāliyāre mūḍha-loka 'kṛṣṇa' kari' māne!
verses.translation: "These fools think that the boat is the Kālīya serpent and the torchlight the jewels on his hoods. People also mistake the fisherman to be Kṛṣṇa.

verses.devanagari: বৃন্দাবনে ‘কৃষ্ণ’ আইলা, — সেহ ‘সত্য’ হয় ।\\nকৃষ্ণেরে দেখিল লোক, — ইহা ‘মিথ্যা’ নয় ॥১০৭॥
verses.transliteration: vṛndāvane 'kṛṣṇa' āilā,—sei 'satya' haya\\nkṛṣṇere dekhila loka,—ihā 'mithyā' naya
verses.translation: "Actually Lord Kṛṣṇa has again returned to Vṛndāvana. That also is a truth, and people have seen Him.

verses.devanagari: কিন্তু কাহোঁ ‘কৃষ্ণ’ দেখে, কাহোঁ ‘ভ্রম’ মানে ।\\nস্থাণু-পুরুষে যৈছে বিপরীত-জ্ঞানে ॥১০৮॥
verses.transliteration: kintu kāhoṅ 'kṛṣṇa' dekhe, kāhoṅ 'bhrama' māne\\nsthāṇu-puruṣe yaiche viparīta-jñāne
verses.translation: "But where they are seeing Kṛṣṇa is their mistake. It is like considering a dry tree to be a person."
verses.purport:
PURPORT
The word
sthāṇu
means "a dry tree without leaves." From a distance one may mistake such a tree for a person. This is called
sthāṇu-puruṣa.
Although Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was living in Vṛndāvana, the inhabitants considered Him an ordinary human being, and they mistook the fisherman to be Kṛṣṇa. Every human being is prone to make such mistakes. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was mistaken for an ordinary
sannyāsī,
the fisherman was mistaken for Kṛṣṇa, and the torchlight was mistaken for bright jewels on Kālīya's hoods.

verses.devanagari: প্রভু কহে, — ‘কাহাঁ পাইলা কৃষ্ণ দরশন ?’\\nলোক কহে, — ‘সন্ন্যাসী তুমি জঙ্গম-নারায়ণ ॥১০৯॥
verses.transliteration: prabhu kahe,—'kāhāṅ pāilā 'kṛṣṇa daraśana?'\\nloka kahe,—'sannyāsī tumi jaṅgama-nārāyaṇa
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then asked them, "Where have you seen Kṛṣṇa directly?" The people replied, "You are a sannyāsī, a renunciant; therefore You are a moving Nārāyaṇa [jaṅgama-nārāyaṇa]."
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is the viewpoint of Māyāvāda philosophy. Māyāvāda philosophy supports the impersonalist view that Nārāyaṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, has no form. One can imagine impersonal Brahman in any form-as Viṣṇu, Lord Śiva, Vivasvān, Gaṇeśa or Devī Durgā. According to the Māyāvāda philosophy, when one becomes a
sannyāsi
he is to be considered a moving Nārāyaṇa. Māyāvāda philosophy holds that the real Nārāyaṇa does not move because, being impersonal, He has no legs. Thus according to Māyāvāda philosophy, whoever becomes a
sannyāsī
declares himself Nārāyaṇa. Foolish people accept such ordinary human beings as the Supreme Personality of Godhead. This is called
vivarta-vāda.
In this regard, Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura comments that
jaṅgama-nārāyaṇa
means that the impersonal Brahman takes a shape and moves here and there in the form of a Māyāvādī
sannyāsī.
The Māyāvāda philosophy confirms this.
Daṇḍa-grahaṇa-mātreṇa naro nārāyaṇo bhavet:
"Simply by accepting the
daṇḍa
of the order of
sannyāsa,
one is immediately transformed into Nārāyaṇa." Therefore Māyāvādī
sannyāsīs
address themselves by saying,
oṁ namo nārāyaṇāya.
In this way one Nārāyaṇa worships another Nārāyaṇa.
Actually an ordinary human being cannot become Nārāyaṇa. Even the chief Māyāvādī
sannyāsī,
Śrī Śaṅkarācārya, says,
nārāyaṇaḥ paro 'vyaktāt:
"Nārāyaṇa is not a creation of this material world. Nārāyaṇa is above the material creation." Due to their poor fund of knowledge, Māyāvādī
sannyāsīs
think that Nārāyaṇa, the Absolute Truth, takes birth as a human being and that when He realizes this, He becomes Nārāyaṇa again. They never consider why Nārāyaṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, accepts an inferior position as a human being and then again becomes Nārāyaṇa when He is perfect. Why should Nārāyaṇa be imperfect? Why should He appear as a human being? Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu very nicely explained these points while at Vṛndāvana.

verses.devanagari: বৃন্দাবনে হইলা তুমি কৃষ্ণ-অবতার ।\\nতোমা দেখি’ সর্বলোক হইল নিস্তার ।।’ ॥ ১১০ ॥
verses.transliteration: vṛndāvane ha-ilā tumi kṛṣṇa-avatāra\\ntomā dekhi' sarva-loka ha-ila nistāra
verses.translation: The people then said, "You have appeared in Vṛndāvana as an incarnation of Kṛṣṇa. Just by seeing You, everyone is now liberated."

verses.devanagari: প্রভু কহে, — ‘বিষ্ণু’ ‘বিষ্ণু’, ইহা না কহিবা !\\nজীবাধমে ‘কৃষ্ণ’-জ্ঞান কভু না করিবা ! ॥ ১১১ ॥
verses.transliteration: prabhu kahe,—'viṣṇu' 'viṣṇu' ihā nā kahibā!\\njīvādhame 'kṛṣṇa'-jñāna kabhu nā karibā!
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu immediately exclaimed, "Viṣṇu! Viṣṇu! Do not call Me the Supreme Personality of Godhead. A jīva cannot become Kṛṣṇa at any time. Do not even say such a thing!
verses.purport:
PURPORT
Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu immediately stated that a living being, however exalted he may be, should never be compared to the Supreme Personality of Godhead. All of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's preaching protests the monistic philosophy of the Māyāvāda school. The central point of Kṛṣṇa consciousness is that the
jīva,
the living entity, can never be accepted as Kṛṣṇa or Viṣṇu. This viewpoint is elaborated in the following verses.

verses.devanagari: সন্ন্যাসী — চিত্কণ জীব, কিরণ-কণ-সম ।\\nষড়ৈশ্বর্যপূর্ণ কৃষ্ণ হয় সূর্যোপম ॥১১২॥
verses.transliteration: sannyāsī—cit-kaṇa jīva, kiraṇa-kaṇa-sama\\nṣaḍ-aiśvarya-pūrṇa kṛṣṇa haya sūryopama
verses.translation: "A sannyāsī in the renounced order is certainly part and parcel of the complete whole, just as a shining molecular particle of sunshine is part and parcel of the sun itself. Kṛṣṇa is like the sun, full of six opulences, but the living entity is only a fragment of the complete whole.

verses.devanagari: জীব, ঈশ্বর-তত্ত্ব — কভু নহে ‘সম’ ।\\nজ্বলদগ্নিরাশি যৈছে স্ফুলিঙ্গের ‘কণ’ ॥১১৩॥
verses.transliteration: jīva, īśvara-tattva—kabhu nahe 'sama'\\njvalad-agni-rāśi yaiche sphuliṅgera 'kaṇa'
verses.translation: "A living entity and the Absolute Personality of Godhead are never to be considered equal, just as a fragmental spark can never be considered the original flame.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
Māyāvādī
sannyāsīs
consider themselves Brahman, and they superficially speak of themselves as Nārāyaṇa. The monistic disciples of the Māyāvāda school (known as
smārta-brāhmaṇas
) are generally householder
brāhmaṇas
who accept the Māyāvādī
sannyāsīs
as Nārāyaṇa incarnate; therefore they offer their obeisances to them. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu immediately protested this unauthorized system, specifically mentioning that a
sannyāsī
(
cit-kaṇa jīva
) is nothing but a fragmental portion of the Supreme. In other words, he is nothing more than an ordinary living being. He is never Nārāyaṇa, just as a molecular portion of sunshine is never the sun itself. The living entity is nothing but a fragmental part of the Absolute Truth; therefore at no stage of perfection can a living entity become the Supreme Personality of Godhead. This Māyāvāda viewpoint is always condemned by the Vaiṣṇava school. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu Himself protested this philosophy. When the Māyāvādīs accept
sannyāsa
and consider themselves Nārāyaṇa, they become so puffed up that they do not even enter the temple of Nārāyaṇa to offer respects, for they falsely think themselves Nārāyaṇa Himself. Although Māyāvādī
sannyāsīs
may offer respects to other
sannyāsīs
and address them as Nārāyaṇa, they do not go to a Nārāyaṇa temple and offer respects. These Māyāvādī
sannyāsīs
are always condemned and are described as demons. The
Vedas
clearly state that living entities are subordinate parts and parcels of the supreme.
Eko bahūnāṁ yo vidadhāti kāmān:
the Supreme Being, Kṛṣṇa, maintains all living entities.

verses.devanagari: হ্লাদিন্যা সংবিদাশ্লিষ্টঃ সচ্চিদানন্দ ঈশ্বরঃ ।\\nস্বাবিদ্যা-সংবৃতো জীবঃ সংক্লেশনিকরাকরঃ ॥১১৪॥
verses.transliteration: hlādinyā saṁvid-āśliṣṭaḥ\\nsac-cid-ānanda īśvaraḥ\\nsvāvidyā-saṁvṛto jīvaḥ\\nsaṅkleśa-nikarākaraḥ
verses.translation: “ 'The Supreme Personality of Godhead, the supreme controller, is always full of transcendental bliss and is accompanied by the potencies known as hlādinī and samvit. The conditioned soul, however, is always covered by ignorance and embarrassed by the threefold miseries of life. Thus he is a treasure-house of all kinds of tribulations.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This quotation of Viṣṇusvāmī is cited in Śrīdhara Svāmī's
Bhāvārtha-dīpikā
commentary on
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(1.7.6).

verses.devanagari: যেই মূঢ় কহে, — জীব ঈশ্বর হয় ‘সম’ ।\\nসেইত ‘পাষণ্ডী’ হয়, দণ্ডে তারে যম ॥১১৫॥
verses.transliteration: yei mūḍha kahe,—jīva īśvara haya 'sama'\\nseita 'pāṣaṇḍī' haya, daṇḍe tāre yama
verses.translation: "A foolish person who says that the Supreme Personality of Godhead is the same as the living entity is an atheist, and he becomes subject to punishment by the superintendent of death, Yamarāja.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura says that the word
pāṣaṇḍī
refers to one who considers the living entity under the control of the illusory energy to be equal with the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is transcendental to all material qualities. Another kind of
pāṣaṇḍī
is one who does not believe in the spirit soul, the superior potency of the Lord, and therefore does not distinguish between spirit and matter. While describing one of the offenses against chanting the holy names, an offense called
śruti-śāstra-nindana
(blaspheming the Vedic literature), Jīva Gosvāmī states in his
Bhakti-sandarbha: yathā pāṣaṇḍa-mārgeṇa dattātreyarṣabha-devopāsakānāṁ pāṣaṇḍīnām.
Worshipers of impersonalists like Dattātreya are also
pāṣaṇḍīs.
Concerning the offense of
ahaṁ-mama-buddhi,
or
dehātma-buddhi
(considering the body to be the self), Jīva Gosvāmī states:
deva-draviṇādi-nimittaka-'pāṣaṇḍa'-śabdena ca daśāparādhā eva lakṣyante, pāṣaṇḍamayatvāt teṣām.
"Those who are overly absorbed in the conception of the body and the bodily necessities are also called
pāṣaṇḍīs.
" Elsewhere in
Bhakti-sandarbha
it is stated:
uddiśya devatā eva
juhoti ca dadāti ca
sa pāṣaṇḍīti vijñeyaḥ
svatantro vāpi karmasu
"A
pāṣaṇḍī
is one who considers the demigods and the Supreme Personality of Godhead to be one; therefore a
pāṣaṇḍī
worships any kind of demigod as the Supreme Personality of Godhead." One who disobeys the orders of the spiritual master is also considered a
pāṣaṇḍī.
The word
pāṣaṇḍī
has been described in many places in
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam,
including 4.2.28, 30, 32; 5.6.9 and 12.2.13, 43.
On the whole, a
pāṣaṇḍī
is a nondevotee who does not accept the Vedic conclusions. In the
Hari-bhakti-vilāsa
(1.117) there is a verse quoted from
Padma Purāṇa
describing the
pāṣaṇḍī.
Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu quotes this verse as the following text.

verses.devanagari: যস্তু নারায়ণং দেবং ব্রহ্মরুদ্রাদিদৈবতৈঃ ।\\nসমত্বেনৈব বীক্ষেত স পাষণ্ডী ভবেদ্ধ্রুবম্ ॥১১৬॥
verses.transliteration: yas tu nārāyaṇaṁ devaṁ\\nbrahma-rudrādi-daivataiḥ\\nsamatvenaiva vīkṣeta\\nsa pāṣaṇḍī bhaved dhruvam
verses.translation: “ 'A person who considers demigods like Brahmā and Śiva to be on an equal level with Nārāyaṇa is to be considered an offender and a pāṣaṇḍī.' "

verses.devanagari: লোক কহে, — তোমাতে কভু নহে ‘জীব’-মতি  ।\\nকৃষ্ণের সদৃশ তোমার আকৃতি-প্রকৃতি ॥১১৭॥
verses.transliteration: loka kahe,—tomāte kabhu nahe jīva'-mati\\nkṛṣṇera sadṛśa tomāra ākṛti-prakṛti
verses.translation: After Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu explained the difference between an ordinary living being and the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the people said, "No one considers You an ordinary human being. You are like Kṛṣṇa in every respect, in both bodily features and characteristics.

verses.devanagari: ‘আকৃত্যে’ তোমারে দেখি ‘ব্রজেন্দ্র-নন্দন’  ।\\nদেহকান্তি পীতাম্বর কৈল আচ্ছাদন ॥১১৮॥
verses.transliteration: 'ākṛtye' tomāre dekhi 'vrajendra-nandana'\\ndeha-kānti pītāmbara kaila ācchādana
verses.translation: "By Your bodily features we can see that You are none other than the son of Nanda Mahārāja, although the golden luster of Your body has covered Your original complexion.

verses.devanagari: মৃগমদ বস্ত্রে বান্ধে, তবু না লুকায় ।\\n‘ঈশ্বর-স্বভাব’ তোমার ঢাকা নাহি যায় ॥১১৯॥
verses.transliteration: mṛga-mada vastre bāndhe, tabu nā lukāya\\n'īśvara-svabhāva' tomāra ṭākā nāhi yāya
verses.translation: "As the aroma of deer musk cannot be concealed by wrapping it in a cloth, Your characteristics as the Supreme Personality of Godhead cannot be concealed by any means.

verses.devanagari: অলৌকিক ‘প্রকৃতি’ তোমার — বুদ্ধি-অগোচর ।\\nতোমা দেখি’ কৃষ্ণপ্রেমে জগৎ পাগল ॥১২০॥
verses.transliteration: alaukika 'prakṛti' tomāra—buddhi-agocara\\ntomā dekhi' kṛṣṇa-preme jagat pāgala
verses.translation: "Indeed, Your characteristics are uncommon and beyond the imagination of an ordinary living being. Simply by seeing You, the entire universe becomes mad with ecstatic love for Kṛṣṇa.

verses.devanagari: স্ত্রী-বাল-বৃদ্ধ, আর ‘চণ্ডাল’, ‘যবন’ ।\\nযেই তোমার একবার পায় দরশন ॥১২১॥\\nকৃষ্ণনাম লয়, নাচে হঞা উন্মত্ত ।\\nআচার্য হইল সেই, তারিল জগত ॥১২২॥
verses.transliteration: kṛṣṇa-nāma laya, nāce hañā unmatta\\nācārya ha-ila sei, tārila jagata
verses.translation: "If even women, children, old men, meat-eaters or members of the lowest caste can see You even once, they immediately chant the holy name of Kṛṣṇa, dance like madmen and become spiritual masters capable of delivering the whole world.

verses.devanagari: দর্শনের কার্য আছুক, যে তোমার ‘নাম’ শুনে ।\\nসেই কৃষ্ণপ্রেমে মত্ত, তারে ত্রিভুবনে ॥১২৩॥
verses.transliteration: darśanera kārya āchuka, ye tomāra 'nāma' śune\\nsei kṛṣṇa-preme matta, tāre tribhuvane
verses.translation: "Apart from seeing You, whoever listens to Your holy name is made mad with ecstatic love for Kṛṣṇa and is able to deliver the three worlds.

verses.devanagari: তোমার নাম শুনি’ হয় শ্বপচ ‘পাবন’ ।\\nঅলৌকিক শক্তি তোমার না যায় কথন ॥১২৪॥
verses.transliteration: tomāra nāma śuni' haya śvapaca 'pāvana'\\nalaukika śakti tomāra nā yāya kathana
verses.translation: "Simply by hearing Your holy name, dog-eaters become holy saints. Your uncommon potencies cannot be described in words.

verses.devanagari: যন্নামধেয়-শ্রবণানুকীর্তনাদ্\\nযৎপ্রহ্বণাদ্যত্স্মরণাদপি ক্বচিৎ ।\\nশ্বাদোঽপি সদ্যঃ সবনায় কল্পতে\\nকুতঃ পুনস্তে ভগবন্নু দর্শনাৎ ॥১২৫॥
verses.transliteration: yan-nāmadheya-śravaṇānukīrtanād\\nyat-prahvaṇād yat-smaraṇād api kvacit\\nśvādo 'pi sadyaḥ savanāya kalpate\\nkutaḥ punas te bhagavan nu darśanāt
verses.translation: “ 'To say nothing of the spiritual advancement of persons who see the Supreme Person face to face, even a person born in a family of dog-eaters becomes immediately eligible to perform Vedic sacrifices if he once utters the holy name of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, or chants about Him, hears about His pastimes, offers Him obeisances or even remembers Him.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a quotation from
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(3.33.6). According to this verse, it doesn't matter what position a person holds. One may be the lowest of the low-a
caṇḍāla,
or dog-eater—but if he takes to chanting and hearing the holy name of the Lord, he is immediately eligible to perform Vedic sacrifices. This is especially true in this Age of Kali.
harer nāma harer nāma
harer nāmaiva kevalam
kalau nāsty eva nāsty eva
nāsty eva gatir anyathā
(
Bṛhan-nāradīya Purāṇa
38.126)
A person born in a
brāhmaṇa
family cannot perform Vedic sacrifices until he is properly purified and has attained his sacred thread. However, according to this verse, it is understood that even a lowborn person can immediately perform sacrifices if he sincerely chants and hears the holy name of the Lord. Sometimes envious people ask how Europeans and Americans in this Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement can become
brāhmaṇas
and perform sacrifices. They do not know that the Europeans and Americans have already been purified by chanting the holy name of the Lord-Hare Kṛṣṇa, Hare Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa Kṛṣṇa, Hare HareHare Rāma, Hare Rāma, Rāma Rāma, Hare Hare. This is the proof.
Śvādo 'pi sadyaḥ savanāya kalpate.
One may be born in a family of dog-eaters, but he can perform sacrifices simply by chanting the
mahā-mantra.
Those who find fault in the Western Vaiṣṇavas should consider this statement from
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
and the commentary on this verse by Śrīla Jīva Gosvāmī. In this regard, Śrīla Jīva Gosvāmī has stated that to become a
brāhmaṇa,
one has to wait for purification and undergo the sacred thread ceremony, but a chanter of the holy name does not have to wait for the sacred thread ceremony. We do not allow devotees to perform sacrifices until they are properly initiated in the sacred thread ceremony. Yet according to this verse, an offenseless chanter of the holy name is already fit to perform a fire ceremony, even though he is not doubly initiated by the sacred thread ceremony. This is the verdict given by Lord Kapiladeva in His instructions to His mother, Devahūti. It was Lord Kapiladeva who instructed Devahūti in pure Sāṅkhya philosophy.

verses.devanagari: এইত’ মহিমা — তোমার ‘তটস্থ’-লক্ষণ ।\\n‘স্বরূপ’-লক্ষণে তুমি — ‘ব্রজেন্দ্রনন্দন’ ॥১২৬॥
verses.transliteration: eita' mahimā—tomāra 'taṭastha'-lakṣaṇa\\n'svarūpa'-lakṣaṇe tumi—'vrajendra-nandana'
verses.translation: "These glories of Yours are only marginal. Originally You are the son of Mahārāja Nanda."
verses.purport:
PURPORT
The original characteristics of a substance are called
svarūpa,
and the subsequent corollaries are called
taṭastha-lakṣaṇa,
or marginal characteristics. The glories of the Lord's marginal characteristics prove Him to be the original Supreme Personality of Godhead, the son of Mahārāja Nanda. As soon as one understands this, one accepts Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu as the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa.

verses.devanagari: সেই সব লোকে প্রভু প্রসাদ করিল ।\\nকৃষ্ণপ্রেমে মত্ত লোক নিজ-ঘরে গেল ॥১২৭॥
verses.transliteration: sei saba loke prabhu prasāda karila\\nkṛṣṇa-preme matta loka nija-ghare gela
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then bestowed His causeless mercy upon all the people there, and everyone became ecstatic with love of God. Finally they all returned to their homes.

verses.devanagari: এইমত কতদিন ‘অক্রূরে’ রহিলা ।\\nকৃষ্ণ-নাম-প্রেম দিয়া লোক নিস্তারিলা ॥১২৮॥
verses.transliteration: ei-mata kata-dina 'akrūre' rahilā\\nkṛṣṇa-nāma-prema diyā loka nistārilā
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu remained for some days in Akrūra-tīrtha. He delivered everyone there simply by distributing the holy name of Kṛṣṇa and ecstatic love for the Lord.

verses.devanagari: মাধবপুরীর শিষ্য সেইত ব্রাহ্মণ ।\\nমথুরার ঘরে-ঘরে করা’ন নিমন্ত্রণ ॥১২৯॥
verses.transliteration: mādhava-purīra śiṣya seita brāhmaṇa\\nmathurāra ghare-ghare karā'na nimantraṇa
verses.translation: The brāhmaṇa disciple of Mādhavendra Purī went from house to house in Mathurā and inspired other brāhmaṇas to invite Caitanya Mahāprabhu to their homes.

verses.devanagari: মথুরার যত লোক ব্রাহ্মণ সজ্জন ।\\nভট্টাচার্য-স্থানে আসি’ করে নিমন্ত্রণ ॥১৩০॥
verses.transliteration: mathurāra yata loka brāhmaṇa sajjana\\nbhaṭṭācārya-sthāne āsi' kare nimantraṇa
verses.translation: Thus all the respectable people of Mathurā, headed by the brāhmaṇas, came to Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya and extended invitations to the Lord.

verses.devanagari: একদিন ‘দশ’ ‘বিশ’ আইসে নিমন্ত্রণ ।\\nভট্টাচার্য একের মাত্র করেন গ্রহণ ॥১৩১॥
verses.transliteration: eka-dina 'daśa' 'biśa' āise nimantraṇa\\nbhaṭṭācārya ekera mātra karena grahaṇa
verses.translation: In one day, ten to twenty invitations were received, but Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya would accept only one of them.

verses.devanagari: অবসর না পায় লোক নিমন্ত্রণ দিতে ।\\nসেই বিপ্রে সাধে লোক নিমন্ত্রণ নিতে ॥১৩২॥
verses.transliteration: avasara nā pāya loka nimantraṇa dite\\nsei vipre sādhe loka nimantraṇa nite
verses.translation: Since everyone did not get an opportunity to offer invitations to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu personally, they requested the Sanoḍiyā brāhmaṇa to ask the Lord to accept their invitations.

verses.devanagari: কান্যকুব্জ-দাক্ষিণাত্যের বৈদিক ব্রাহ্মণ ।\\nদৈন্য করি, করে মহাপ্রভুর নিমন্ত্রণ ॥১৩৩॥
verses.transliteration: kānyakubja-dākṣiṇātyera vaidika brāhmaṇa\\ndainya kari, kare mahāprabhura nimantraṇa
verses.translation: The brāhmaṇas from different places, such as Kānyakubja and South India, who were all strict followers of the Vedic religion, offered invitations to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu with great humility.

verses.devanagari: প্রাতঃকালে অক্রূরে আসি’ রন্ধন করিয়া ।\\nপ্রভুরে ভিক্ষা দেন শালগ্রামে সমর্পিয়া ॥১৩৪॥
verses.transliteration: prātaḥ-kāle akrūre āsi' randhana kariyā\\nprabhure bhikṣā dena śālagrāme samarpiyā
verses.translation: In the morning they would come to Akrūra-tīrtha and cook food. After offering it to the śālagrāma-śilā, they offered it to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
There are
brāhmaṇas
known as
pañca-gauḍa-brāhmaṇas
who come from five places in northern India, and there are
brāhmaṇas
known as
pañca-dākṣiṇātya-brāhmaṇas
who come from five places in southern India. In northern India the places are Kānyakubja, Sārasvata, Gauḍa, Maithila and Utkala. In southern India the places are Āndhra, Karṇāta, Gurjara, Drāviḍa and Mahārāṣṭra. The
brāhmaṇas
from these places are considered to be very strict followers of the Vedic principles, and they are accepted as pure
brāhmaṇas.
They strictly observe Vedic principles and are not polluted by tantric misdeeds. All of these
brāhmaṇas
respectfully invited Caitanya Mahāprabhu for lunch.

verses.devanagari: একদিন সেই অক্রূর-ঘাটের উপরে ।\\nবসি’ মহাপ্রভু কিছু করেন বিচারে ॥১৩৫॥
verses.transliteration: eka-dina sei akrūra-ghāṭera upare\\nvasi' mahāprabhu kichu karena vicāre
verses.translation: One day Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu sat at the bathing ghat of Akrūra-tīrtha and thought the following thoughts.
verses.purport: PURPORT\nAkrūra-tīrtha is located on the road between Vṛndāvana and Mathurā. When Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma were being taken to Mathurā by Akrūra, the Lord rested at this place and took His bath in the Yamunā. When Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma took Their baths, Akrūra saw the entire world of Vaikuṇṭha within the water. The inhabitants of Vṛndāvana also saw the Vaikuṇṭha planets within the water.

verses.devanagari: এই ঘাটে অক্রূর বৈকুণ্ঠ দেখিল ।\\nব্রজবাসী লোক ‘গোলোক’ দর্শন কৈল ॥১৩৬॥
verses.transliteration: ei ghāṭe akrūra vaikuṇṭha dekhila\\nvrajavāsī loka 'goloka' darśana kaila
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu thought, "At this bathing place, Akrūra saw Vaikuṇṭha, the spiritual world, and all the inhabitants of Vraja saw Goloka Vṛndāvana."

verses.devanagari: এত বলি’ ঝাঁপ দিলা জলের উপরে ।\\nডুবিয়া রহিলা প্রভু জলের ভিতরে ॥১৩৭॥
verses.transliteration: eta bali' jhāṅpa dilā jalera upare\\nḍubiyā rahilā prabhu jalera bhitare
verses.translation: While considering how Akrūra remained within the water, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu immediately jumped in and stayed under water for some time.

verses.devanagari: দেখি’ কৃষ্ণদাস কান্দি’ ফুকার করিল ।\\nভট্টাচার্য শীঘ্র আসি’ প্রভুরে উঠাইল ॥১৩৮॥
verses.transliteration: dekhi' kṛṣṇadāsa kāndi' phukāra karila\\nbhaṭṭācārya śīghra āsi' prabhure uṭhāila
verses.translation: When Kṛṣṇadāsa saw that Caitanya Mahāprabhu was drowning, he cried and shouted very loudly. Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya immediately came and pulled the Lord out.

verses.devanagari: তবে ভট্টাচার্য সেই ব্রাহ্মণে লঞা ।\\nযুক্তি করিলা কিছু নিভৃতে বসিয়া ॥১৩৯॥
verses.transliteration: tabe bhaṭṭācārya sei brāhmaṇe lañā\\nyukti karilā kichu nibhṛte vasiyā
verses.translation: After this, Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya took the Sanoḍiyā brāhmaṇa to a secluded place and consulted with him.

verses.devanagari: আজি আমি আছিলাঙ উঠাইলুঁ প্রভুরে ।\\nবৃন্দাবনে ডুবেন যদি, কে উঠাবে তাঁরে ? ॥ ১৪০ ॥
verses.transliteration: āji āmi āchilāṅa uṭhāiluṅ prabhure\\nvṛndāvane ḍubena yadi, ke uṭhābe tāṅre?
verses.translation: Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya said, "Since I was present today, it was possible for me to pull the Lord up. However, if He starts to drown at Vṛndāvana, who will help Him?

verses.devanagari: লোকের সংঘট্ট, আর নিমন্ত্রণের জঞ্জাল ।\\nনিরন্তর আবেশ প্রভুর না দেখিয়ে ভাল ॥১৪১॥
verses.transliteration: lokera saṅghaṭṭa, āra nimantraṇera jañjāla\\nnirantara āveśa prabhura nā dekhiye bhāla
verses.translation: "Now there is a crowd of people here, and these invitations are causing much disturbance. In addition, the Lord is always ecstatic and emotional. I do not find the situation here very good.

verses.devanagari: বৃন্দাবন হৈতে যদি প্রভুরে কাড়িয়ে ।\\nতবে মঙ্গল হয়, — এই ভাল যুক্তি হয়ে ॥১৪২॥
verses.transliteration: vṛndāvana haite yadi prabhure kāḍiye\\ntabe maṅgala haya,—ei bhāla yukti haye
verses.translation: "It would be good if we could get Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu out of Vṛndāvana. That is my final conclusion."

verses.devanagari: বিপ্র কহে, — প্রয়াগে প্রভু লঞা যাই ।\\nগঙ্গাতীর-পথে যাই, তবে সুখ পাই ॥১৪৩॥
verses.transliteration: vipra kahe,—prayāge prabhu lañā yāi\\ngaṅgā-tīra-pathe yāi, tabe sukha pāi
verses.translation: The Sanoḍiyā brāhmaṇa said, "Let us take Him to Prayāga and go along the banks of the Ganges. It will be very pleasurable to go that way.

verses.devanagari: ‘সোরোক্ষেত্রে, আগে যাঞা করি’ গঙ্গাস্নান ।\\nসেই পথে প্রভু লঞা করিয়ে পয়ান ॥১৪৪॥
verses.transliteration: 'soro-kṣetre, āge yāñā kari' gaṅgā-snāna\\nsei pathe prabhu lañā kariye payāna
verses.translation: "After going to the holy place named Soro-kṣetra, and taking bath in the Ganges, let us take Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu that way and go.

verses.devanagari: মাঘ-মাস লাগিল, এবে যদি যাইয়ে ।\\nমকরে প্রয়াগ-স্নান কত দিন পাইয়ে ॥১৪৫॥
verses.transliteration: māgha-māsa lāgila, ebe yadi yāiye\\nmakare prayāga-snāna kata dina pāiye
verses.translation: "It is now the beginning of the month of Māgha. If we go to Prayāga at this time, we shall have an opportunity to bathe for a few days during Makara-saṅkrānti."
verses.purport:
PURPORT
Bathing during the month of Māgha at Māgha-melā still takes place. This has been a very old
melā
(assembly) from time immemorial. It is said that the Lord in the form of Mohinī took a bucket of nectar and kept it at Prayāga. Consequently Māgha-melā has been observed, and there is an assembly of holy men there every year. Every twelfth year there is a Kumbha-melā, a great festival, and all the holy men from all over India assemble there. The
brāhmaṇa
wanted to take advantage of the Māgha-melā and bathe there.
Bathing at the confluence of the Ganges and Yamunā near the fort at Allahabad, Prayāga, is mentioned in revealed scriptures:
māghe māsi gamiṣyanti
gaṅgā-yāmuna-saṅgamam
gavāṁ śata-sahasrasya
samyag dattaṁ ca yat-phalam
prayāge māgha-māse vai
tryahaṁ snātasya tat-phalam
"If one goes to Prayāga and bathes at the confluence of the Ganges and Yamunā in the month of Māgha, he attains the result of giving hundreds and thousands of cows in charity. Simply by bathing for three days there, he attains the results of such a pious activity." Because of this, the Sanoḍiyā
brāhmaṇa
was very eager to go to Prayāga and bathe. Generally
karmīs
(fruitive laborers) take advantage of bathing there during the month of Māgha, thinking that they will be rewarded in the future. Those who are situated in devotional service do not very strictly follow this
karma-kāṇḍīya
process.

verses.devanagari: আপনার দুঃখ কিছু করি’ নিবেদন ।\\n‘মকর-পঁচসি প্রয়াগে’ করিহ সূচন ॥১৪৬॥
verses.transliteration: āpanāra duḥkha kichu kari' nivedana\\n'makara-paṅcasi prayāge' kariha sūcana
verses.translation: The Sanoḍiyā brāhmaṇa continued, "Kindly submit to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu the unhappiness you are feeling within yourself. Then propose that we all go to Prayāga on the full-moon day of the month of Māgha.

verses.devanagari: গঙ্গাতীর-পথে সুখ জানাইহ তাঁরে ।\\nভট্টাচার্য আসি’ তবে কহিল প্রভুরে ॥১৪৭॥
verses.transliteration: gaṅgā-tīra-pathe sukha jānāiha tāṅre\\nbhaṭṭācārya āsi' tabe kahila prabhure
verses.translation: "Tell the Lord of the happiness you will feel in traveling via the banks of the Ganges." Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya therefore submitted this prayer to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

verses.devanagari: “সহিতে না পারি আমি লোকের গড়বড়ি ।\\nনিমন্ত্রণ লাগি’ লোক করে হুড়াহুড়ি ॥১৪৮॥
verses.transliteration: "sahite nā pāri āmi lokera gaḍabaḍi\\nnimantraṇa lāgi' loka kare huḍāhuḍi
verses.translation: Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya told the Lord, "I can no longer tolerate the disturbance of the crowd. People are coming one after another to offer invitations.

verses.devanagari: প্রাতঃকালে আইসে লোক, তোমারে না পায় ।\\nতোমারে না পাঞা লোক মোর মাথা খায় ॥১৪৯॥
verses.transliteration: prātaḥ-kāle āise loka, tomāre nā pāya\\ntomāre nā pāñā loka mora māthā khāya
verses.translation: "Early in the morning people come here, and not seeing You present, they simply tax my brain.

verses.devanagari: তবে সুখ হয় যবে গঙ্গাপথে যাইয়ে ।\\nএবে যদি যাই, ‘মকরে’ গঙ্গাস্নান পাইয়ে ॥১৫০॥
verses.transliteration: tabe sukha haya yabe gaṅgā-pathe yāiye\\nebe yadi yāi, 'makare' gaṅgā-snāna pāiye
verses.translation: "I will be very happy if we all leave and take the path by the banks of the Ganges. Then we can have the opportunity to bathe in the Ganges in Prayāga during Makara-saṅkrānti.
verses.purport: PURPORT\nThere are two great occasions for bathing in the Ganges during Māgha-melā. One is on the day of the dark moon, and the other is on the day of the full moon during the month of Māgha.

verses.devanagari: উদ্বিগ্ন হইল প্রাণ, সহিতে না পারি ।\\nপ্রভুর যে আজ্ঞা হয়, সেই শিরে ধরি ।।” ॥ ১৫১ ॥
verses.transliteration: udvigna ha-ila prāṇa, sahite nā pāri\\nprabhura ye ājñā haya, sei śire dhari"
verses.translation: "My mind has become very agitated, and I cannot bear this anxiety. May everything rest on the permission of Your Lordship. I will accept whatever You want to do."

verses.devanagari: যদ্যপি বৃন্দাবন-ত্যাগে নাহি প্রভুর মন ।\\nভক্ত-ইচ্ছা পূরিতে কহে মধুর বচন ॥১৫২॥
verses.transliteration: yadyapi vṛndāvana-tyāge nāhi prabhura mana\\nbhakta-icchā pūrite kahe madhura vacana
verses.translation: Although Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu had no desire to leave Vṛndāvana, He began to speak sweet words just to fulfill the desire of His devotee.

verses.devanagari: “তুমি আমায় আনি’ দেখাইলা বৃন্দাবন ।\\nএই ‘ঋণ’ আমি নারিব করিতে শোধন ॥১৫৩॥
verses.transliteration: "tumi āmāya āni' dekhāilā vṛndāvana\\nei 'ṛṇa' āmi nāriba karite śodhana
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "You have brought Me here to show Me Vṛndāvana. I am very much indebted to you, and I shall not be able to repay this debt.

verses.devanagari: যে তোমার ইচ্ছা, আমি সেইত করিব ।\\nযাহাঁ লঞা যাহ তুমি, তাহাঁই যাইব ।।” ॥ ১৫৪ ॥
verses.transliteration: ye tomāra icchā, āmi seita kariba\\nyāhāṅ lañā yāha tumi, tāhāṅi yāiba"
verses.translation: "Whatever you desire, I must do. Wherever you take Me, I shall go."

verses.devanagari: প্রাতঃকালে মহাপ্রভু প্রাতঃস্নান কৈল ।\\n‘বৃন্দাবন ছাড়িব’ জানি’ প্রেমাবেশ হৈল ॥১৫৫॥
verses.transliteration: prātaḥ-kāle mahāprabhu prātaḥ-snāna kaila\\n'vṛndāvana chāḍiba' jāni' premāveśa haila
verses.translation: The next morning, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu got up early. After taking His bath, He became ecstatic with love, knowing that He now had to leave Vṛndāvana.

verses.devanagari: বাহ্য বিকার নাহি, প্রেমাবিষ্ট মন ।\\nভট্টাচার্য কহে, — চল, যাই মহাবন ॥১৫৬॥
verses.transliteration: bāhya vikāra nāhi, premāviṣṭa mana\\nbhaṭṭācārya kahe,—cala, yāi mahāvana
verses.translation: Although the Lord did not exhibit any external symptoms, His mind was filled with ecstatic love. At that time, Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya said, "Let us go to Mahāvana [Gokula]."

verses.devanagari: এত বলি’ মহাপ্রভুরে নৌকায় বসাঞা ।\\nপার করি’ ভট্টাচার্য চলিলা লঞা ॥১৫৭॥
verses.transliteration: eta bali' mahāprabhure naukāya vasāñā\\npāra kari' bhaṭṭācārya calilā lañā
verses.translation: Saying this, Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya made Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu sit aboard a boat. After they crossed the river, he took the Lord with him.

verses.devanagari: প্রেমী কৃষ্ণদাস, আর সেইত ব্রাহ্মণ ।\\nগঙ্গাতীর-পথে যাইবার বিজ্ঞ দুইজন ॥১৫৮॥
verses.transliteration: premī kṛṣṇadāsa, āra seita brāhmaṇa\\ngaṅgā-tīra-pathe yāibāra vijña dui-jana
verses.translation: Both Rājaputa Kṛṣṇadāsa and the Sanoḍiyā brāhmaṇa knew the path along the Ganges bank very well.

verses.devanagari: যাইতে এক বৃক্ষতলে প্রভু সবা লঞা ।\\nবসিলা, সবার পথ-শ্রান্তি দেখিয়া ॥১৫৯॥
verses.transliteration: yāite eka vṛkṣa-tale prabhu sabā lañā\\nvasilā, sabāra patha-śrānti dekhiyā
verses.translation: While walking, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, understanding that the others were fatigued, took them all beneath a tree and sat down.

verses.devanagari: সেই বৃক্ষ-নিকটে চরে বহু গাভীগণ ।\\nতাহা দেখি’ মহাপ্রভুর উল্লসিত মন ॥১৬০॥
verses.transliteration: sei vṛkṣa-nikaṭe care bahu gābhī-gaṇa\\ntāhā dekhi' mahāprabhura ullasita mana
verses.translation: There were many cows grazing near that tree, and the Lord was very pleased to see them.

verses.devanagari: আচম্বিতে এক গোপ বংশী বাজাইল ।\\nশুনি’ মহাপ্ৰভুর মহা-প্রেমাবেশ হৈল ॥১৬১॥
verses.transliteration: ācambite eka gopa vaṁśī bājāila\\nśuni' mahāprabhura mahā-premāveśa haila
verses.translation: Suddenly a cowherd boy blew on his flute, and immediately the Lord was struck with ecstatic love.

verses.devanagari: অচেতন হঞা প্রভু ভূমিতে পড়িলা ।\\nমুখে ফেনা পড়ে, নাশায় শ্বাস রুদ্ধ হৈলা ॥১৬২॥
verses.transliteration: acetana hañā prabhu bhūmite paḍilā\\nmukhe phenā paḍe, nāsāya śvāsa ruddha hailā
verses.translation: Filled with ecstatic love, the Lord fell unconscious to the ground. He foamed about the mouth, and His breathing stopped.

verses.devanagari: হেনকালে তাহাঁ আশোয়ার দশ আইলা ।\\nম্লেচ্ছ-পাঠান ঘোড়া হৈতে উত্তরিলা ॥১৬৩॥
verses.transliteration: hena-kāle tāhāṅ āśoyāra daśa āilā\\nmleccha-pāṭhāna ghoḍā haite uttarilā
verses.translation: While the Lord was unconscious, ten cavalry soldiers belonging to the Mohammedan Pāṭhāna military order rode up and dismounted.

verses.devanagari: প্রভুরে দেখিয়া ম্লেচ্ছ করয়ে বিচার ।\\nএই যতি-পাশ ছিল সুবর্ণ অপার ॥১৬৪॥
verses.transliteration: prabhure dekhiyā mleccha karaye vicāra\\nei yati-pāśa chila suvarṇa apāra
verses.translation: Seeing the Lord unconscious, the soldiers thought, "This sannyāsī must have possessed a large quantity of gold.

verses.devanagari: এই চারি বাটোয়ার ধুতুরা খাওয়াঞা ।\\nমারি’ ডারিয়াছে, যতির সব ধন লঞা ॥১৬৫॥
verses.transliteration: ei cāri bāṭoyāra dhuturā khāoyāñā\\nmāri' ḍāriyāche, yatira saba dhana lañā
verses.translation: "These four rogues here must have taken away that sannyāsī's riches after killing Him by making Him take the poison dhuturā."

verses.devanagari: তবে সেই পাঠান চারি-জনেরে বাঁধিল ।\\nকাটিতে চাহে, গৌড়িয়া সব কাঁপিতে লাগিল ॥১৬৬॥
verses.transliteration: tabe sei pāṭhāna cāri-janere bāṅdhila\\nkāṭite cāhe, gauḍiyā saba kāṅpite lāgila
verses.translation: Thinking this, the Pāṭhāna soldiers arrested the four persons and decided to kill them. Because of this, the two Bengalis began to tremble.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
The four persons were Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya, his assistant
brāhmaṇa,
Rājaputa Kṛṣṇadāsa and the Sanoḍiyā
brāhmaṇa
devotee of Mādhavendra Purī.

verses.devanagari: কৃষ্ণদাস — রাজপুত, নির্ভয় সে বড় ।\\nসেই বিপ্র — নির্ভয়, সে — মুখে বড় দড় ॥১৬৭॥
verses.transliteration: kṛṣṇadāsa—rājaputa, nirbhaya se baḍa\\nsei vipra—nirbhaya, se—mukhe baḍa daḍa
verses.translation: The devotee Kṛṣṇadāsa, who belonged to the Rājaputa race, was very fearless. The Sanoḍiyā brāhmaṇa was also fearless, and he spoke very bravely.

verses.devanagari: বিপ্র কহে, — পাঠান, তোমার পাৎসার দোহাই ।\\nচল তুমি আমি সিক্দার-পাশ যাই ॥১৬৮॥
verses.transliteration: vipra kahe,—pāṭhāna, tomāra pātsāra dohāi\\ncala tumi āmi sikdāra-pāśa yāi
verses.translation: The brāhmaṇa said, "You Pāṭhāna soldiers are all under the protection of your king. Let us go to your commander and get his decision.

verses.devanagari: এই যতি — আমার গুরু, আমি — মাথুর ব্রাহ্মণ ।\\nপাৎসার আগে আছে মোর ‘শত জন’ ॥১৬৯॥
verses.transliteration: ei yati—āmāra guru, āmi—māthura brāhmaṇa\\npātsāra āge āche mora 'śata jana'
verses.translation: "This sannyāsī is my spiritual master, and I am from Mathurā. I am a brāhmaṇa, and I know many people who are in the service of the Mohammedan king.

verses.devanagari: এই যতি ব্যাধিতে কভু হয়েন মূর্চ্ছিত ।\\nঅবঁহি চেতন পাইবে, হইবে সম্বিত ॥১৭০॥
verses.transliteration: ei yati vyādhite kabhu hayena mūrcchita\\nabaṅhi cetana pāibe, ha-ibe samvita
verses.translation: "This sannyāsī sometimes falls unconscious due to the influence of a disease. Please sit down here, and you will see that He will very soon regain consciousness and His normal condition.

verses.devanagari: ক্ষণেক ইহাঁ বৈস, বান্ধি’ রাখহ সবারে ।\\nইঁহাকে পুছিয়া, তবে মারিহ সবারে ॥১৭১॥
verses.transliteration: kṣaṇeka ihāṅ vaisa, bāndhi' rākhaha sabāre\\niṅhāke puchiyā, tabe māriha sabāre
verses.translation: "Sit down here for a while and keep us all under arrest. When the sannyāsī regains his senses, you can question Him. Then, if you like, you can kill us all."

verses.devanagari: পাঠান কহে, — তুমি পশ্চিমা মাথুর দুইজন ।\\n‘গৌড়িয়া’ ঠক্ এই কাঁপে দুইজন ॥১৭২॥
verses.transliteration: pāṭhāna kahe,—tumi paścimā māthura dui-jana\\n'gauḍiyā' ṭhak ei kāṅpe dui-jana
verses.translation: The Pāṭhāna soldiers said, "You are all rogues. Two of you belong to the district of Mathurā, and the other two, who are trembling, belong to Bengal."

verses.devanagari: কৃষ্ণদাস কহে, — আমার ঘর এই গ্রামে ।\\nদুইশত তুর্কী আছে, শতেক কামানে ॥১৭৩॥
verses.transliteration: kṛṣṇadāsa kahe,—āmāra ghara ei grāme\\ndui-śata turkī āche, śateka kāmāne
verses.translation: Rājaputa Kṛṣṇadāsa said, "I have my home here, and I also have about two hundred Turkish soldiers and about one hundred cannons.

verses.devanagari: এখনি আসিবে সব, আমি যদি ফুকারি ।\\nঘোড়া-পিড়া লুটি’ লবে তোমা-সবা মারি’ ॥১৭৪॥
verses.transliteration: ekhani āsibe saba, āmi yadi phukāri\\nghoḍā-piḍā luṭi' labe tomā-sabā māri'
verses.translation: "If I call loudly, they will come immediately to kill you and plunder your horses and saddles.

verses.devanagari: গৌড়িয়া — ‘বাটপাড়’ নহে, তুমি — ‘বাটপাড়’ ।\\nতীর্থবাসী লুঠ’, আর চাহ’ মারিবার ॥১৭৫॥
verses.transliteration: gauḍiyā—'bāṭapāḍa' nahe, tumi—'bāṭapāḍa'\\ntīrtha-vāsī luṭha', āra cāha' māribāra
verses.translation: "The Bengali pilgrims are not rogues. You are rogues, for you want to kill the pilgrims and plunder them."

verses.devanagari: শুনিয়া পাঠান মনে সঙ্কোচ হইল ।\\nহেনকালে মহাপ্রভু ‘চৈতন্য’ পাইল ॥১৭৬॥
verses.transliteration: śuniyā pāṭhāna mane saṅkoca ha-ila\\nhena-kāle mahāprabhu 'caitanya' pāila
verses.translation: Upon hearing this challenge, the Pāṭhāna soldiers became hesitant. Then suddenly Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu regained consciousness.

verses.devanagari: হুঙ্কার করিয়া উঠে, বলে ‘হরি’ ‘হরি’ ।\\nপ্রেমাবেশে নৃত্য করে ঊর্ধ্ববাহু করি’ ॥১৭৭॥
verses.transliteration: huṅkāra kariyā uṭhe, bale 'hari' 'hari'\\npremāveśe nṛtya kare ūrdhva-bāhu kari'
verses.translation: Coming to His senses, the Lord very loudly began chanting the holy name, "Hari! Hari!" The Lord raised His arms upward and began to dance in ecstatic love.

verses.devanagari: প্রেমাবেশে প্রভু যবে করেন চিৎকার ।\\nম্লেচ্ছের হৃদয়ে যেন লাগে শেলধার ॥১৭৮॥
verses.transliteration: premāveśe prabhu yabe karena citkāra\\nmlecchera hṛdaye yena lāge śeladhāra
verses.translation: When the Lord shouted very loudly in ecstatic love, it appeared to the Mohammedan soldiers that their hearts were struck by thunderbolts.

verses.devanagari: ভয় পাঞা ম্লেচ্ছ ছাড়ি’ দিল চারিজন ।\\nপ্রভু না দেখিল নিজ-গণের বন্ধন ॥১৭৯॥
verses.transliteration: bhaya pāñā mleccha chāḍi' dila cāri-jana\\nprabhu nā dekhila nija-gaṇera bandhana
verses.translation: Seized by fear, all the Pāṭhāna soldiers immediately released the four persons. Thus Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu did not see His personal associates arrested.

verses.devanagari: ভট্টাচার্য আসি’ প্রভুরে ধরি’ বসাইল ।\\nম্লেচ্ছগণ দেখি’ মহাপ্রভুর ‘বাহ্য’ হৈল ॥১৮০॥
verses.transliteration: bhaṭṭācārya āsi' prabhure dhari' vasāila\\nmleccha-gaṇa dekhi' mahāprabhura 'bāhya' haila
verses.translation: At that time, Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya went to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and made Him sit down. Seeing the Mohammedan soldiers, the Lord regained His normal senses.

verses.devanagari: ম্লেচ্ছগণ আসি’ প্রভুর বন্দিল চরণ ।\\nপ্রভু-আগে কহে, — এই ঠক্ চারিজন ॥১৮১॥
verses.transliteration: mleccha-gaṇa āsi' prabhura vandila caraṇa\\nprabhu-āge kahe,—ei ṭhak cāri-jana
verses.translation: All the Mohammedan soldiers then came before the Lord, worshiped His lotus feet and said, "Here are four rogues.

verses.devanagari: এই চারি মিলি’ তোমায় ধুতুরা খাওয়াঞা ।\\nতোমার ধন লৈল তোমায় পাগল করিয়া ॥১৮২॥
verses.transliteration: ei cāri mili' tomāya dhuturā khāoyāñā\\ntomāra dhana laila tomāya pāgala kariyā
verses.translation: "These rogues have made You take dhuturā. Having made You mad, they have taken all Your possessions."

verses.devanagari: প্রভু কহেন, — ঠক্ নহে, মোর ‘সঙ্গী’ জন ।\\nভিক্ষুক সন্ন্যাসী, মোর নাহি কিছু ধন ॥১৮৩॥
verses.transliteration: prabhu kahena,—ṭhak nahe, mora 'saṅgī' jana\\nbhikṣuka sannyāsī, mora nāhi kichu dhana
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "These are not rogues. They are My associates. Being a sannyāsī beggar, I do not possess anything.

verses.devanagari: মৃগী-ব্যাধিতে আমি কভু হই অচেতন ।\\nএই চারি দয়া করি’ করেন পালন ॥১৮৪॥
verses.transliteration: mṛgī-vyādhite āmi kabhu ha-i acetana\\nei cāri dayā kari' karena pālana
verses.translation: "Due to epilepsy, I sometimes fall unconscious. Out of their mercy, these four men maintain Me."

verses.devanagari: সেই ম্লেচ্ছ-মধ্যে এক পরম গম্ভীর ।\\nকাল বস্ত্র পরে সেই, — লোকে কহে ‘পীর’ ॥১৮৫॥
verses.transliteration: sei mleccha-madhye eka parama gambhīra\\nkāla vastra pare sei,—loke kahe 'pīra'
verses.translation: Among the Mohammedans was a grave person who was wearing a black dress. People called him a saintly person.

verses.devanagari: চিত্ত আর্দ্র হৈল তাঁর প্রভুরে দেখিয়া ।\\n‘নির্বিশেষ-ব্রহ্ম’ স্থাপে স্বশাস্ত্র উঠাঞা ॥১৮৬॥
verses.transliteration: citta ārdra haila tāṅra prabhure dekhiyā\\n'nirviśeṣa-brahma' sthāpe svaśāstra uṭhāñā
verses.translation: The heart of that saintly person softened upon seeing Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. He wanted to talk to Him and establish impersonal Brahman on the basis of his own scripture, the Koran.

verses.devanagari: ‘অদ্বৈত-ব্রহ্মবাদ’ সেই করিল স্থাপন ।\\nতার শাস্ত্রযুক্ত্যে তারে প্রভু কৈলা খণ্ডন ॥১৮৭॥
verses.transliteration: 'advaita-brahma-vāda' sei karila sthāpana\\ntāra śāstra-yuktye tāre prabhu kailā khaṇḍana
verses.translation: When that person established the impersonal Brahman conception of the Absolute Truth on the basis of the Koran, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu refuted his argument.

verses.devanagari: যেই যেই কহিল, প্রভু সকলি খণ্ডিল ।\\nউত্তর না আইসে মুখে, মহাস্তব্ধ হৈল ॥১৮৮॥
verses.transliteration: yei yei kahila, prabhu sakali khaṇḍila\\nuttara nā āise mukhe, mahā-stabdha haila
verses.translation: Whatever arguments he put forward, the Lord refuted them all. Finally the person became stunned and could not speak.

verses.devanagari: প্রভু কহে, — তোমার শাস্ত্র স্থাপে ‘নির্বিশেষে’ ।\\nতাহা খণ্ডি’ ‘সবিশেষ’ স্থাপিয়াছে শেষে ॥১৮৯॥
verses.transliteration: prabhu kahe,—tomāra śāstra sthāpe 'nirviśeṣe'\\ntāhā khaṇḍi' 'saviśeṣa' sthāpiyāche śeṣe
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "The Koran has certainly established impersonalism, but at the end it refutes that impersonalism and establishes the personal God.

verses.devanagari: তোমার শাস্ত্রে কহে শেষে ‘একই ঈশ্বর’ ।\\n‘সর্বৈশ্বর্যপূর্ণ তেঁহো — শ্যাম-কলেবর ॥১৯০॥
verses.transliteration: tomāra śāstre kahe śeṣe 'eka-i īśvara'\\n'sarvaiśvarya-pūrṇa teṅho—śyāma-kalevara
verses.translation: "The Koran accepts the fact that ultimately there is only one God. He is full of opulence, and His bodily complexion is blackish.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
The revealed scripture of the Mohammedans is the Koran. There is one Mohammedan
sampradāya
known as the Sufis. The Sufis accept impersonalism, believing in the oneness of the living entity with the Absolute Truth. Their supreme slogan is
"analahak.
" The Sufi
sampradāya
was certainly derived from Śaṅkarācārya's impersonalists.

verses.devanagari: সচ্চিদানন্দ-দেহ, পূর্ণব্রহ্ম-স্বরূপ ।\\n‘সর্বাত্মা’, ‘সর্বজ্ঞ’, নিত্য সর্বাদি-স্বরূপ ॥১৯১॥
verses.transliteration: sac-cid-ānanda-deha, pūrṇa-brahma-svarūpa\\n'sarvātmā', 'sarvajña', nitya sarvādi-svarūpa
verses.translation: "According to the Koran, the Lord has a supreme, blissful, transcendental body. He is the Absolute Truth, the all-pervading, omniscient and eternal being. He is the origin of everything.

verses.devanagari: সৃষ্টি, স্থিতি, প্রলয় তাঁহা হৈতে হয় ।\\nস্থূল-সূক্ষ্ম-জগতের তেঁহো সমাশ্রয় ॥১৯২॥
verses.transliteration: sṛṣṭi, sthiti, pralaya tāṅhā haite haya\\nsthūla-sūkṣma-jagatera teṅho samāśraya
verses.translation: "Creation, maintenance and dissolution come from Him. He is the original shelter of all gross and subtle cosmic manifestations.

verses.devanagari: ‘সর্ব-শ্রেষ্ঠ, সর্বারাধ্য, কারণের কারণ ।\\nতাঁর ভক্ত্যে হয় জীবের সংসার-তারণ ॥১৯৩॥
verses.transliteration: sarva-śreṣṭha, sarvārādhya, kāraṇera kāraṇa\\ntāṅra bhaktye haya jīvera saṁsāra-tāraṇa
verses.translation: "The Lord is the Supreme Truth worshipable by everyone. He is the cause of all causes. By engaging in His devotional service, the living entity is relieved from material existence.

verses.devanagari: তাঁর সেবা বিনা জীবের না যায় ‘সংসার’ ।\\nতাঁহার চরণে প্রীতি — ‘পুরুষার্থ-সার’ ॥১৯৪॥
verses.transliteration: tāṅra sevā vinā jīvera nā yāya 'saṁsāra'\\ntāṅhāra caraṇe prīti—'puruṣārtha-sāra'
verses.translation: "No conditioned soul can get out of material bondage without serving the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Love at His lotus feet is the ultimate goal of life.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
According to the Mohammedan scripture, without
evādat,
offering prayers at a mosque or elsewhere five times daily (
namāja
), one cannot be successful in life. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu pointed out that in the revealed scripture of the Mohammedans, love of Godhead is the ultimate goal.
Karma-yoga
and
jñāna-yoga
are certainly described in the Koran, but ultimately the Koran states that the ultimate goal is the offering of prayers to the Supreme Person (
evādat
).

verses.devanagari: মোক্ষাদি আনন্দ যার নহে এক ‘কণ’ ।\\nপূর্ণানন্দ-প্রাপ্তি তাঁর চরণ-সেবন ॥১৯৫॥
verses.transliteration: mokṣādi ānanda yāra nahe eka 'kaṇa'\\npūrṇānanda-prāpti tāṅra caraṇa-sevana
verses.translation: "The happiness of liberation, whereby one merges into the Lord's existence, cannot even be compared to a fragment of the transcendental bliss obtained by service unto the Lord's lotus feet.

verses.devanagari: ‘কর্ম’, ‘জ্ঞান’, ‘যোগ’ আগে করিয়া স্থাপন ।\\nসব খণ্ডি’ স্থাপে ‘ঈশ্বর’, ‘তাঁহার সেবন’ ॥১৯৬॥
verses.transliteration: 'karma', jñāna', 'yoga' āge kariyā sthāpana\\nsaba khaṇḍi' sthāpe 'īśvara', 'tāṅhāra sevana'
verses.translation: "In the Koran there are descriptions of fruitive activity, speculative knowledge, mystic power and union with the Supreme, but ultimately everything is refuted as the Lord's personal feature and His devotional service is established.

verses.devanagari: তোমার পণ্ডিত-সবার নাহি শাস্ত্র-জ্ঞান ।\\nপূর্বাপর-বিধি-মধ্যে ‘পর’ — বলবান্ ॥১৯৭॥
verses.transliteration: tomāra paṇḍita-sabāra nāhi śāstra-jñāna\\npūrvāpara-vidhi-madhye 'para'—balavān
verses.translation: "The scholars of the Koran are not very advanced in knowledge. Although there are many methods prescribed, they do not know that the ultimate conclusion should be considered the most powerful.

verses.devanagari: নিজ-শাস্ত্র দেখি’ তুমি বিচার করিয়া ।\\nকি লিখিয়াছে শেষে কহ নির্ণয় করিয়া ॥১৯৮॥
verses.transliteration: nija-śāstra dekhi' tumi vicāra kariyā\\nki likhiyāche śeṣe kaha nirṇaya kariyā
verses.translation: "Seeing your own Koran and deliberating over what is written there, what is your conclusion?"

verses.devanagari: ম্লেচ্ছ কহে, — যেই কহ, সেই ‘সত্য’ হয় ।\\nশাস্ত্রে লিখিয়াছে, কেহ লইতে না পারয় ॥১৯৯॥
verses.transliteration: mleccha kahe,—yei kaha, sei 'satya' haya\\nśāstre likhiyāche, keha la-ite nā pāraya
verses.translation: The saintly Mohammedan replied, "All that You have said is true. This has certainly been written in the Koran, but our scholars can neither understand nor accept it.

verses.devanagari: ‘নির্বিশেষ-গোসাঞি’ লঞা করেন ব্যাখ্যান ।\\n‘সাকার-গোসাঞি’ — সেব্য, কারো নাহি জ্ঞান ॥২০০॥
verses.transliteration: 'nirviśeṣa-gosāñi' lañā karena vyākhyāna\\n'sākāra-gosāñi'—sevya, kāro nāhi jñāna
verses.translation: "Usually they describe the Lord's impersonal aspect, but they hardly know that the Lord's personal feature is worshipable. They are undoubtedly lacking this knowledge.
verses.purport: PURPORT\nThe saintly Mohammedan admitted that those who were supposedly conversant in the teachings of the Koran could not ultimately understand the essence of the Koran. Because of this, they accepted only the Lord's impersonal feature. Generally they recite and explain this portion only. Although the transcendental body of the Lord is worshipable, most of them are unaware of this.

verses.devanagari: সেইত ‘গোসাঞি’ তুমি — সাক্ষাৎ ‘ঈশ্বর’ ।\\nমোরে কৃপা কর, মুঞি — অযোগ্য পামর ॥২০১॥
verses.transliteration: seita 'gosāñi' tumi—sākṣāt 'īśvara'\\nmore kṛpā kara, muñi—ayogya pāmara
verses.translation: "Since You are that very same Supreme Personality of Godhead Himself, please be merciful upon me. I am fallen and unfit.

verses.devanagari: অনেক দেখিনু মুঞি ম্লেচ্ছ-শাস্ত্র হৈতে ।\\n‘সাধ্য-সাধন-বস্তু’ নারি নির্ধারিতে ॥২০২॥
verses.transliteration: aneka dekhinu muñi mleccha-śāstra haite\\n'sādhya-sādhana-vastu' nāri nirdhārite
verses.translation: "I have studied the Mohammedan scripture very extensively, but from it I cannot conclusively decide what the ultimate goal of life is or how I can approach it.

verses.devanagari: তোমা দেখি’ জিহ্বা মোর বলে ‘কৃষ্ণনাম’ ।\\n‘আমি — বড় জ্ঞানী’ — এই গেল অভিমান ॥২০৩॥
verses.transliteration: tomā dekhi' jihvā mora bale 'kṛṣṇa-nāma'\\n'āmi—baḍa jñānī'—ei gela ābhimāna
verses.translation: "Now that I have seen You, my tongue is chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā mantra. The false prestige I felt from being a learned scholar is now gone."

verses.devanagari: কৃপা করি’ বল মোরে ‘সাধ্য-সাধনে’ ।\\nএত বলি’ পড়ে মহাপ্রভুর চরণে ॥২০৪॥
verses.transliteration: kṛpā kari' bala more 'sādhya-sādhane'\\neta bali' paḍe mahāprabhura caraṇe
verses.translation: Saying this, the saintly Mohammedan fell at the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and requested Him to speak of life's ultimate goal and the process by which it could be obtained.

verses.devanagari: প্রভু কহে, — উঠ, কৃষ্ণনাম তুমি লইলা ।\\nকোটি-জন্মের পাপ গেল, ‘পবিত্র’ হইলা ॥২০৫॥
verses.transliteration: prabhu kahe,—uṭha, kṛṣṇa-nāma tumi la-ilā\\nkoṭi-janmera pāpa gela, 'pavitra' ha-ilā
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "Please get up. You have chanted the holy name of Kṛṣṇa; therefore the sinful reactions you have accrued for many millions of lives are now gone. You are now pure."

verses.devanagari: ‘কৃষ্ণ’ কহ, ‘কৃষ্ণ’ কহ, — কৈলা উপদেশ ।\\nসবে ‘কৃষ্ণ’ কহে, সবার হৈল প্রেমাবেশ ॥২০৬॥
verses.transliteration: 'kṛṣṇa' kaha, 'kṛṣṇa' kaha,—kailā upadeśa\\nsabe'kṛṣṇa' kahe, sabāra haila premāveśa
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then told all the Mohammedans there, "Chant the holy name of Kṛṣṇa! Chant the holy name of Kṛṣṇa!" As they all began to chant, they were overwhelmed by ecstatic love.

verses.devanagari: ‘রামদাস’ বলি’ প্রভু তাঁর কৈল নাম ।\\nআর এক পাঠান, তাঁর নাম — ‘বিজুলী-খাঁন’ ॥২০৭॥
verses.transliteration: 'rāmadāsa' bali' prabhu tāṅra kaila nāma\\nāra eka pāṭhāna, tāṅra nāma—'vijulī-khāṅna'
verses.translation: In this way Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu indirectly initiated the saintly Mohammedan by advising him to chant the holy name of Kṛṣṇa. The Mohammedan's name was changed to Rāmadāsa. There was also another Pāṭhāna Moslem present whose name was Vijulī Khān.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
After being initiated, the devotees in the Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement change their names. Whenever a person in the Western world becomes interested in this Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement, he is initiated by this process. In India we are falsely accused of converting
mlecchas
and
yavanas
into the Hindu religion. In India there are many Māyāvādī
sannyāsīs
known as
jagad-guru,
although they have hardly visited the whole world. Some are not even sufficiently educated, yet they make accusations against our movement and accuse us of destroying the principles of the Hindu religion by accepting Mohammedans and
yavanas
as Vaiṣṇavas. Such people are simply envious. We are not spoiling the Hindu system of religion but are simply following in the footsteps of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu by traveling all over the world and accepting those who are interested in understanding Kṛṣṇa as Kṛṣṇadāsa or Rāmadāsa. By the process of a bona fide initiation, their names are changed.

verses.devanagari: অল্প বয়স তাঁর, রাজার কুমার ।\\n‘রামদাস’ আদি পাঠান — চাকর তাঁহার ॥২০৮॥
verses.transliteration: alpa vayasa tāṅra, rājāra kumāra\\n'rāmadāsa' ādi pāṭhāna—cākara tāṅhāra
verses.translation: Vijulī Khān was very young, and he was the son of the king. All the other Mohammedans, Pāṭhānas, headed by Rāmadāsa, were his servants.

verses.devanagari: ‘কৃষ্ণ’ বলি’ পড়ে সেই মহাপ্রভুর পায় ।\\nপ্রভু শ্রীচরণ দিল তাঁহার মাথায় ॥২০৯॥
verses.transliteration: 'kṛṣṇa' bali' paḍe sei mahāprabhura pāya\\nprabhu śrī-caraṇa dila tāṅhāra māthāya
verses.translation: Vijulī Khān also fell down at the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and the Lord placed His foot on his head.

verses.devanagari: তাঁ-সবারে কৃপা করি’ প্রভু ত’ চলিলা ।\\nসেইত পাঠান সব ‘বৈরাগী’ হইলা ॥২১০॥
verses.transliteration: tāṅ-sabāre kṛpā kari' prabhu ta' calilā\\nseita pāṭhāna saba 'vairāgī' ha-ilā
verses.translation: Bestowing His mercy upon them in this way, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu left. All the Pāṭhāna Mohammedans then became mendicants.

verses.devanagari: পাঠান-বৈষ্ণব’ বলি, হৈল তাঁর খ্যাতি ।\\nসর্বত্র গাহিয়া বুলে মহাপ্রভুর কীর্তি ॥২১১॥
verses.transliteration: pāṭhāna-vaiṣṇava bali' haila tāṅra khyāti\\nsarvatra gāhiyā bule mahāprabhura kīrti
verses.translation: Later these very Pāṭhānas became celebrated as the Pāṭhāna Vaiṣṇavas. They toured all over the country and chanted the glorious activities of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

verses.devanagari: সেই বিজুলী-খাঁন হৈল ‘মহাভাগবত’ ।\\nসর্বতীর্থে হৈল তাঁর পরম-মহত্ত্ব ॥২১২॥
verses.transliteration: sei vijulī-khāṅna haila 'mahā-bhāgavata'\\nsarva-tīrthe haila tāṅra parama-mahattva
verses.translation: Vijulī Khān became a greatly advanced devotee, and his importance was celebrated at every holy place of pilgrimage.

verses.devanagari: ঐছে লীলা করে প্রভু শ্রীকৃষ্ণচৈতন্য ।\\n‘পশ্চিমে’ আসিয়া কৈল যবনাদি ধন্য ॥২১৩॥
verses.transliteration: aiche līlā kare prabhu śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya\\n'paścime' āsiyā kaila yavanādi dhanya
verses.translation: In this way Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu performed His pastimes. Coming to the western part of India, He bestowed good fortune upon the yavanas and mlecchas.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
The word
yavana
means "meat-eater." Anyone from a meat-eating community is called a
yavana.
One who does not strictly observe the Vedic regulative principles is called a
mleccha.
These words do not refer to any particular man. Even if a person is born in a
brāhmaṇa, kṣatriya, vaiśya
or
śūdra
family, he is a
mleccha
or
yavana
if he does not strictly follow the regulative principles or if he eats meat.

verses.devanagari: সোরোক্ষেত্রে আসি’ প্রভু কৈলা গঙ্গাস্নান ।\\nগঙ্গাতীর-পথে কৈলা প্রয়াগে প্রয়াণ ॥২১৪॥
verses.transliteration: soro-kṣetre āsi' prabhu kailā gaṅgā-snāna\\ngaṅgā-tīra-pathe kailā prayāge prayāṇa
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu next went to a holy place of pilgrimage called Soro-kṣetra. He took His bath in the Ganges there and started for Prayāga on the path along the banks of the Ganges.

verses.devanagari: সেই বিপ্রে, কৃষ্ণদাসে, প্রভু বিদায় দিলা ।\\nযোড়-হাতে দুইজন কহিতে লাগিলা ॥২১৫॥
verses.transliteration: sei vipre, kṛṣṇadāse, prabhu vidāya dilā\\nyoḍa-hāte dui-jana kahite lāgilā
verses.translation: At Soro-kṣetra, the Lord requested the Sanoḍiyā brāhmaṇa and Rājaputa Kṛṣṇadāsa to return home, but with folded hands they began to speak as follows.

verses.devanagari: প্রয়াগ-পর্যন্ত দুঁহে তোমা-সঙ্গে যাব ।\\nতোমার চরণ-সঙ্গ পুনঃ কাহাঁ পাব ? ॥ ২১৬ ॥
verses.transliteration: prayāga-paryanta duṅhe tomā-saṅge yāba\\ntomāra caraṇa-saṅga punaḥ kāhāṅ pāba?
verses.translation: They prayed, "Let us go to Prayāga with You. If we do not go, when shall we again get the association of Your lotus feet?

verses.devanagari: ম্লেচ্ছদেশ, কেহ কাহাঁ করয়ে উৎপাত ।\\nভট্টাচার্য — পণ্ডিত, কহিতে না জানেন বাত়্ ॥২১৭॥
verses.transliteration: mleccha-deśa, keha kāhāṅ karaye utpāta\\nbhaṭṭācārya—paṇḍita, kahite nā jānena vāt
verses.translation: "This country is mainly occupied by Mohammedans. At any place someone can create a disturbance, and although Your companion Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya is a learned scholar, he does not know how to speak the local language."

verses.devanagari: শুনি’ মহাপ্রভু ঈষৎ হাসিতে লাগিলা ।\\nসেই দুইজন প্রভুর সঙ্গে চলি’ আইলা ॥২১৮॥
verses.transliteration: śuni' mahāprabhu īṣat hāsite lāgilā\\nsei dui-jana prabhura saṅge cali' āilā
verses.translation: Hearing this, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu accepted their proposal by smiling mildly. Thus those two persons continued to accompany Him.

verses.devanagari: যেই যেই জন প্রভুর পাইল দরশন ।\\nসেই প্রেমে মত্ত হয়, করে কৃষ্ণ-সংকীর্তন ॥২১৯॥
verses.transliteration: yei yei jana prabhura pāila daraśana\\nsei preme matta haya, kare kṛṣṇa-saṅkīrtana
verses.translation: Whoever got to see Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu would feel himself overwhelmed with ecstatic love and would begin to chant the Hare Kṛṣṇa mantra.

verses.devanagari: তাঁর সঙ্গে অন্যোন্যে, তাঁর সঙ্গে আন ।\\nএইমত ‘বৈষ্ণব’ কৈলা সব দেশ-গ্রাম ॥২২০॥
verses.transliteration: tāṅra saṅge anyonye, tāṅra saṅge āna\\nei-mata 'vaiṣṇava' kailā saba deśa-grāma
verses.translation: Whoever met Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu became a Vaiṣṇava, and whoever met that Vaiṣṇava also became a Vaiṣṇava. In this way, all the towns and villages one after the other became Vaiṣṇava.

verses.devanagari: দক্ষিণ যাইতে যৈছে শক্তি প্রকাশিলা ।\\nসেইমত পশ্চিম দেশ, প্রেমে ভাসাইলা ॥২২১॥
verses.transliteration: dakṣiṇa yāite yaiche śakti prakāśilā\\nsei-mata paścima deśa, preme bhāsāilā
verses.translation: Just as the Lord inundated South India on His tour there, He also inundated the western part of the country with love of Godhead.
verses.purport: PURPORT\nAccording to some opinions, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu visited Kurukṣetra while going to Prayāga from Vṛndāvana. There is a temple of Bhadra-kālī in Kurukṣetra, and near that temple there is a temple containing the Deity of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

verses.devanagari: এইমত চলি’ প্রভু ‘প্রয়াগ’ আইলা ।\\nদশ-দিন ত্রিবেণীতে মকর-স্নান কৈলা ॥২২২॥
verses.transliteration: ei-mata cali' prabhu 'prayāga' āilā\\ndaśa-dina triveṇīte makara-snāna kailā
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu finally arrived at Prayāga and for ten successive days bathed in the confluence of the Rivers Yamunā and Ganges during the festival of Makara-saṅkrānti [Māgha-melā].
verses.purport:
PURPORT
Actually the word
triveṇī
indicates the confluence of three rivers-namely the Ganges, Yamunā and Sarasvatī. Presently the Sarasvatī River is not visible, but the River Ganges and the River Yamunā merge at Allahabad.

verses.devanagari: বৃন্দাবন-গমন, প্রভু-চরিত্র অনন্ত ।\\n‘সহস্র-বদন’ যাঁর নাহি পা’ন অন্ত ॥২২৩॥
verses.transliteration: vṛndāvana-gamana, prabhu-caritra ananta\\n'sahasra-vadana' yāṅra nāhi pā'na anta
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's visit to Vṛndāvana and His activities there are unlimited. Even Lord Śeṣa, who has thousands of hoods, cannot reach the end of His activities.

verses.devanagari: তাহা কে কহিতে পারে ক্ষুদ্র জীব হঞা ।\\nদিগ্-দরশন কৈলুঁ মুঞি সূত্র করিয়া ॥২২৪॥
verses.transliteration: tāhā ke kahite pāre kṣudra jīva hañā\\ndig-daraśana kailuṅ muñi sūtra kariyā
verses.translation: What ordinary living being can describe the pastimes of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu? I have only indicated the general direction in the form of codes.

verses.devanagari: অলৌকিক-লীলা প্রভুর অলৌকিক-রীতি ।\\nশুনিলেও ভাগ্যহীনের না হয় প্রতীতি ॥২২৫॥
verses.transliteration: alaukika-līlā prabhura alaukika-rīti\\nśunileo bhāgya-hīnera nā haya pratīti
verses.translation: The pastimes and methods of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu are uncommon. Unfortunate is he who cannot believe even after hearing all these things.

verses.devanagari: আদ্যোপান্ত চৈতন্যলীলা — ‘অলৌকিক’ জান’ ।\\nশ্রদ্ধা করি’ শুন ইহা, ‘সত্য’ করি’ মান’ ॥২২৬॥
verses.transliteration: ādyopānta caitanya-līlā—'alaukika' jāna'\\nśraddhā kari' śuna ihā, 'satya' kari' māna'
verses.translation: From beginning to end the pastimes of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu are uncommon. Just hear them with faith and accept them as true and correct.

verses.devanagari: যেই তর্ক করে ইহাঁ, সেই — ‘মূর্খরাজ’ ।\\nআপনার মুণ্ডে সে আপনি পাড়ে বাজ ॥২২৭॥
verses.transliteration: yei tarka kare ihāṅ, sei—'mūrkha-rāja'\\nāpanāra muṇḍe se āpani pāḍe vāja
verses.translation: Whoever argues about this is a great fool. He intentionally and personally brings a thunderbolt down upon his head.

verses.devanagari: চৈতন্য-চরিত্র এই — ‘অমৃতের সিন্ধু’ ।\\nজগৎ আনন্দে ভাসায় যার একবিন্দু ॥২২৮॥
verses.transliteration: caitanya-caritra ei—'amṛtera sindhu'\\njagat ānande bhāsāya yāra eka-bindu
verses.translation: The pastimes of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu are an ocean of nectar. Even a drop of this ocean can inundate the whole world with transcendental bliss.

verses.devanagari: শ্রীরূপ-রঘুনাথ-পদে যার আশ ।\\nচৈতন্যচরিতামৃত কহে কৃষ্ণদাস ॥২২৯॥
verses.transliteration: śrī-rūpa-raghunātha-pade yāra āśa\\ncaitanya-caritāmṛta kahe kṛṣṇadāsa
verses.translation: Praying at the lotus feet of Śrī Rūpa and Śrī Raghunātha, always desiring their mercy, I, Kṛṣṇadāsa, narrate Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, following in their footsteps.
verses.purport: PURPORT\nThus end the Bhaktivedanta purports of the Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā,  Eighteenth Chapter, describing the Lord's visit to Śrī Vṛndāvana and His conversion of the Mohammedan soldiers on the way to Prayāga.

sections.title: Chapter 19: Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu Instructs Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī

verses.devanagari: বৃন্দাবনীয়াং রসকেলিবার্তাং\\nকালেন লুপ্তাং নিজশক্তিমুৎকঃ ।\\nসঞ্চার্য রূপে ব্যতনোৎ পুনঃ স\\nপ্রভুর্বিধৌ প্রাগিব লোকসৃষ্টিম্ ॥১॥
verses.transliteration: vṛndāvanīyāṁ rasa-keli-vārtāṁ\\nkālena luptāṁ nija-śaktim utkaḥ\\nsañcārya rūpe vyatanot punaḥ sa\\nprabhur vidhau prāg iva loka-sṛṣṭim
verses.translation: Before the creation of this cosmic manifestation, the Lord enlightened the heart of Lord Brahmā with the details of the creation and manifested the Vedic knowledge. In exactly the same way, the Lord, being anxious to revive the Vṛndāvana pastimes of Lord Kṛṣṇa, impregnated the heart of Rūpa Gosvāmī with spiritual potency. By this potency, Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī could revive the activities of Kṛṣṇa in Vṛndāvana, activities almost lost to memory. In this way, He spread Kṛṣṇa consciousness throughout the world.

verses.devanagari: জয় জয় শ্রীচৈতন্য জয় নিত্যানন্দ ।\\nজয়াদ্বৈতচন্দ্র জয় গৌরভক্তবৃন্দ ॥২॥
verses.transliteration: jaya jaya śrī-caitanya jaya nityānanda\\njayādvaita-candra jaya gaura-bhakta-vṛnda
verses.translation: All glories to Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu! All glories to Lord Nityānanda! All glories to Advaitacandra! And all glories to all the devotees of the Lord!

verses.devanagari: শ্রীরূপ-সনাতন রহে রামকেলি-গ্রামে ।\\nপ্রভুরে মিলিয়া গেলা আপন-ভবনে ॥৩॥
verses.transliteration: śrī-rūpa-sanātana rahe rāmakeli-grāme\\nprabhure miliyā gelā āpana-bhavane
verses.translation: After meeting Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu in the village of Rāmakeli, the brothers Rūpa and Sanātana returned to their homes.

verses.devanagari: দুইভাই বিষয়-ত্যাগের উপায় সৃজিল ।\\nবহুধন দিয়া দুই ব্রাহ্মণে বরিল ॥৪॥
verses.transliteration: dui-bhāi viṣaya-tyāgera upāya sṛjila\\nbhau-dhana diyā dui brāhmaṇe varila
verses.translation: The two brothers devised a means whereby they could give up their material activities. For this purpose, they appointed two brāhmaṇas and paid them a large amount of money.

verses.devanagari: কৃষ্ণমন্ত্রে করাইল দুই পুরশ্চরণ ।\\nঅচিরাৎ পাইবারে চৈতন্য-চরণ ॥৫॥
verses.transliteration: kṛṣṇa-mantre karāila dui puraścaraṇa\\nacirāt pāibāre caitanya-caraṇa
verses.translation: The brāhmaṇas performed religious ceremonies and chanted the holy name of Kṛṣṇa so that the two brothers might attain shelter at the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu very soon.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
A
puraścaraṇa
is a ritualistic ceremony performed under the guidance of an expert spiritual master or a
brāhmaṇa.
It is performed for the fulfillment of certain desires. One rises early in the morning, chants the Hare Kṛṣṇa
mantra,
performs
arcana
by the
ārati
ceremony and worships the Deities. These activities are described in the Fifteenth Chapter, verse 108.

verses.devanagari: শ্রীরূপ-গোসাঞি তবে নৌকাতে ভরিয়া ।\\nআপনার ঘরে আইলা বহুধন লঞা ॥৬॥
verses.transliteration: śrī-rūpa-gosāñi tabe naukāte bhariyā\\nśrī-rūpa-gosāñi āpanāra ghare āilā bahu-dhana lañā
verses.translation: At this time, Śrī Rūpa Gosvāmī returned home, taking with him large quantities of riches loaded in boats.

verses.devanagari: ব্রাহ্মণ-বৈষ্ণবে দিলা তার অর্ধ-ধনে ।\\nএক চৌঠি ধন দিলা কুটুম্ব-ভরণে ॥৭॥
verses.transliteration: brāhmaṇa-vaiṣṇave dilā tāra ardha-dhane\\neka cauṭhi dhana dilā kuṭumba-bharaṇe
verses.translation: Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī divided the wealth that he brought back home. He gave fifty percent in charity to brāhmaṇas and Vaiṣṇavas and twenty-five percent to his relatives.
verses.purport: PURPORT\nThis is a practical example of how one should divide his money and retire from household life. Fifty percent of one's money should be distributed to qualified and pure devotees of the Lord. Twenty-five percent may be given to family members, and twenty-five percent may be kept for personal use in case of emergency.

verses.devanagari: দণ্ডবন্ধ লাগি’ চৌঠি সঞ্চয় করিলা ।\\nভাল-ভাল বিপ্র-স্থানে স্থাপ্য রাখিলা ॥৮॥
verses.transliteration: daṇḍa-bandha lāgi' cauṭhi sañcaya karilā\\nbhāla-bhāla vipra-sthāne sthāpya rākhilā
verses.translation: He kept one-fourth of his wealth with a respectable brāhmaṇa. He kept this for his personal safety because he was expecting some legal complications.

verses.devanagari: গৌড়ে রাখিল মুদ্রা দশ-হাজারে ।\\nসনাতন ব্যয় করে, রাখে মুদি-ঘরে ॥৯॥
verses.transliteration: gauḍe rākhila mudrā daśa-hājāre\\nsanātana vyaya kare, rākhe mudi-ghare
verses.translation: He deposited ten thousand coins, which were later spent by Śrī Sanātana Gosvāmī, in the custody of a local Bengali grocer.

verses.devanagari: শ্রীরূপ শুনিল প্রভুর নীলাদ্রি-গমন ।\\nবনপথে যাবেন প্রভু শ্রীবৃন্দাবন ॥১০॥
verses.transliteration: śrī-rūpa śunila prabhura nīlādri-gamana\\nvana-pathe yābena prabhu śrī-vṛndāvana
verses.translation: Śrī Rūpa Gosvāmī heard that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu had returned to Jagannātha Purī and was preparing to go to Vṛndāvana through the forest.

verses.devanagari: রূপ-গোসাঞি নীলাচলে পাঠাইল দুইজন ।\\nপ্রভু যবে বৃন্দাবন করেন গমন ॥১১॥
verses.transliteration: rūpa-gosāñi nīlācale pāṭhāila dui-jana\\nprabhu yabe vṛndāvana karena gamana
verses.translation: Śrī Rūpa Gosvāmī sent two people to Jagannātha Purī to find out when Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu would depart for Vṛndāvana.

verses.devanagari: শীঘ্র আসি’ মোরে তাঁর দিবা সমাচার ।\\nশুনিয়া তদনুরূপ করিব ব্যবহার ॥১২॥
verses.transliteration: śīghra āsi' more tāṅra dibā samācāra\\nśuniyā tad-anurūpa kariba vyavahāra
verses.translation: Śrī Rūpa Gosvāmī told the two men, "You are to return quickly and let me know when He will depart. Then I shall make the proper arrangements."

verses.devanagari: এথা সনাতন-গোসাঞি ভাবে মনে মন ।\\nরাজা মোরে প্রীতি করে, সে — মোর বন্ধন ॥১৩॥
verses.transliteration: ethā sanātana-gosāñi bhāve mane mana\\nrājā more prīti kare, se—mora bandhana
verses.translation: While Sanātana Gosvāmī was at Gauḍa-deśa, he was thinking, "The Nawab is very pleased with me. I certainly have an obligation.

verses.devanagari: কোন মতে রাজা যদি মোরে ক্রুদ্ধ হয় ।\\nতবে অব্যাহতি হয়, করিলুঁ নিশ্চয় ॥১৪॥
verses.transliteration: kona mate rājā yadi more kruddha haya\\ntabe avyāhati haya, kariluṅ niścaya
verses.translation: "Somehow or other, if the Nawab becomes angry with me, I shall be greatly relieved. That is my conclusion."

verses.devanagari: অস্বাস্থ্যের ছদ্ম করি’ রহে নিজ-ঘরে ।\\nরাজকার্য ছাড়িলা, না যায় রাজদ্বারে ॥১৫॥
verses.transliteration: asvāsthyera chadma kari' rahe nija-ghare\\nrāja-kārya chāḍilā, nā yāya rāja-dvāre
verses.translation: On the pretext of bad health, Sanātana Gosvāmī remained home. Thus he gave up government service and did not go to the royal court.

verses.devanagari: লোভী কায়স্থগণ রাজকার্য করে ।\\nআপনে স্বগৃহে করে শাস্ত্রের বিচারে ॥১৬॥
verses.transliteration: lobhī kāyastha-gaṇa rāja-kārya kare\\nāpane svagṛhe kare śāstrera vicāre
verses.translation: The greedy masters of his clerical and secretarial staff performed the government duties while Sanātana personally remained home and discussed revealed scriptures.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
Sanātana Gosvāmī was the minister in charge of the government secretariat, and his assistants—the undersecretaries and clerks-all belonged to the
kāyastha
community. Formerly the
kāyasthas
belonged to the clerical and secretarial staff of the government, and later if one served in such a post, he was called a
kāyastha.
Eventually if a person could not identify himself as a
brāhmaṇa, kṣatriya, vaiśya
or
śūdra,
he used to introduce himself as a
kāyastha
to get a wealthy and honorable position. In Bengal it is said that if one cannot give the identity of his caste, he calls himself a
kāyastha.
On the whole, the
kāyastha
community is a mixture of all castes, and it especially includes those engaged in clerical or secretarial work. Materially such people are always busy occupying responsible government posts.
When Sanātana Gosvāmī was relaxing and feeling inclined to retire from government service, many
kāyasthas
on his secretarial staff were very eager to occupy his post. In this regard, Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura states that when Sanātana Gosvāmī was a government minister and the
kāyasthas
who assisted him saw that he was reluctant to continue, they became very expert in their duties. Sanātana Gosvāmī was a
brāhmaṇa
belonging to the Sārasvata
brāhmaṇa
community. It is said that when he resigned, an underworker named Purandara Khān, who was a
kāyastha,
occupied his post.

verses.devanagari: ভট্টাচার্য পণ্ডিত বিশ ত্রিশ লঞা ।\\nভাগবত বিচার করেন সভাতে বসিয়া ॥১৭॥
verses.transliteration: bhaṭṭācārya paṇḍita biśa triśa lañā\\nbhāgavata vicāra karena sabhāte vasiyā
verses.translation: Śrī Sanātana Gosvāmī used to discuss Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam in an assembly of twenty or thirty learned brāhmaṇa scholars.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura gives the following commentary on the words
bhāgavata vicāra.
As confirmed in the
Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad
(1.1.4,5), there are two kinds of educational systems:
dve vidye veditavya iti, ha sma yad brahma-vido vadanti-parā caivāparā ca. tatrāparā ṛg-vedo yajur-vedaḥ sāma-vedo 'tharva-vedaḥ śikṣā kalpo vyākaraṇaṁ niruktaṁ chando jyotiṣam iti. atha parā yayā tad-akṣaram adhigamyate.
"There are two kinds of educational systems. One deals with transcendental knowledge [
parā vidyā
] and the other with material knowledge [
aparā vidyā
]. All the
Vedas-Ṛg Veda, Yajur Veda, Sāma Veda, Atharva Veda
and their corollaries known as
śikṣā, kalpa, vyākaraṇa, nirukta, chanda
and
jyotiṣa
—belong to the inferior system of material knowledge [
aparā vidyā
]. By
parā vidyā,
one can understand the
akṣara,
Brahman or the Absolute Truth." As far as Vedic literature is concerned,
Vedānta-sūtra
is accepted as the
parā vidyā. Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
is an explanation of that
parā vidyā.
Those who aspire for liberation (
mukti
or
mokṣa
) and introduce themselves as
vaidāntika
are also equal to those groups aspiring to improve religion (
dharma
), economic development (
artha
) and sense gratification (
kāma
).
Dharma, artha, kāma
and
mokṣa
are called
catur-varga.
They are all within the system of inferior material knowledge. Any literature giving information about the spiritual world, spiritual life, spiritual identity and the spirit soul is called
parā vidyā. Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
does not have anything to do with the materialistic way of life; it gives transcendental information to educate people in the superior system of
parā vidyā.
Sanātana Gosvāmī was engaged in discussing the
bhāgavata-vidyā,
which means he discussed transcendental superior knowledge. Those who are
karmīs, jñānīs
or
yogīs
are not actually fit to discuss
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam.
Only Vaiṣṇavas or pure devotees are fit to discuss that literature. As stated in
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
itself (12.13.18):
śrīmad-bhāgavataṁ purāṇam amalaṁ yad vaiṣṇavānāṁ priyaṁ
yasmin pāramahaṁsyam ekam amalaṁ jñānaṁ paraṁ gīyate
yatra jñāna-virāga-bhakti-sahitaṁ naiṣkarmyam āviṣkṛtaṁ
tac chṛṇvan supaṭhan vicāraṇa-paro bhaktyā vimucyen naraḥ
Although
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
is counted among the
Purāṇas,
it is called the spotless
Purāṇa.
Because it does not discuss anything material, it is liked by transcendental Vaiṣṇava devotees. The subject matter found in
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
is meant for
paramahaṁsas.
As it is said:
paramo-nirmatsarāṇām. A paramahaṁsa
is one who does not live in the material world and who does not envy others. In
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam,
devotional service is discussed to arouse the living entity to the transcendental position of
jñāna
(knowledge) and
vairāgya
(renunciation). As stated in
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(1.2.12):
tac chraddadhānāḥ munayo
jñāna-vairāgya-yuktayā
paśyanty ātmani cātmānaṁ
bhaktyā śruta-gṛhītayā
"That Absolute Truth is realized by the seriously inquisitive student or sage who is well equipped with knowledge and who has become detached by rendering devotional service and hearing the
