verses.translation: “ 'There are people who say, "I know everything about Kṛṣṇa." Let them think that way. As far as I am concerned, I do not wish to speak very much about this matter. O my Lord, let me say this much. As far as Your opulences are concerned, they are all beyond the reach of my mind, body and words.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a quotation from
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(10.14.38), spoken by Lord Brahmā after he had stolen Lord Kṛṣṇa's cows, calves and cowherd boys and Kṛṣṇa had exhibited His transcendental opulence by re-creating all the stolen cows, calves and cowherd boys by His
viṣṇu-mūrti
expansions. After he had seen this, Brahmā offered the above prayer.

verses.devanagari: কৃষ্ণের মহিমা রহু — কেবা তার জ্ঞাতা ।\\nবৃন্দাবন-স্থানের দেখ আশ্চর্য বিভুতা ॥২৮॥
verses.transliteration: kṛṣṇera mahimā rahu—kebā tāra jñātā\\nvṛndāvana-sthānera dekha āścarya vibhutā
verses.translation: "Let the glories of Lord Kṛṣṇa be! Who could be aware of all of them? His abode, Vṛndāvana, has many wonderful opulences. Just try to see them all.

verses.devanagari: ষোলক্রোশ বৃন্দাবন, — শাস্ত্রের প্রকাশে ।\\nতার একদেশে বৈকুণ্ঠাজাণ্ডগণ ভাসে ॥২৯॥
verses.transliteration: ṣola-krośa vṛndāvana,—śāstrera prakāśe\\ntāra eka-deśe vaikuṇṭhājāṇḍa-gaṇa bhāse
verses.translation: "According to the revelations of revealed scripture, Vṛndāvana extends only sixteen krośas [thirty-two miles]. Nonetheless, all the Vaikuṇṭha planets and innumerable universes are located in one corner of this tract.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
In Vraja, the land is divided into various
vanas,
or forests. The forests total twelve, and their extension is estimated to be eighty-four
krośas.
Of these, the special forest known as Vṛndāvana is located from the present municipal city of Vṛndāvana to the village called Nanda-grāma. This distance is sixteen
krośas
(thirty-two miles).

verses.devanagari: অপার ঐশ্বর্য কৃষ্ণের — নাহিক গণন ।\\nশাখা-চন্দ্র-ন্যায়ে করি দিগ্দরশন ॥৩০॥
verses.transliteration: apāra aiśvarya kṛṣṇera—nāhika gaṇana\\nśākhā-candra-nyāye kari dig-daraśana
verses.translation: "No one can estimate the opulence of Kṛṣṇa. That is unlimited. However, just as one sees the moon through the branches of a tree, I wish to give a little indication."
verses.purport:
PURPORT
First a child is shown the branches of a tree, and then he is shown the moon through the branches. This is called
śākhā-candra-nyāya.
The idea is that first one must be given a simpler example. Then the more difficult background is explained.

verses.devanagari: ঐশ্বর্য কহিতে স্ফুরিল ঐশ্বর্য-সাগর ।\\nমনেন্দ্রিয় ডুবিলা, প্রভু হইলা ফাঁপর ॥৩১॥
verses.transliteration: aiśvarya kahite sphurila aiśvarya-sāgara\\nmanendriya ḍubilā, prabhu ha-ilā phāṅpara
verses.translation: While describing the transcendental opulences of Kṛṣṇa, the ocean of opulence manifested in the mind of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and His mind and senses were immersed in this ocean. Thus He was perplexed.

verses.devanagari: ভাগবতের এই শ্লোক পড়িলা আপনে ।\\nঅর্থ আস্বাদিতে সুখে করেন ব্যাখ্যানে ॥৩২॥
verses.transliteration: bhāgavatera ei śloka paḍilā āpane\\nartha āsvādite sukhe karena vyākhyāne
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu personally recited the following verse from Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, and to relish the meaning, He began to explain it Himself.

verses.devanagari: স্বয়ন্ত্বসাম্যাতিশয়স্ত্র্যধীশঃ স্বারাজ্যলক্ষ্ম্যাপ্তসমস্তকামঃ ।\\nবলিং হরদ্ভিশ্চিরলোকপালৈঃ কিরীটকোটীড়িতপাদপীঠঃ ॥৩৩॥
verses.transliteration: svayaṁ tv asāmyātiśayas tryadhīśaḥ\\nsvārājya-lakṣmy-āpta-samasta-kāmaḥ\\nbaliṁ haradbhiś cira-loka-pālaiḥ\\nkirīṭa-koṭīḍita-pāda-pīṭhaḥ
verses.translation: “ 'The Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa, is the master of the three worlds and the three principal demigods [Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva]. No one is equal to or greater than Him. By His spiritual potency, known as svārājya-lakṣmī, all His desires are fulfilled. While offering their dues and presents in worship, the predominating deities of all the planets touch the lotus feet of the Lord with their helmets. Thus they offer prayers to the Lord.'
verses.purport: PURPORT\nThis quotation is verse 21 of the Second Chapter, Third Canto of\nŚrīmad-Bhāgavatam.

verses.devanagari: পরম ঈশ্বর কৃষ্ণ স্বয়ং ভগবান্ ।\\nতাতে বড়, তাঁর সম কেহ নাহি আন ॥৩৪॥
verses.transliteration: parama īśvara kṛṣṇa svayaṁ bhagavān\\ntāte baḍa, tāṅra sama keha nāhi āna
verses.translation: "Kṛṣṇa is the original Supreme Personality of Godhead; therefore He is the greatest of all. No one is equal to Him, nor is anyone greater than Him.

verses.devanagari: ঈশ্বরঃ পরমঃ কৃষ্ণঃ সচ্চিদানন্দবিগ্রহঃ ।\\nঅনাদিরাদির্গোবিন্দঃ সর্বকারণকারণম্ ॥৩৫॥
verses.transliteration: īśvaraḥ paramaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ\\nsac-cid-ānanda-vigrahaḥ\\nanādir ādir govindaḥ\\nsarva-kāraṇa-kāraṇam
verses.translation: “ 'Kṛṣṇa, known as Govinda, is the supreme controller. He has an eternal, blissful, spiritual body. He is the origin of all. He has no other origin, for He is the prime cause of all causes.'
verses.purport: PURPORT\nThis is the first verse of the Fifth Chapter of\nBrahma-saṁhitā.

verses.devanagari: ব্রহ্মা, বিষ্ণু, হর, — এই সৃষ্ট্যাদি-ঈশ্বর ।\\nতিনে আজ্ঞাকারী কৃষ্ণের, কৃষ্ণ — অধীশ্বর ॥৩৬॥
verses.transliteration: brahmā, viṣṇu, hara,—ei sṛṣṭyādi-īśvara\\ntine ājñākārī kṛṣṇera, kṛṣṇa—adhīśvara
verses.translation: "The primary predominating deities of this material creation are Lord Brahmā, Lord Śiva and Lord Viṣṇu. Nonetheless, they simply carry out the orders of Lord Kṛṣṇa, who is master of them all.

verses.devanagari: সৃজামি তন্নিযুক্তোঽহং হরো হরতি তদ্বশঃ ।\\nবিশ্বং পুরুষরূপেণ পরিপাতি ত্রিশক্তিধৃক্ ॥৩৭॥
verses.transliteration: sṛjāmi tan-niyukto 'haṁ\\nharo harati tad-vaśaḥ\\nviśvaṁ puruṣa-rūpeṇa\\nparipāti triśakti-dhṛk
verses.translation: "Lord Brahmā said, 'Following the will of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, I create, Lord Śiva destroys, and He Himself in the form of Kṣīrodakaśāyī Viṣṇu maintains all the affairs of material nature. Thus the supreme controller of the three modes of material nature is Lord Viṣṇu.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a quotation from
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(2.6.32).

verses.devanagari: এ সামান্য, ত্র্যধীশ্বরের শুন অর্থ আর ।\\nজগৎকারণ তিন পুরুষাবতার ॥৩৮॥
verses.transliteration: e sāmānya, tryadhīśvarera śuna artha āra\\njagat-kāraṇa tina puruṣāvatāra
verses.translation: "This is only a general description. Please try to understand another meaning of tryadhīśa. The three puruṣa incarnations of Viṣṇu are the original cause of the material creation.

verses.devanagari: মহাবিষ্ণু, পদ্মনাভ, ক্ষীরোদকস্বামী ।\\nএই তিন — স্থূল-সূক্ষ্ম-সর্ব-অন্তর্যামী ॥৩৯॥
verses.transliteration: mahā-viṣṇu, padmanābha, kṣīrodaka-svāmī\\nei tina—sthūla-sūkṣma-sarva-antaryāmī
verses.translation: "Mahā-Viṣṇu, Padmanābha and Kṣīrodakaśāyī Viṣṇu are the Supersouls of all subtle and gross existences.
verses.purport: PURPORT\nLord Mahā-Viṣṇu is known as Kāraṇodakaśāyī Viṣṇu, the Supersoul of everything. Garbhodakaśāyī Viṣṇu, from whose lotus navel Brahmā was created, is also called Hiraṇyagarbha and is the total Supersoul and the subtle Supersoul. Kṣīrodakaśāyī Viṣṇu is the universal form and the gross Supersoul.

verses.devanagari: এই তিন — সর্বাশ্রয়, জগৎ-ঈশ্বর ।\\nএহো সব কলা-অংশ, কৃষ্ণ — অধীশ্বর ॥৪০॥
verses.transliteration: ei tina—sarvāśraya, jagat-īśvara\\neho saba kalā-aṁśa, kṛṣṇa—adhīśvara
verses.translation: "Although Mahā-Viṣṇu, Padmanābha and Kṣīrodakaśāyī Viṣṇu are all shelters and controllers of the entire universe, They are nonetheless but plenary portions or portions of the plenary portions of Kṛṣṇa. Therefore He is the original Personality of Godhead.

verses.devanagari: যস্যৈকনিশ্বসিতকালমথাবলম্ব্য\\nজীবন্তি লোমবিলজা জগদণ্ডনাথাঃ ।\\nবিষ্ণুর্মহান্ স ইহ যস্য কলাবিশেষো\\nগোবিন্দমাদিপুরুষং তমহং ভজামি ॥৪১॥
verses.transliteration: yasyaika-niśvasita-kālam athāvalambya\\njīvanti loma-vilajā jagad-aṇḍa-nāthāḥ\\nviṣṇur mahān sa iha yasya kalā-viśeṣo\\ngovindam ādi-puruṣaṁ tam ahaṁ bhajāmi
verses.translation: “ 'The Brahmās and other lords of the mundane worlds appear from the pores of the Mahā-Viṣṇu and remain alive for the duration of His one exhalation. I adore the primeval Lord, Govinda, for Mahā-Viṣṇu is a portion of His plenary portion.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a quotation from
Brahma-saṁhitā
(5.48). See also
Ādi-līlā
(5.71).

verses.devanagari: এই অর্থ — মধ্যম, শুন ‘গূঢ়’ অর্থ আর ।\\nতিন আবাস-স্থান কৃষ্ণের শাস্ত্রে খ্যাতি যার ॥৪২॥
verses.transliteration: ei artha—madhyama, śuna 'gūḍha' artha āra\\ntina āvāsa-sthāna kṛṣṇera śāstre khyāti yāra
verses.translation: "This is the middle meaning. Now please hear the confidential meaning. Lord Kṛṣṇa has three places of residence, which are well known from revealed scriptures.
verses.purport: PURPORT\nKṛṣṇa has three abodes-His internal abode (Goloka Vṛndāvana), His intermediate abode (the spiritual sky), and His external abode (this material world).

verses.devanagari: ‘অন্তঃপুর’ — গোলোক-শ্রীবৃন্দাবন ।\\nযাহাঁ নিত্যস্থিতি মাতাপিতা-বন্ধুগণ ॥৪৩॥
verses.transliteration: 'antaḥpura'—goloka-śrī-vṛndāvana\\nyāhāṅ nitya-sthiti mātā-pitā-bandhu-gaṇa
verses.translation: "The internal abode is called Goloka Vṛndāvana. It is there that Lord Kṛṣṇa's personal friends, associates, father and mother live.

verses.devanagari: মধুরৈশ্বর্য-মাধুর্য-কৃপাদি-ভাণ্ডার ।\\nযোগমায়া দাসী যাহাঁ রাসাদি লীলা-সার ॥৪৪॥
verses.transliteration: madhuraiśvarya-mādhurya-kṛpādi-bhāṇḍāra\\nyogamāyā dāsī yāhāṅ rāsādi līlā-sāra
verses.translation: "Vṛndāvana is the storehouse of Kṛṣṇa's mercy and the sweet opulences of conjugal love. That is where the spiritual energy, working as a maidservant, exhibits the rāsa dance, the quintessence of all pastimes.

verses.devanagari: করুণানিকুরম্বকোমলে মধুরৈশ্বর্যবিশেষশালিনি ।\\nজয়তি ব্রজরাজনন্দনে ন হি চিন্তাকণিকাভ্যুদেতি নঃ ॥৪৫॥
verses.transliteration: karuṇā-nikuramba-komale\\nmadhuraiśvarya-viśeṣa-śālini\\njayati vraja-rāja-nandane\\nna hi cintā-kaṇikābhyudeti naḥ
verses.translation: "Vṛndāvana-dhāma is very soft due to the mercy of the Supreme Lord, and it is especially opulent due to conjugal love. The transcendental glories of the son of Mahārāja Nanda are exhibited here. Under the circumstances, not the least anxiety is awakened within us.

verses.devanagari: তার তলে পরব্যোম — ‘বিষ্ণুলোক’-নাম ।\\nনারায়ণ-আদি অনন্ত স্বরূপের ধাম ॥৪৬॥
verses.transliteration: tāra tale paravyoma—'viṣṇuloka'-nāma\\nnārāyaṇa-ādi ananta svarūpera dhāma
verses.translation: "Below the Vṛndāvana planet is the spiritual sky, which is known as Viṣṇuloka. In Viṣṇuloka there are innumerable Vaikuṇṭha planets controlled by Nārāyaṇa and other innumerable expansions of Kṛṣṇa.

verses.devanagari: ‘মধ্যম-আবাস’ কৃষ্ণের — ষড়ৈশ্বর্য-ভাণ্ডার ।\\nঅনন্ত স্বরূপে যাহাঁ করেন বিহার ॥৪৭॥
verses.transliteration: 'madhyama-āvāsa' kṛṣṇera—ṣaḍ-aiśvarya-bhāṇḍāra\\nananta svarūpe yāhāṅ karena vihāra
verses.translation: "The spiritual sky, which is full in all six opulences, is the interim residence of Lord Kṛṣṇa. It is there that an unlimited number of forms of Kṛṣṇa enjoy Their pastimes.

verses.devanagari: অনন্ত বৈকুণ্ঠ যাহাঁ ভাণ্ডার-কোঠরি ।\\nপারিষদগণে ষড়ৈশ্বর্যে আছে ভরি’ ॥৪৮॥
verses.transliteration: ananta vaikuṇṭha yāhāṅ bhāṇḍāra-koṭhari\\npāriṣada-gaṇe ṣaḍ-aiśvarye āche bhari'
verses.translation: "Innumerable Vaikuṇṭha planets, which are just like different rooms of a treasure-house, are all there, filled with all opulences. Those unlimited planets house the Lord's eternal associates, who are also enriched with the six opulences."

verses.devanagari: গোলোকনাম্নি নিজধাম্নি তলে চ তস্য\\nদেবী-মহেশ-হরিধামসু তেষু তেষু ।\\nতে তে প্রভাবনিচয়া বিহিতাশ্চ যেন\\nগোবিন্দমাদিপুরুষং তমহং ভজামি ॥৪৯॥
verses.transliteration: goloka-nāmni nija-dhāmni tale ca tasya\\ndevī-maheśa-hari-dhāmasu teṣu teṣu\\nte te prabhāva-nicayā vihitāś ca yena\\ngovindam ādi-puruṣaṁ tam ahaṁ bhajāmi
verses.translation: “ 'Below the planet named Goloka Vṛndāvana are the planets known as Devī-dhāma, Maheśa-dhāma and Hari-dhāma. These are opulent in different ways. They are managed by the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Govinda, the original Lord. I offer my obeisances unto Him.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a quotation from
Brahma-saṁhitā
(5.43).

verses.devanagari: প্রধান-পরমব্যোম্নোরন্তরে বিরজা নদী ।\\nবেদাঙ্গস্বেদজনিতৈস্তোয়ৈঃ প্রস্রাবিতা শুভা ॥৫০॥
verses.transliteration: pradhāna-parama-vyomnor\\nantare virajā nadī\\nvedāṅga-sveda-janitais\\ntoyaiḥ prasrāvitā śubhā
verses.translation: “ 'Between the spiritual and material worlds is a body of water known as the river Virajā. This water is generated from the bodily perspiration of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is known as Vedāṅga. Thus the river flows.'
verses.purport: PURPORT\nThis verse and the following verse are from the\nPadma Purāṇa.

verses.devanagari: তস্যাঃ পারে পরব্যোম ত্রিপাদ্ভূতং সনাতনম্ ।\\nঅমৃতং শাশ্বতং নিত্যমনন্তং পরমং পদম্ ॥৫১॥
verses.transliteration: tasyāḥ pāre paravyoma\\ntripād-bhūtaṁ sanātanam\\namṛtaṁ śāśvataṁ nityam\\nanantaṁ paramaṁ padam
verses.translation: “ 'Beyond the river Virajā is a spiritual nature, which is indestructible, eternal, inexhaustible and unlimited. It is the supreme abode consisting of three fourths of the Lord's opulences. It is known as paravyoma, the spiritual sky.'
verses.purport: PURPORT\nIn the spiritual sky there is neither anxiety nor fear. It is eternally existing, and it consists of three fourths of the Lord's energy. The material world is an exhibition of only one fourth of the Lord's energy. Therefore it is called\neka-pāda-vibhūti.

verses.devanagari: তার তলে ‘বাহ্যাবাস’ বিরজার পার ।\\nঅনন্ত ব্রহ্মাণ্ড যাহাঁ কোঠরি অপার ॥৫২॥
verses.transliteration: tāra tale 'bāhyāvāsa' virajāra pāra\\nananta brahmāṇḍa yāhāṅ koṭhari apāra
verses.translation: "On the other side of the river Virajā is the external abode, which is full of unlimited universes, each containing unlimited atmospheres.

verses.devanagari: ‘দেবীধাম’ নাম তার, জীব যার বাসী ।\\nজগল্লক্ষ্মী রাখি’ রহে যাহাঁ মায়া দাসী ॥৫৩॥
verses.transliteration: 'devī-dhāma' nāma tāra, jīva yāra vāsī\\njagal-lakṣmī rākhi' rahe yāhāṅ māyā dāsī
verses.translation: "The abode of the external energy is called Devī-dhāma, and its inhabitants are conditioned souls. It is there that the material energy, Durgā, resides with many opulent maidservants.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
Because he wants to enjoy the material energy, the conditioned soul is allowed to reside in Devī-dhāma, the external energy, where the goddess Durgā carries out the orders of the Supreme Lord as His maidservant. The material energy is called
jagal-lakṣmī
because she protects the bewildered conditioned souls. The goddess Durgā is therefore known as the mother, and Lord Śiva, her husband, is known as the father. Lord Śiva and goddess Durgā are therefore known as the material father and mother. Goddess Durgā is so named because this material world is like a big fort where the conditioned soul is placed under her care. For material facilities, the conditioned soul tries to please the goddess Durgā, and mother Durgā supplies all kinds of material facilities. Because of this, the conditioned souls are allured and do not wish to leave the external energy. Consequently they are continuously making plans to live here peacefully and happily. Such is the material world.

verses.devanagari: এই তিন ধামের হয় কৃষ্ণ অধীশ্বর ।\\nগোলোক-পরব্যোম — প্রকৃতির পর ॥৫৪॥
verses.transliteration: ei tina dhāmera haya kṛṣṇa adhīśvara\\ngoloka-paravyoma—prakṛtira para
verses.translation: "Kṛṣṇa is the supreme proprietor of all dhāmas, including Goloka-dhāma, Vaikuṇṭha-dhāma and Devī-dhāma. The paravyoma and Goloka-dhāma are beyond Devī-dhāma, this material world.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
When a living entity is liberated from Devī-dhāma but does not know of the opulence of Hari-dhāma, he is placed in Maheśa-dhāma, which is between the other two
dhāmas.
The liberated soul does not get an opportunity to serve the Supreme Personality of Godhead there; therefore although this Maheśa-dhāma is Lord Śiva's
dhāma
and above the Devī-dhāma, it is not the spiritual world. The spiritual world begins with Hari-dhāma, or Vaikuṇṭhaloka.

verses.devanagari: চিচ্ছক্তিবিভূতি-ধাম — ত্রিপাদৈশ্বর্য-নাম ।\\nমায়িক বিভূতি — একপাদ অভিধান ॥৫৫॥
verses.transliteration: cic-chakti-vibhūti-dhāma—tripād-aiśvarya-nāma\\nmāyika vibhūti—eka-pāda abhidhāna
verses.translation: "The spiritual world is considered to be three fourths of the energy and opulence of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, whereas this material world is only one fourth of that energy. That is our understanding.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
Hari-dhāma (
paravyoma
) and Goloka Vṛndāvana are beyond the material cosmic manifestation. They are celebrated as three fourths of the Lord's energy. The material world, conducted by the Supreme Lord's external energy, is called Devī-dhāma and is a manifestation of one fourth of His energy.

verses.devanagari: ত্রিপাদ্বিভূতের্ধামত্বাৎ ত্রিপাদ্ভূতং হি তৎ পদম্ ।\\nবিভূতির্মায়িকী সর্বা প্রোক্তা পাদাত্মিকা যতঃ ॥৫৬॥
verses.transliteration: tripād-vibhūter dhāmatvāt\\ntripād-bhūtaṁ hi tat padam\\nvibhūtir māyikī sarvā\\nproktā pādātmikā yataḥ
verses.translation: “ 'Because it consists of three fourths of the Lord's energy, the spiritual world is called tripād-bhūta. Being a manifestation of one fourth of the Lord's energy, the material world is called eka-pāda.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This verse is found in
Laghu-bhāgavatāmṛta
(1.5.286).

verses.devanagari: ত্রিপাদবিভূতি কৃষ্ণের — বাক্য-অগোচর ।\\nএকপাদ বিভূতির শুনহ বিস্তার ॥৫৭॥
verses.transliteration: tripāda-vibhūti kṛṣṇera—vākya-agocara\\neka-pāda vibhūtira śunaha vistāra
verses.translation: "The three-fourths part of Lord Kṛṣṇa's energy is beyond our speaking power. Let us therefore hear elaborately about the remaining one fourth of His energy.

verses.devanagari: অনন্ত ব্রহ্মাণ্ডের যত ব্রহ্মা-রুদ্রগণ ।\\nচিরলোকপাল-শব্দে তাহার গণন ॥৫৮॥
verses.transliteration: ananta brahmāṇḍera yata brahmā-rudra-gaṇa\\ncira-loka-pāla-śabde tāhāra gaṇana
verses.translation: "Actually it is very difficult to ascertain the number of universes. Every universe has its separate Lord Brahmā and Lord Śiva, who are known as permanent governors. Therefore there is also no counting of them.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
Lord Brahmā and Lord Śiva are called
cira-loka-pāla,
permanent governors. This means that they govern the affairs of the universe from the beginning of the creation to the end. In the next creation, the same living entities may not be present, but because Brahmā and Śiva are existing from the beginning to the end, they are called
cira-loka-pāla,
permanent governors.
Loka-pāla
means "predominating deities." There are eight predominating deities of the prominent heavenly planets, and they are Indra, Agni, Yama, Varuṇa, Nirṛti, Vāyu, Kuvera and Śiva.

verses.devanagari: একদিন দ্বারকাতে কৃষ্ণ দেখিবারে ।\\nব্রহ্মা আইলা, — দ্বারপাল জানাইল কৃষ্ণেরে ॥৫৯॥
verses.transliteration: eka-dina dvārakāte kṛṣṇa dekhibāre\\nbrahmā āilā,—dvāra-pāla jānāila kṛṣṇere
verses.translation: "Once, when Kṛṣṇa was ruling Dvārakā, Lord Brahmā came to see Him, and the doorman immediately informed Lord Kṛṣṇa of Brahmā's arrival.

verses.devanagari: কৃষ্ণ কহেন — ‘কোন্ ব্রহ্মা, কি নাম তাহার ?’\\nদ্বারী আসি’ ব্রহ্মারে পুছে আর বার ॥৬০॥
verses.transliteration: kṛṣṇa kahena—'kon brahmā, ki nāma tāhāra?'\\ndvārī āsi' brahmāre puche āra bāra
verses.translation: "When Kṛṣṇa was so informed, He immediately asked the doorman, 'Which Brahmā? What is his name?' The doorman therefore returned and questioned Lord Brahmā.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
From this verse we can understand that Brahmā is the name of the post and that the person occupying the post has a particular name also. From
Bhagavad-gītā: imaṁ vivasvate yogam.
Vivasvān is the name of the present predominating deity of the sun. He is generally called Sūrya, the sun-god, but he also has his own particular name. The governor of the state is generally called
rāja-pāla,
but he also has his own individual name. Since there are hundreds and thousands of Brahmās with different names, Kṛṣṇa wanted to know which of them had come to see Him.

verses.devanagari: বিস্মিত হঞা ব্রহ্মা দ্বারীকে কহিলা ।\\n‘কহ গিয়া সনক-পিতা চতুর্মুখ আইলা’ ॥৬১॥
verses.transliteration: vismita hañā brahmā dvārīke kahilā\\n'kaha giyā sanaka-pitā caturmukha āilā'
verses.translation: "When the doorman asked, 'Which Brahmā?' Lord Brahmā was surprised. He told the doorman, 'Please go inform Lord Kṛṣṇa that I am the four-headed Brahmā who is the father of the four Kumāras.'

verses.devanagari: কৃষ্ণে জানাঞা দ্বারী ব্রহ্মারে লঞা গেলা ।\\nকৃষ্ণের চরণে ব্রহ্মা দণ্ডবৎ কৈলা ॥৬২॥
verses.transliteration: kṛṣṇe jānāñā dvārī brahmāre lañā gelā\\nkṛṣṇera caraṇe brahmā daṇḍavat kailā
verses.translation: "The doorman then informed Lord Kṛṣṇa of Lord Brahmā's description, and Lord Kṛṣṇa gave him permission to enter. The doorman escorted Lord Brahmā in, and as soon as Brahmā saw Lord Kṛṣṇa, he offered obeisances at His lotus feet.

verses.devanagari: কৃষ্ণ মান্য-পূজা করি’ তাঁরে প্রশ্ন কৈল ।\\n‘কি লাগি’ তোমার ইহাঁ আগমন হৈল ?’ ॥ ৬৩ ॥
verses.transliteration: kṛṣṇa mānya-pūjā kari' tāṅre praśna kaila\\n'ki lāgi' tomāra ihāṅ āgamana haila?'
verses.translation: "After being worshiped by Lord Brahmā, Lord Kṛṣṇa also honored him with suitable words. Then Lord Kṛṣṇa asked him, 'Why have you come here?'

verses.devanagari: ব্রহ্মা কহে, — ‘তাহা পাছে করিব নিবেদন ।\\nএক সংশয় মনে হয়, করহ ছেদন ॥৬৪॥
verses.transliteration: brahmā kahe,—'tāhā pāche kariba nivedana\\neka saṁśaya mane haya, karaha chedana
verses.translation: "Being questioned, Lord Brahmā immediately replied, 'I shall later tell You why I have come. First of all there is a doubt in my mind which I wish You would kindly dissipate.

verses.devanagari: ‘কোন্ ব্রহ্মা?’ পুছিলে তুমি কোন্ অভিপ্রায়ে ?\\nআমা বই জগতে আর কোন্ ব্রহ্মা হয়ে ?’ ॥ ৬৫ ॥
verses.transliteration: 'kon brahmā?' puchile tumi kon abhiprāye?\\nāmā ba-i jagate āra kon brahmā haye?'
verses.translation: “ 'Why did you inquire which Brahmā had come to see You? What is the purpose of such an inquiry? Is there any other Brahmā besides me within this universe?'

verses.devanagari: শুনি’ হাসি’ কৃষ্ণ তবে করিলেন ধ্যানে ।\\nঅসংখ্য ব্রহ্মার গণ আইলা ততক্ষণে ॥৬৬॥
verses.transliteration: śuni' hāsi' kṛṣṇa tabe karilena dhyāne\\nasaṅkhya brahmāra gaṇa āilā tata-kṣaṇe
verses.translation: "Upon hearing this, Śrī Kṛṣṇa smiled and immediately meditated. Unlimited Brahmās arrived instantly.

verses.devanagari: দশ-বিশ-শত-সহস্র-অযুত-লক্ষ-বদন ।\\nকোট্যর্বুদ মুখ কারো, না যায় গণন ॥৬৭॥
verses.transliteration: daśa-biśa-śata-sahasra-ayuta-lakṣa-vadana\\nkoṭy-arbuda mukha kāro, nā yāya gaṇana
verses.translation: "These Brahmās had different numbers of heads. Some had ten heads, some twenty, some a hundred, some a thousand, some ten thousand, some a hundred thousand, some ten million and others a hundred million. No one can count the number of faces they had.

verses.devanagari: রুদ্রগণ আইলা লক্ষ কোটি-বদন ।\\nইন্দ্রগণ আইলা লক্ষ কোটি-নয়ন ॥৬৮॥
verses.transliteration: rudra-gaṇa āilā lakṣa koṭi-vadana\\nindra-gaṇa āilā lakṣa koṭi-nayana
verses.translation: "There also arrived many Lord Śivas with various heads numbering one hundred thousand and ten million. Many Indras also arrived, and they had hundreds of thousands of eyes all over their bodies.
verses.purport: PURPORT\nIt is said that Indra, the King of heaven, is very lusty. Once he tactfully had sexual intercourse with the wife of a great sage, and when the sage learned about this, he cursed the lusty Indra with a curse that put vaginas all over his body. Being very ashamed, Indra fell down at the lotus feet of the great sage and begged his pardon. Being compassionate, the sage turned the vaginas into eyes; therefore Indra possesses hundreds and thousands of eyes all over his body. Just as Lord Brahmā and Lord Śiva have many faces, the King of heaven, Indra, has many eyes.

verses.devanagari: দেখি’ চতুর্মুখ ব্রহ্মা ফাঁপর হইলা ।\\nহস্তিগণ-মধ্যে যেন শশক রহিলা ॥৬৯॥
verses.transliteration: dekhi' caturmukha brahmā phāṅpara ha-ilā\\nhasti-gaṇa-madhye yena śaśaka rahilā
verses.translation: "When the four-headed Brahmā of this universe saw all these opulences of Kṛṣṇa, he became very bewildered and considered himself a rabbit among many elephants.

verses.devanagari: আসি’ সব ব্রহ্মা কৃষ্ণ-পাদপীঠ-আগে ।\\nদণ্ডবৎ করিতে মুকুট পাদপীঠে লাগে ॥৭০॥
verses.transliteration: āsi' saba brahmā kṛṣṇa-pāda-pīṭha-āge\\ndaṇḍavat karite mukuṭa pāda-pīṭhe lāge
verses.translation: "All the Brahmās who came to see Kṛṣṇa offered their respects at His lotus feet, and when they did this, their helmets touched His lotus feet.

verses.devanagari: কৃষ্ণের অচিন্ত্য-শক্তি লখিতে কেহ নারে ।\\nযত ব্রহ্মা, তত মূর্তি একই শরীরে ॥৭১॥
verses.transliteration: kṛṣṇera acintya-śakti lakhite keha nāre\\nyata brahmā, tata mūrti eka-i śarīre
verses.translation: "No one can estimate the inconceivable potency of Kṛṣṇa. All the Brahmās who were there were resting in the one body of Kṛṣṇa.

verses.devanagari: পাদপীট-মুকুটাগ্র-সংঘট্টে উঠে ধ্বনি ।\\nপাদপীঠে স্তুতি করে মুকুট হেন জানি’ ॥৭২॥
verses.transliteration: pāda-pīṭa-mukuṭāgra-saṅghaṭṭe uṭhe dhvani\\npāda-pīṭhe stuti kare mukuṭa hena jāni'
verses.translation: "When all the helmets struck together at Kṛṣṇa's lotus feet, there was a tumultuous sound. It appeared that the helmets themselves were offering prayers unto Kṛṣṇa's lotus feet.

verses.devanagari: যোড়-হাতে ব্রহ্মা-রুদ্রাদি করয়ে স্তবন ।\\n“বড় কৃপা করিলা প্রভু, দেখাইলা চরণ ॥৭৩॥
verses.transliteration: yoḍa-hāte brahmā-rudrādi karaye stavana\\n"baḍa kṛpā karilā prabhu, dekhāilā caraṇa
verses.translation: "With folded hands, all the Brahmās and Śivas began to offer prayers unto Lord Kṛṣṇa, saying, 'O Lord, You have shown me a great favor. I have been able to see Your lotus feet.'

verses.devanagari: ভাগ্য, মোরে বোলাইলা ‘দাস’ অঙ্গীকরি’ ।\\nকোন্ আজ্ঞা হয়, তাহা করি শিরে ধরি’ ।।” ॥ ৭৪ ॥
verses.transliteration: bhāgya, more bolāilā 'dāsa' aṅgīkari'\\nkon ājñā haya, tāhā kari śire dhari' "
verses.translation: "All of them then said, 'It is my great fortune, Lord, that You have called me, thinking of me as Your servant. Now let me know what Your order is so that I may carry it on my heads.'

verses.devanagari: কৃষ্ণ কহে, — তোমা-সবা দেখিতে চিত্ত হৈল ।\\nতাহা লাগি’ এক ঠাঞি সবা বোলাইল ॥৭৫॥
verses.transliteration: kṛṣṇa kahe,—tomā-sabā dekhite citta haila\\ntāhā lāgi' eka ṭhāñi sabā bolāila
verses.translation: "Lord Kṛṣṇa replied, 'Since I wanted to see all of you together, I have called all of you here.

verses.devanagari: সুখী হও সবে, কিছু নাহি দৈত্য-ভয় ?\\nতারা কহে, — ‘তোমার প্রসাদে সর্বত্রই জয় ॥৭৬॥
verses.transliteration: sukhī hao sabe, kichu nāhi daitya-bhaya?\\ntārā kahe,—'tomāra prasāde sarvatra-i jaya
verses.translation: “ 'All of you should be happy. Is there any fear from the demons?' They replied, 'By Your mercy, we are victorious everywhere.

verses.devanagari: সম্প্রতি পৃথিবীতে যেবা হৈয়াছিল ভার ।\\nঅবতীর্ণ হঞা তাহা করিলা সংহার ।।’ ॥ ৭৭ ॥
verses.transliteration: samprati pṛthivīte yebā haiyāchila bhāra\\navatīrṇa hañā tāhā karilā saṁhāra'
verses.translation: “ 'Whatever burden was upon the earth You have taken away by descending on that planet.'

verses.devanagari: দ্বারকাদি — বিভু, তার এই ত প্রমাণ ।\\n‘আমারই ব্রহ্মাণ্ডে কৃষ্ণ’ সবার হৈল জ্ঞান ॥৭৮॥
verses.transliteration: dvārakādi—vibhu, tāra ei ta pramāṇa\\n'āmāra-i brahmāṇḍe kṛṣṇa' sabāra haila jñāna
verses.translation: "This is the proof of Dvārakā's opulence: all the Brahmās thought, 'Kṛṣṇa is now staying in my jurisdiction.'

verses.devanagari: কৃষ্ণ-সহ দ্বারকা-বৈভব অনুভব হৈল ।\\nএকত্র মিলনে কেহ কাহো না দেখিল ॥৭৯॥
verses.transliteration: kṛṣṇa-saha dvārakā-vaibhava anubhava haila\\nekatra milane keha kāho nā dekhila
verses.translation: "Thus the opulence of Dvārakā was perceived by each and every one of them. Although they were all assembled together, no one could see anyone but himself.
verses.purport: PURPORT\nThe four-headed Brahmā perceived the opulence of Dvārakā-dhāma where Kṛṣṇa was staying, and although there were Brahmās present having ten to ten million heads, and also many Lord Śivas were also assembled, only the four-headed Brahmā of this universe could see all of them. By the inconceivable potency of Kṛṣṇa, the others could not see one another. Although all the Brahmās and Śivas were assembled together, due to Kṛṣṇa's energy, they could not meet or talk among themselves individually.

verses.devanagari: তবে কৃষ্ণ সর্ব-ব্রহ্মাগণে বিদায় দিলা ।\\nদণ্ডবৎ হঞা সবে নিজ ঘরে গেলা ॥৮০॥
verses.transliteration: tabe kṛṣṇa sarva-brahmā-gaṇe vidāya dilā\\ndaṇḍavat hañā sabe nija ghare gelā
verses.translation: "Lord Kṛṣṇa then bade farewell to all the Brahmās there, and after offering their obeisances, they all returned to their respective homes.

verses.devanagari: দেখি’ চতুর্মুখ ব্রহ্মার হৈল চমৎকার ।\\nকৃষ্ণের চরণে আসি’ কৈলা নমস্কার ॥৮১॥
verses.transliteration: dekhi' caturmukha brahmāra haila camatkāra\\nkṛṣṇera caraṇe āsi' kailā namaskāra
verses.translation: "After observing all these opulences, the four-headed Brahmā of this universe was astonished. He again came before the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa and offered Him obeisances.

verses.devanagari: ব্রহ্মা বলে, — পূর্বে আমি যে নিশ্চয় করিলুঁ ।\\nতার উদাহরণ আমি আজি ত’ দেখিলুঁ ॥৮২॥
verses.transliteration: brahmā bale,—pūrve āmi ye niścaya kariluṅ\\ntāra udāharaṇa āmi āji ta' dekhiluṅ
verses.translation: "Brahmā then said, 'Whatever I formerly decided about my knowledge, I have just now had personally verified.'

verses.devanagari: জানন্ত এব জানন্তু কিং বহূক্ত্যা ন মে প্রভো ।\\nমনসো বপুষো বাচো বৈভবং তব গোচরঃ ॥৮৩॥
verses.transliteration: jānanta eva jānantu\\nkiṁ bahūktyā na me prabho\\nmanaso vapuṣo vāco\\nvaibhavaṁ tava gocaraḥ
verses.translation: “ 'There are people who say, "I know everything about Kṛṣṇa." Let them think in that way. As far as I am concerned, I do not wish to speak very much about this matter. O my Lord, let me say this much. As far as your opulences are concerned, they are all beyond the reach of my mind, body and words.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a quotation from
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(10.14.38), spoken by Lord Brahmā.

verses.devanagari: কৃষ্ণ কহে, “এই ব্রহ্মাণ্ড পঞ্চাশৎ কোটি যোজন ।\\nঅতি ক্ষুদ্র, তাতে তোমার চারি বদন ॥৮৪॥
verses.transliteration: kṛṣṇa kahe, "ei brahmāṇḍa pañcāśat koṭi yojana\\nati kṣudra, tāte tomāra cāri vadana
verses.translation: "Kṛṣṇa said, 'Your particular universe extends four billion miles; therefore it is the smallest of all the universes. Consequently you have only four heads.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura, one of the greatest astrologers of his time, gives information from
Siddhānta-śiromaṇi
that this universe measures 18,712,069,200,000,000 x 8 miles. This is the circumference of this universe. According to some, this is only half the circumference.

verses.devanagari: কোন ব্রহ্মাণ্ড শতকোটি, কোন লক্ষকোটি ।\\nকোন নিযুতকোটি, কোন কোটি-কোটি ॥৮৫॥
verses.transliteration: kona brahmāṇḍa śata-koṭi, kona lakṣa-koṭi\\nkona niyuta-koṭi, kona koṭi-koṭi
verses.translation: “ 'Some of the universes are one billion yojanas, some one trillion, some ten trillion and some one hundred trillion yojanas. Thus they are almost unlimited in area.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
A
yojana
equals eight miles.

verses.devanagari: ব্রহ্মাণ্ডানুরূপ ব্রহ্মার শরীর-বদন ।\\nএইরূপে পালি আমি ব্রহ্মাণ্ডের গণ ॥৮৬॥
verses.transliteration: brahmāṇḍānurūpa brahmāra śarīra-vadana\\nei-rūpe pāli āmi brahmāṇḍera gaṇa
verses.translation: “ 'According to the size of the universe, there are so many heads on the body of Brahmā. In this way I maintain innumerable universes [brahmāṇḍas].

verses.devanagari: ‘একপাদ বিভূতি’ ইহার নাহি পরিমাণ ।\\n‘ত্রিপাদ বিভূতি’র কেবা করে পরিমাণ ।।” ॥ ৮৭ ॥
verses.transliteration: 'eka-pāda vibhūti' ihāra nāhi parimāṇa\\n'tripāda vibhūti'ra kebā kare parimāṇa"
verses.translation: “ 'No one can measure the length and breadth of one fourth of My energy. Who can measure the three fourths that is manifested in the spiritual world?'

verses.devanagari: তস্যাঃ পারে পরব্যোম ত্রিপাদ্ভূতং সনাতনম্ ।\\nঅমৃতং শাশ্বতং নিত্যমনন্তং পরমং পদম্ ॥৮৮॥
verses.transliteration: tasyāḥ pāre paravyoma\\ntripād-bhūtaṁ sanātanam\\namṛtaṁ śāśvataṁ nityam\\nanantaṁ paramaṁ padam
verses.translation: “ 'Beyond the river Virajā is a spiritual nature, which is indestructible, eternal, inexhaustible and unlimited. It is the supreme abode consisting of three fourths of the Lord's opulences. It is known as paravyoma, the spiritual sky.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a verse from the
Padma Purāṇa,
recited here by Lord Kṛṣṇa.

verses.devanagari: তবে কৃষ্ণ ব্রহ্মারে দিলেন বিদায় ।\\nকৃষ্ণের বিভূতি-স্বরূপ জানান না যায় ॥৮৯॥
verses.transliteration: tabe kṛṣṇa brahmāre dilena vidāya\\nkṛṣṇera vibhūti-svarūpa jānāna nā yāya
verses.translation: "In this way Lord Kṛṣṇa bade farewell to the four-headed Brahmā of this universe. We may thus understand that no one can calculate the extent of Kṛṣṇa's energies.

verses.devanagari: ‘ত্র্যধীশ্বর’-শব্দের অর্থ ‘গূঢ়’ আর হয় ।\\n‘ত্রি’-শব্দে কৃষ্ণের তিন লোক কয় ॥৯০॥
verses.transliteration: 'tryadhīśvara'-śabdera artha 'gūḍha' āra haya\\n'tri'-śabde kṛṣṇera tina loka kaya
verses.translation: "There is a very deep meaning in the word tryadhīśvara, which indicates that Kṛṣṇa possesses three different lokas, or natures.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
The word
tryadhīśvara
means "proprietor of the three worlds." There are three worlds of which Kṛṣṇa is the supreme proprietor. This is explained in
Bhagavad-gītā:
bhoktāraṁ yajña-tapasāṁ
sarva-loka-maheśvaram
suhṛdaṁ sarva-bhūtānāṁ
jñātvā māṁ śāntim ṛcchati
"The sages, knowing Me as the ultimate purpose of all sacrifices and austerities, the Supreme Lord of all planets and demigods and the benefactor and well-wisher of all living entities, attain peace from the pangs of material miseries." (Bg. 5.29)
The word
sarva-loka
means "all three worlds," and the word
maheśvara
means "the supreme proprietor." Kṛṣṇa is the proprietor of both material and spiritual worlds. The spiritual world is divided into two portions-Goloka Vṛndāvana and the Vaikuṇṭhas. The material world is a combination of universes unlimited in number.

verses.devanagari: গোলোকাখ্য গোকুল, মথুরা, দ্বারাবতী ।\\nএই তিন লোকে কৃষ্ণের সহজে নিত্যস্থিতি ॥৯১॥
verses.transliteration: golokākhya gokula, mathurā, dvārāvatī\\nei tina loke kṛṣṇera sahaje nitya-sthiti
verses.translation: "The three lokas are Gokula (Goloka), Mathurā and Dvārakā. Kṛṣṇa lives eternally in these three places.
verses.purport: PURPORT\nŚrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura comments that in the Goloka planet there are three divisions: Gokula, Mathurā and Dvārakā. In His incarnation as Gaurasundara, Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the Lord conducts His pastimes in three areas: Navadvīpa, Jagannātha Purī (and South India) and Vraja-maṇḍala (the area of Vṛndāvana-dhāma).

verses.devanagari: অন্তরঙ্গ-পূর্ণৈশ্বর্যপূর্ণ তিন ধাম ।\\nতিনের অধীশ্বর — কৃষ্ণ স্বয়ং ভগবান্ ॥৯২॥
verses.transliteration: antaraṅga-pūrṇaiśvarya-pūrṇa tina dhāma\\ntinera adhīśvara—kṛṣṇa svayaṁ bhagavān
verses.translation: "These three places are full of internal potencies, and Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, is their sole proprietor.

verses.devanagari: পূর্ব-উক্ত ব্রহ্মাণ্ডের যত দিক্পাল ।\\nঅনন্ত বৈকুণ্ঠাবরণ, চিরলোকপাল ॥৯৩॥\\nতাঁ-সবার মুকুট কৃষ্ণপাদপীঠ-আগে ।\\nদণ্ডবৎকালে তার মণি পীঠে লাগে ॥৯৪॥
verses.transliteration: tāṅ-sabāra mukuṭa kṛṣṇa-pāda-pīṭha-āge\\ndaṇḍavat-kāle tāra maṇi pīṭhe lāge
verses.translation: "As previously mentioned, the jewels on the helmets of all the predominating deities of all the universes and Vaikuṇṭha planets touched the throne and the lotus feet of the Lord when they all offered obeisances.

verses.devanagari: মণি-পীঠে ঠেকাঠেকি, উঠে ঝন্ঝনি ।\\nপীঠের স্তুতি করে মুকুট — হেন অনুমানি ॥৯৫॥
verses.transliteration: maṇi-pīṭhe ṭhekāṭheki, uṭhe jhanjhani\\npīṭhera stuti kare mukuṭa—hena anumāni
verses.translation: "When the gems on the helmets of all the predominating deities collide before the throne and the Lord's lotus feet, there is a jingling sound, which seems like prayers offered by the helmets at Kṛṣṇa's lotus feet.

verses.devanagari: নিজ-চিচ্ছক্তে কৃষ্ণ নিত্য বিরাজমান ।\\nচিচ্ছক্তি-সম্পত্তির ‘ষড়ৈশ্বর্য’ নাম ॥৯৬॥
verses.transliteration: nija-cic-chakte kṛṣṇa nitya virājamāna\\ncic-chakti-sampattira 'ṣaḍ-aiśvarya' nāma
verses.translation: "Kṛṣṇa is thus situated eternally in His spiritual potency, and the opulence of that spiritual potency is called ṣaḍ-aiśvarya, indicating six kinds of opulence.

verses.devanagari: সেই স্বারাজ্যলক্ষ্মী করে নিত্য পূর্ণ কাম ।\\nঅতএব বেদে কহে ‘স্বয়ং ভগবান্’ ॥৯৭॥
verses.transliteration: sei svārājya-lakṣmī kare nitya pūrṇa kāma\\nataeva vede kahe 'svayaṁ bhagavān'
verses.translation: "Because Be possesses the spiritual potencies which fulfill all His desires, Kṛṣṇa is accepted as the Supreme Personality of Godhead. This is the Vedic version.

verses.devanagari: কৃষ্ণের ঐশ্বর্য — অপার অমৃতের সিন্ধু ।\\nঅবগাহিতে নারি, তার ছুইলঁ এক বিন্দু ॥৯৮॥
verses.transliteration: kṛṣṇera aiśvarya—apāra amṛtera sindhu\\navagāhite nāri, tāra chuilaṅ eka bindu
verses.translation: "The unlimited potencies of Kṛṣṇa are just like an ocean of nectar. Since one cannot bathe within that ocean, I have only touched a drop of it."

verses.devanagari: ঐশ্বর্য কহিতে প্রভুর কৃষ্ণস্ফূর্তি হৈল ।\\nমাধুর্যে মজিল মন, এক শ্লোক পড়িল ॥৯৯॥
verses.transliteration: aiśvarya kahite prabhura kṛṣṇa-sphūrti haila\\nmādhurye majila mana, eka śloka paḍila
verses.translation: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu described the opulences and spiritual potencies of Kṛṣṇa in this way, there was an awakening of love of Kṛṣṇa within Him. His mind was immersed in the sweetness of conjugal love, and He quoted the following verse from Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam.

verses.devanagari: যন্মর্ত্যলীলৌপয়িকং স্বযোগমায়াবলং দর্শয়তা গৃহীতম্ ।\\nবিস্মাপনং স্বস্য চ সৌভগর্ধেঃ পরং পদং ভূষণভূষণাঙ্গম্ ॥১০০॥
verses.transliteration: yan martya-līlaupayikaṁ svayoga-\\nmāyā-balaṁ darśayatā gṛhītam\\nvismāpanaṁ svasya ca saubhagardheḥ\\nparaṁ padaṁ bhūṣaṇa-bhūṣaṇāṅgam
verses.translation: “ 'To exhibit the strength of His own spiritual potency, Lord Kṛṣṇa manifested a suitable form just for His pastimes in the material world. This form was wonderful even for Him and was the supreme abode of the wealth of good fortune. Its limbs were so beautiful that they increased the beauty of the ornaments worn on different parts of His body.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This verse from
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(3.2.12) is stated in a conversation between Vidura and Uddhava. Uddhava thus begins his description of the pastimes of Śrī Kṛṣṇa in His form exhibited by
yogamāyā.

verses.devanagari: কৃষ্ণের যতেক খেলা, সর্বোত্তম নরলীলা,\\nনরবপু তাহার স্বরূপ ।\\nগোপবেশ, বেণুকর, নবকিশোর, নটবর,\\nনরলীলার হয় অনুরূপ ॥১০১॥
verses.transliteration: kṛṣṇera yateka khelā, sarvottama nara-līlā,\\nnara-vapu tāhāra svarūpa\\ngopa-veśa, veṇu-kara, nava-kiśora, naṭa-vara,\\nnara-līlāra haya anurūpa
verses.translation: "Lord Kṛṣṇa has many pastimes, of which His pastimes as a human being are the best. His form as a human being is the supreme transcendental form. In this form He is a cowherd boy. He carries a flute in His hand, and His youth is new. He is also an expert dancer. All this is just suitable for His pastimes as a human being.

verses.devanagari: কৃষ্ণের মধুর রূপ, শুন, সনাতন ।\\nযে রূপের এক কণ, ডুবায় সব ত্রিভুবন,\\nসর্ব প্রাণী করে আকর্ষণ ।। ১০২ ।। ধ্রু ।। ॥১০২॥
verses.transliteration: kṛṣṇera madhura rūpa, śuna, sanātana\\nye rūpera eka kaṇa, ḍubāya saba tribhuvana,\\nsarva prāṇī kare ākarṣaṇa
verses.translation: "My dear Sanātana, the sweet, attractive transcendental form of Kṛṣṇa is so nice. Just try to understand it. Even a fractional understanding of Kṛṣṇa's beauty can merge all three worlds in the ocean of love. He attracts all the living entities within the three worlds.

verses.devanagari: যোগমায়া চিচ্ছক্তি, বিশুদ্ধসত্ত্ব-পরিণতি,\\nতার শক্তি লোকে দেখাইতে ।\\nএই রূপ-রতন, ভক্তগণের গূঢ়ধন,\\nপ্রকট কৈলা নিত্যলীলা হৈতে ॥১০৩॥
verses.transliteration: yogamāyā cic-chakti, viśuddha-sattva-pariṇati,\\ntāra śakti loke dekhāite\\nei rūpa-ratana, bhakta-gaṇera gūḍha-dhana,\\nprakaṭa kailā nitya-līlā haite
verses.translation: "The transcendental form of Kṛṣṇa is shown to the world by Lord Kṛṣṇa's internal spiritual energy, which is a transformation of pure goodness. This jewellike form is the most confidential treasure of the devotees. This form is manifest from Kṛṣṇa's eternal pastimes.

verses.devanagari: রূপ দেখি’ আপনার, কৃষ্ণের হৈল চমৎকার,\\nআস্বাদিতে মনে উঠে কাম ।\\n‘স্বসৌভাগ্য’ যাঁর নাম, সৌন্দর্যাদি-গুণগ্রাম,\\nএইরূপ নিত্য তার ধাম ॥১০৪॥
verses.transliteration: rūpa dekhi' āpanāra, kṛṣṇera haila camatkāra,\\nāsvādite mane uṭhe kāma\\n'svasaubhāgya' yāṅra nāma, saundaryādi-guṇa-grāma,\\nei-rūpa nitya tāra dhāma
verses.translation: "The wonder of Kṛṣṇa in His personal feature is so great that it attracts even Kṛṣṇa to taste His own association. Thus Kṛṣṇa becomes very eager to taste that wonder. Total beauty, knowledge, wealth, strength, fame and renunciation are the six opulences of Kṛṣṇa. He is eternally situated in His opulences.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
Kṛṣṇa has many pastimes, of which His pastimes in Goloka Vṛndāvana (the
gokula-līlā
) are supreme. He also has pastimes in the Vaikuṇṭhas, the spiritual world, as Vāsudeva, Saṅkarṣaṇa, Pradyumna and Aniruddha. In His pastimes in the spiritual sky, He lies down in the Causal Ocean as Kāraṇārṇavaśāyī, the
puruṣa-avatāra.
His incarnations as a fish, tortoise and so on are called His causal incarnations. He incarnates in the modes of nature as Lord Brahmā, Lord Śiva and Lord Viṣṇu. He also incarnates as empowered living entities like Pṛthu and Vyāsa. The Supersoul is His localized incarnation, and His all-pervasive aspect is the impersonal Brahman.
When we consider impartially all the unlimited pastimes of the Lord, we find that His pastimes as a human being on this planet-wherein He sports as a cowherd boy with a flute in His hands and appears youthful and fresh like a ballet dancer-are pastimes and features that are never subjected to material laws and inebrieties. The wonderful beauty of Kṛṣṇa is presented in the supreme planet, Gokula (Goloka Vṛndāvana). Inferior to that is His representation in the spiritual sky, and inferior to that is His representation in the external energy (Devī-dhāma). A mere drop of Kṛṣṇa's sweetness can drown these three worlds-Goloka Vṛndāvana, Hari-dhāma (Vaikuṇṭhaloka), and Devī-dhāma (the material world). Everywhere, Kṛṣṇa's beauty merges everyone in the ecstasy of transcendental bliss. Actually the activities of
yogamāyā
are absent in the spiritual sky and the Vaikuṇṭha planets. She simply works in the supreme planet, Goloka Vṛndāvana, and she works to manifest the activities of Kṛṣṇa when He descends to the material universe to please His innumerable devotees within the material world. Thus a replica of the Goloka Vṛndāvana planet and the pastimes there are manifest on this planet on a specific tract of land-Bhauma Vṛndāvana, the Vṛndāvana-dhāma on this planet.

verses.devanagari: ভূষণের ভূষণ অঙ্গ, তাহেঁ ললিত ত্রিভঙ্গ,\\nতাহার উপর ভ্রূধনু-নর্তন ।\\nতেরছে নেত্রান্ত বাণ, তার দৃঢ় সন্ধান,\\nবিন্ধে রাধা-গোপীগণ-মন ॥১০৫॥
verses.transliteration: bhūṣaṇera bhūṣaṇa aṅga, tāheṅ lalita tribhaṅga,\\ntāhāra upara bhrūdhanu-nartana\\nterache netrānta bāṇa, tāra dṛḍha sandhāna,\\nvindhe rādhā-gopī-gaṇa-mana
verses.translation: "Ornaments caress that body, but the transcendental body of Kṛṣṇa is so beautiful that it beautifies the ornaments He wears. Therefore Kṛṣṇa's body is said to be the ornament of ornaments. Despite the wonderful beauty of Kṛṣṇa, there is His three-curved style of standing, which beautifies that form. Above all these beautiful features, Kṛṣṇa's eyes dance and move obliquely, acting like arrows to pierce the minds of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī and the gopīs. When the arrow succeeds in hitting its target, their minds become agitated.

verses.devanagari: ব্রহ্মাণ্ডোপরি পরব্যোম, তাহাঁ যে স্বরূপগণ,\\nতাঁ-সবার বলে হরে মন ।\\nপতিব্রতা-শিরোমণি, যাঁরে কহে বেদবাণী,\\nআকর্ষয়ে সেই লক্ষ্মীগণ ॥১০৬॥
verses.transliteration: brahmāṇḍopari paravyoma, tāhāṅ ye svarūpa-gaṇa,\\ntāṅ-sabāra bale hare mana\\npati-vratā-śiromaṇi, yāṅre kahe veda-vāṇī,\\nākarṣaye sei lakṣmī-gaṇa
verses.translation: "The beauty of Kṛṣṇa's body is so attractive that it attracts not only the demigods and other living entities within this material world but the personalities of the spiritual sky as well, including the Nārāyaṇas, who are expansions of Kṛṣṇa's personality. The minds of the Nārāyaṇas are thus attracted by the beauty of Kṛṣṇa's body. In addition, the goddesses of fortune [Lakṣmīs]—who are wives of the Nārāyaṇas and are the women described in the Vedas as most chaste-are also attracted by the wonderful beauty of Kṛṣṇa.

verses.devanagari: চড়ি’ গোপী-মনোরথে, মন্মথের মন মথে,\\nনাম ধরে ‘মদনমোহন’ ।\\nজিনি’ পঞ্চশর-দর্প, স্বয়ং নবকন্দর্প,\\nরাস করে লঞা গোপীগণ ॥১০৭॥
verses.transliteration: caḍi' gopī-manorathe, manmathera mana mathe,\\nnāma dhare 'madana-mohana'\\njini' pañcaśara-darpa, svayaṁ nava-kandarpa,\\nrāsa kare lañā gopī-gaṇa
verses.translation: "Favoring them, Kṛṣṇa rides on the chariot of the minds of the gopīs, and just to receive loving service from them, He attracts their minds like Cupid. Therefore He is also called Madana-mohana, the attractor of Cupid. Cupid has five arrows, representing form, taste, smell, sound and touch. Kṛṣṇa is the owner of these five arrows, and with His Cupid-like beauty, He conquers the minds of the gopīs, though they are very proud of their superexcellent beauty. Becoming a new Cupid, Kṛṣṇa attracts their minds and engages in the rāsa dance.

verses.devanagari: নিজ-সম সখা-সঙ্গে, গোগণ-চারণ রঙ্গে,\\nবৃন্দাবনে স্বচ্ছন্দ বিহার ।\\nযাঁর বেণু-ধ্বনি শুনি,’ স্থাবর-জঙ্গম প্রাণী,\\nপুলক, কম্প, অশ্রু বহে ধার ॥১০৮॥
verses.transliteration: nija-sama sakhā-saṅge, go-gaṇa-cāraṇa raṅge,\\nvṛndāvane svacchanda vihāra\\nyāṅra veṇu-dhvani śuni' sthāvara-jaṅgama prāṇī,\\npulaka, kampa, aśru vahe dhāra
verses.translation: "When Lord Kṛṣṇa wanders in the forest of Vṛndāvana with His friends on an equal level, there are innumerable cows grazing. This is another of the Lord's blissful enjoyments. When He plays on His flute, all living entities-including trees, plants, animals and human beings-tremble and are saturated with jubilation. Tears flow constantly from their eyes.

verses.devanagari: মুক্তাহার — বকপাঁতি, ইন্দ্রধনু-পিঞ্ছ ততি,\\nপীতাম্বর — বিজুরী-সঞ্চার ।\\nকৃষ্ণ নব-জলধর, জগৎ-শস্য-উপর,\\nবরিষয়ে লীলামৃত-ধার ॥১০৯॥
verses.transliteration: muktā-hāra—baka-pāṅti, indra-dhanu-piñcha tati,\\npītāmbara—vijurī-sañcāra\\nkṛṣṇa nava-jaladhara, jagat-śasya-upara,\\nvariṣaye līlāmṛta-dhāra
verses.translation: "Kṛṣṇa wears a pearl necklace that appears like a chain of white ducks around His neck. The peacock feather in His hair appears like a rainbow, and His yellow garments appear like lightning in the sky. Kṛṣṇa appears like a newly risen cloud, and the gopīs appear like newly grown grains in the field. Constant rains of nectarean pastimes fall upon these newly grown grains, and it seems that the gopīs are receiving beams of life from Kṛṣṇa, exactly as grains receive life from the rains.

verses.devanagari: মাধুর্য ভগবত্তা-সার, ব্রজে কৈল পরচার,\\nতাহা শুক — ব্যাসের নন্দন ।\\nস্থানে স্থানে ভাগবতে, বর্ণিয়াছে জানাইতে,\\nতাহা শুনি’ মাতে ভক্তগণ ॥১১০॥
verses.transliteration: mādhurya bhagavattā-sāra, vraje kaila paracāra,\\ntāhā śuka—vyāsera nandana\\nsthāne sthāne bhāgavate, varṇiyāche jānāite,\\ntāhā śuni' māte bhakta-gaṇa
verses.translation: "The Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa, is full in all six opulences, including His attractive beauty, which engages Him in conjugal love with the gopīs. Such sweetness is the quintessence of His qualities. Śukadeva Gosvāmī, the son of Vyāsadeva, has described these pastimes of Kṛṣṇa throughout Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam. Hearing the descriptions, the devotees become mad with love of God."

verses.devanagari: কহিতে কৃষ্ণের রসে, শ্লোক পড়ে প্রেমাবেশে,\\nপ্রেমে সনাতন-হাত ধরি’ ।\\nগোপী-ভাগ্য, কৃষ্ণ গুণ, যে করিল বর্ণন,\\nভাবাবেশে মথুরা-নাগরী ॥১১১॥
verses.transliteration: kahite kṛṣṇera rase, śloka paḍe premāveśe,\\npreme sanātana-hāta dhari'\\ngopī-bhāgya, kṛṣṇa guṇa, ye karila varṇana,\\nbhāvāveśe mathurā-nāgarī
verses.translation: Just as the women of Mathurā ecstatically described the fortune of the gopīs of Vṛndāvana and the transcendental qualities of Kṛṣṇa, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu described the different mellows of Kṛṣṇa and became overwhelmed with ecstatic love. Grasping the hand of Sanātana Gosvāmī, He recited the following verse.

verses.devanagari: গোপ্যস্তপঃ কিমচরন্ যদমুষ্য রূপং\\nলাবণ্যসারমসমোর্ধ্বমনন্যসিদ্ধম্ ।\\nদৃগ্ভিঃ পিবন্ত্যনুসবাভিনবং দুরাপ-\\nমেকান্তধাম যশসঃ শ্রিয় ঐশ্বরস্য ॥১১২॥
verses.transliteration: gopyas tapaḥ kim acaran yad amuṣya rūpaṁ\\nlāvaṇya-sāram asamordhvam ananya-siddham\\ndṛgbhiḥ pibanty anusavābhinavaṁ durāpam\\nekānta-dhāma yaśasaḥ śriya aiśvarasya
verses.translation: “ 'What austerities must the gopīs have performed? With their eyes they always drink the nectar of the face of Lord Kṛṣṇa, which is the essence of loveliness and is not to be equaled or surpassed. That loveliness is the only abode of beauty, fame and opulence. It is self-perfect, ever fresh and unique.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This verse from
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(10.44.14) was spoken by the women of Mathurā when they saw Kṛṣṇa in the wrestling arena.

verses.devanagari: তারুণ্যামৃত — পারাবার, তরঙ্গ — লাবণ্যসার,\\nতাতে সে আবর্ত ভাবোদ্গম ।\\nবংশীধ্বনি — চক্রবাত, নারীর মন — তৃণপাত,\\nতাহা ডুবায়, না হয় উদ্গম ॥১১৩॥
verses.transliteration: tāruṇyāmṛta—pārāvāra, taraṅga—lāvaṇya-sāra,\\ntāte se āvarta bhāvodgama\\nvaṁśī-dhvani—cakravāta, nārīra mana—tṛṇa-pāta,\\ntāhā ḍubāya nā haya udgama
verses.translation: "The bodily beauty of Śrī Kṛṣṇa is like a wave in the ocean of eternal youth. In that great ocean is the whirlpool of the awakening of ecstatic love. The vibration of Kṛṣṇa's flute is like a whirlwind, and the flickering minds of the gopīs are like straws and dry leaves. After they fall down in the whirlwind, they never rise again but remain eternally at the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa.

verses.devanagari: সখি হে, কোন্ তপ কৈল গোপীগণ ।\\nকৃষ্ণরূপ-সুমাধুরী, পিবি’ পিবি’ নেত্র ভরি’,\\nশ্লাঘ্য করে জন্ম-তনু-মন ।। ১১৪ ।। ধ্রু ।। ॥১১৪॥
verses.transliteration: sakhī he, kon tapa kaila gopī-gaṇa\\nkṛṣṇa-rūpa-sumādhurī, pibi' pibi' netra bhari',\\nślāghya kare janma-tanu-mana
verses.translation: "O my dear friend, what severe austerities have the gopīs performed to drink His transcendental beauty and sweetness through their eyes in complete fulfillment? Thus they glorify their births, bodies and minds.

verses.devanagari: যে মাধুরীর ঊর্ধ্ব আন, নাহি যার সমান,\\nপরব্যোমে স্বরূপের গণে ।\\nযেঁহো সব-অবতারী, পরব্যোম-অধিকারী,\\nএ মাধুর্য নাহি নারায়ণে ॥১১৫॥
verses.transliteration: ye mādhurīra ūrdhva āna, nāhi yāra samāna,\\nparavyome svarūpera gaṇe\\nyeṅho saba-avatārī, paravyoma-adhikārī,\\ne mādhurya nāhi nārāyaṇe
verses.translation: "The sweetness of Kṛṣṇa's beauty enjoyed by the gopīs is unparalleled. Nothing is equal to or greater than such ecstatic sweetness. Even the predominating Deities of the Vaikuṇṭha planets, the Nārāyaṇas, do not possess such sweetness. Indeed, none of the incarnations of Kṛṣṇa up to Nārāyaṇa possess such transcendental beauty.

verses.devanagari: তাতে সাক্ষী সেই রমা, নারায়ণের প্রিয়তমা,\\nপতিব্রতাগণের উপাস্যা ।\\nতিঁহো যে মাধুর্যলোভে, ছাড়ি’ সব কামভোগে,\\nব্রত করি’ করিলা তপস্যা ॥১১৬॥
verses.transliteration: tāte sākṣī sei ramā, nārāyaṇera priyatamā,\\npativratā-gaṇera upāsyā\\ntiṅho ye mādhurya-lobhe, chāḍi' saba kāma-bhoge,\\nvrata kari' karilā tapasyā
verses.translation: "Even the dearest consort of Nārāyaṇa, the goddess of fortune, who is worshiped by all chaste women, is captivated by the unparalleled sweetness of Kṛṣṇa. She even gave up everything in her desire to enjoy Kṛṣṇa, and taking a great vow, she underwent severe austerities.

verses.devanagari: সেই ত’ মাধুর্য-সার, অন্য-সিদ্ধি নাহি তার,\\nতিঁহো — মাধুর্যাদি-গুণখনি ।\\nআর সব প্রকাশে, তাঁর দত্ত গুণ ভাসে,\\nযাহাঁ যত প্রকাশে কার্য জানি ॥১১৭॥
verses.transliteration: sei ta' mādhurya-sāra, anya-siddhi nāhi tāra,\\ntiṅho—mādhuryādi-guṇa-khani\\nāra saba prakāśe, tāṅra datta guṇa bhāse,\\nyāhāṅ yata prakāśe kārya jāni
verses.translation: "The quintessence of Kṛṣṇa's sweet bodily luster is so perfect that there is no perfection above it. He is the immutable mine of all transcendental qualities. In His other manifestations and personal expansions, there is only a partial exhibition of such qualities. We understand all His personal expansions in this way.

verses.devanagari: গোপীভাব-দরপণ, নব নব ক্ষণে ক্ষণ,\\nতার আগে কৃষ্ণের মাধুর্য ।\\nদোঁহে করে হুড়াহুড়ি, বাড়ে, মুখ নাহি মুড়ি,\\nনব নব দোঁহার প্রাচুর্য ॥১১৮॥
verses.transliteration: gopī-bhāva-darapaṇa, nava nava kṣaṇe kṣaṇa,\\ntāra āge kṛṣṇera mādhurya\\ndoṅhe kare huḍāhuḍi, bāḍe, mukha nāhi muḍi,\\nnava nava doṅhāra prācurya
verses.translation: "Both the gopīs and Kṛṣṇa are complete. The gopīs' ecstatic love is like a mirror that becomes newer and newer at every moment and reflects Kṛṣṇa's bodily luster and sweetness. Thus competition increases. Since neither give up, their pastimes become newer and newer, and both sides constantly increase.

verses.devanagari: কর্ম, তপ, যোগ, জ্ঞান, বিধি-ভক্তি, জপ, ধ্যান,\\nইহা হৈতে মাধুর্য দুর্লভ ।\\nকেবল যে রাগমার্গে, ভজে কৃষ্ণে অনুরাগে,\\nতারে কৃষ্ণমাধুর্য সুলভ ॥১১৯॥
verses.transliteration: karma, tapa, yoga, jñāna, vidhi-bhakti, japa, dhyāna,\\nihā haite mādhurya durlabha\\nkevala ye rāga-mārge, bhaje kṛṣṇe anurāge,\\ntāre kṛṣṇa-mādhurya sulabha
verses.translation: "The transcendental mellows generated from the dealings between the gopīs and Kṛṣṇa cannot be tasted by fruitive activity, yogic austerities, speculative knowledge, regulative devotional service, mantra-yoga or meditation. This sweetness can be tasted only through the spontaneous love of liberated persons who chant the holy names with great ecstatic love.

verses.devanagari: সেইরূপ ব্রজাশ্রয়, ঐশ্বর্য-মাধুর্যময়,\\nদিব্যগুণগণ-রত্নালয় ।\\nআনের বৈভব-সত্তা, কৃষ্ণদত্ত ভগবত্তা,\\nকৃষ্ণ — সর্ব-অংশী, সর্বাশ্রয় ॥১২০॥
verses.transliteration: sei-rūpa vrajāśraya, aiśvarya-mādhuryamaya,\\ndivya-guṇa-gaṇa-ratnālaya\\nānera vaibhava-sattā, kṛṣṇa-datta bhagavattā,\\nkṛṣṇa—sarva-aṁśī, sarvāśraya
verses.translation: "Such ecstatic transactions between Kṛṣṇa and the gopīs are only possible in Vṛndāvana, which is full of the opulences of transcendental love. The form of Kṛṣṇa is the original source of all transcendental qualities. It is like a mine of gems. The opulences belonging to all the personal expansions of Kṛṣṇa are to be understood to be bestowed by Kṛṣṇa; therefore Kṛṣṇa is the original source and shelter of everyone.

verses.devanagari: শ্রী, লজ্জা, দয়া, কীর্তি, ধৈর্য, বৈশারদী মতি,\\nএই সব কৃষ্ণে প্রতিষ্ঠিত ।\\nসুশীল, মৃদু, বদান্য, কৃষ্ণ-সম নাহি অন্য,\\nকৃষ্ণ করে জগতের হিত ॥১২১॥
verses.transliteration: śrī, lajjā, dayā, kīrti, dhairya, vaiśāradī mati,\\nei saba kṛṣṇe pratiṣṭhita\\nsuśīla, mṛdu, vadānya, kṛṣṇa-sama nāhi anya,\\nkṛṣṇa kare jagatera hita
verses.translation: "Beauty, humility, mercy, merit, patience and expert intelligence are all manifest in Kṛṣṇa. But besides these, Kṛṣṇa has other qualities like good behavior, mildness and magnanimity. He also performs welfare activities for the whole world. All these qualities are not visible in expansions like Nārāyaṇa.
verses.purport: PURPORT\nŚrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura mentions that the qualities of beauty, humility, mercy, merit, patience and expert intelligence are brilliant qualities, and when they are exhibited in the person of Nārāyaṇa, one should know that they are bestowed upon Nārāyaṇa by Kṛṣṇa. Good behavior, mildness and magnanimity are found only in Kṛṣṇa. Only Kṛṣṇa performs welfare activities for the whole world.

verses.devanagari: কৃষ্ণ দেখি’ নানা জন, কৈল নিমিষে নিন্দন,\\nব্রজে বিধি নিন্দে গোপীগণ ।\\nসেই সব শ্লোক পড়ি’, মহাপ্রভু অর্থ করি’,\\nসুখে মাধুর্য করে আস্বাদন ॥১২২॥
verses.transliteration: kṛṣṇa dekhi' nānā jana, kaila nimiṣe nindana,\\nvraje vidhi ninde gopī-gaṇa\\nsei saba śloka paḍi', mahāprabhu artha kari',\\nsukhe mādhurya kare āsvādana
verses.translation: "After seeing Kṛṣṇa, various people criticize the blinking of their eyes. In Vṛndāvana, especially, all the gopīs criticize Lord Brahmā because of this defect in the eyes." Then Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu recited some verses from Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam and explained them vividly, thus enjoying the taste of transcendental sweetness with great happiness.

verses.devanagari: যস্যাননং মকরকুণ্ডলচারুকর্ণ-\\nভ্রাজৎকপোলসুভগং সবিলাসহাসম্ ।\\nনিত্যোৎসবং ন ততৃপুর্দৃশিভিঃ পিবন্ত্যো\\nনার্যো নরাশ্চ মুদিতাঃ কুপিতা নিমেশ্চ ॥১২৩॥
verses.transliteration: yasyānanaṁ makara-kuṇḍala-cāru-karṇa-\\nbhrājat-kapola-subhagaṁ savilāsa-hāsam\\nnityotsavaṁ na tatṛpur dṛśibhiḥ pibantyo\\nnāryo narāś ca muditāḥ kupitā nimeś ca
verses.translation: “ 'All men and women were accustomed to enjoying the beauty of the shining face of Lord Kṛṣṇa, as well as His sharklike earrings swinging on His ears. His beautiful features, His cheeks and His playful smiles all combined to form a constant festival for the eyes, and the blinking of the eyes became obstacles that impeded one from seeing that beauty. For this reason, men and women became very angry at the creator [Lord Brahmā].'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a verse from
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(9.24.65).

verses.devanagari: অটতি যদ্ভবানহ্নি কাননং ক্রটির্যুগায়তে ত্বামপশ্যতাম্ ।\\nকুটিলকুন্তলং শ্রী মুখঞ্চ তে জড় উদীক্ষতাং পক্ষ্মকৃদ্দৃশাম্ ॥১২৪॥
verses.transliteration: aṭati yad bhavān ahni kānanaṁ\\ntruṭir yugāyate tvām apaśyatām\\nkuṭila-kuntalaṁ śrī-mukhaṁ ca te\\njaḍa udīkṣatāṁ pakṣma-kṛd dṛśām
verses.translation: “ 'O Kṛṣṇa, when You go to the forest during the day and we do not see Your sweet face, which is surrounded by beautiful, curling hair, half a second becomes as long as an entire age for us. And we consider the creator, who has put eyelids on the eyes we use for seeing You, to be simply a fool.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This verse is spoken by the
gopīs
in
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(10.31.15).

verses.devanagari: কামগায়ত্রী-মন্ত্ররূপ, হয় কৃষ্ণের স্বরূপ,\\nসার্ধ-চব্বিশ অক্ষর তার হয় ।\\nসে অক্ষর ‘চন্দ্র’ হয়, কৃষ্ণে করি’ উদয়,\\nত্রিজগৎ কৈলা কামময় ॥১২৫॥
verses.transliteration: kāma-gāyatrī-mantra-rūpa, haya kṛṣṇera svarūpa,\\nsārdha-cabbiśa akṣara tāra haya\\nse akṣara 'candra' haya, kṛṣṇe kari' udaya,\\ntrijagat kailā kāmamaya
verses.translation: "Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, is identical with the Vedic hymn known as the kāma-gāyatrī, which is composed of twenty-four and a half syllables. Those syllables are compared to moons that arise in Kṛṣṇa. Thus all three worlds are filled with desire.

verses.devanagari: সখি হে, কৃষ্ণমুখ — দ্বিজরাজ-রাজ ।\\nকৃষ্ণবপু-সিংহাসনে, বসি’ রাজ্য-শাসনে,\\nকরে সঙ্গে চন্দ্রের সমাজ ।। ১২৬ ।। ধ্রু ।। ॥১২৬॥
verses.transliteration: sakhī he, kṛṣṇa-mukha—dvija-rāja-rāja\\nkṛṣṇa-vapu-siṁhāsane, vasi' rājya-śāsane,\\nkare saṅge candrera samāja
verses.translation: "The face of Kṛṣṇa is the king of all moons, and the body of Kṛṣṇa is the throne. Thus the king governs a society of moons.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
The entire face is called the king of moons. The mouth is another moon, the left cheek is a moon, and the right cheek is a moon. The spots of sandalwood pulp on Kṛṣṇa's face are also considered different moons, and His fingernails and toenails are also different moons. His forehead is considered a half moon, His face is considered the king of moons, and His body is considered the throne. All the other
candras
(moons) are considered to be subordinate moons.

verses.devanagari: দুই গণ্ড সুচিক্কণ, জিনি’ মণিসুদর্পণ,\\nসেই দুই পূর্ণচন্দ্র জানি ।\\nললাটে অষ্টমী-ইন্দু, তাহাতে চন্দন-বিন্দু,\\nসেহ এক পূর্ণচন্দ্র মানি ॥১২৭॥
verses.transliteration: dui gaṇḍa sucikkaṇa, jini' maṇi-sudarpaṇa,\\nsei dui pūrṇa-candra jāni\\nlalāṭe aṣṭamī-indu, tāhāte candana-bindu,\\nsei eka pūrṇa-candra māni
verses.translation: "Kṛṣṇa has two cheeks that shine like glowing gems. Both are considered full moons. His forehead is considered a half moon, and His spots of sandalwood are considered full moons.

verses.devanagari: করনখ-চান্দের হাট, বংশী-উপর করে নাট,\\nতার গীত মুরলীর তান ।\\nপদনখ-চন্দ্রগণ, তলে করে নর্তন,\\nনূপুরের ধ্বনি যার গান ॥১২৮॥
verses.transliteration: kara-nakha-cāndera hāṭa, vaṁśī-upara kare nāṭa,\\ntāra gīta muralīra tāna\\npada-nakha-candra-gaṇa, tale kare nartana,\\nnūpurera dhvani yāra gāna
verses.translation: "His fingernails are many full moons, and they dance on the flute on His hands. Their song is the melody of that flute. His toenails are also many full moons, and they dance on the ground. Their song is the jingling of His ankle bells.

verses.devanagari: নাচে মকর-কুণ্ডল, নেত্র — লীলা-কমল,\\nবিলাসী রাজা সতত নাচায় ।\\nভ্রূ — ধনু, নেত্র — বাণ, ধনুর্গুণ — দুই কাণ,\\nনারীমন-লক্ষ্য বিন্ধে তায় ॥১২৯॥
verses.transliteration: nāce makara-kuṇḍala, netra—līlā-kamala,\\nvilāsī rājā satata nācāya\\nbhrū—dhanu, netra—bāṇa, dhanur-guṇa—dui kāṇa,\\nnārī-mana-lakṣya vindhe tāya
verses.translation: "Kṛṣṇa's face is the enjoyer king. That full-moon face makes His shark-shaped earrings and lotus eyes dance. His eyebrows are like bows, and His eyes are like arrows. His ears are fixed on the string of that bow, and when His eyes spread to His ears, He pierces the hearts of the gopīs.

verses.devanagari: এই চান্দের বড় নাট, পসারি’ চান্দের হাট,\\nবিনিমূলে বিলায় নিজামৃত ।\\nকাহোঁ স্মিত-জ্যোত্স্নামৃতে, কাঁহারে অধরামৃতে,\\nসব লোক করে আপ্যায়িত ॥১৩০॥
verses.transliteration: ei cāndera baḍa nāṭa, pasāri' cāndera hāṭa,\\nvinimūle vilāya nijāmṛta\\nkāhoṅ smita-jyotsnāmṛte, kāṅhāre adharāmṛte,\\nsaba loka kare āpyāyita
verses.translation: "The dancing features of His face surpass all other full moons and expand the marketplace of full moons. Although priceless, the nectar of Kṛṣṇa's face is distributed to everyone. Some purchase the moonrays of His sweet smiles, and others purchase the nectar of His lips. Thus He pleases everyone.

verses.devanagari: বিপুলায়তারুণ, মদন-মদ-ঘূর্ণন,\\nমন্ত্রী যার এ দুই নয়ন ।\\nলাবণ্যকেলি-সদন, জন-নেত্র-রসায়ন,\\nসুখময় গোবিন্দ-বদন ॥১৩১॥
verses.transliteration: vipulāyatāruṇa, madana-mada-ghūrṇana,\\nmantrī yāra e dui nayana\\nlāvaṇya-keli-sadana, jana-netra-rasāyana,\\nsukhamaya govinda-vadana
verses.translation: "Kṛṣṇa has two reddish, widely spread eyes. These are ministers of the king, and they subdue the pride of Cupid, who also has beautiful eyes. That face of Govinda, which is full of happiness, is the home of the pastimes of beauty, and it is very pleasing to everyone's eyes.

verses.devanagari: যাঁর পুণ্যপুঞ্জফলে, সে-মুখ-দর্শন মিলে,\\nদুই আঁখি কি করিবে পানে ?\\nদ্বিগুণ বাড়ে তৃষ্ণা-লোভ, পিতে নারে — মনঃক্ষোভ,\\nদুঃখে করে বিধির নিন্দনে ॥১৩২॥
verses.transliteration: yāṅra puṇya-puñja-phale, se-mukha-darśana mile,\\ndui āṅkhi ki karibe pāne?\\ndviguṇa bāḍe tṛṣṇā-lobha, pite nāre—manaḥ-kṣobha,\\nduḥkhe kare vidhira nindane
verses.translation: "If by devotional service one gets the results of pious activities and sees Lord Kṛṣṇa's face, he can relish the Lord with his eyes. His greed and thirst then increase twofold by seeing the nectarean face of Kṛṣṇa. Due to one's inability to sufficiently drink that nectar, one becomes very unhappy and criticizes the creator for not having given more than two eyes.

verses.devanagari: না দিলেক লক্ষ-কোটি, সবে দিলা আঁখি দুটি,\\nতাতে দিলা নিমিষ-আচ্ছাদন ।\\nবিধি — জড় তপোধন, রসশূন্য তার মন,\\nনাহি জানে যোগ্য সৃজন ॥১৩৩॥
verses.transliteration: nā dileka lakṣa-koṭi, sabe dilā āṅkhi duṭi,\\ntāte dilā nimiṣa-ācchādana\\nvidhi—jaḍa tapodhana, rasa-śūnya tāra mana,\\nnāhi jāne yogya sṛjana
verses.translation: "When the onlooker of Kṛṣṇa's face becomes dissatisfied in this way, he thinks, 'Why didn't the creator give me thousands and millions of eyes? Why has he given me only two? Even these two eyes are disturbed by blinking, which keeps me from continuously seeing Kṛṣṇa's face.' Thus one accuses the creator of being dry and tasteless due to engaging in severe austerities. 'The creator is only a dry manufacturer. He does not know how to create and set things in their proper places.

verses.devanagari: যে দেখিবে কৃষ্ণানন, তার করে দ্বি-নয়ন,\\nবিধি হঞা হেন অবিচার ।\\nমোর যদি বোল ধরে, কোটি আঁখি তার করে,\\nতবে জানি যোগ্য সৃষ্টি তার ॥১৩৪॥
verses.transliteration: ye dekhibe kṛṣṇānana, tāra kare dvi-nayana,\\nvidhi hañā hena avicāra\\nmora yadi bola dhare, koṭi āṅkhi tāra kare,\\ntabe jāni yogya sṛṣṭi tāra
verses.translation: “ 'The creator says, "Let those who will see Kṛṣṇa's beautiful face have two eyes." Just see the lack of consideration exhibited by this person posing as a creator. If the creator took my advice, he would give millions of eyes to the person who intends to see Śrī Kṛṣṇa's face. If the creator will accept this advice, then I would say that he is competent in his work.'

verses.devanagari: কৃষ্ণাঙ্গ-মাধুর্য — সিন্ধু, সুমধুর মুখ — ইন্দু,\\nঅতি-মধু স্মিত — সুকিরণে ।\\nএ-তিনে লাগিল মন, লোভে করে আস্বাদন,\\nশ্লোক পড়ে স্বহস্ত-চালনে ॥১৩৫॥
verses.transliteration: kṛṣṇāṅga-mādhurya—sindhu, sumadhura mukha—indu,\\nati-madhu smita—sukiraṇe\\ne-tine lāgila mana, lobhe kare āsvādana,\\nśloka paḍe svahasta-cālane
verses.translation: "The transcendental form of Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa is compared to an ocean. A particularly extraordinary vision is the moon above that ocean, and another vision is His smile, which is sweeter than sweet and is like shining beams of moonlight." While speaking of these things with Sanātana Gosvāmī, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu began to remember one thing after another. Moving His hands in ecstasy, He recited a verse.

verses.devanagari: মধুরং মধুরং বপুরস্য বিভোর্মধুরং মধুরং বদনং মধুরম্ ।\\nমধুগন্ধি মৃদুস্মিতমেতদহো মধুরং মধুরং মধুরং মধুরম্ ॥১৩৬॥
verses.transliteration: madhuraṁ madhuraṁ vapur asya vibhor\\nmadhuraṁ madhuraṁ vadanaṁ madhuram\\nmadhu-gandhi mṛdu-smitam etad aho\\nmadhuraṁ madhuraṁ madhuraṁ madhuram
verses.translation: “ 'O my Lord, the transcendental body of Kṛṣṇa is very sweet, and His face is even sweeter than His body. The soft smile on His face, which is like the fragrance of honey, is sweeter still.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a verse quoted from
Kṛṣṇa-karṇāmṛta
by Bilvamaṅgala Ṭhākura.

verses.devanagari: সনাতন, কৃষ্ণমাধুর্য — অমৃতের সিন্ধু ।\\nমোর মন — সন্নিপাতি, সব পিতে করে মতি,\\nদুর্দৈব-বৈদ্য না দেয় এক বিন্দু ।। ১৩৭ ।। ধ্রু ।। ॥১৩৭॥
verses.transliteration: sanātana, kṛṣṇa-mādhurya—amṛtera sindhu\\nmora mana—sannipāti, saba pite kare mati,\\ndurdaiva-vaidya nā deya eka bindu
verses.translation: "My dear Sanātana, the sweetness of Kṛṣṇa's personality is just like an ocean of ambrosia. Although My mind is now afflicted by convulsive diseases and I wish to drink that entire ocean, the repressive physician does not allow Me to drink even one drop.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
When there is a combination of
kapha, pitta
and
vāyu,
the three bodily elements, there occurs
sannipāti,
or a convulsive disease. "This disease is caused by the personal features of Lord Kṛṣṇa. The three elements are the beauty of Kṛṣṇa's body, the beauty of His face, and the beauty of His smile. Stricken by these three beauties, My mind goes into convulsions. It wishes to drink the ocean of Kṛṣṇa's beauty, but because I am undergoing convulsions, My physician, who is Śrī Kṛṣṇa Himself, does not even allow Me to take a drop of water from that ocean." Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was ecstatic in this way because He was presenting Himself in the mood of the
gopīs.
The
gopīs
wanted to drink the ocean of sweetness arising from the bodily features of Kṛṣṇa, but Kṛṣṇa did not allow them to come near. Consequently their desire to meet Kṛṣṇa increased, and being unable to drink the ambrosia of Kṛṣṇa's bodily features, they became very unhappy.

verses.devanagari: কৃষ্ণাঙ্গ — লাবণ্যপূর, মধুর হৈতে সুমধুর, তাতে যেই মুখ সুধাকর  ।\\nমধুর হৈতে সুমধুর, তাহা হইতে সুমধুর, তার যেই স্মিত জ্যোৎস্না-ভর ॥১৩৮॥
verses.transliteration: kṛṣṇāṅga—lāvaṇya-pūra, madhura haite sumadhura,\\ntāte yei mukha sudhākara\\nmadhura haite sumadhura, tāhā ha-ite sumadhura,\\ntāra yei smita jyotsnā-bhara
verses.translation: "Kṛṣṇa's body is a city of attractive features, and it is sweeter than sweet. His face, which is like the moon, is sweeter still, and the gentle smile on that moonlike face is like rays of moonshine.
verses.purport: PURPORT\nThe smile on Kṛṣṇa's face is just like the smiling of the moon, which generates greater and greater happiness for the\ngopīs.

verses.devanagari: মধুর হৈতে সুমধুর, তাহা হৈতে সুমধুর, তাহা হৈতে অতি সুমধুর  ।\\nআপনার এক কণে, ব্যাপে সব ত্রিভুবনে, দশদিক্ ব্যাপে যার পূর ॥১৩৯॥
verses.transliteration: madhura haite sumadhura, tāhā haite sumadhura,\\ntāhā haite ati sumadhura\\nāpanāra eka kaṇe, vyāpe saba tribhuvane,\\ndaśa-dik vyāpe yāra pūra
verses.translation: "The beauty of Kṛṣṇa's smile is the sweetest feature of all. His smile is like a full moon that spreads its rays throughout the three worlds-Goloka Vṛndāvana, the spiritual sky of the Vaikuṇṭhas, and Devī-dhāma, the material world. Thus Kṛṣṇa's shining beauty spreads in all ten directions.

verses.devanagari: স্মিত-কিরণ-সুকর্পূরে, পৈশে অধর-মধুরে,\\nসেই মধু মাতায় ত্রিভুবনে ।\\nবংশীছিদ্র আকাশে, তার গুণ শব্দে পৈশে,\\nধ্বনিরূপে পাঞা পরিণামে ॥১৪০॥
verses.transliteration: smita-kiraṇa-sukarpūre, paiśe adhara-madhure,\\nsei madhu mātāya tribhuvane\\nvaṁśī-chidra ākāśe, tāra guṇa śabde paiśe,\\ndhvani-rūpe pāñā pariṇāme
verses.translation: "His slight smiling and fragrant illumination are compared to camphor, which enters the sweetness of the lips. That sweetness is transformed and enters into space as vibrations from the holes of His flute.

verses.devanagari: সে ধ্বনি চৌদিকে ধায়, অণ্ড ভেদি’ বৈকুণ্ঠে যায়,\\nবলে পৈশে জগতের কাণে ।\\nসবা মাতোয়াল করি’, বলাৎকারে আনে ধরি’,\\nবিশেষতঃ যুবতীর গণে ॥১৪১॥
verses.transliteration: se dhvani caudike dhāya, aṇḍa bhedi' vaikuṇṭhe yāya,\\nbale paiśe jagatera kāṇe\\nsabā mātoyāla kari', balātkāre āne dhari',\\nviśeṣataḥ yuvatīra gaṇe
verses.translation: "The sound of Kṛṣṇa's flute spreads in four directions. Even though Kṛṣṇa vibrates His flute within this universe, its sound pierces the universal covering and goes to the spiritual sky. Thus the vibration enters the ears of all inhabitants. It especially enters Goloka Vṛndāvana-dhāma and attracts the minds of the young damsels of Vrajabhūmi, bringing them forcibly to where Kṛṣṇa is present.

verses.devanagari: ধ্বনি — বড় উদ্ধত, পতিব্রতার ভাঙ্গে ব্রত,\\nপতি কোল হৈতে টানি’ আনে ।\\nবৈকুণ্ঠের লক্ষ্মীগণে, যেই করে আকর্ষণে,\\nতার আগে কেবা গোপীগণে ॥১৪২॥
verses.transliteration: dhvani—baḍa uddhata, pativratāra bhāṅge vrata,\\npati-kola haite ṭāni' āne\\nvaikuṇṭhera lakṣmī-gaṇe, yei kare ākarṣaṇe,\\ntāra āge kebā gopī-gaṇe
verses.translation: "The vibration of Kṛṣṇa's flute is very aggressive, and it breaks the vows of all chaste women. Indeed, its vibration takes them forcibly from the laps of their husbands. The vibration of His flute attracts even the goddesses of fortune in the Vaikuṇṭha planets, to say nothing of the poor damsels of Vṛndāvana.

verses.devanagari: নীবি খসায় পতি-আগে, গৃহধর্ম করায় ত্যাগে,\\nবলে ধরি’ আনে কৃষ্ণস্থানে ।\\nলোকধর্ম, লজ্জা, ভয়, সব জ্ঞান লুপ্ত হয়,\\nঐছে নাচায় সব নারীগণে ॥১৪৩॥
verses.transliteration: nīvi khasāya pati-āge, gṛha-dharma karāya tyāge,\\nbale dhari' āne kṛṣṇa-sthāne\\nloka-dharma, lajjā, bhaya, saba jñāna lupta haya,\\naiche nācāya saba nārī-gaṇe
verses.translation: "The vibration of His flute slackens the knots of their underwear even in front of their husbands. Thus the gopīs are forced to abandon their household duties and come before Lord Kṛṣṇa. In this way all social etiquette, shame and fear are vanquished. The vibration of His flute causes all women to dance.

verses.devanagari: কাণের ভিতর বাসা করে, আপনে তাঁহা সদা স্ফুরে,\\nঅন্য শব্দ না দেয় প্রবেশিতে ।\\nআন কথা না শুনে কাণ, আন বলিতে বোলয় আন,\\nএই কৃষ্ণের বংশীর চরিতে ॥১৪৪॥
verses.transliteration: kāṇera bhitara vāsā kare, āpane tāṅhā sadā sphure,\\nanya śabda nā deya praveśite\\nāna kathā nā śune kāṇa, āna balite bolaya āna,\\nei kṛṣṇera vaṁśīra carite
verses.translation: "The vibration of His flute is just like a bird that creates a nest within the ears of the gopīs and always remains prominent there, not allowing any other sound to enter their ears. Indeed, the gopīs cannot hear anything else, nor are they able to concentrate on anything else, not even to give a suitable reply. Such are the effects of the vibration of Lord Kṛṣṇa's flute."
verses.purport:
PURPORT
The vibration of Kṛṣṇa's flute is always prominent in the ears of the
gopīs.
Naturally they cannot hear anything else. Constant remembrance of the holy sound of Kṛṣṇa's flute keeps them enlightened and enlivened, and they do not allow any other sound to enter their ears. Since their attention is fixed on Kṛṣṇa's flute, they cannot divert their minds to any other subject. In other words, a devotee who has heard the sound of Kṛṣṇa's flute forgets to talk or hear of any other subject. This vibration of Kṛṣṇa's flute is represented by the Hare Kṛṣṇa
mahā-mantra.
A serious devotee of the Lord who chants and hears this transcendental vibration becomes so accustomed to it that he cannot divert his attention to any subject matter not related to Kṛṣṇa's blissful characteristics and paraphernalia.

verses.devanagari: পুনঃ কহে বাহ্যজ্ঞানে, আন কহিতে কহিলুঁ আনে,\\nকৃষ্ণ-কৃপা তোমার উপরে ।\\nমোর চিত্ত-ভ্রম করি’, নিজৈশ্বর্য-মাধুরী,\\nমোর মুখে শুনায় তোমারে ॥১৪৫॥
verses.transliteration: punaḥ kahe bāhya-jñāne, āna kahite kahiluṅ āne,\\nkṛṣṇa-kṛpā tomāra upare\\nmora citta-bhrama kari', nijaiśvarya-mādhurī,\\nmora mukhe śunāya tomāre
verses.translation: Resuming His external consciousness, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu told Sanātana Gosvāmī, "I have not spoken of what I intended. Lord Kṛṣṇa is very merciful to you because by bewildering My mind, He has exposed His personal opulence and sweetness. He has caused you to hear all these things from Me for your understanding.
verses.purport: PURPORT\nŚrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu admitted that He was speaking like a madman, which He should not have done for the understanding of those who are externally situated. Statements about Kṛṣṇa's body, His characteristics and His flute would appear like a madman's statements to a mundane person. It was actually a fact that Kṛṣṇa wanted to expose Himself to Sanātana Gosvāmī due to His specific mercy upon him. Somehow or other, Kṛṣṇa explained Himself and His flute to Sanātana Gosvāmī through the mouth of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, who appeared as though mad. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu admitted that He wanted to tell Sanātana Gosvāmī something else, but somehow or other, in a transcendental ecstasy, He spoke of a different subject matter.

verses.devanagari: আমি ত’ বাউল, আন কহিতে আন কহি ।\\nকৃষ্ণের মাধুর্যামৃতস্রোতে যাই বহি’ ॥১৪৬॥
verses.transliteration: āmi ta' bāula, āna kahite āna kahi\\nkṛṣṇera mādhuryāmṛta-srote yāi vahi'
verses.translation: "Since I have become a madman, I am saying one thing instead of another. This is because I am being carried away by the waves of the nectarean ocean of Lord Kṛṣṇa's transcendental sweetness."

verses.devanagari: তবে মহাপ্রভু ক্ষণেক মৌন করি’ রহে ।\\nমনে এক করি’ পুনঃ সনাতনে কহে ॥১৪৭॥
verses.transliteration: tabe mahāprabhu kṣaṇeka mauna kari' rahe\\nmane eka kari' punaḥ sanātane kahe
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then remained silent for a moment. Finally, adjusting things within His mind, He again spoke to Sanātana Gosvāmī.

verses.devanagari: কৃষ্ণের মাধুরী আর মহাপ্রভুর মুখে ।\\nইহা যেই শুনে, সেই ভাসে প্রেমসুখে ॥১৪৮॥
verses.transliteration: kṛṣṇera mādhurī āra mahāprabhura mukhe\\nihā yei śune, sei bhāse prema-sukhe
verses.translation: I now summarize these teachings of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. If anyone gets an opportunity to hear about the sweetness of Kṛṣṇa in this chapter of Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, he will certainly be eligible to float in the transcendentally blissful ocean of love of God.

verses.devanagari: শ্রীরূপ-রঘুনাথ-পদে যার আশ ।\\nচৈতন্যচরিতামৃত কহে কৃষ্ণদাস ॥১৪৯॥
verses.transliteration: śrī-rūpa-raghunātha-pade yāra āśa\\ncaitanya-caritāmṛta kahe kṛṣṇadāsa
verses.translation: Praying at the lotus feet of Śrī Rūpa and Śrī Raghunātha, always desiring their mercy, I, Kṛṣṇadāsa, narrate Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, following in their footsteps.
verses.purport: PURPORT\nThus end the Bhaktivedanta purports to Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā,  Twenty-first Chapter, describing the blissful characteristics of Kṛṣṇa.

sections.title: Chapter 22: The Process of Devotional Service

verses.devanagari: বন্দে শ্রীকৃষ্ণচৈতন্যদেবং তং করুণার্ণবম্ ।\\nকলাবপ্যতিগূঢ়েয়ং ভক্তির্যেন প্রকাশিতা ॥১॥
verses.transliteration: vande śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya-\\ndevaṁ taṁ karuṇārṇavam\\nkalāv apy ati-gūḍheyaṁ\\nbhaktir yena prakāśitā
verses.translation: I offer my respectful obeisances unto Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. He is an ocean of transcendental mercy, and although the subject matter of bhakti-yoga is very confidential, He has nonetheless manifested it so niceIy, even in this Age of Kali, the age of quarrel.

verses.devanagari: জয় জয় শ্রীকৃষ্ণচৈতন্য নিত্যানন্দ ।\\nজয়াদ্বৈতচন্দ্র জয় গৌরভক্তবৃন্দ ॥২॥
verses.transliteration: jaya jaya śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya nityānanda\\njayādvaita-candra jaya gaura-bhakta-vṛnda
verses.translation: All glories to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu! All glories to Nityānanda Prabhu! All glories to Advaitacandra! All glories to all the devotees of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu!

verses.devanagari: এইত কহিলুঁ সম্বন্ধ-তত্ত্বের বিচার ।\\nবেদশাস্ত্রে উপদেশে, কৃষ্ণ — এক সার ॥৩॥
verses.transliteration: eita kahiluṅ sambandha-tattvera vicāra\\nveda-śāstre upadeśe, kṛṣṇa—eka sāra
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "I have described one's relation with Kṛṣṇa in various ways. This is the subject matter of all the Vedas. Kṛṣṇa is the center of all activities.

verses.devanagari: এবে কহি, শুন, অভিধেয় লক্ষণ ।\\nযাহা হৈতে পাই — কৃষ্ণ, কৃষ্ণপ্রেমধন ॥৪॥
verses.transliteration: ebe kahi, śuna, abhidheya-lakṣaṇa\\nyāhā haite pāi—kṛṣṇa, kṛṣṇa-prema-dhana
verses.translation: "Now I shall speak about the characteristics of devotional service, by which one can attain the shelter of Kṛṣṇa and His loving transcendental service.

verses.devanagari: কৃষ্ণভক্তি — অভিধেয়, সর্বশাস্ত্রে কয় ।\\nঅতএব মুনিগণ করিয়াছে নিশ্চয় ॥৫॥
verses.transliteration: kṛṣṇa-bhakti—abhidheya, sarva-śāstre kaya\\nataeva muni-gaṇa kariyāche niścaya
verses.translation: "A human being's activities should be centered only about devotional service to Lord Kṛṣṇa. That is the verdict of all Vedic literatures, and all saintly people have ascertained this.

verses.devanagari: শ্রুতির্মাতা-পৃষ্টা দিশতি ভবদারাধনবিধিং\\nযথা মাতুর্বাণী স্মৃতিরপি তথা বক্তি ভগিনী ।\\nপুরাণাদ্যা যে বা সহজনিবহাস্তে তদনুগা\\nঅতঃ সত্যং জ্ঞাতং মুরহর ভবানেব শরণম্ ॥৬॥
verses.transliteration: śrutir mātā pṛṣṭā diśati bhavad-ārādhana-vidhiṁ\\nyathā mātur vāṇī smṛtir api tathā vakti bhaginī\\npurāṇādyā ye vā sahaja-nivahās te tad-anugā\\nataḥ satyaṁ jñātaṁ murahara bhavān eva śaraṇam
verses.translation: “ 'When the mother Vedas [śruti] is questioned as to whom to worship, she says that You are the only Lord and worshipable object. Similarly, the corollaries of the śruti-śāstras, the smṛti-śāstras, give the same instructions, just like sisters. The Purāṇas, which are like brothers, follow in the footsteps of their mother. O enemy of the demon Mura, the conclusion is that You are the only shelter. Now I have understood this in truth.'
verses.purport: PURPORT\nThis quotation from the Vedic literature was spoken by great sages.

verses.devanagari: অদ্বয়জ্ঞান-তত্ত্ব কৃষ্ণ — স্বয়ং ভগবান্ ।\\n‘স্বরূপ-শক্তি’রূপে তাঁর হয় অবস্থান ॥৭॥
verses.transliteration: advaya-jñāna-tattva kṛṣṇa—svayaṁ bhagavān\\n'svarūpa-śakti' rūpe tāṅra haya avasthāna
