verses.transliteration: māyā-śaktye brahmāṇḍādi-paripāṭī-sṛjana\\n'urukrama'-śabdera ei artha nirūpaṇa
verses.translation: "The word urukrama indicates the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who, by His external potency, has perfectly created innumerable universes.

verses.devanagari: “ক্রমঃ শক্তৌ পরিপাট্যাং ক্রমশ্চালনকম্পয়োঃ ।।” ॥ ২৪ ॥
verses.transliteration: "kramaḥ śaktau paripāṭyāṁ kramaś cālana-kampayoḥ"
verses.translation: “ 'These are the different meanings of the word krama. It is used in the sense of potency, systematic arrangement, step, moving or trembling.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a quotation from the
Viśva-prakāśa
dictionary. The Supreme Personality of Godhead is all-pervasive. Not only does He carry the three worlds by His inconceivable energy, but He maintains them also. He is also maintaining His spiritual planet, Goloka Vṛndāvana, by His conjugal love, and He is maintaining the Vaikuṇṭhalokas by His opulences. He maintains these material universes through the external energy. Material universes are perfectly situated because they are created by the Supreme Personality of Godhead.

verses.devanagari: ‘কুর্বন্তি’-পদ এই পরস্মৈপদ হয় ।\\nকৃষ্ণসুখনিমিত্ত ভজনে তাৎপর্য কহয় ॥২৫॥
verses.transliteration: 'kurvanti'-pada ei parasmaipada haya\\nkṛṣṇa-sukha-nimitta bhajane tātparya kahaya
verses.translation: "The word kurvanti, which means 'they do something for others,' is a form of the verb 'things done for others.' It is used in connection with devotional service, which must be executed for the satisfaction of Kṛṣṇa. That is the purport of the word kurvanti.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
In Sanskrit the verb "to do" has two forms, technically called
parasmaipada
and
ātmanepada.
When things are done for one's personal satisfaction, the form is called
ātmanepada.
In that case, the word "do" in English is
kurvante
in Sanskrit. When things are done for others, the verb form changes to
kurvanti.
Thus Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu informed Sanātana Gosvāmī that in the
ātmārāma
verse the verb
kurvanti
means that things should be done only for the satisfaction of Kṛṣṇa. This is supported by the grammarian Pāṇini. The verb is formed as
ātmanepada
when the work is to be done for one's own benefit, and when it is done for others, it is called
parasmaipada.
Thus the verb is formed according to whether something is done for one's self-satisfaction or for another's satisfaction.

verses.devanagari: “স্বরিতঞিতঃ কর্ত্রভিপ্রায়ে ক্রিয়াফলে ।।” ॥ ২৬ ॥
verses.transliteration: "svaritañitaḥ kartrabhiprāye kriyā-phale"
verses.synonyms:
svarita-ñitaḥ
—of verbs having an indicatory
ñ
or a
svarita
accent;
kartṛ-abhiprāye
—is meant for the agent;
kriyā-phale
—when the fruit of the action.
verses.translation: “ 'The terminations of the ātmanepada are employed when the fruit of the action accrues to the agent of verbs having an indicatory ñ or a svarita accent.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a quotation from Pāṇini's
sūtras
(1.3.72).

verses.devanagari: ‘হেতু’-শব্দে কহে — ভুক্তি-আদি বাঞ্ছান্তরে ।\\nভুক্তি, সিদ্ধি, মুক্তি — মুখ্য এই তিন প্রকারে ॥২৭॥
verses.transliteration: 'hetu'-śabde kahe—bhukti-ādi vāñchāntare\\nbhukti, siddhi, mukti—mukhya ei tina prakāre
verses.translation: "The word hetu [cause] means that a thing is done for some motive. There can be three motives. One may act to enjoy the result personally, to achieve some material perfection, or to act in such a way that one may be liberated.

verses.devanagari: এক ভুক্তি কহে, ভোগ — অনন্ত-প্রকার ।\\nসিদ্ধি — অষ্টাদশ, মুক্তি — পঞ্চবিধাকার ॥২৮॥
verses.transliteration: eka bhukti kahe, bhoga—ananta-prakāra\\nsiddhi—aṣṭādaśa, mukti—pañca-vidhākāra
verses.translation: "First we take the word bhukti [material enjoyment], which is of unlimited variety. We may also take the word siddhi [perfection], which has eighteen varieties. Similarly, the word mukti has five varieties.

verses.devanagari: এই যাঁহা নাহি, তাহা ভক্তি — ‘অহৈতুকী’ ।\\nযাহা হৈতে বশ হয় শ্রীকৃষ্ণ কৌতুকী ॥২৯॥
verses.transliteration: ei yāṅhā nāhi, tāhā bhakti—'ahaitukī'\\nyāhā haite vaśa haya śrī-kṛṣṇa kautukī
verses.translation: "Causeless devotional service is unmotivated by sense enjoyment, perfection or liberation. When one is freed from all these contaminations, he can bring Lord Kṛṣṇa, who is very funny, under control.

verses.devanagari: ‘ভক্তি’-শব্দের অর্থ হয় দশবিধাকার ।\\nএক — ‘সাধন’, ‘প্রেমভক্তি’ — নব প্রকার ॥৩০॥
verses.transliteration: 'bhakti'-śabdera artha haya daśa-vidhākāra\\neka—'sādhana', 'prema-bhakti'—nava prakāra
verses.translation: "There are ten meanings to the word bhakti, devotional service. One is execution of devotional service according to the regulative principles, and the other, called prema-bhakti [ecstatic love] has nine varieties.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
The nine varieties are
rati, prema, sneha, māna, praṇaya, rāga, anurāga, bhāva
and
mahābhāva
—attraction, love, affection, adverse feelings, intimacy, attachment, subattachment, ecstatic love and sublime ecstatic love. For the execution of devotional service according to regulative principles, there is only one meaning.

verses.devanagari: ‘রতি’-লক্ষণা, ‘প্রেম’-লক্ষণা, ইত্যাদি প্রচার ।\\nভাবরূপা, মহাভাব-লক্ষণরূপা আর ॥৩১॥
verses.transliteration: 'rati'-lakṣaṇā, 'prema'-lakṣaṇā, ityādi pracāra\\nbhāva-rūpā, mahābhāva-lakṣaṇa-rūpā āra
verses.translation: "Next are explained the symptoms of love of Godhead, which can be divided into nine varieties, beginning with attraction up to ecstatic love and finally up to the topmost ecstatic love [mahābhāva].

verses.devanagari: শান্ত-ভক্তের রতি বাড়ে ‘প্রেম’-পর্যন্ত ।\\nদাস্য-ভক্তের রতি হয় ‘রাগ’-দশা-অন্ত ॥৩২॥
verses.transliteration: śānta-bhaktera rati bāḍe 'prema'-paryanta\\ndāsya-bhaktera rati haya 'rāga'-daśā-anta
verses.translation: "The attraction to Kṛṣṇa of devotees on the platform of neutrality increases up to love of Godhead [prema], and the attraction of devotees on the platform of servitorship increases to spontaneous attachment [rāga].

verses.devanagari: সখাগণের রতি হয় ‘অনুরাগ’ পর্যন্ত ।\\nপিতৃ-মাতৃ-স্নেহ আদি ‘অনুরাগ’-অন্ত ॥৩৩॥
verses.transliteration: sakhā-gaṇera rati haya 'anurāga' paryanta\\npitṛ-mātṛ-sneha ādi 'anurāga'-anta
verses.translation: "Devotees in Vṛndāvana who are friends of the Lord can increase their ecstatic love to the point of anurāga. Paternal affectionate lovers, Kṛṣṇa's father and mother, can increase their love of Godhead up to the anurāga point also.

verses.devanagari: কান্তাগণের রতি পায় ‘মহাভাব’-সীমা ।\\n‘ভক্তি’-শব্দের এই সব অর্থের মহিমা ॥৩৪॥
verses.transliteration: kāntā-gaṇera rati pāya 'mahābhāva'-sīmā\\n'bhakti'-śabdera ei saba arthera mahimā
verses.translation: "The gopīs of Vṛndāvana who are attached to Kṛṣṇa in conjugal love can increase their ecstatic love up to the point of mahābhāva [the greatest ecstatic love]. These are some of the glorious meanings of the word bhakti, devotional service.

verses.devanagari: ‘ইত্থম্ভূতগুণঃ’-শব্দের শুনহ ব্যাখ্যান ।\\n‘ইত্থং’-শব্দের ভিন্ন অর্থ, ‘গুণ’-শব্দের আন ॥৩৫॥
verses.transliteration: 'ittham-bhūta-guṇaḥ'-śabdera śunaha vyākhyāna\\n'itthaṁ'-śabdera bhinna artha, 'guṇa'-śabdera āna
verses.translation: "Please hear the meaning of the word ittham-bhūta-guṇa, which is found in the ātmārāma verse. Ittham-bhūta has different meanings, and guṇa has other meanings.

verses.devanagari: ‘ইত্থম্ভূত’-শব্দের অর্থ — পূর্ণানন্দময় ।\\nযাঁর আগে ব্রহ্মানন্দ তৃণপ্রায় হয় ॥৩৬॥
verses.transliteration: 'ittham-bhūta'-śabdera artha—pūrṇānandamaya\\nyāṅra āge brahmānanda tṛṇa-prāya haya
verses.translation: "The word ittham-bhūta is transcendentally exalted because it means 'full of transcendental bliss.' Before this transcendental bliss, the bliss derived from merging into the existence of the Absolute [brahmānanda] becomes like a piece of straw in comparison.

verses.devanagari: ত্বত্সাক্ষাত্করণাহ্লাদবিশুদ্ধাব্ধিস্থিতস্য মে ।\\nসুখানি গোষ্পদায়ন্তে ব্রাহ্মাণ্যপি জগদ্গুরো ॥৩৭॥
verses.transliteration: tvat-sākṣāt-karaṇāhlāda-\\nviśuddhābdhi-sthitasya me\\nsukhāni goṣpadāyante\\nbrāhmāṇy api jagad-guro
verses.translation: “ 'My dear Lord, O master of the universe, since I have directly seen You, my transcendental bliss has taken the shape of a great ocean. Being situated in that ocean, I now realize all other so-called happiness to be like the water contained in the hoofprint of a calf.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a verse from the
Hari-bhakti-sudhodaya
(14.36).

verses.devanagari: সর্বাকর্ষক, সর্বাহ্লাদক, মহারসায়ন ।\\nআপনার বলে করে সর্ব-বিস্মারণ ॥৩৮॥
verses.transliteration: sarvākarṣaka, sarvāhlādaka, mahā-rasāyana\\nāpanāra bale kare sarva-vismāraṇa
verses.translation: "Lord Kṛṣṇa is so exalted that He is more attractive than anything else and more pleasing than anything else. He is the most sublime abode of bliss. By His own strength, He causes one to forget all other ecstasies.

verses.devanagari: ভুক্তি-মুক্তি-সিদ্ধি-সুখ ছাড়য় যার গন্ধে ।\\nঅলৌকিক শক্তি-গুণে কৃষ্ণকৃপায় বান্ধে ॥৩৯॥
verses.transliteration: bhukti-mukti-siddhi-sukha chāḍaya yāra gandhe\\nalaukika śakti-guṇe kṛṣṇa-kṛpāya bāndhe
verses.translation: "Pure devotional service is so sublime that one can very easily forget the happiness derived from material happiness, material liberation and mystic or yogic perfection. Thus the devotee is bound by Kṛṣṇa's mercy and His uncommon power and qualifications.

verses.devanagari: শাস্ত্রযুক্তি নাহি ইহাঁ সিদ্ধান্ত-বিচার ।\\nএই স্বভাব-গুণে, যাতে মাধুর্যের সার ॥৪০॥
verses.transliteration: śāstra-yukti nāhi ihāṅ siddhānta-vicāra\\nei svabhāva-guṇe, yāte mādhuryera sāra
verses.translation: "When one is attracted to Kṛṣṇa on the transcendental platform, there is no longer any logical argument on the basis of revealed scripture, nor are there considerations of such conclusions. This is His transcendental quality that is the essence of all transcendental sweetness.

verses.devanagari: ‘গুণ’ শব্দের অর্থ — কৃষ্ণের গুণ অনন্ত ।\\nসচ্চিদ্রূপ-গুণ সর্ব পূর্ণানন্দ ॥৪১॥
verses.transliteration: 'guṇa' śabdera artha—kṛṣṇera guṇa ananta\\nsac-cid-rūpa-guṇa sarva pūrṇānanda
verses.translation: "The word guṇa means 'quality.' The qualities of Kṛṣṇa are transcendentally situated and are unlimited in quantity. All of the spiritual qualities are full of transcendental bliss.

verses.devanagari: ঐশ্বর্য-মাধুর্য-কারুণ্যে স্বরূপ-পূর্ণতা ।\\nভক্তবাৎসল্য, আত্মপর্যন্ত বদান্যতা ॥৪২॥
verses.transliteration: aiśvarya-mādhurya-kāruṇye svarūpa-pūrṇatā\\nbhakta-vātsalya, ātma-paryanta vadānyatā
verses.translation: "Kṛṣṇa's transcendental qualities such as opulence, sweetness and mercy are perfect and full. As far as Kṛṣṇa's affectionate leaning toward His devotees is concerned, He is so magnanimous that He can give Himself to His devotees.

verses.devanagari: অলৌকিক রূপ, রস, সৌরভাদি গুণ ।\\nকারো মন কোন গুণে করে আকর্ষণ ॥৪৩॥
verses.transliteration: alaukika rūpa, rasa, saurabhādi guṇa\\nkāro mana kona guṇe kare ākarṣaṇa
verses.translation: "Kṛṣṇa has unlimited qualities. The devotees are attracted by His uncommon beauty, mellows and fragrance. Thus they are differently situated in the different transcendental mellows. Therefore Kṛṣṇa is called all-attractive.

verses.devanagari: সনকাদির মন হরিল সৌরভাদি গুণে ॥৪৪॥
verses.transliteration: sanakādira mana harila saurabhādi guṇe
verses.translation: "The minds of the four boy sages [Sanaka, Sanātana, Sanandana and Sanat-kumāra] were attracted to the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa by the aroma of the tulasī that had been offered to the Lord.

verses.devanagari: তস্যারবিন্দনয়নস্য পদারবিন্দ-\\nকিঞ্জল্কমিশ্রতুলসীমকরন্দবায়ুঃ ।\\nঅন্তর্গতঃ স্ববিবরেণ চকার তেষাং\\nসংক্ষোভমক্ষরজুষামপি চিত্ততন্বোঃ ॥৪৫॥
verses.transliteration: tasyāravinda-nayanasya padāravinda-\\nkiñjalka-miśra-tulasī-makaranda-vāyuḥ\\nantargataḥ svavivareṇa cakāra teṣāṁ\\nsaṅkṣobham akṣara-juṣām api citta-tanvoḥ
verses.translation: “ 'When the breeze carrying the aroma of tulasī leaves and saffron from the lotus feet of the lotus-eyed Personality of Godhead entered through the nostrils into the hearts of those sages [the Kumāras], they experienced a change in both body and mind, even though they were attached to impersonal Brahman understanding.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a verse from
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(3.15.43). For an explanation, see
Madhya-līlā
(17.142).

verses.devanagari: শুকদেবের মন হরিল লীলা-শ্রবণে ॥৪৬॥
verses.transliteration: śukadevera mana harila līlā-śravaṇe
verses.translation: "Śukadeva's mind was carried away by remembering the pastimes of the Lord.

verses.devanagari: পরিনিষ্ঠিতোহপি নৈর্গুণ্যে উত্তমঃশ্লোকলীলয়া ।\\nগৃহীতচেতা রাজর্ষে আখ্যানং যদধীতবান্ ॥৪৭॥
verses.transliteration: pariniṣṭhito 'pi nairguṇye\\nuttamaḥśloka-līlayā\\ngṛhīta-cetā rājarṣe\\nākhyānaṁ yad adhītavān
verses.translation: “ 'Śukadeva Gosvāmī addressed Parīkṣit Mahārāja, "My dear King, although I was fully situated in the transcendental position, I was nonetheless attracted to the pastimes of Lord Kṛṣṇa. Therefore I studied Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam from my father.' "
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a quotation from
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(2.1.9).

verses.devanagari: স্বসুখনিভৃতচেতাস্তদ্ব্যুদস্তান্যভাবোঽ-\\nপ্যজিতরুচিরলীলাকৃষ্টসারস্তদীয়ম্ ।\\nব্যতনুত কৃপয়া যস্তত্ত্বদীপং পুরাণং\\nতমখিলবৃজিনঘ্নং ব্যাস-সূনুং নতোঽস্মি ॥৪৮॥
verses.transliteration: svasukha-nibhṛta-cetās tad-vyudastānya-bhāvo\\n'py ajita-rucira-līlākṛṣṭa-sāras tadīyam\\nvyatanuta kṛpayā yas tattva-dīpaṁ purāṇaṁ\\ntam akhila-vṛjina-ghnaṁ vyāsa-sūnuṁ nato 'smi
verses.translation: “ 'I offer my respectful obeisances unto Śrīla Śukadeva Gosvāmī, the son of Vyāsadeva. He is the destroyer of all sinful reactions and is full in self-realization and bliss. Because of this, he has no other desire. Still, he was attracted by the transcendental pastimes of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and out of compassion for the people, he described the transcendental historical literature called Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam. This is compared to the light of the Absolute Truth.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This verse is from
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(12.12.68).

verses.devanagari: শ্রীঅঙ্গ-রূপে হরে গোপিকার মন ॥৪৯॥
verses.transliteration: śrī-aṅga-rūpe hare gopikāra mana
verses.translation: "Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa attracts the minds of all the gopīs with His beautiful transcendental bodily features.

verses.devanagari: বীক্ষ্যালকাবৃতমুখং তব কুণ্ডলশ্রী-\\nগণ্ডস্থলাধরসুধং হসিতাবলোকম্ ।\\nদত্তাভয়ঞ্চ ভুজদণ্ডযুগং বিলোক্য\\nবক্ষঃ শ্রিয়ৈকরমণঞ্চ ভবাম দাস্যঃ ॥৫০॥
verses.transliteration: vīkṣyālakāvṛta-mukhaṁ tava kuṇḍala-śrī-\\ngaṇḍa-sthalādhara-sudhaṁ hasitāvalokam\\ndattābhayaṁ ca bhuja-daṇḍa-yugaṁ vilokya\\nvakṣaḥ śriyaika-ramaṇaṁ ca bhavāma dāsyaḥ
verses.translation: “ 'Dear Kṛṣṇa, we have simply surrendered ourselves as Your maidservants, for we have seen Your beautiful face decorated with tresses of hair, Your earrings falling upon Your cheeks and the nectar of Your lips. We have also seen the beauty of Your smile and have been embraced by Your arms, which give us courage. Because we have seen Your chest, which is beautiful and broad, we have surrendered ourselves.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This verse from
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(10.29.39) was spoken by the
gopīs
when they arrived near Kṛṣṇa for the
rāsa
dance on a full moonlit night. The attracted
gopīs
were awestruck, and they began to speak about how they came to Kṛṣṇa to enjoy the
rāsa
dance.

verses.devanagari: রূপ-গুণ-শ্রবণে রুক্মিণ্যাদির আকর্ষণ ॥৫১॥
verses.transliteration: rūpa-guṇa-śravaṇe rukmiṇy-ādira ākarṣaṇa
verses.translation: "The queens in Dvārakā, who are headed by Rukmiṇī, are also attracted to Kṛṣṇa simply by hearing about His transcendental beauty and qualities.

verses.devanagari: শ্রুত্বা গুণান্ ভুবনসুন্দর শৃণ্বতাং তে\\nনির্বিশ্য কর্ণবিবরৈর্হরতোঽঙ্গতাপম্ ।\\nরূপং দৃশাং দৃশিমতামখিলার্থলাভং\\nত্বয্যচ্যুতাবিশতি চিত্তমপত্রপং মে ॥৫২॥
verses.transliteration: śrutvā guṇān bhuvana-sundara śṛṇvatāṁ te\\nnirviśya karṇa-vivarair harato 'ṅga-tāpam\\nrūpaṁ dṛśāṁ dṛśimatām akhilārtha-lābhaṁ\\ntvayy acyutāviśati cittam apatrapaṁ me
verses.translation: “ 'O most beautiful Kṛṣṇa, I have heard about Your transcendental qualities from others, and therefore all my bodily miseries are relieved. If one sees Your transcendental beauty, his eyes have attained everything profitable in life. O infallible one, I have become shameless after hearing of Your qualities, and I have become attracted to You.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This verse (
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
10.52.37) was written by Rukmiṇīdevī in a letter to Kṛṣṇa inviting Him to kidnap her. Śukadeva Gosvāmī described this to Mahārāja Parīkṣit when the King asked him how Rukmiṇī had been kidnapped. Rukmiṇī had heard about Kṛṣṇa's qualities from different people, and after she heard about them, she decided to accept Kṛṣṇa as her husband. Everything had been arranged for her marriage to Śiśupāla; therefore she wrote a letter to Kṛṣṇa, which she sent through a
brāhmaṇa,
and invited Him to kidnap her.

verses.devanagari: বংশী-গীতে হরে কৃষ্ণ লক্ষ্ম্যাদির মন ॥৫৩॥
verses.transliteration: vaṁśī-gīte hare kṛṣṇa lakṣmy-ādira mana
verses.translation: "Lord Kṛṣṇa even attracts the mind of the goddess of fortune simply by vibrating His transcendental flute.

verses.devanagari: কস্যানুভাবোঽস্য ন দেব বিদ্মহে\\nতবাঙ্ঘ্রিরেণুস্পরশাধিকারঃ ।\\nযদ্বাঞ্ছয়া শ্রীর্ললনাচরত্তপো\\nবিহায় কামান্ সুচিরং ধৃতব্রতা ॥৫৪॥
verses.transliteration: kasyānubhāvo 'sya na deva vidmahe\\ntavāṅghri-reṇu-sparaśādhikāraḥ\\nyad-vāñchayā śrīr lalanācarat tapo\\nvihāya kāmān suciraṁ dhṛta-vratā
verses.translation: “ 'O Lord, we do not know how the serpent Kāliya attained such an opportunity to be touched by the dust of Your lotus feet. For this end, the goddess of fortune performed austerities for centuries, giving up all other desires and taking austere vows. Indeed, we do not know how this serpent Kāliya got such an opportunity.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This verse from
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(10.16.36) was spoken by the wives of the Kāliya demon.

verses.devanagari: যোগ্যভাবে জগতে যত যুবতীর গণ ॥৫৫॥
verses.transliteration: yogya-bhāve jagate yata yuvatīra gaṇa
verses.translation: "Kṛṣṇa attracts not only the minds of the gopīs and the goddesses of fortune but the minds of all the young girls in the three worlds as well.

verses.devanagari: কাস্ত্র্যঙ্গ তে কলপদামৃতবেণুগীত-\\nসম্মোহিতার্যচরিতান্ন চলেত্রিলোক্যাম্ ।\\nত্রৈলোক্যসৌভগমিদঞ্চ নিরীক্ষ্য রূপং\\nযদ্গোদ্বিজদ্রুমমৃগাঃ পুলকান্যবিভ্রন্ ॥৫৬॥
verses.transliteration: kā stry aṅga te kala-padāmṛta-veṇu-gīta-\\nsammohitārya-caritān na calet trilokyām\\ntrailokya-saubhagam idaṁ ca nirīkṣya rūpaṁ\\nyad go-dvija-druma-mṛgāḥ pulakāny abibhran
verses.translation: “ 'My dear Lord Kṛṣṇa, where is that woman within the three worlds who cannot be captivated by the rhythms of the sweet songs coming from Your wonderful flute? Who cannot fall down from the path of chastity in this way? Your beauty is the most sublime within the three worlds. Upon seeing Your beauty, even cows, birds, animals and trees in the forest are stunned in jubilation.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This verse is from
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(10.29.40).

verses.devanagari: গুরুতুল্য স্ত্রীগণের বাৎসল্যে আকর্ষণ ।\\nদাস্য-সখ্যাদি-ভাবে পুরুষাদি গণ ॥৫৭॥
verses.transliteration: guru-tulya strī-gaṇera vātsalye ākarṣaṇa\\ndāsya-sakhyādi-bhāve puruṣādi gaṇa
verses.translation: "The women of Vṛndāvana, who are on the level of superior guardians, are attracted maternally. The men of Vṛndāvana are attracted as servants, friends and fathers to Lord Kṛṣṇa.

verses.devanagari: পক্ষী, মৃগ, বৃক্ষ, লতা, চেতনাচেতন ।\\nপ্রেমে মত্ত করি’ আকর্ষয়ে কৃষ্ণগুণ ॥৫৮॥
verses.transliteration: pakṣī, mṛga, vṛkṣa, latā, cetanācetana\\npreme matta kari' ākarṣaye kṛṣṇa-guṇa
verses.translation: "The qualities of Kṛṣṇa captivate and attract everything, living and dead. Even birds, animals and trees are attracted to Kṛṣṇa's qualities.

verses.devanagari: ‘হরিঃ’-শব্দে নানার্থ, দুই মুখ্যতম ।\\nসর্ব অমঙ্গল হরে, প্রেম দিয়া হরে মন ॥৫৯॥
verses.transliteration: 'hariḥ'-śabde nānārtha, dui mukhyatama\\nsarva amaṅgala hare, prema diyā hare mana
verses.translation: "Although the word hari has many different meanings, two of them are foremost. One meaning is that the Lord takes away all inauspicious things from His devotee, and the second meaning is that He attracts the mind by ecstatic love for God.

verses.devanagari: যৈছে তৈছে যোহি কোহি করয়ে স্মরণ ।\\nচারিবিধ তাপ তার করে সংহরণ ॥৬০॥
verses.transliteration: yaiche taiche yohi kohi karaye smaraṇa\\ncāri-vidha tāpa tāra kare saṁharaṇa
verses.translation: "When the devotee somehow or other always remembers the Supreme Personality of Godhead anywhere and everywhere, Lord Hari takes away life's four miserable conditions.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
The four miserable conditions are due to the four kinds of sinful activities, known as (1)
pātaka,
(2)
urupātaka,
(3)
mahā-pātaka
and (4)
atipātaka
—preliminary sin, very great sin, greater sin and topmost sin. However, Kṛṣṇa assures the devotee,
ahaṁ tvāṁ sarva-pāpebhyo mokṣayiṣyāmi mā śucaḥ:
"I will protect you from all sinful reactions. Do not fear." The word
sarva-pāpebhyaḥ
indicates four kinds of sinful activity. As soon as the devotee surrenders unto Kṛṣṇa's lotus feet, he is certainly relieved from all sinful activities and their results. The four basic sinful activities are summarized as illicit sex, intoxication, gambling and meat-eating.

verses.devanagari: যথাগ্নিঃ সুসমৃদ্ধার্চিঃ করোত্যেধাংসি ভস্মসাত্ ।\\nতথা মদ্বিষয়া ভক্তিরুদ্ধবৈনাংসি কৃত্স্নশঃ ॥৬১॥
verses.transliteration: yathāgniḥ susamṛddhārciḥ\\nkaroty edhāṁsi bhasmasāt\\ntathā mad-viṣayā bhaktir\\nuddhavaināṁsi kṛtsnaśaḥ
verses.translation: “ 'As all fuel is burned to ashes by a full-fledged fire, all sinful activities are totally erased when one engages in devotional service to Me.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This verse is from
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(11.14.19).

verses.devanagari: তবে করে ভক্তিবাধক কর্ম, অবিদ্যা নাশ ।\\nশ্রবণাদ্যের ফল ‘প্রেমা’ করয়ে প্রকাশ ॥৬২॥
verses.transliteration: tabe kare bhakti-bādhaka karma, avidyā nāśa\\nśravaṇādyera phala 'premā' karaye prakāśa
verses.translation: "In this way, when all sinful activities are vanquished by the grace of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, one gradually vanquishes all kinds of impediments on the path of devotional service, as well as the ignorance resulting from these impediments. After this, one totally manifests his original love of Godhead through devotional service in nine different ways-hearing, chanting and so forth.

verses.devanagari: নিজ-গুণে তবে হরে দেহেন্দ্রিয়মন ।\\nঐছে কৃপালু কৃষ্ণ, ঐছে তাঁর গুণ ॥৬৩॥
verses.transliteration: nija-guṇe tabe hare dehendriya-mana\\naiche kṛpālu kṛṣṇa, aiche tāṅra guṇa
verses.translation: "When the devotee is freed from all sinful material activities, Kṛṣṇa attracts his body, mind and senses to His service. Thus Kṛṣṇa is very merciful, and His transcendental qualities are very attractive.

verses.devanagari: চারি পুরুষার্থ ছাড়ায়, গুণে হরে সবার মন ।\\n‘হরি’-শব্দের এই মুখ্য কহিলুঁ লক্ষণ ॥৬৪॥
verses.transliteration: cāri puruṣārtha chāḍāya, guṇe hare sabāra mana\\n'hari'-śabdera ei mukhya kahiluṅ lakṣaṇa
verses.translation: "When one's mind, senses and body are attracted to the transcendental qualities of Hari, one gives up the four principles of material success. Thus I have explained the chief meanings of the word hari.
verses.purport: PURPORT\nThe four principles of material success are (1) religious performance, (2) economic development, (3) sense gratification and (4) liberation, or merging in the impersonal effulgence of Brahman. These things do not interest the devotee.

verses.devanagari: ‘চ’ ‘অপি’, দুই শব্দ তাতে ‘অব্যয়’ হয় ।\\nযেই অর্থ লাগাইয়ে, সেই অর্থ হয় ॥৬৫॥
verses.transliteration: 'ca' 'api', dui śabda tāte 'avyaya' haya\\nyei artha lāgāiye, sei artha haya
verses.translation: "When the conjunction ca [and] and the adverb api [although] are added to this verse, the verse can assume whatever meaning one wants to give it.

verses.devanagari: তথাপি চ-কারের কহে মুখ্য অর্থ সাত ॥৬৬॥
verses.transliteration: tathāpi ca-kārera kahe mukhya artha sāta
verses.translation: "The word ca can be explained in seven ways.

verses.devanagari: চান্বাচয়ে সমাহারেঽন্যোঽন্যার্থে চ সমুচ্চয়ে ।\\nযত্নান্তরে তথা পাদপূরণেঽপ্যবধারণে ॥৬৭॥
verses.transliteration: cānvācaye samāhāre\\n'nyo 'nyārthe ca samuccaye\\nyatnāntare tathā pāda-\\npūraṇe 'py avadhāraṇe
verses.translation: “ 'The word ca [and] is used to connect a word or sentence with a previous word or sentence, to give the sense of aggregation, to assist the meaning, to give a collective understanding, to suggest another effort or exertion, or to fulfill the meter of a verse. It is also used in the sense of certainty.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a quotation from the
Viśva-prakāśa
dictionary.

verses.devanagari: অপি-শব্দে মুখ্য অর্থ সাত বিখ্যাত ॥৬৮॥
verses.transliteration: api-śabde mukhya artha sāta vikhyāta
verses.translation: "There are seven chief meanings of the word api. They are as follows.

verses.devanagari: অপি সম্ভাবনা-প্রশ্ন-শঙ্কা-গর্হা-সমুচ্চয়ে ।\\nতথা যুক্তপদার্থেষু কামচারক্রিয়াসু চ ॥৬৯॥
verses.transliteration: api sambhāvanā-praśna-\\nśaṅkā-garhā-samuccaye\\ntathā yukta-padārtheṣu\\nkāma-cāra-kriyāsu ca
verses.translation: “ 'The word api is used in the sense of possibility, question, doubt, censure, aggregation, appropriate application of things, and extravagance.'
verses.purport: PURPORT\nThis is another quotation from the\nViśva-prakāśa.

verses.devanagari: এই ত’ একাদশ পদের অর্থ-নির্ণয় ।\\nএবে শ্লোকার্থ করি, যথা যে লাগয় ॥৭০॥
verses.transliteration: ei ta' ekādaśa padera artha-nirṇaya\\nebe ślokārtha kari, yathā ye lāgaya
verses.translation: "I have now described the different meanings of the eleven separate words. Now let Me give the complete meaning of the śloka, as it is applied in different places.

verses.devanagari: ‘ব্রহ্ম’ শব্দের অর্থ — তত্ত্ব সর্ব-বৃহত্তম ।\\nস্বরূপ ঐশ্বর্য করি’ নাহি যাঁর সম ॥৭১॥
verses.transliteration: 'brahma' śabdera artha—tattva sarva-bṛhattama\\nsvarūpa aiśvarya kari' nāhi yāṅra sama
verses.translation: "The word brahma indicates the summum bonum, the Absolute Truth, which is greater than all other truths. It is the original identity, and there can be no truth equal to that Absolute Truth.

verses.devanagari: বৃহত্ত্বাদ্বৃংহণত্বাচ্চ তদ্ব্রহ্ম পরমং বিদুঃ ।\\nতস্মৈ নমস্তে সর্বাত্মন্ যোগিচিন্ত্যাবিকারবত্ ॥৭২॥
verses.transliteration: bṛhattvād bṛṁhaṇatvāc ca\\ntad brahma paramaṁ viduḥ\\ntasmai namas te sarvātman\\nyogi-cintyāvikāravat
verses.translation: “ 'I offer my respectful obeisances to the Absolute Truth, the summum bonum. He is the all-pervasive, all-increasing subject matter for the great yogīs. He is changeless, and He is the soul of all.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a quotation from the
Viṣṇu Purāṇa
(1.12.57).

verses.devanagari: সেই ব্রহ্ম-শব্দে কহে স্বয়ং-ভগবান্ ।\\nঅদ্বিতীয়-জ্ঞান, যাঁহা বিনা নাহি আন ॥৭৩॥
verses.transliteration: sei brahma-śabde kahe svayaṁ-bhagavān\\nadvitīya-jñāna, yāṅhā vinā nāhi āna
verses.translation: "The proper meaning of the word brahma is the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is one without a second and without whom nothing exists.

verses.devanagari: বদন্তি তত্তত্ত্ববিদস্তত্ত্বং যজ্জ্ঞানমদ্বয়ম্ ।\\nব্রহ্মেতি পরমাত্মেতি ভগবানিতি শব্দ্যতে ॥৭৪॥
verses.transliteration: vadanti tat tattva-vidas\\ntattvaṁ yaj jñānam advayam\\nbrahmeti paramātmeti\\nbhagavān iti śabdyate
verses.translation: “ 'Learned transcendentalists who know the Absolute Truth say that it is nondual knowledge and is called impersonal Brahman, localized Paramātmā and the Personality of Godhead.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a quotation from
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(1.2.11). For an explanation, see
Ādi-līlā
(2.11).

verses.devanagari: সেই অদ্বয়-তত্ত্ব কৃষ্ণ — স্বয়ং-ভগবান্ ।\\nতিনকালে সত্য তিঁহো — শাস্ত্র-প্রমাণ ॥৭৫॥
verses.transliteration: sei advaya-tattva kṛṣṇa—svayaṁ-bhagavān\\ntina-kāle satya tiṅho—śāstra-pramāṇa
verses.translation: "That Absolute Truth without a second is Lord Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead. He is the supreme truth in the past, present and future. That is the evidence of all revealed scriptures.

verses.devanagari: অহমেবাসমেবাগ্রে নান্যদ্যত্ সদসত্পরম্ ।\\nপশ্চাদহং যদেতচ্চ যোঽবশিষ্যেত সোঽস্ম্যহম্ ॥৭৬॥
verses.transliteration: aham evāsam evāgre\\nnānyad yat sad-asat-param\\npaścād ahaṁ yad etac ca\\nyo 'vaśiṣyeta so 'smy aham
verses.translation: “ 'Prior to the cosmic creation, only I exist, and no phenomena exist, either gross, subtle or primordial. After creation, only I exist in everything, and after annihilation only I remain eternally.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a quotation from
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(2.9.33). For an explanation see
Ādi-līlā
(1.53).

verses.devanagari: ‘আত্ম’-শব্দে কহে কৃষ্ণ বৃহত্ত্বস্বরূপ ।\\nসর্বব্যাপক, সর্বসাক্ষী, পরমস্বরূপ ॥৭৭॥
verses.transliteration: 'ātma'-śabde kahe kṛṣṇa bṛhattva-svarūpa\\nsarva-vyāpaka, sarva-sākṣī, parama-svarūpa
verses.translation: "The word ātmā [self] indicates the highest truth, Kṛṣṇa. He is the all-pervasive witness of all, and He is the supreme form.

verses.devanagari: আততত্বাচ্চ মাতৃত্বাদাত্মা হি পরমো হরিঃ ॥৭৮॥
verses.transliteration: ātatatvāc ca mātṛtvād\\nātmā hi paramo hariḥ
verses.translation: “ 'Hari, the Personality of Godhead, is the all-pervasive original source of everything; He is therefore the Supersoul of everything.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a quotation from the
Bhāvārtha-dīpikā,
Śrīdhara Svāmī's commentary on
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam.

verses.devanagari: সেই কৃষ্ণপ্রাপ্তি-হেতু ত্রিবিধ ‘সাধন’ ।\\nজ্ঞান, যোগ, ভক্তি, — তিনের পৃথক্ লক্ষণ ॥৭৯॥
verses.transliteration: sei kṛṣṇa-prāpti-hetu trividha 'sādhana'\\njñāna, yoga, bhakti,—tinera pṛthak lakṣaṇa
verses.translation: "There are three ways to attain the lotus feet of the Absolute Truth, Kṛṣṇa. There is the process of philosophical speculation, the practice of mystic yoga and the execution of devotional service. Each of these has its different characteristics.

verses.devanagari: তিন সাধনে ভগবান্ তিন স্বরূপে ভাসে ।\\nব্রহ্ম, পরমাত্মা, ভগবত্তা, — ত্রিবিধ প্রকাশে ॥৮০॥
verses.transliteration: tina sādhane bhagavān tina svarūpe bhāse\\nbrahma, paramātmā, bhagavattā,—trividha prakāśe
verses.translation: "The Absolute Truth is the same, but according to the process by which one understands Him, He appears in three forms-as Brahman, Paramātmā, and Bhagavān, the Supreme Personality of Godhead.

verses.devanagari: বদন্তি তত্তত্ত্ববিদস্তত্ত্বং যজ্জ্ঞানমদ্বয়ম্ ।\\nব্রহ্মেতি পরমাত্মেতি ভগবানিতি শব্দ্যতে ॥৮১॥
verses.transliteration: vadanti tat tattva-vidas\\ntattvaṁ yaj jñānam advayam\\nbrahmeti paramātmeti\\nbhagavān iti śabdyate
verses.translation: “ 'Learned transcendentalists who know the Absolute Truth say that it is nondual knowledge and is called impersonal Brahman, localized Paramātmā and the Personality of Godhead.'

verses.devanagari: ‘ব্রহ্ম-আত্মা’-শব্দে যদি কৃষ্ণেরে কহয় ।\\n‘রূঢ়িবৃত্ত্যে’ নির্বিশেষ অন্তর্যামী কয় ॥৮২॥
verses.transliteration: 'brahma-ātmā'-śabde yadi kṛṣṇere kahaya\\n'rūḍhi-vṛttye' nirviśeṣa antaryāmī kaya
verses.translation: "Although the words brahma and ātmā indicate Kṛṣṇa, their direct meaning refers only to the impersonal Brahman and the Supersoul.

verses.devanagari: জ্ঞানমার্গে — নির্বিশেষ-ব্রহ্ম প্রকাশে ।\\nযোগমার্গে — অন্তর্যামী-স্বরূপেতে ভাসে ॥৮৩॥
verses.transliteration: jñāna-mārge—nirviśeṣa-brahma prakāśe\\nyoga-mārge—antaryāmi-svarūpete bhāse
verses.translation: "If one follows the path of philosophical speculation, the Absolute Truth manifests Himself as impersonal Brahman, and if one follows the path of mystic yoga, He manifests Himself as the Supersoul.

verses.devanagari: রাগভক্তি, বিধিভক্তি হয় দুইরূপ ।\\n‘স্বয়ং-ভগবত্ত্বে’, ভগবত্ত্বে — প্রকাশ দ্বিরূপ ॥৮৪॥
verses.transliteration: rāga-bhakti-vidhi-bhakti haya dui-rūpa\\n'svayaṁ-bhagavattve', bhagavattve—prakāśa dvi-rūpa
verses.translation: "There are two kinds of devotional activity-spontaneous and regulative. By spontaneous devotional service, one attains the original Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa, and by the regulative process one attains the expansion of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.

verses.devanagari: রাগভক্ত্যে ব্রজে স্বয়ং-ভগবানে পায় ॥৮৫॥
verses.transliteration: rāga-bhaktye vraje svayaṁ-bhagavāne pāya
verses.translation: "By executing spontaneous devotional service in Vṛndāvana, one attains the original Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa.

verses.devanagari: নায়ং সুখাপো ভগবান্ দেহিনাং গোপিকাসুতঃ ।\\nজ্ঞানিনাঞ্চাত্মভূতানাং যথা ভক্তিমতামিহ ॥৮৬॥
verses.transliteration: nāyaṁ sukhāpo bhagavān\\ndehināṁ gopikā-sutaḥ\\njñānināṁ cātma-bhūtānāṁ\\nyathā bhaktimatām iha
verses.translation: “ 'The Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa, the son of mother Yaśodā, is accessible to those devotees engaged in spontaneous loving service, but He is not as easily accessible to mental speculators, to those striving for self-realization by severe austerities and penances, or to those who consider the body the same as the self.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This verse from
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(10.9.21) is spoken by Śrīla Śukadeva Gosvāmī. It concerns the statement about Kṛṣṇa's being subjugated by the
gopīs
and thus glorifying them.

verses.devanagari: বিধিভক্ত্যে পার্ষদদেহে বৈকুণ্ঠেতে যায় ॥৮৭॥
verses.transliteration: vidhi-bhaktye pārṣada-dehe vaikuṇṭhete yāya
verses.translation: "By executing regulative devotional service, one becomes an associate of Nārāyaṇa and attains the Vaikuṇṭhalokas, the spiritual planets in the spiritual sky.

verses.devanagari: বৈক্লব্যবাষ্পকলয়া পুলকীকৃতাঙ্গাঃ ॥৮৮॥
verses.transliteration: yac ca vrajanty animiṣām ṛṣabhānuvṛttyā\\ndūre-yamā hy upari naḥ spṛhaṇīya-śīlāḥ\\nbhartur mithaḥ suyaśasaḥ kathanānurāga-\\nvaiklavya-bāṣpa-kalayā pulakīkṛtāṅgāḥ
verses.translation: “ 'Those who discuss the activities of Lord Kṛṣṇa are on the highest platform of devotional life, and they evince the symptoms of tears in the eyes and bodily jubilation. Such persons discharge devotional service to Kṛṣṇa without practicing the rules and regulations of the mystic yoga system. They possess all spiritual qualities, and they are elevated to the Vaikuṇṭha planets, which exist above us.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a quotation from
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(3.15.25). In this verse Lord Brahmā is speaking to all the demigods, who feared the two
asuras
in Diti's womb. Lord Brahmā described the Kumāras' visit to Vaikuṇṭha, and this was again explained by Maitreya, the friend of Vyāsadeva, when he gave instructions to Vidura.

verses.devanagari: সেই উপাসক হয় ত্রিবিধ প্রকার ।\\nঅকাম, মোক্ষকাম, সর্বকাম আর ॥৮৯॥
verses.transliteration: sei upāsaka haya trividha prakāra\\nakāma, mokṣa-kāma, sarva-kāma āra
verses.translation: "The devotees are divided into three categories-akāma [desireless], mokṣa-kāma [desiring liberation], and sarva-kāma [desiring material perfection].

verses.devanagari: অকামঃ সর্বকামো বা মোক্ষকাম উদারধীঃ ।\\nতীব্রেণ ভক্তিযোগেন যজেত পুরুষং পরম্ ॥৯০॥
verses.transliteration: akāmaḥ sarva-kāmo vā\\nmokṣa-kāma udāra-dhīḥ\\ntīvreṇa bhakti-yogena\\nyajeta puruṣaṁ param
verses.translation: “ 'One who is actually intelligent, although he may be a devotee free from material desires, a karmī desiring all kinds of material facilities, or a jñānī desiring liberation, should seriously engage in bhakti-yoga for the satisfaction of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a quotation from
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(2.3.10).

verses.devanagari: বুদ্ধিমান্-অর্থে — যদি ‘বিচারজ্ঞ’ হয় ।\\nনিজ-কাম লাগিহ তবে কৃষ্ণেরে ভজয় ॥৯১॥
verses.transliteration: buddhimān-arthe—yadi 'vicāra-jña' haya\\nnija-kāma lāgiha tabe kṛṣṇere bhajaya
verses.translation: "The meaning of the word udāra-dhīḥ is buddhimān-intelligent or considerate. Because of this, even for one's own sense gratification one engages in the devotional service of Lord Kṛṣṇa.

verses.devanagari: ভক্তি বিনু কোন সাধন দিতে নারে ফল ।\\nসব ফল দেয় ভক্তি স্বতন্ত্র প্রবল ॥৯২॥
verses.transliteration: bhakti vinu kona sādhana dite nāre phala\\nsaba phala deya bhakti svatantra prabala
verses.translation: "The other processes cannot yield results unless they are associated with devotional service. Devotional service, however, is so strong and independent that it can give one all the desired results.

verses.devanagari: অজাগলস্তন-ন্যায় অন্য সাধন ।\\nঅতএব হরি ভজে বুদ্ধিমান্ জন ॥৯৩॥
verses.transliteration: ajā-gala-stana-nyāya anya sādhana\\nataeva hari bhaje buddhimān jana
verses.translation: "With the exception of devotional service, all the methods of self-realization are like nipples on the neck of a goat. An intelligent person adopts only devotional service, giving up all other processes of self-realization.
verses.purport: PURPORT\nWithout devotional service, other methods for self-realization and spiritual life are useless. Other methods cannot produce good results at any time, and therefore they are compared to the nipples on the neck of a goat. These nipples cannot produce milk, although it may appear that they can. An unintelligent person cannot understand that only devotional service can elevate one to the transcendental position.

verses.devanagari: চতুর্বিধা ভজন্তে মাং জনাঃ সুকৃতিনোঽর্জুন ।\\nআর্তো জিজ্ঞাসুরর্থার্থী জ্ঞানী চ ভরতর্ষভ ॥৯৪॥
verses.transliteration: catur-vidhā bhajante māṁ\\njanāḥ sukṛtino 'rjuna\\nārto jijñāsur arthārthī\\njñānī ca bharatarṣabha
verses.translation: “ 'O best among the Bharatas [Arjuna], four kinds of pious men render devotional service unto Me—the distressed, the desirer of wealth, the inquisitive, and he who is searching for knowledge of the Absolute.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a quotation from
Bhagavad-gītā
(Bg. 7.16). The word
sukṛtinaḥ
is very important in this verse.
Su
means "auspicious," and
kṛtī
means "meritorious" or "regulated." Unless one follows the regulative principles of religious life, human life is no different from animal life. Religious life means following the principles of
varṇa
and
āśrama.
In the
Viṣṇu Purāṇa
it is said:
varṇāśramācāra-vatā
puruṣeṇa paraḥ pumān
viṣṇur ārādhyate panthā
nānyat tat-toṣa-kāraṇam
According to religious life, society is divided into four social divisions—
brāhmaṇa, kṣatriya, vaiśya
and
śūdra
—and four spiritual divisions—
brahmacarya, gṛhastha, vānaprastha
and
sannyāsa.
One needs to be trained to become a
brāhmaṇa, kṣatriya, vaiśya
or
śūdra,
just as one is trained to become an engineer, doctor or lawyer. Those who are properly trained can be considered human beings; if one is not trained socially and spiritually—that is, if one is uneducated and unregulated-his life is on the animal platform. Among animals there is no question of spiritual advancement. Spiritual life can be attained by proper training-either by following the principles of
varṇa
and
āśrama
or by being directly trained in the
bhakti
school by the methods of
śravaṇaṁ kīrtanaṁ viṣṇoḥ smaraṇaṁ pāda-sevanamarcanaṁ vandanaṁ dāsyaṁ sakhyam ātma-nivedanam.
Without being trained, one cannot be
sukṛtī,
auspicious. In this verse Kṛṣṇa says that people approach Him when in distress, in need of money or when actually inquisitive to understand the Supreme Being or the original source of everything. Some people approach Him in the pursuit of knowledge of the Absolute Truth, and others approach Him when they are distressed, like the devotee Gajendra. Others are inquisitive, like the great sages headed by Sanaka, and others need money, like Dhruva Mahārāja. Śukadeva Gosvāmī approached the Lord when he pursued knowledge. All these great personalities thus took to the devotional service of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa.

verses.devanagari: আর্ত, অর্থার্থী, — দুই সকাম-ভিতরে গণি ।\\nজিজ্ঞাসু, জ্ঞানী, — দুই মোক্ষকাম মানি ॥৯৫॥
verses.transliteration: ārta, arthārthī,—dui sakāma-bhitare gaṇi\\njijñāsu, jñānī,—dui mokṣa-kāma māni
verses.translation: "Materialistic devotees take to devotional service and worship Kṛṣṇa when they are distressed or in need of money. Those who are actually inquisitive to understand the supreme source of everything and those who are in search of knowledge are called transcendentalists, for they desire liberation from all material contamination.

verses.devanagari: এই চারি সুকৃতি হয় মহাভাগ্যবান্ ।\\nতত্তৎকামাদি ছাড়ি’ হয় শুদ্ধভক্তিমান্ ॥৯৬॥
verses.transliteration: ei cāri sukṛti haya mahā-bhāgyavān\\ntat-tat-kāmādi chāḍi' haya śuddha-bhaktimān
verses.translation: "Because they have a pious background, all four types of people are to be considered greatly fortunate. Such people gradually give up material desires and become pure devotees.

verses.devanagari: সাধুসঙ্গ-কৃপা কিম্বা কৃষ্ণের কৃপায় ।\\nকামাদি ‘দুঃসঙ্গ’ ছাড়ি’ শুদ্ধভক্তি পায় ॥৯৭॥
verses.transliteration: sādhu-saṅga-kṛpā kimvā kṛṣṇera kṛpāya\\nkāmādi 'duḥsaṅga' chāḍi' śuddha-bhakti pāya
verses.translation: "One is elevated to the platform of devotional life by the mercy of a Vaiṣṇava, the bona fide spiritual master, and by the special mercy of Kṛṣṇa. On that platform, one gives up all material desires and the association of unwanted people. Thus one is elevated to the platform of pure devotional service.

verses.devanagari: সত্সঙ্গান্মুক্ত-দুঃসঙ্গো হাতুং নোত্সহতে বুধঃ ।\\nকীর্ত্যমানং যশো যস্য সকৃদাকর্ণ্য রোচনম্ ॥৯৮॥
verses.transliteration: sat-saṅgān mukta-duḥsaṅgo\\nhātuṁ notsahate budhaḥ\\nkīrtyamānaṁ yaśo yasya\\nsakṛd ākarṇya rocanam
verses.translation: “ 'The intelligent, who have understood the Supreme Lord in the association of pure devotees and have become free from bad materialistic association, can never avoid hearing the glories of the Lord, even though they have heard them only once.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a verse from
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(1.10.11). All the members of the Kuru dynasty offered respects when Kṛṣṇa was leaving Hastināpura after the Battle of Kurukṣetra. Kṛṣṇa was going to His own kingdom, and all the members of the Kuru dynasty were overwhelmed by His departure. This verse was spoken in that connection by Śukadeva Gosvāmī. A pure devotee becomes attached to Kṛṣṇa by hearing the Lord's glories. The Lord's glories and the Lord Himself are identical. One has to be qualified to understand this Absolute Truth; therefore one should be given a chance to associate with a pure devotee. Our Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement is meant for this purpose. We want to create pure devotees so that other people will benefit by their association. In this way the number of pure devotees increases. Professional preachers cannot create pure devotees. There are many professional preachers of
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
who read this work to earn their livelihood. However, they cannot convert materialistic people to devotional service. Only a pure devotee can convert others to pure devotional service. It is therefore important for all the preachers in our Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement to first become pure devotees and follow the regulative principles, refraining from illicit sex, meat-eating, gambling and intoxication. They should regularly chant the Hare Kṛṣṇa
mahā-mantra
on their beads, follow the devotional process, rise early in the morning, attend
maṅgala-ārati
and recite
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
and
Bhagavad-gītā
regularly. In this way, one can become purified and free from all material contamination.
sarvopādhi-vinirmuktaṁ
tat-paratvena nirmalam
hṛṣīkeṇa hṛṣīkeśa-
sevanaṁ bhaktir ucyate
(
Nārada-pañcarātra
)
To make a show of devotional service will not help one. One must be a pure devotee following the devotional process; then one can convert others to devotional service. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu practiced devotional service and preached (
āpani ācari' bhakti karila pracāra
). If a preacher behaves properly in devotional service, he will be able to convert others. Otherwise, his preaching will have no effect.

verses.devanagari: ‘দুঃসঙ্গ’ কহিয়ে — ‘কৈতব’, ‘আত্মবঞ্চনা’ ।\\nকৃষ্ণ, কৃষ্ণভক্তি বিনু অন্য কামনা ॥৯৯॥
verses.transliteration: 'duḥsaṅga' kahiye—'kaitava', 'ātma-vañcanā'\\nkṛṣṇa, kṛṣṇa-bhakti vinu anya kāmanā
verses.translation: "Cheating oneself and cheating others is called kaitava. Associating with cheaters is called duḥsaṅga, bad association. Those who desire things other than Kṛṣṇa's service are also called duḥsaṅga, bad association.

verses.devanagari: ধর্মঃ প্রোজ্ঝিত-কৈতবোঽত্র পরমো নির্মত্সরাণাং সতাং\\nবেদ্যং বাস্তবমত্র বস্তু শিবদং তাপত্রয়োন্মূলনম্ ।\\nশ্রীমদ্ভাগবতে মহামুনিকৃতে কিংবা পরৈরীশ্বরঃ\\nসদ্যো হৃদ্যবরুধ্যতেঽত্র কৃতিভিঃ শুশ্রূষুভিস্তত্ক্ষণাত্ ॥১০০॥
verses.transliteration: dharmaḥ projjhita-kaitavo 'tra paramo nirmatsarāṇāṁ satāṁ\\nvedyaṁ vāstavam atra vastu śivadaṁ tāpa-trayonmūlanam\\nśrīmad-bhāgavate mahāmuni-kṛte kiṁ vā parair īśvaraḥ\\nsadyo hṛdy avarudhyate 'tra kṛtibhiḥ śuśrūṣubhis tat-kṣaṇāt
verses.translation: “ 'The great scripture Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, compiled by Mahāmuni Vyāsadeva from four original verses, describes the most elevated and kindhearted devotees and completely rejects the cheating ways of materially motivated religiosity. It propounds the highest principle of eternal religion, which can factually mitigate the threefold miseries of a living being and award the highest benediction of full prosperity and knowledge. Those willing to hear the message of this scripture in a submissive attitude of service can at once capture the Supreme Lord in their hearts. Therefore there is no need for any scripture other than Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a quotation from
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(1.1.2). For an explanation see also
Ādi-līlā
(1.91).

verses.devanagari: ‘প্র’-শব্দে — মোক্ষবাঞ্ছা কৈতবপ্রধান  ।\\nএই শ্লোকে শ্রীধরস্বামী করিয়াছেন ব্যাখ্যান ॥১০১॥
verses.transliteration: 'pra'-śabde—mokṣa-vāñchā kaitava-pradhāna\\nei śloke śrīdhara-svāmī kariyāchena vyākhyāna
verses.translation: "The prefix pra in the word projjhita specifically refers to those desiring liberation or oneness with the Supreme. Such a desire should be understood to result from a cheating propensity. The great commentator Śrīdhara Svāmī has explained this verse in that way.

verses.devanagari: সকাম-ভক্তে ‘অজ্ঞ’ জানি’ দয়ালু ভগবান্  ।\\nস্ব-চরণ দিয়া করে ইচ্ছার পিধান ॥১০২॥
verses.transliteration: sakāma-bhakte 'ajña' jāni' dayālu bhagavān\\nsva-caraṇa diyā kare icchāra pidhāna
verses.translation: "When the merciful Lord Kṛṣṇa understands a devotee's foolish desire for material prosperity, He gratefully gives him the shelter of His lotus feet. In this way, the Lord covers his undesirable ambitions.

verses.devanagari: সত্যং দিশত্যর্থিতমর্থিতো নৃণাং\\nনৈবার্থদো যত্ পুনরর্থিতা যতঃ ।\\nস্বয়ং বিধত্তে ভজতামনিচ্ছতা-\\nমিচ্ছাপিধানং নিজপাদপল্লবম্ ॥১০৩॥
verses.transliteration: satyaṁ diśaty arthitam arthito nṛṇāṁ\\nnaivārthado yat punar arthitā yataḥ\\nsvayaṁ vidhatte bhajatām anicchatām\\nicchā-pidhānaṁ nija-pāda-pallavam
verses.translation: “ 'Whenever Kṛṣṇa is requested to fulfill one's desire, He undoubtedly does so, but He does not award anything which, after being enjoyed, will cause someone to petition Him again and again to fulfill further desires. When one has other desires but engages in the Lord's service, Kṛṣṇa forcibly gives one shelter at His lotus feet, where one will forget all other desires.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a quotation from
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(5.19.27).

verses.devanagari: সাধুসঙ্গ, কৃষ্ণকৃপা, ভক্তির স্বভাব ।\\nএ তিনে সব ছাড়ায়, করে কৃষ্ণে ‘ভাব’ ॥১০৪॥
verses.transliteration: sādhu-saṅga, kṛṣṇa-kṛpā, bhaktira svabhāva\\ne tine saba chāḍāya, kare kṛṣṇe 'bhāva'
verses.translation: "Association with a devotee, the mercy of Kṛṣṇa, and the nature of devotional service help one to give up all undesirable association and gradually attain elevation to the platform of love of Godhead.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This verse refers to the association of pure devotees, the mercy of Kṛṣṇa and the rendering of devotional service. All these help one give up the association of nondevotees and the material opulence awarded by the external energy,
māyā.
A pure devotee is never attracted by material opulence, for he understands that wasting time to acquire material opulence is a misuse of the gift of human life. In
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
it is said:
śrama eva hi kevalam.
In the eyes of a devotee, politicians, social workers, philanthropists, philosophers and humanitarians are simply wasting their time, for human society is not freed from the cycle of birth and death by their activity and propaganda. These so-called philanthropists, politicians and philosophers have no knowledge because they do not know that there is life after death. Understanding that there is life after death is the beginning of spiritual knowledge. A person can understand himself and what he is simply by understanding the first lessons of
Bhagavad-gītā.
dehino 'smin yathā dehe
kaumāraṁ yauvanaṁ jarā
tathā dehāntara-prāptir
dhīras tatra na muhyati
"As the embodied soul continually passes, in this body, from boyhood to youth to old age, the soul similarly passes into another body at death. The self-realized soul is not bewildered by such a change." (Bg. 2.13)
Not knowing the real science of life one engages in the temporary activities of this life and thus becomes further entangled in the cycle of birth and death. Thus one always desires material opulence, which can be attained by
karma, jñāna
and
yoga.
However, when one is actually elevated to the devotional platform, he gives up all these desires. This is called
anyābhilāṣitā-śūnya.
Then one becomes a pure devotee.

verses.devanagari: আগে যত যত অর্থ ব্যাখ্যান করিব ।\\nকৃষ্ণগুণাস্বাদের এই হেতু জানিব ॥১০৫॥
verses.transliteration: āge yata yata artha vyākhyāna kariba\\nkṛṣṇa-guṇāsvādera ei hetu jāniba
verses.translation: "In this way I shall progressively explain all the words in the verse. It should be understood that all these words are meant to enable one to taste the transcendental quality of Kṛṣṇa.

verses.devanagari: শ্লোকব্যাখ্যা লাগি’ এই করিলুঁ আভাস ।\\nএবে করি শ্লোকের মূলার্থ প্রকাশ ॥১০৬॥
verses.transliteration: śloka-vyākhyā lāgi' ei kariluṅ ābhāsa\\nebe kari ślokera mūlārtha prakāśa
verses.translation: "I have given all these explanations just to indicate the purpose of the verse. Allow Me to explain the real purpose of the verse.

verses.devanagari: জ্ঞানমার্গে উপাসক — দুইত’ প্রকার ।\\nকেবল ব্রহ্মোপাসক, মোক্ষাকাঙ্ক্ষী আর ॥১০৭॥
verses.transliteration: jñāna-mārge upāsaka—duita' prakāra\\nkevala brahmopāsaka, mokṣākāṅkṣī āra
verses.translation: "There are two kinds of worshipers on the path of philosophical speculation-one is brahma-upāsaka, a worshiper of the impersonal Brahman, and the other is called mokṣākāṅkṣī, one who desires liberation.

verses.devanagari: কেবল ব্রহ্মোপাসক তিন ভেদ হয় ।\\nসাধক, ব্রহ্মময়, আর প্রাপ্ত-ব্রহ্মলয় ॥১০৮॥
verses.transliteration: kevala brahmopāsaka tina bheda haya\\nsādhaka, brahmamaya, āra prāpta-brahma-laya
verses.translation: "There are three types of people who worship the impersonal Brahman. The first is the beginner, the second is one whose thoughts are absorbed in Brahman, and the third is one who is actually merged in the impersonal Brahman.

verses.devanagari: ভক্তি বিনা কেবল জ্ঞানে ‘মুক্তি’ নাহি হয় ।\\nভক্তি সাধন করে যেই ‘প্রাপ্ত-ব্রহ্মলয়’ ॥১০৯॥
verses.transliteration: bhakti vinā kevala jñāne 'mukti' nāhi haya\\nbhakti sādhana kare yei 'prāpta-brahma-laya'
verses.translation: "One cannot attain liberation simply through philosophical speculation devoid of devotional service. However, if one renders devotional service, he is automatically on the Brahman platform.

verses.devanagari: ভক্তির স্বভাব, — ব্রহ্ম হৈতে করে আকর্ষণ ।\\nদিব্য দেহ দিয়া করায় কৃষ্ণের ভজন ॥১১০॥
verses.transliteration: bhaktira svabhāva,—brahma haite kare ākarṣaṇa\\ndivya deha diyā karāya kṛṣṇera bhajana
verses.translation: "Characteristically, one in devotional service is attracted away from the impersonal Brahman platform. He is offered a transcendental body to engage in Lord Kṛṣṇa's service.

verses.devanagari: ভক্তদেহ পাইলে হয় গুণের স্মরণ ।\\nগুণাকৃষ্ট হঞা করে নির্মল ভজন ॥১১১॥
verses.transliteration: bhakta-deha pāile haya guṇera smaraṇa\\nguṇākṛṣṭa hañā kare nirmala bhajana
verses.translation: "When one gets a devotee's spiritual body, he can remember the transcendental qualities of Kṛṣṇa. Simply by being attracted to Kṛṣṇa's transcendental qualities, one becomes a pure devotee engaged in His service.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura has given the following summary of verses 107-111. Transcendentalists on the path of philosophical speculation can be divided into two categories—the pure worshiper of impersonal Brahman and he who wishes to merge into the existence of impersonal Brahman. When one is fully absorbed in the thought that one is not different from the Supreme Absolute Truth, one is said to be a worshiper of the impersonal Brahman. The impersonal worshipers of Brahman can again be divided into three categories-(1)
sādhaka,
those who are nearing perfect execution of the process of Brahman realization; (2) those who are fully absorbed in meditation on Brahman; and (3) those who are on the
brahma-bhūta
platform and have no relationship with material existence. Even though the worshiper of impersonal Brahman can be highly advanced, he cannot attain liberation without discharging devotional service. Anyone who has realized himself as spirit soul can engage in devotional service. This is the verdict of
Bhagavad-gītā:
brahma-bhūtaḥ prasannātmā
na śocati na kāṅkṣati
samaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu
mad-bhaktiṁ labhate parām
"One who is thus transcendentally situated at once realizes the Supreme Brahman and is fully joyful. He never laments nor desires to have anything; he is equally disposed to every living entity. In that state he attains pure devotional service unto Me." (Bg. 18.54)
To attain the platform of pure devotional service, one has to become spiritually pure and attain the
brahma-bhūta
platform, which is beyond material anxiety and material discrimination. When one approaches pure devotional service after realizing Brahman, one becomes attracted by pure devotional service. At such a time, by rendering devotional service, one gets a spiritual body with purified senses.
sarvopādhi-vinirmuktaṁ
tatparatvena nirmalam
hṛṣīkeṇa hṛṣīkeśa-
sevanaṁ bhaktir ucyate
When one's senses are pure, one can render loving devotional service to Kṛṣṇa. A pure devotee can only remember Kṛṣṇa's transcendental qualities. Remembering them, he fully engages in the loving service of the Lord.

verses.devanagari: “মুক্তা অপি লীলয়া বিগ্রহং কৃত্বা ভগবন্তং ভজন্তে ।।” ॥ ১১২ ॥
verses.transliteration: "muktā api līlayā vigrahaṁ\\nkṛtvā bhagavantaṁ bhajante"
verses.translation: “ 'Even a liberated soul merged in the impersonal Brahman effulgence is attracted to the pastimes of Kṛṣṇa. He thus installs a Deity and renders the Lord service.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
Highly elevated Māyāvādī
sannyāsīs
sometimes worship the Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa Deity and discuss the pastimes of the Lord, but their purpose is not elevation to Goloka Vṛndāvana. They want to merge into the Lord's effulgence. This statement is quoted from Śaṅkarācārya's commentary on the
Upaniṣad
known as
Nṛsiṁha-tāpanī.

verses.devanagari: জন্ম হৈতে শুক-সনকাদি ‘ব্রহ্মময়’ ।\\nকৃষ্ণগুণাকৃষ্ট হঞা কৃষ্ণেরে ভজয় ॥১১৩॥
verses.transliteration: janma haite śuka-sanakādi 'brahmamaya'\\nkṛṣṇa-guṇākṛṣṭa hañā kṛṣṇere bhajaya
verses.translation: "Although Śukadeva Gosvāmī and the four Kumāras were always absorbed in the thought of impersonal Brahman and were thus Brahmavādīs, they were nonetheless attracted by the transcendental pastimes and qualities of Kṛṣṇa. Therefore they later became devotees of Kṛṣṇa.

verses.devanagari: সনকাদ্যের কৃষ্ণকৃপায় সৌরভে হরে মন ।\\nগুণাকৃষ্ট হঞা করে নির্মল ভজন ॥১১৪॥
verses.transliteration: sanakādyera kṛṣṇa-kṛpāya saurabhe hare mana\\nguṇākṛṣṭa hañā kare nirmala bhajana
verses.translation: "The minds of the four Kumāras were attracted by the aroma of the flowers offered to Kṛṣṇa's lotus feet. Being thus attracted by the transcendental qualities of Kṛṣṇa, they engaged in pure devotional service.

verses.devanagari: তস্যারবিন্দনয়নস্য পদারবিন্দ-\\nকিঞ্জল্কমিশ্রতুলসীমকরন্দবায়ুঃ ।\\nঅন্তর্গতঃ স্ববিবরেণ চকার তেষাং\\nসংক্ষোভমক্ষরজুষামপি চিত্ততন্বোঃ ॥১১৫॥
verses.transliteration: tasyāravinda-nayanasya padāravinda-\\nkiñjalka-miśra-tulasī-makaranda-vāyuḥ\\nantargataḥ svavivareṇa cakāra teṣāṁ\\nsaṅkṣobham akṣara-juṣām api citta-tanvoḥ
verses.translation: “ 'When the breeze carrying the aroma of tulasī leaves and saffron from the lotus feet of the lotus-eyed Personality of Godhead entered through the nostrils into the hearts of those sages [the Kumāras], they experienced a change in both body and mind, even though they were attached to impersonal Brahman understanding.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a verse from
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(3.15.43).

verses.devanagari: ব্যাসকৃপায় শুকদেবের লীলাদি-স্মরণ ।\\nকৃষ্ণগুণাকৃষ্ট হঞা করেন ভজন ॥১১৬॥
verses.transliteration: vyāsa-kṛpāya śukadevera līlādi-smaraṇa\\nkṛṣṇa-guṇākṛṣṭa hañā karena bhajana
verses.translation: "By the mercy of Śrīla Vyāsadeva, Śukadeva Gosvāmī was attracted by the pastimes of Lord Kṛṣṇa. Being thus attracted by Kṛṣṇa's transcendental qualities, he also became a devotee and engaged in His service.

verses.devanagari: হরের্গুণাক্ষিপ্তমতির্ভগবান্ বাদরায়ণিঃ ।\\nঅধ্যগান্মহদাখ্যানং নিত্যং বিষ্ণুজনপ্রিয়ঃ ॥১১৭॥
verses.transliteration: harer guṇākṣipta-matir\\nbhagavān bādarāyaṇiḥ\\nadhyagān mahad-ākhyānaṁ\\nnityaṁ viṣṇu-jana-priyaḥ
verses.translation: “ 'Being very much attracted by the transcendental pastimes of the Lord, the mind of Śrīla Śukadeva Gosvāmī was agitated by Kṛṣṇa consciousness. He therefore began to study Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam by the grace of his father.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a quotation from
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(1.7.11).

verses.devanagari: নব-যোগীশ্বর জন্ম হৈতে ‘সাধক’ জ্ঞানী ।\\nবিধি-শিব-নারদ-মুখে কৃষ্ণগুণ শুনি’ ॥১১৮॥
verses.transliteration: nava-yogīśvara janma haite 'sādhaka' jñānī\\nvidhi-śiva-nārada-mukhe kṛṣṇa-guṇa śuni'
verses.translation: "From their very births, the nine great mystic yogīs [Yogendras] were impersonal philosophers of the Absolute Truth. However, because they heard about Lord Kṛṣṇa's qualities from Lord Brahmā, Lord Śiva and the great sage Nārada, they also became Kṛṣṇa's devotees.

verses.devanagari: গুণাকৃষ্ট হঞা করে কৃষ্ণের ভজন ।\\nএকাদশ-স্কন্ধে তাঁর ভক্তি-বিবরণ ॥১১৯॥
verses.transliteration: guṇākṛṣṭa hañā kare kṛṣṇera bhajana\\nekādaśa-skandhe tāṅra bhakti-vivaraṇa
verses.translation: "In the Eleventh Canto of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam there is a full description of the devotional service of the nine Yogendras, who rendered devotional service because they were attracted by the Lord's transcendental qualities.

verses.devanagari: অক্লেশাং কমলভুবঃ প্রবিশ্য গোষ্ঠীং\\nকুর্বন্তঃ শ্রুতিশিরসাং শ্রুতিং শ্রুতজ্ঞাঃ ।\\nউত্তুঙ্গং যদুপুরসঙ্গমায় রঙ্গং\\nযোগীন্দ্রাঃ পুলকভৃতো নবাপ্যবাপুঃ ॥১২০॥
verses.transliteration: akleśāṁ kamala-bhuvaḥ praviśya goṣṭhīṁ\\nkurvantaḥ śruti-śirasāṁ śrutiṁ śrutajñāḥ\\nuttuṅgaṁ yadu-pura-saṅgamāya raṅgaṁ\\nyogīndrāḥ pulaka-bhṛto navāpy avāpuḥ
verses.translation: “ 'The nine Yogendras entered Lord Brahmā's association and heard from him the real meaning of the topmost Vedic literatures—the Upaniṣads. Although they were already conversant in Vedic knowledge, they became very jubilant in Kṛṣṇa consciousness just by listening to Brahmā. Thus they wanted to enter Dvārakā, the abode of Lord Kṛṣṇa. In this way they finally achieved the place known as Raṅga-kṣetra.'
verses.purport: PURPORT\nThis is a quotation from the\nMahā Upaniṣad.

verses.devanagari: মোক্ষাকাঙ্ক্ষী জ্ঞানী হয় তিনপ্রকার ।\\nমুমুক্ষু, জীবন্মুক্ত, প্রাপ্তস্বরূপ আর ॥১২১॥
verses.transliteration: mokṣākāṅkṣī jñānī haya tina-prakāra\\nmumukṣu, jīvan-mukta, prāpta-svarūpa āra
verses.translation: "Those who wish to merge into the impersonal Brahman are also divided into three categories—those desiring to be liberated, those already liberated and those who have realized Brahman.

verses.devanagari: ‘মুমুক্ষু’ জগতে অনেক সংসারী জন ।\\n‘মুক্তি’ লাগি’ ভক্ত্যে করে কৃষ্ণের ভজন ॥১২২॥
verses.transliteration: 'mumukṣu' jagate aneka saṁsārī jana\\n'mukti' lāgi' bhaktye kare kṛṣṇera bhajana
verses.translation: "There are many people within this material world who desire liberation, and for this purpose they render devotional service to Lord Kṛṣṇa.

verses.devanagari: মুমুক্ষবো ঘোররূপান্ হিত্বা ভূতপতীনথ ।\\nনারায়ণ-কলাঃ শান্তা ভজন্তি হ্যনসূয়বঃ ॥১২৩॥
verses.transliteration: mumukṣavo ghora-rūpān\\nhitvā bhūta-patīn atha\\nnārāyaṇa-kalāḥ śāntā\\nbhajanti hy anasūyavaḥ
verses.translation: “ 'Those who want to be relieved from the material clutches give up the worship of the various demigods, who have fearful bodily features. Such peaceful devotees, who are not envious of the demigods, worship the different forms of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Nārāyaṇa.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a quotation from
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(1.2.26). Those who actually want the highest perfection worship Lord Viṣṇu in His different incarnations. Those who are attracted to the materialistic way of life and who are always agitated and full of anxiety worship demigods who appear fierce, demigods like goddess Kālī and Kāla-bhairava (Rudra). The devotees of Kṛṣṇa, however, do not envy the demigods or their worshipers but peacefully render devotional service to the incarnations of Nārāyaṇa instead.

verses.devanagari: সেই সবের সাধুসঙ্গে গুণ স্ফুরায় ।\\nকৃষ্ণভজন করায়, ‘মুমুক্ষা’ ছাড়ায় ॥১২৪॥
verses.transliteration: sei sabera sādhu-saṅge guṇa sphurāya\\nkṛṣṇa-bhajana karāya, 'mumukṣā' chāḍāya
verses.translation: "If those who are attached to demigod worship fortunately associate with the devotees, their dormant devotional service and appreciation of the Lord's qualities gradually awaken. In this way they also engage in Kṛṣṇa's devotional service and give up the desire for liberation and the desire to merge into the existence of impersonal Brahman.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
The four Kumāras (Catuḥ-sana), Śukadeva Gosvāmī and the nine Yogendras were absorbed in Brahman realization, and how they became devotees is described herein. There are three kinds of impersonalists—the
mumukṣu
(those desiring liberation), the
jīvan-muktas
(those liberated in this life) and the
prāpta-svarūpas
(those merged in Brahman realization). All three types of
jñānīs
are called
mokṣākāṅkṣīs,
those desiring liberation. By associating with devotees, such people give up the
mumukṣu
principle and render devotional service. The real cause for this change is the association of devotees. This Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement is meant to attract all types of men, even those who desire things other than the Lord's devotional service. Through the association of devotees, they gradually begin to render devotional service.

verses.devanagari: অহো মহাত্মন্ বহুদোষদুষ্টোঽ-\\nপ্যেকেন ভাত্যেষ ভবো গুণেন ।\\nসৎসঙ্গমাখ্যেন সুখাবহেন\\nকৃতাদ্য নো যেন কৃশা মুমুক্ষা ॥১২৫॥
verses.transliteration: aho mahātman bahu-doṣa-duṣṭo\\n'py ekena bhāty eṣa bhavo guṇena\\nsat-saṅgamākhyena sukhāvahena\\nkṛtādya no yena kṛśā mumukṣā
verses.translation: “ 'O great learned devotee, although there are many faults in this material world, there is one good opportunity—the association with devotees. Such association brings about great happiness. Due to this good quality, our strong desire to achieve liberation by merging into the Brahman effulgence has become weakened.'
verses.purport: PURPORT\nThis is a quotation from the\nHari-bhakti-sudhodaya.

verses.devanagari: নারদের সঙ্গে শৌনকাদি মুনিগণ ।\\nমুমুক্ষা ছাড়িয়া কৈলা কৃষ্ণের ভজন ॥১২৬॥
verses.transliteration: nāradera saṅge śaunakādi muni-gaṇa\\nmumukṣā chāḍiyā kailā kṛṣṇera bhajana
verses.translation: "By associating with the great saint Nārada, the great sages like Śaunaka and others gave up the desire for liberation and engaged in Kṛṣṇa's devotional service.

verses.devanagari: কৃষ্ণের দর্শনে, কারো কৃষ্ণের কৃপায় ।\\nমুমুক্ষা ছাড়িয়া গুণে ভজে তাঁর পা’য় ॥১২৭॥
verses.transliteration: kṛṣṇera darśane, kāro kṛṣṇera kṛpāya\\nmumukṣā chāḍiyā guṇe bhaje tāṅra pā'ya
verses.translation: "Simply by meeting Kṛṣṇa or receiving Kṛṣṇa's special favor, one can give up the desire for liberation. Being attracted by the transcendental qualities of Kṛṣṇa, one can engage in His service.

verses.devanagari: অস্মিন্ সুখঘনমূর্তৌ পরমাত্মনি বৃষ্ণিপত্তনে স্ফুরতি ।\\nআত্মারামতয়া মে বৃথা গতো বত চিরং কালঃ ॥১২৮॥
verses.transliteration: asmin sukha-ghana-mūrtau param-\\nātmani vṛṣṇi-pattane sphurati\\nātmārāmatayā me vṛthā\\ngato bata ciraṁ kālaḥ
verses.translation: “ 'In this Dvārakā-dhāma, I am being attracted by the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa, who is personified spiritual bliss. Simply by seeing Him, I am feeling great happiness. Oh, I have wasted so much time trying to become self-realized through impersonal cultivation. This is a cause for lamentation!'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This verse is also found in
Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu
(3.1.34).

verses.devanagari: ‘জীবন্মুক্ত’ অনেক, সেই দুই ভেদ জানি ।\\n‘ভক্ত্যে জীবন্মুক্ত’, ‘জ্ঞানে জীবন্মুক্ত’ মানি ॥১২৯॥
verses.transliteration: jīvan-mukta' aneka, sei dui bheda jāni\\n'bhaktye jīvan-mukta', jñāne jīvan-mukta' māni
verses.translation: "There are many people who are liberated even in this lifetime. Some are liberated by discharging devotional service, and others are liberated through the philosophical speculative process.

verses.devanagari: ‘ভক্ত্যে জীবন্মুক্ত’ গুণাকৃষ্ট হঞা কৃষ্ণ ভজে ।\\nশুষ্কজ্ঞানে জীবন্মুক্ত অপরাধে অধো মজে ॥১৩০॥
verses.transliteration: 'bhaktye jīvan-mukta' guṇākṛṣṭa hañā kṛṣṇa bhaje\\nśuṣka-jñāne jīvan-mukta aparādhe adho maje
verses.translation: "Those who are liberated by devotional service become more and more attracted by the transcendental qualities of Kṛṣṇa. Thus they engage in His service. Those who are liberated by the speculative process eventually fall down again due to offensive activity.

verses.devanagari: যেঽন্যেঽরবিন্দাক্ষ বিমুক্তমানিন-\\nস্ত্বয্যস্তভাবাদবিশুদ্ধবুদ্ধয়ঃ ।\\nআরুহ্য কৃচ্ছ্রেণ পরং পদং ততঃ\\nপতন্ত্যধোঽনাদৃতযুষ্মদঙ্ঘ্রয়ঃ ॥১৩১॥
verses.transliteration: ye 'nye 'ravindākṣa vimukta-māninas\\ntvayy asta-bhāvād aviśuddha-buddhayaḥ\\nāruhya kṛcchreṇa paraṁ padaṁ tataḥ\\npatanty adho 'nādṛta-yuṣmad-aṅghrayaḥ
verses.translation: “ 'O lotus-eyed one, those who think they are liberated in this life but are without devotional service to You are of impure intelligence. Although they accept severe austerities and penances and rise to the spiritual position, to impersonal Brahman realization, they fall down again because they neglect to worship Your lotus feet.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a quotation from
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(10.2.32).

verses.devanagari: ব্রহ্মভূতঃ প্রসন্নাত্মা ন শোচতি ন কাঙ্ক্ষতি ।\\nসমঃ সর্বেষু ভূতেষু মদ্ভক্তিং লভতে পরাম্ ॥১৩২॥
verses.transliteration: brahma-bhūtaḥ prasannātmā\\nna śocati na kāṅkṣati\\nsamaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu\\nmad-bhaktiṁ labhate parām
verses.translation: “ 'One who is thus transcendentally situated at once realizes the Supreme Brahman and is fully joyful. He never laments nor desires to have anything; he is equally disposed to every living entity. In that state he attains pure devotional service unto Me.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a quotation from
Bhagavad-gītā
(Bg. 18.54).

verses.devanagari: অদ্বৈতবীথীপথিকৈরুপাস্যাঃ\\nস্বানন্দসিংহাসনলব্ধদীক্ষাঃ ।\\nশঠেন কেনাপি বয়ং হঠেন\\nদাসীকৃতা গোপবধূবিটেন ॥১৩৩॥
verses.transliteration: advaita-vīthī-pathikair upāsyāḥ\\nsvānanda-siṁhāsana-labdha-dīkṣāḥ\\nśaṭhena kenāpi vayaṁ haṭhena\\ndāsī-kṛtā gopa-vadhū-viṭena
verses.translation: “ 'Although I was worshiped by those on the path of monism and initiated into self-realization through the yoga system, I am nonetheless forcibly turned into a maidservant by some cunning boy who is always joking with the gopīs.'
verses.purport: PURPORT\nThis is a verse written by Bilvamaṅgala Ṭhākura.

verses.devanagari: ভক্তিবলে ‘প্রাপ্তস্বরূপ’ দিব্যদেহ পায় ।\\nকৃষ্ণগুণাকৃষ্ট হঞা ভজে কৃষ্ণ-পা’য় ॥১৩৪॥
verses.transliteration: bhakti-bale 'prāpta-svarūpa' divya-deha pāya\\nkṛṣṇa-guṇākṛṣṭa hañā bhaje kṛṣṇa-pā'ya
verses.translation: "One who has attained his constitutional position by the strength of devotional service attains a transcendental body even in this lifetime. Being attracted by Lord Kṛṣṇa's transcendental qualities, one fully engages in service at His lotus feet.

verses.devanagari: নিরোধোঽস্যানুশয়নমাত্মনঃ সহ শক্তিভিঃ ।\\nমুক্তির্হিত্বান্যথারূপং স্বরূপেণ ব্যবস্থিতিঃ ॥১৩৫॥
verses.transliteration: nirodho 'syānu śayanam\\nātmanaḥ saha śaktibhiḥ\\nmuktir hitvānyathā-rūpaṁ\\nsvarūpeṇa vyavasthitiḥ
verses.translation: “ 'The living entities and other potencies merge in the Mahā-Viṣṇu as the Lord lies down and winds up [destroys] the cosmic manifestation. Liberation means being situated in one's eternal original form, which he attains after giving up the changeable gross and subtle bodies.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a quotation from
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(2.10.6).

verses.devanagari: কৃষ্ণ-বহির্মুখ-দোষে মায়া হৈতে ভয় ।\\nকৃষ্ণোন্মুখ ভক্তি হৈতে মায়া-মুক্ত হয় ॥১৩৬॥
verses.transliteration: kṛṣṇa-bahirmukha-doṣe māyā haite bhaya\\nkṛṣṇonmukha bhakti haite māyā-mukta haya
verses.translation: "By opposing Kṛṣṇa consciousness, one again becomes conditioned and fearful due to the influence of māyā. By executing devotional service faithfully, one is liberated from māyā.

verses.devanagari: ভয়ং দ্বিতীয়াভিনিবেশতঃ স্যা-\\nদীশাদপেতস্য বিপর্যয়োঽস্মৃতিঃ ।\\nতন্মায়য়াতো বুধ আভজেত্তং\\nভক্ত্যৈকয়েশং গুরুদেবতাত্মা ॥১৩৭॥
verses.transliteration: bhayaṁ dvitīyābhiniveśataḥ syād\\nīśād apetasya viparyayo 'smṛtiḥ\\ntan-māyayāto budha ābhajet taṁ\\nbhaktyaikayeśaṁ guru-devatātmā
verses.translation: “ 'When the living entity is attracted by the material energy that is separate from Kṛṣṇa, he is overpowered by fear. Because he is separated from the Supreme Personality of Godhead by the material energy, his conception of life is reversed. In other words, instead of being the eternal servant of Kṛṣṇa, he becomes Kṛṣṇa's competitor. This is called viparyayaḥ asmṛtiḥ. To nullify this mistake, one who is actually learned and advanced worships the Supreme Personality of Godhead as his spiritual master, worshipful Deity and source of life. He thus worships the Lord by the process of unalloyed devotional service.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This verse is quoted from
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(11.2.37).

verses.devanagari: দৈবী হ্যেষা গুণময়ী মম মায়া দুরত্যয়া ।\\nমামেব যে প্রপদ্যন্তে মায়ামেতাং তরন্তি তে ॥১৩৮॥
verses.transliteration: daivī hy eṣā guṇa-mayī\\nmama māyā duratyayā\\nmām eva ye prapadyante\\nmāyām etāṁ taranti te
verses.translation: “ 'This divine energy of Mine, consisting of the three modes of material nature, is difficult to overcome. But those who have surrendered unto Me can easily cross beyond it.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a quotation from
Bhagavad-gītā
(Bg. 7.14).

verses.devanagari: ভক্তি বিনু মুক্তি নাহি, ভক্ত্যে মুক্তি হয় ॥১৩৯॥
verses.transliteration: bhakti vinu mukti nāhi, bhaktye mukti haya
verses.translation: "One does not attain liberation without rendering devotional service. Liberation is only attained by devotional service.

verses.devanagari: শ্রেয়ঃসৃতিং ভক্তিমুদস্য তে বিভো\\nক্লিশ্যন্তি যে কেবল-বোধলব্ধয়ে ।\\nতেষামসৌ ক্লেশল এব শিষ্যতে\\nনান্যদ্যথা স্থূলতুষাবঘাতিনাম্ ॥১৪০॥
verses.transliteration: śreyaḥ-sṛtiṁ bhaktim udasya te vibho\\nkliśyanti ye kevala-bodha-labdhaye\\nteṣām asau kleśala eva śiṣyate\\nnānyad yathā sthūla-tuṣāvaghātinām
verses.translation: “ 'My dear Lord, devotional service unto You is the only auspicious path. If one gives it up simply for speculative knowledge or the understanding that these living beings are spirit souls and the material world is false, he undergoes a great deal of trouble. He only gains troublesome and inauspicious activities. His actions are like beating a husk that is already devoid of rice. One's labor becomes fruitless.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a quotation from
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(10.14.4).

verses.devanagari: যেঽন্যেঽরবিন্দাক্ষ বিমুক্তমানিন-\\nস্ত্বয্যস্তভাবাদবিশুদ্ধবুদ্ধয়ঃ ।\\nআরুহ্য কৃচ্ছ্রেণ পরং পদং ততঃ\\nপতন্ত্যধোঽনাদৃতযুষ্মদঙ্ঘ্রয়ঃ ॥১৪১॥
verses.transliteration: ye 'nye 'ravindākṣa vimukta-māninas\\ntvayy asta-bhāvād aviśuddha-buddhayaḥ\\nāruhya kṛcchreṇa paraṁ padaṁ tataḥ\\npatanty adho 'nādṛta-yuṣmad-aṅghrayaḥ
verses.translation: “ 'O lotus-eyed one, those who think they are liberated in this life but are without devotional service to You are of impure intelligence. Although they accept severe austerities and penances and rise to the spiritual position, to impersonal Brahman realization, they fall down again because they neglect to worship Your lotus feet.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a verse from
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(10.2.32).

verses.devanagari: য এষাং পুরুষং সাক্ষাদাত্মপ্রভবমীশ্বরম্ ।\\nন ভজন্ত্যবজানন্তি স্থানাদ্ভ্রষ্টাঃ পতন্ত্যধঃ ॥১৪২॥
verses.transliteration: ya eṣāṁ puruṣaṁ sākṣād\\nātma-prabhavam īśvaram\\nna bhajanty avajānanti\\nsthānād bhraṣṭāḥ patanty adhaḥ
verses.translation: “ 'If one simply maintains an official position in the four varṇas and āśramas but does not worship the Supreme Lord Viṣṇu, he falls down from his puffed up position into a hellish condition.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is also a quotation from
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(11.5.3).

verses.devanagari: ভক্ত্যে মুক্তি পাইলেহ অবশ্য কৃষ্ণেরে ভজয় ॥১৪৩॥
verses.transliteration: bhaktye mukti pāileha avaśya kṛṣṇere bhajaya
verses.translation: "When one is actually liberated by executing devotional service, he always engages in the transcendental loving service of the Lord.

verses.devanagari: “মুক্তা অপি লীলয়া বিগ্রহং কৃত্বা ভগবন্তং ভজন্তে ।।” ॥ ১৪৪ ॥
verses.transliteration: "muktā api līlayā vigrahaṁ\\nkṛtvā bhagavantaṁ bhajante"
verses.translation: “ 'Even a liberated soul merged in the impersonal Brahman effulgence is attracted to the pastimes of Kṛṣṇa. Be thus installs a Deity and renders the Lord service.'
verses.purport: PURPORT\nThis is a quotation from Śaṅkarācārya's commentary on the\nNṛsiṁha-tāpanī Upaniṣad.

verses.devanagari: এই ছয় আত্মারাম কৃষ্ণেরে ভজয় ।\\nপৃথক্ পৃথক্ চ-কারে ইহা ‘অপি’র অর্থ কয় ॥১৪৫॥
verses.transliteration: ei chaya ātmārāma kṛṣṇere bhajaya\\npṛthak pṛthak ca-kāre ihā 'api'ra artha kaya
verses.translation: "These six kinds of ātmārāmas engage in the loving service of Kṛṣṇa. The varieties of service are indicated by adding ca, and they also bear the meaning of api, 'indeed.'

verses.devanagari: “আত্মারামাশ্চ অপি” করে কৃষ্ণে অহৈতুকী ভক্তি ।\\n“মুনয়ঃ সন্তঃ” ইতি কৃষ্ণমননে আসক্তি ॥১৪৬॥
verses.transliteration: "ātmārāmāś ca api" kare kṛṣṇe ahaitukī bhakti\\n"munayaḥ santaḥ" iti kṛṣṇa-manane āsakti
verses.translation: "The six kinds of ātmārāmas render devotional service to Kṛṣṇa without ulterior motives. The words munayaḥ and santaḥ indicate those who are very attached to meditating upon Kṛṣṇa.

verses.devanagari: “নির্গ্রন্থাঃ” — অবিদ্যাহীন, কেহ — বিধিহীন ।\\nযাহাঁ যেই যুক্ত, সেই অর্থের অধীন ॥১৪৭॥
verses.transliteration: "nirgranthāḥ"—avidyā-hīna, keha—vidhi-hīna\\nyāhāṅ yei yukta, sei arthera adhīna
verses.translation: "The word nirgranthāḥ means 'without ignorance' and 'devoid of rules and regulations.' Whichever meaning fits may be applied.

verses.devanagari: চ-শব্দে করি যদি ‘ইতরেতর’ অর্থ ।\\nআর এক অর্থ কহে পরম সমর্থ ॥১৪৮॥
verses.transliteration: ca-śabde kari yadi'itaretara' artha\\nāra eka artha kahe parama samartha
verses.translation: "By using the word ca in different places, there are different meanings. Over and above them, there is another meaning that is very important.

verses.devanagari: “আত্মারামাশ্চ আত্মারামাশ্চ” করি’ বার ছয় ।\\nপঞ্চ আত্মারাম ছয় চ-কারে লুপ্ত হয় ॥১৪৯॥
verses.transliteration: "ātmārāmāś ca ātmārāmāś ca" kari' bāra chaya\\npañca ātmārāma chaya ca-kāre lupta haya
verses.synonyms:
ātmārāmāḥ ca ātmārāmāḥ ca
—repeating the words
ātmārāmāḥ
and
ca
;
kari'
—doing;
bāra chaya
—six times;
pañca ātmārāma
—five kinds of
ātmārāmas
;
chaya
—six;
ca-kāre
—by the word
ca
;
lupta haya
—become unpronounced.
verses.translation: "Although the words ātmārāmāś ca would be repeated six times, simply by adding the word ca, five ātmārāmas are deleted.

verses.devanagari: এক ‘আত্মারাম’-শব্দ অবশেষ রহে ।\\nএক ‘আত্মারাম’-শব্দে ছয় জন কহে ॥১৫০॥
verses.transliteration: eka 'ātmārāma'-śabda avaśeṣa rahe\\neka 'ātmārāma'-śabde chaya-jana kahe
verses.translation: "Therefore there is no need to repeat the word ātmārāma. One is sufficient, and that one word indicates six persons.

verses.devanagari: “সরূপাণামেকশেষ একবিভক্তৌ” ।\\nউক্তার্থানামপ্ৰয়োগঃ ।\\nরামশ্চ রামশ্চ রামশ্চ রামা ইতিবত্ ॥১৫১॥
verses.transliteration: "sarūpāṇām eka-śeṣa eka-vibhaktau"\\nuktārthānām aprayogaḥ\\nrāmaś ca rāmaś ca rāmaś ca rāmā itivat
verses.translation: “ 'Of words having the same form and case termination, the last one is the only one retained. For example, the word rāmaḥ is used to stand for rāmaś ca, rāmaś ca, rāmaś ca, etc.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a quotation from Pāṇini's
sūtras
(1.2.64).

verses.devanagari: তবে যে চ-কার, সেই ‘সমুচ্চয়’ কয় ।\\n“আত্মারামাশ্চ মুনয়শ্চ” কৃষ্ণেরে ভজয় ॥১৫২॥
verses.transliteration: tabe ye ca-kāra, sei 'samuccaya' kaya\\n"ātmārāmāś ca munayaś ca" kṛṣṇere bhajaya
verses.translation: "By the aggregate use of the word ca, it is indicated that all the ātmārāmas and saints serve and worship Kṛṣṇa.

verses.devanagari: “নির্গ্রন্থা অপি”র এই ‘অপি’ — সম্ভাবনে ।\\nএই সাত অর্থ প্রথমে করিলুঁ ব্যাখ্যানে ॥১৫৩॥
verses.transliteration: "nirgranthā api"ra ei 'api'—sambhāvane\\nei sāta artha prathame kariluṅ vyākhyāne
verses.translation: "Api added to the word nirgranthāḥ is used for exposition. Thus I have tried to clarify the seven types of meaning.

verses.devanagari: অন্তর্যামি-উপাসক ‘আত্মারাম’ কয় ।\\nসেই আত্মারাম যোগীর দুই ভেদ হয় ॥১৫৪॥
verses.transliteration: antaryāmi-upāsaka 'ātmārāma' kaya\\nsei ātmārāma yogīra dui bheda haya
verses.synonyms:
antaryāmi
—of the Supersoul;
upāsaka
—worshiper;
ātmārāma kaya
—is also said to be an
ātmārāma
;
sei ātmārāma
—that
ātmārāma
;
yogīra
—of the mystic
yogī
;
dui bheda haya
—there are two kinds.
verses.translation: "The yogī who worships the Supersoul within himself is also called ātmārāma. There are two types of ātmārāma-yogīs.

verses.devanagari: সগর্ভ, নিগর্ভ, — এই হয় দুই ভেদ ।\\nএক এক তিন ভেদে ছয় বিভেদ ॥১৫৫॥
verses.transliteration: sagarbha, nigarbha,—ei haya dui bheda\\neka eka tina bhede chaya vibheda
verses.translation: "The two ātmārāma-yogīs are called sagarbha and nigarbha. Each of these is divided into three; therefore there are six types of worshipers of the Supersoul.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
The word
sagarbha-yogī
refers to a
yogī
who worships the Supersoul in the Viṣṇu form. The
nigarbha-yogī
worships the Supersoul without form. The
sagarbha
and
nigarbha yogīs
are further categorized: (1)
sagarbha-yogārurukṣu,
(2)
nigarbha-yogārurukṣu,
(3)
sagarbha-yogārūḍha,
(4)
nigarbha-yogārūḍha,
(5)
sagarbha-prāpta-siddhi
and (6)
nigarbha-prāpta-siddhi.

verses.devanagari: কেচিৎ স্বদেহান্তর্হৃদয়াবকাশে প্রাদেশমাত্রং পুরুষং বসন্তম্ ।\\nচতুর্ভুজং কঞ্জরথাঙ্গশঙ্খগদাধরং ধারণয়া স্মরন্তি ॥১৫৬॥
verses.transliteration: kecit svadehāntar hṛdayāvakāśe\\nprādeśa-mātraṁ puruṣaṁ vasantam\\ncatur-bhujaṁ kañja-rathāṅga-śaṅkha-\\ngadā-dharaṁ dhāraṇayā smaranti
verses.translation: “ 'Some yogīs think of the Lord within their hearts as measuring about six inches. The Lord has four hands, in which He holds a conchshell, club, disc and lotus flower. Those who worship this form of Viṣṇu within the heart are called sagarbha-yogīs.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This verse is from
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(2.2.8).

verses.devanagari: এবং হরৌ ভগবতি প্রতিলব্ধভাবো\\nভক্ত্যা দ্রবদ্ধৃদয় উৎপুলকঃ প্রমোদাত্ ।\\nঔৎকণ্ঠ্যবাষ্পকলয়া মুহুরর্দ্যমান-\\nস্তচ্চাপি চিত্তবড়িশং শনকৈর্বিযুঙ্ক্তে ॥১৫৭॥
verses.transliteration: evaṁ harau bhagavati pratilabdha-bhāvo\\nbhaktyā dravad-dhṛdaya utpulakaḥ pramodāt\\nautkaṇṭhya-bāṣpa-kalayā muhur ardyamānas\\ntac cāpi citta-baḍiśaṁ śanakair viyuṅkte
verses.translation: “ 'When one is in ecstatic love with the Supreme Personality of Godhead, one's heart is melted by bhakti-yoga, and one feels transcendental bliss.
