The sunshine is not the sun, but still the sunshine is not separate from the sun. The philosophy of
acintya-bhedābheda-tattva
(simultaneously one and different) cannot be understood by one who is fully under the influence of the external energy. Consequently a person under the influence of the material energy cannot understand the nature and form of the Personality of the Absolute Truth.

verses.devanagari: ঋতেঽর্থং যৎ প্রতীয়েত ন প্রতীয়েত চাত্মনি ।\\nতদ্বিদ্যাদাত্মনো মায়াং যথাভাসো যথা তমঃ ॥১১৯॥
verses.transliteration: ṛte 'rthaṁ yat pratīyeta\\nna pratīyeta cātmani\\ntad vidyād ātmano māyāṁ\\nyathābhāso yathā tamaḥ
verses.translation: “ 'What appears to be truth without Me, is certainly My illusory energy, for nothing can exist without Me. It is like a reflection of a real light in the shadows, for in the light there are neither shadows nor reflections.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a quotation from
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(2.9.34). It is the second verse of the
catuḥ-ślokī.
For an explanation of this verse, see
Ādi-līlā,
Chapter One, text 54.

verses.devanagari: ‘অভিধেয়’ সাধনভক্তির শুনহ বিচার ।\\nসর্ব-জন-দেশ-কাল-দশাতে ব্যাপ্তি যার ॥১২০॥
verses.transliteration: 'abhidheya' sādhana-bhaktira śunaha vicāra\\nsarva-jana-deśa-kāla-daśāte vyāpti yāra
verses.translation: “ 'Now please hear from Me about the process of devotional service, which is applicable in any country, for any person, at all times and in all circumstances.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
The cult of
bhāgavata-dharma
can be spread in all circumstances, among all people and in all countries. Many envious people accuse this Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement of spoiling the rigidity of so-called Hinduism. That is not actually the fact. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu confirms that devotional service to the Lord—the cult of
bhāgavata-dharma,
which is now being spread as the Hare Kṛṣṇa movement-can be spread in every country, for every person, in any condition of life, and in all circumstances.
Bhāgavata-dharma
does not restrict pure devotees to the Hindu community. A pure devotee is above a
brāhmaṇa;
therefore it is not incompatible to offer the sacred thread to devotees in Europe, America, Australia, Japan, Canada, and so on. Sometimes these pure devotees, who have been accepted by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, are not allowed to enter certain temples in India. Some high-caste
brāhmaṇas
and
gosvāmīs
refuse to take
prasāda
in the temples of the International Society for Krishna Consciousness. Actually this is against the instruction of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Devotees can come from any country, and they can belong to any creed or race. On the strength of this verse, those who are actually devotees and followers of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu must accept devotees from all parts of the world as pure Vaiṣṇavas. They should be accepted not artificially but factually. One should see how they are advanced in Kṛṣṇa consciousness and how they are conducting Deity worship,
saṅkīrtana
and Ratha-yātrā. Considering all these points, an envious person should refrain from malicious atrocities.

verses.devanagari: ‘ধর্মাদি’ বিষয়ে যৈছে এ ‘চারি’ বিচার ।\\nসাধন-ভক্তি — এই চারি বিচারের পার ॥১২১॥
verses.transliteration: 'dharmādi' viṣaye yaiche e 'cāri, vicāra\\nsādhana-bhakti-ei cāri vicārera pāra
verses.translation: “ 'As far as religious principles are concerned, there is a consideration of the person, the country, the time and the circumstance. In devotional service, however, there are no such considerations. Devotional service is transcendental to all considerations.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
When we are on the material platform, there are different types of religions-Hinduism, Christianity, Mohammedanism, Buddhism, and so on. These are instituted for a particular time, a particular country or a particular person. Consequently there are differences. Christian principles are different from Hindu principles, and Hindu principles are different from Mohammedan and Buddhist principles. These may be considered on the material platform, but when we come to the platform of transcendental devotional service, there are no such considerations. The transcendental service of the Lord (
sādhana-bhakti
) is above these principles. The world is anxious for religious unity, and that common platform can be achieved in transcendental devotional service. This is the verdict of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. When one becomes a Vaiṣṇava, he becomes transcendental to all these limited considerations. This is also confirmed in
Bhagavad-gītā
(Bg. 14.26):
māṁ ca yo 'vyabhicāreṇa
bhakti-yogena sevate
sa guṇān samatītyaitān
brahma-bhūyāya kalpate
"One who engages in full devotional service, who does not fall down in any circumstance, at once transcends the modes of material nature and thus comes to the level of Brahman."
The devotional activities of the Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement are completely transcendental to material considerations. As far as different faiths are concerned, religions may be of different types, but on the spiritual platform, everyone has an equal right to execute devotional service. That is the platform of oneness and the basis for a classless society. In his
Amṛta-pravāha-bhāṣya,
Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura confirms that one has to learn from a bona fide spiritual master about religious principles, economic development, sense gratification and ultimately liberation. These are the four divisions of regulated life, but they are subjected to the material platform. On the spiritual platform, the four principles are
jñāna, vijñāna, tad-aṅga
and
tad-rahasya.
Rules, regulations and restrictions are on the material platform, but on the spiritual platform one has to be equipped with transcendental knowledge, which is above the principles of religious rituals. Mundane religious activity is known as
smārta-viddhi,
but transcendental devotional service is called
Gosvāmī-viddhi.
Unfortunately many so-called
gosvāmīs
are on the platform of
smārta-viddhi,
yet they try to pass as
Gosvāmī-viddhi,
and thus the people are cheated.
Gosvāmī-viddhi
is strictly explained in Sanātana Gosvāmī's
Hari-bhakti-vilāsa,
wherein it is stated:
yathā kāñcanatāṁ yāti
kāṁsyaṁ rasa-vidhānataḥ
tathā dīṣkā-vidhānena
dvijatvaṁ jāyate nṛṇām
The conclusion is that devotional service is open for everyone, regardless of caste, creed, time and country. This Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement is functioning according to this principle.

verses.devanagari: সর্ব-দেশ-কাল-দশায় জনের কর্তব্য ।\\nগুরু-পাশে সেই ভক্তি প্রষ্টব্য, শ্রোতব্য ॥১২২॥
verses.transliteration: sarva-deśa-kāla-daśāya janera kartavya\\nguru-pāśe sei bhakti praṣṭavya, śrotavya
verses.translation: “ 'It is therefore the duty of every man-in every country, in every circumstance and at all times-to approach the bona fide spiritual master, question him about devotional service and listen to him explain the process.

verses.devanagari: এতাবদেব জিজ্ঞাস্যং তত্ত্বজিজ্ঞাসুনাত্মনঃ ।\\nঅন্বয়-ব্যতিরেকাভ্যাং যৎ স্যাৎ সর্বত্র সর্বদা ॥১২৩॥
verses.transliteration: etāvad eva jijñāsyaṁ\\ntattva-jijñāsunātmanaḥ\\nanvaya-vyatirekābhyāṁ\\nyat syāt sarvatra sarvadā
verses.translation: “ 'A person interested in transcendental knowledge must therefore always directly and indirectly inquire about it to know about the all-pervading truth.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a quotation from
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(2.9.36). It is the fourth verse of the
catuḥ-ślokī.
For an explanation see
Ādi-līlā,
Chapter One, text 56.

verses.devanagari: আমাতে যে ‘প্রীতি’, সেই ‘প্রেম’ — ‘প্রয়োজন’ ।\\nকার্যদ্বারে কহি তার ‘স্বরূপ’-লক্ষণ ॥১২৪॥
verses.transliteration: āmāte ye 'prīti', sei 'prema'-'prayojana'\\nkārya-dvāre kahi tāra 'svarūpa'-lakṣaṇa
verses.translation: “ 'Supreme affection for Me is called love of Godhead, and that is the ultimate goal of life. Let Me explain by practical example the natural characteristics of such love.

verses.devanagari: পঞ্চভূত যৈছে ভূতের ভিতরে-বাহিরে ।\\nভক্তগণে স্ফুরি আমি বাহিরে-অন্তরে ॥১২৫॥
verses.transliteration: pañca-bhūta yaiche bhūtera bhitare-bāhire\\nbhakta-gaṇe sphuri āmi bāhire-antare
verses.translation: “ 'The five material elements are existing inside and outside of every living entity. Similarly, I, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, am manifest within the heart of the devotee as well as outside his body.
verses.purport: PURPORT\nThe pure devotee knows that he is a servant of Kṛṣṇa eternally. He knows that everything can be used in the service of the Lord.

verses.devanagari: যথা মহান্তি ভূতানি ভূতেষূচ্চাবচেষ্বনু ।\\nপ্রবিষ্টান্যপ্রবিষ্টানি তথা তেষু ন তেষ্বহম্ ॥১২৬॥
verses.transliteration: yathā mahānti bhūtāni\\nbhūteṣūccāvaceṣv anu\\npraviṣṭāny apraviṣṭāni\\ntathā teṣu na teṣv aham
verses.translation: “ 'As the material elements enter the bodies of all living beings and yet remain outside them all, I exist within all material creations and yet am not within them.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a quotation from
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(2.9.35). It is also the third verse of the
catuḥ-ślokī.
For an explanation see
Ādi-līlā,
Chapter One, text 55.

verses.devanagari: ভক্ত আমা প্রেমে বান্ধিয়াছে হৃদয়-ভিতরে ।\\nযাহাঁ নেত্র পড়ে তাহাঁ দেখয়ে আমারে ॥১২৭॥
verses.transliteration: bhakta āmā preme bāndhiyāche hṛdaya-bhitare\\nyāhāṅ netra paḍe tāhāṅ dekhaye āmāre
verses.translation: “ 'A highly elevated devotee can bind Me, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, in his heart by love. Wherever he looks, he sees Me and nothing else.

verses.devanagari: বিসৃজতি হৃদয়ং ন যস্য সাক্ষাং\\nদ্ধরিরবশাভিহিতোঽপ্যঘৌঘনাশঃ ।\\nপ্রণয়রসনয়া ধৃতাঙ্ঘ্রিপদ্মঃ\\nস ভবতি ভাগবতপ্রধান উক্তঃ ॥১২৮॥
verses.transliteration: visṛjati hṛdayaṁ na yasya sākṣād\\ndharir avaśābhihito 'py aghaugha-nāśaḥ\\npraṇaya-rasanayā dhṛtāṅghri-padmaḥ\\nsa bhavati bhāgavata-pradhāna uktaḥ
verses.translation: “ 'Hari, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who destroys everything inauspicious for His devotees, does not leave the hearts of His devotees even if they remember Him and chant about Him inattentively. This is because the rope of love always binds the Lord within the devotees' hearts. Such devotees should be accepted as most elevated.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a quotation from
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(11.2.55).

verses.devanagari: সর্বভূতেষু যঃ পশ্যেদ্ভগবদ্ভাবমাত্মনঃ ।\\nভূতানি ভগবত্যাত্মন্যেষ ভাগবতোত্তমঃ ॥১২৯॥
verses.transliteration: sarva-bhūteṣu yaḥ paśyed\\nbhagavad-bhāvam ātmanaḥ\\nbhūtāni bhagavaty ātmany\\neṣa bhāgavatottamaḥ
verses.translation: “ 'A person advanced in devotional service sees within everything the soul of souls, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Śrī Kṛṣṇa. Consequently he always sees the form of the Supreme Personality of Godhead as the cause of all causes and understands that all things are situated in Him.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a quotation from
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(11.2.45).

verses.devanagari: গায়ন্ত উচ্চৈরমুমেব সংহতাঃ\\nবিচিক্যুরুন্মত্তকবদ্বনাদ্বনম্ ।\\nপপ্রচ্ছুরাকাশবদন্তরং বহি-\\nর্ভূতেষু সন্তং পুরুষং বনস্পতীন্ ॥১৩০॥
verses.transliteration: gāyanta uccair amum eva saṁhatāḥ\\nvicikyur unmattakavad vanād vanam\\npapracchur ākāśavad antaraṁ bahir\\nbhūteṣu santaṁ puruṣaṁ vanaspatīn
verses.translation: “ 'All the gopīs assembled to chant the transcendental qualities of Kṛṣṇa very loudly, and they began to wander from one forest to another like madwomen. They began to inquire about the Lord, who is situated in all living entities internally and externally. Indeed, they even asked all the plants and vegetables about Him, the Supreme Person.' "
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a quotation from
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(10.30.4). The
gopīs
almost went mad due to Kṛṣṇa's suddenly leaving the
rāsa
dance. Because the
gopīs
were fully absorbed in thoughts of Kṛṣṇa, they were imitating His different postures and pastimes. They became very saddened because of His absence, and this incident is explained by Śukadeva Gosvāmī to Mahārāja Parīkṣit.

verses.devanagari: অতএব ভাগবতে এই ‘তিন’ কয় ।\\nসম্বন্ধ-অভিধেয়-প্রয়োজন-ময় ॥১৩১॥
verses.transliteration: ataeva bhāgavate ei 'tina' kaya\\nsambandha-abhidheya-prayojana-maya
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu continued, "One's relationship with the Lord, activities and devotional service, and the attainment of the highest goal of life, love of Godhead, are the subject matters of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam.

verses.devanagari: বদন্তি তত্তত্ত্ববিদস্তত্ত্বং যজ্জ্ঞানমদ্বয়ম্ ।\\nব্রহ্মেতি পরমাত্মেতি ভগবানিতি শব্দ্যতে ॥১৩২॥
verses.transliteration: vadanti tat tattva-vidas\\ntattvaṁ yaj jñānam advayam\\nbrahmeti paramātmeti\\nbhagavān iti śabdyate
verses.translation: “ 'The Absolute Truth is known by the self-realized souls as a unified identity known by different names-impersonal Brahman, localized Paramātmā, and Bhagavān, the Supreme Personality of Godhead.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a quotation from
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(1.2.11).

verses.devanagari: ভগবানেক আসেদমগ্র আত্মাত্মনাং বিভুঃ ।\\nআত্মেচ্ছানুগতাবাত্মা অনানামত্যুপলক্ষণঃ ॥১৩৩॥
verses.transliteration: bhagavān eka āsedam\\nagra ātmātmanāṁ vibhuḥ\\nātmecchānugatāv ātmā\\nanānāmaty-upalakṣaṇaḥ
verses.translation: “ 'Before the cosmic manifestation was created, the creative propensity was merged in His person. At that time all potencies and manifestations were preserved in the personality of the Supreme Lord. The Lord is the cause of all causes, and He is the all-pervading, self-sufficient person. Before the creation, He existed with His spiritual potency in the spiritual world, wherein various Vaikuṇṭha planets are manifest.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a quotation from
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(3.5.23).

verses.devanagari: এতে চাংশকলাঃ পুংসঃ কৃষ্ণস্তু ভগবান্ স্বয়ম্ ।\\nইন্দ্রারি-ব্যাকুলং লোকং মৃড়য়ন্তি যুগে যুগে ॥১৩৪॥
verses.transliteration: ete cāṁśa-kalāḥ puṁsaḥ\\nkṛṣṇas tu bhagavān svayam\\nindrāri-vyākulaṁ lokaṁ\\nmṛḍayanti yuge yuge
verses.translation: “ 'All these incarnations of Godhead are either plenary portions or parts of the plenary portions of the puruṣa-avatāras. But Kṛṣṇa is the Supreme Personality of Godhead Himself. In every age He protects the world through His different features when the world is disturbed by the enemies of Indra.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a quotation from
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(1.3.28). For an explanation, see
Ādi-līlā,
Chapter Two, text 67.

verses.devanagari: এইত’ ‘সম্বন্ধ’, শুন ‘অভিধেয়’ ভক্তি ।\\nভাগবতে প্রতি-শ্লোকে ব্যাপে যার স্থিতি ॥১৩৫॥
verses.transliteration: eita' 'sambandha', śuna 'abhidheya' bhakti\\nbhāgavate prati-śloke vyāpe yāra sthiti
verses.translation: "This is one's eternal relationship with the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Now please hear about the execution of devotional service. This principle pervades practically all the verses of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam.

verses.devanagari: ভক্ত্যাহমেকয়া গ্রাহ্যঃ শ্রদ্ধয়াত্মা প্রিয়ঃ সতাম্ ।\\nভক্তিঃ পুনাতি মন্নিষ্ঠা শ্বপাকানপি সম্ভবাৎ ॥১৩৬॥
verses.transliteration: bhaktyāham ekayā grāhyaḥ\\nśraddhayātmā priyaḥ satām\\nbhaktiḥ punāti man-niṣṭhā\\nśva-pākān api sambhavāt
verses.translation: “ 'Being very dear to the devotees and sādhus, I am attained through unflinching faith and devotional service. This bhakti-yoga system, which gradually increases attachment for Me, purifies even a human being born among dog-eaters. That is to say, everyone can be elevated to the spiritual platform by the process of bhakti-yoga.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This verse is from
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(11.14.21).

verses.devanagari: ন সাধয়তি মাং যোগো ন সাংখ্যং ধর্ম উদ্ধব ।\\nন স্বাধ্যায়স্তপস্ত্যাগো যথা ভক্তির্মমোর্জিতা ॥১৩৭॥
verses.transliteration: na sādhayati māṁ yogo\\nna sāṅkhyaṁ dharma uddhava\\nna svādhyāyas tapas tyāgo\\nyathā bhaktir mamorjitā
verses.translation: “ 'The Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa, said: "My dear Uddhava, neither through aṣṭāṅga-yoga [the mystic yoga system to control the senses], nor through impersonalism or an analytical study of the Absolute Truth, nor through study of the Vedas, nor through practice of austerities, nor through charity, nor through acceptance of sannyāsa, can one satisfy Me as much as one can by developing unalloyed devotional service unto Me.' "
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a quotation from
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(11.14.20). For an explanation see
Ādi-līlā,
Chapter Seventeen, text 76.

verses.devanagari: ভয়ং দ্বিতীয়াভিনিবেশতঃ স্যা-\\nদীশাদপেতস্য বিপর্যয়োঽস্মৃতিঃ ।\\nতন্মায়য়াতো বুধ আভজেত্তং\\nভক্ত্যৈকয়েশং গুরুদেবতাত্মা ॥১৩৮॥
verses.transliteration: bhayaṁ dvitīyābhiniveśataḥ syād\\nīśād apetasya viparyayo 'smṛtiḥ\\ntan-māyayāto budha ābhajet taṁ\\nbhaktyaikayeśaṁ guru-devatātmā
verses.translation: “ 'When the living entity is attracted by the material energy, which is separate from Kṛṣṇa, he is overpowered by fear. Because he is separated from the Supreme Personality of Godhead by the material energy, his conception of life is reversed. In other words, instead of being the eternal servant of Kṛṣṇa, he becomes Kṛṣṇa's competitor. This is called viparyayo 'smṛtiḥ. To nullify this mistake, one who is actually learned and advanced worships the Supreme Personality of Godhead as his spiritual master, worshipful Deity and source of life. He thus worships the Lord by the process of unalloyed devotional service.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a quotation from
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(11.2.37).

verses.devanagari: এবে শুন, প্রেম, যেই — মূল ‘প্রয়োজন’ ।\\nপুলকাশ্রু-নৃত্য-গীত — যাহার লক্ষণ ॥১৩৯॥
verses.transliteration: ebe śuna, prema, yei-mūla 'prayojana'\\npulakāśru-nṛtya-gīta-yāhāra lakṣaṇa
verses.translation: "Now hear from Me what actual love of Godhead is. It is the prime object of life and is symptomized by bodily trembling, tears in the eyes, chanting and dancing.

verses.devanagari: স্মরন্তঃ স্মারয়ন্ত্যশ্চ মিথোঽঘৌঘহরং হরিম্ ।\\nভক্ত্যা সংজাতয়া ভক্ত্যা বিভ্রত্যুৎপুলকাং তনুম্ ॥১৪০॥
verses.transliteration: smarantaḥ smārayaś ca\\nmitho 'ghaugha-haraṁ harim\\nbhaktyā sañjātayā bhaktyā\\nbibhraty utpulakāṁ tanum
verses.translation: “ 'Pure devotees develop a spiritual body and symptoms of ecstatic love simply by remembering and reminding others of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Hari, who takes away everything inauspicious from the devotee. This position is attained by rendering devotional service according to the regulative principles and then rising to the platform of spontaneous love.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a quotation from
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(11.3.31).

verses.devanagari: এবংব্রতঃ স্বপ্রিয়নামকীর্ত্যা\\nজাতানুরাগো দ্রুতচিত্ত উচ্চৈঃ ।\\nহসত্যথো রোদিতি রৌতি গায়-\\nত্যুন্মাদবন্নৃত্যতি লোকবাহ্যঃ ॥১৪১॥
verses.transliteration: evaṁ-vrataḥ sva-priya-nāma-kīrtyā\\njātānurāgo druta-citta uccaiḥ\\nhastay atho roditi rauti gāyaty\\nunmādavan nṛtyati loka-bāhyaḥ
verses.translation: “ 'When a person is actually advanced and takes pleasure in chanting the holy name of the Lord, who is very dear to him, he is agitated and loudly chants the holy name. He also laughs, cries, becomes agitated and chants like a madman, not caring for outsiders.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a quotation from
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(11.2.40).

verses.devanagari: অতএব ভাগবত — সূত্রের ‘অর্থ’-রূপ ।\\nনিজ-কৃত সূত্রের নিজ-‘ভাষ্য’-স্বরূপ ॥১৪২॥
verses.transliteration: ataeva bhāgavata-sūtrera 'artha'-rūpa\\nnija-kṛta sūtrera nija-'bhāṣya'-svarūpa
verses.translation: "Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam gives the actual meaning of the Vedānta-sūtra. The author of the Vedānta-sūtra is Vyāsadeva, and he himself has explained those codes in the form of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam.

verses.devanagari: অর্থোঽয়ং ব্রহ্মসূত্রাণাং ভারতার্থবিনির্ণয়ঃ ।\\nগায়ত্রীভাষ্যরূপোঽসৌ বেদার্থপরিবৃংহিতঃ ॥১৪৩॥\\nপুরাণানাং সামরূপঃ সাক্ষাদ্ভগবতোদিতঃ ।\\nদ্বাদশস্কন্ধযুক্তোঽয়ং শতবিচ্ছেদ-সংযুতঃ ।\\nগ্রন্থোঽষ্টাদশসাহস্রঃ শ্রীমদ্ভাগবতাভিধঃ ॥১৪৪॥
verses.transliteration: purāṇānāṁ sāma-rūpaḥ\\nsākṣād-bhagavatoditaḥ\\ndvādaśa-skandha-yukto 'yaṁ\\nśata-viccheda-saṁyutaḥ\\ngrantho 'ṣṭādaśa-sāhasraḥ\\nśrīmad-bhāgavatābhidhaḥ
verses.translation: “ 'The meaning of the Vedānta-sūtra is present in Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam. The full purport of the Mahābhārata is also there. The commentary of the Brahma-gāyatrī is also there and fully expanded with all Vedic knowledge. Śrīmad Bhāgavatam is the supreme Purāṇa, and it was compiled by the Supreme Personality of Godhead in His incarnation as Vyāsadeva. There are twelve cantos, 335 chapters and eighteen thousand verses.'
verses.purport: PURPORT\nThis is a quotation from the\nGaruda Purāṇa.

verses.devanagari: সর্ব-বেদেতিহাসানাং সারং সারং সমুদ্ধৃতম্ ॥১৪৫॥
verses.transliteration: sarva-vedetihāsānāṁ\\nsāraṁ sāraṁ samuddhṛtam
verses.translation: “ 'The essence of all Vedic literature and all histories has been collected in this Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam was collected by the incarnation of God, Vyāsadeva, and it was later taught to his son, Śukadeva Gosvāmī. This is a quotation from
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(1.3.42).

verses.devanagari: সর্ববেদান্তসারং হি শ্রীমদ্ভাগবতমিষ্যতে ।\\nতদ্রসামৃততৃপ্তস্য নান্যত্র স্যাদ্রতিঃ ক্বচিৎ ॥১৪৬॥
verses.transliteration: sarva-vedānta-sāraṁ hi\\nśrīmad-bhāgavatam iṣyate\\ntad-rasāmṛta-tṛptasya\\nnānyatra syād ratiḥ kvacit
verses.translation: “ 'Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam is accepted as the essence of all Vedic literature and Vedānta philosophy. Whoever tastes the transcendental mellow of Śrīmad Bhāgavatam is never attracted to any other literature.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a quotation from
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(12.13.15).

verses.devanagari: গায়ত্রীর অর্থে এই গ্রন্থ-আরম্ভন ।\\n“সত্যং পরং” — সম্বন্ধ, “ধীমহি” — সাধন-প্রয়োজন ॥১৪৭॥
verses.transliteration: gāyatrīra arthe ei grantha-ārambhana\\n"satyaṁ paraṁ"-sambandha, "dhīmahi"-sādhana-prayojana
verses.translation: "In the beginning of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam there is an explanation of the Brahma-gāyatrī mantra. 'The Absolute Truth [satyaṁ param]' indicates the relationship, and 'we meditate [dhīmahi] on Him' indicates the execution of devotional service and the ultimate goal of life.

verses.devanagari: জন্মাদ্যস্য যতোঽন্বয়াদিতরতশ্চার্থেষ্বভিজ্ঞঃ স্বরাট্\\nতেনে ব্রহ্ম হৃদা য আদিকবয়ে মুহ্যন্তি যৎ সূরয়ঃ ।\\nতেজোবারিমৃদাং যথা বিনিময়ো যত্র ত্রিসর্গোঽমৃষা\\nধাম্না স্বেন সদা নিরস্তকুহকং সত্যং পরং ধীমহি ॥১৪৮॥
verses.transliteration: janmādy asya yato 'nvayād itarataś cārtheṣv abhijñaḥ svarāṭ\\ntene brahma hṛdā ya ādi-kavaye muhyanti yat sūrayaḥ\\ntejo-vāri-mṛdāṁ yathā vinimayo yatra tri-sargo 'mṛṣā\\ndhāmnā svena sadā nirasta-kuhakaṁ satyaṁ paraṁ dhīmahi
verses.translation: “ 'I offer my obeisances unto Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, son of Vasudeva, who is the supreme all-pervading Personality of Godhead. I meditate upon Him, the transcendent reality, who is the primeval cause of all causes, from whom all manifested universes arise, in whom they dwell and by whom they are destroyed. I meditate upon that eternally effulgent Lord who is directly and indirectly conscious of all manifestations and yet is beyond them. It is He only who first imparted Vedic knowledge unto the heart of Brahmā, the first created being. Through Him this world, like a mirage, appears real even to great sages and demigods. Because of Him, the material universes, created by the three modes of nature, appear to be factual, although they are unreal. I meditate therefore upon Him, the Absolute Truth, who is eternally existent in His transcendental abode, and who is forever free of illusion.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is the opening invocation of
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(1.1.1).

verses.devanagari: ধর্মঃ প্রোজ্ঝিতকৈতবোঽত্র পরমো নির্মৎসরাণাং সতাং\\nবেদ্যং বাস্তবমত্র বস্তু শিবদং তাপত্রয়োন্মূলনম্ ।\\nশ্রীমদ্ভাগবতে মহামুনিকৃতে কিংবাপরৈরীশ্বরঃ\\nসদ্যো হৃদ্যবরুধ্যতেঽত্র কৃতিভিঃ শুশ্রূষুভিস্তৎক্ষণাৎ ॥১৪৯॥
verses.transliteration: dharmaḥ projjhita-kaitavo 'tra paramo nirmatsarāṇāṁ satāṁ\\nvedyaṁ vāstavam atra vastu śivadaṁ tāpa-trayonmūlanam\\nśrīmad-bhāgavate mahāmuni-kṛte kiṁ vā parair īśvaraḥ\\nsadyo hṛdy avarudhyate 'tra kṛtibhiḥ śuśrūṣubhis tat-kṣaṇāt
verses.translation: “ 'Completely rejecting all religious activities which are materially motivated, this Bhāgavata Purāṇa propounds the highest truth, which is understandable by those devotees who are pure in heart. The highest truth is reality distinguished from illusion for the welfare of all. Such truth uproots the threefold miseries. This beautiful Bhāgavatam, compiled by the great sage Śrī Vyāsadeva, is sufficient in itself for God realization. As soon as one attentively and submissively hears the message of Bhāgavatam, he becomes attached to the Supreme Lord.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a quotation from
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(1.1.2). See also
Ādi-līlā,
Chapter One, text 91.

verses.devanagari: ‘কৃষ্ণভক্তিরসস্বরূপ’ শ্রীভাগবত ।\\nতাতে বেদশাস্ত্র হৈতে পরম মহত্ত্ব ॥১৫০॥
verses.transliteration: 'kṛṣṇa-bhakti-rasa-svarūpa' śrī-bhāgavata\\ntāte veda-śāstra haite parama mahattva
verses.translation: "Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam gives direct information of the mellow derived from service to Kṛṣṇa. Therefore Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam is above all other Vedic literatures.

verses.devanagari: নিগমকল্পতরোর্গলিতং ফলং\\nশুকমুখাদমৃতদ্রবসংযুতম্ ।\\nপিবত ভাগবতং রসমালয়ং\\nমুহুরহো রসিকা ভুবি ভাবুকাঃ ॥১৫১॥
verses.transliteration: nigama-kalpa-taror galitaṁ phalaṁ\\nśuka-mukhād amṛta-drava-saṁyutam\\npibata bhāgavataṁ rasam ālayaṁ\\nmuhur aho rasikā bhuvi bhāvukāḥ
verses.translation: “ 'Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam is the essence of all Vedic literatures, and it is considered the ripened fruit of the wish-fulfilling tree of Vedic knowledge. It has been sweetened by emanating from the mouth of Śukadeva Gosvāmī. You who are thoughtful and who relish mellows should always try to taste this ripened fruit. O thoughtful devotees, as long as you are not absorbed in transcendental bliss, you should continue tasting this Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, and when you are fully absorbed in bliss, you should go on tasting its mellows forever.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a quotation from
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(1.1.3).

verses.devanagari: বয়ন্তু ন বিতৃপ্যাম উত্তমঃশ্লোক বিক্রমে ।\\nযচ্ছৃণ্বতাং রসজ্ঞানাং স্বাদু স্বাদু পদে পদে ॥১৫২॥
verses.transliteration: vayaṁ tu na vitṛpyāma\\nuttamaḥśloka-vikrame\\nyac chṛṇvatāṁ rasa-jñānāṁ\\nsvādu svādu pade pade
verses.translation: “ 'We never tire of hearing the transcendental pastimes of the Personality of Godhead, who is glorified by hymns and prayers. Those who enjoy association with Him relish hearing His pastimes at every moment.' "
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a quotation from
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(1.1.19).

verses.devanagari: অতএব ভাগবত করহ বিচার ।\\nইহা হৈতে পাবে সূত্র-শ্রুতির অর্থ-সার ॥১৫৩॥
verses.transliteration: ataeva bhāgavata karaha vicāra\\nihā haite pābe sūtra-śrutira artha-sāra
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu advised Prakāśānanda Sarasvatī, "Study Śrīmad Bhāgavatam very scrutinizingly. Then you will understand the actual meaning of Brahma-sūtra"

verses.devanagari: নিরন্তর কর কৃষ্ণনাম-সংকীর্তন ।\\nহেলায় মুক্তি পাবে, পাবে প্রেমধন ॥১৫৪॥
verses.transliteration: nirantara kara kṛṣṇa-nāma-saṅkīrtana\\nhelāya mukti pābe, pābe prema-dhana
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu continued, "Always discuss Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam and constantly chant the holy name of Lord Kṛṣṇa. In this way you will be able to attain liberation very easily, and you will be elevated to the enjoyment of love of Godhead.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura states that without studying
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam,
one cannot understand the purport of
Brahma-sūtra
(
Vedānta-sūtra
) or the
Upaniṣads.
If one tries to understand Vedānta philosophy and the
Upaniṣads
without studying
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam,
he will be bewildered and, construing a different meaning will gradually become an atheist or an impersonalist.

verses.devanagari: ব্রহ্মভূতঃ প্রসন্নাত্মা ন শোচতি ন কাঙ্ক্ষতি ।\\nসমঃ সর্বেষু ভূতেষু মদ্ভক্তিং লভতে পরাম্ ॥১৫৫॥
verses.transliteration: brahma-bhūtaḥ prasannātmā\\nna śocati na kāṅkṣati\\nsamaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu\\nmad-bhaktiṁ labhate parām
verses.translation: “ 'One who is thus transcendentally situated at once realizes the Supreme Brahman and becomes fully joyful. He never laments nor desires to have anything; he is equally disposed to every living entity. In that state he attains pure devotional service unto Me.'

verses.devanagari: “মুক্তা অপি লীলয়া বিগ্রহং কৃত্বা ভগবন্তং ভজন্তে ।।” ॥১৫৬॥
verses.transliteration: "muktā api līlayā vigrahaṁ\\nkṛtvā bhagavantaṁ bhajante"
verses.translation: “ 'Even a liberated soul merged in the impersonal Brahman effulgence is attracted to the pastimes of Kṛṣṇa. He thus installs a Deity and renders the Lord service.'
verses.purport: PURPORT\nThis is a quotation from Śaṅkarācārya's commentary on the\nNṛsiṁha-tāpanī.

verses.devanagari: পরিনিষ্ঠিতোঽপি নৈর্গুণ্যে উত্তমঃশ্লোকলীলয়া ।\\nগৃহীতচেতা রাজর্ষে আখ্যানং যদধীতবান্ ॥১৫৭॥
verses.transliteration: pariniṣṭhito 'pi nairguṇye\\nuttamaḥśloka-līlayā\\ngṛhīta-cetā rājarṣe\\nākhyānaṁ yad adhītavān
verses.translation: “ 'Śukadeva Gosvāmī addressed Parīkṣit Mahārāja, "My dear King, although I was fully situated in the transcendental position, I was nonetheless attracted to the pastimes of Lord Kṛṣṇa. Therefore I studied Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam from my father.' "
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a quotation from
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(2.1.9).

verses.devanagari: তস্যারবিন্দনয়নস্য পদারবিন্দ-\\nকিঞ্জল্কমিশ্রতুলসীমকরন্দবায়ুঃ ।\\nঅন্তর্গতঃ স্ববিবরেণ চকার তেষাং\\nসংক্ষোভমক্ষরজুষামপি চিত্ততন্বোঃ ॥১৫৮॥
verses.transliteration: tasyāravinda-nayanasya padāravinda-\\nkiñjalka-miśra-tulasī-makaranda-vāyuḥ\\nantargataḥ svavivareṇa cakāra teṣāṁ\\nsaṅkṣobham akṣara-juṣām api citta-tanvoḥ
verses.translation: “ 'When the breeze carrying the aroma of tulasī leaves and saffron from the lotus feet of the lotus-eyed Personality of Godhead entered through the nostrils into the hearts of those sages [the Kumāras], they experienced a change in both body and mind, even though they were attached to impersonal Brahman understanding.'
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a quotation from
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(3.15.43).

verses.devanagari: আত্মারামাশ্চ মুনয়ো নির্গ্রন্থা অপ্যুরুক্রমে ।\\nকুর্বন্ত্যহৈতুকীং ভক্তিমিত্থম্ভূতগুণো হরিঃ ॥১৫৯॥
verses.transliteration: ātmārāmāś ca munayo\\nnirgranthā apy urukrame\\nkurvanty ahaitukīṁ bhaktim\\nittham-bhūta-guṇo hariḥ
verses.translation: “ 'Those who are self-satisfied and unattracted by external material desires are also attracted to the loving service of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, whose qualities are transcendental and whose activities are wonderful. Hari, the Personality of Godhead, is called Kṛṣṇa because He has such transcendentally attractive features.' "
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a quotation from
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
(1.7.10).

verses.devanagari: হেনকালে সেই মহারাষ্ট্রীয় ব্রাহ্মণ ।\\nসভাতে কহিল সেই শ্লোক-বিবরণ ॥১৬০॥
verses.transliteration: hena-kāle sei mahārāṣṭrīya brāhmaṇa\\nsabhāte kahila sei śloka-vivaraṇa
verses.translation: At this time the brāhmaṇa from the province of Mahārāṣṭra mentioned Lord Caitanya's explanation of the ātmārāma verse.

verses.devanagari: এই শ্লোকের অর্থ প্রভু ‘একষষ্টি’ প্রকার ।\\nকরিয়াছেন, যাহা শুনি’ লোকে চমৎকার ॥১৬১॥
verses.transliteration: ei ślokera artha prabhu 'ekaṣaṣṭi' prakāra\\nkariyāchena, yāhā śuni' loke camatkāra
verses.translation: The Mahārāṣṭrian brāhmaṇa stated that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu had already explained that verse in sixty-one ways. Everyone was astonished to hear this.

verses.devanagari: তবে সব লোক শুনিতে আগ্রহ করিল ।\\n‘একষষ্টি’ অর্থ প্রভু বিবরি’ কহিল ॥১৬২॥
verses.transliteration: tabe saba loka śunite āgraha karila\\n'ekaṣaṣṭi' artha prabhu vivari' kahila
verses.translation: When all the people gathered there expressed the desire to hear again the sixty-one different meanings of the ātmārāma-śloka, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu again explained them.

verses.devanagari: শুনিয়া লোকের বড় চমৎকার হৈল ।\\nচৈতন্যগোসাঞি — ‘শ্রীকৃষ্ণ’, নির্ধারিল ॥১৬৩॥
verses.transliteration: śuniyā lokera baḍa camatkāra haila\\ncaitanya-gosāñi-'śrī-kṛṣṇa', nirdhārila
verses.translation: When everyone heard Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's explanation of the ātmārāma-śloka, everyone was astonished and struck with wonder. They concluded that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was none other than Lord Kṛṣṇa Himself.

verses.devanagari: এত কহি’ উঠিয়া চলিলা গৌরহরি ।\\nনমস্কার করে লোক হরিধ্বনি করি ॥১৬৪॥
verses.transliteration: eta kahi' uṭhiyā calilā gaurahari\\nnamaskāra kare loka hari-dhvani kari
verses.translation: After giving those explanations again, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu arose and took His leave. All the people there offered their obeisances unto Him and chanted the mahā-mantra.

verses.devanagari: সব কাশীবাসী করে নামসংকীর্তন ।\\nপ্রেমে হাসে, কাঁদে, গায়, করয়ে নর্তন ॥১৬৫॥
verses.transliteration: saba kāśī-vāsī kare nāma-saṅkīrtana\\npreme hāse, kāṅde, gāya, karaye nartana
verses.translation: All the inhabitants of Kāśī [Vārāṇasī] began chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra in ecstatic love. Sometimes they laughed, sometimes they cried, sometimes they chanted, and sometimes they danced.

verses.devanagari: সন্ন্যাসী পণ্ডিত করে ভাগবত বিচার ।\\nবারাণসীপুর প্রভু করিলা নিস্তার ॥১৬৬॥
verses.transliteration: sannyāsī paṇḍita kare bhāgavata vicāra\\nvārāṇasī-pura prabhu karilā nistāra
verses.translation: After this, all the Māyāvādī sannyāsīs and learned scholars at Vārāṇasī began discussing Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam. In this way Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu delivered them.

verses.devanagari: নিজ-লোক লঞা প্রভু আইলা বাসাঘর ।\\nবারাণসী হৈল দ্বিতীয় নদীয়া-নগর ॥১৬৭॥
verses.transliteration: nija-loka lañā prabhu āilā vāsāghara\\nvārāṇasī haila dvitīya nadīyā-nagara
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then returned to His residence with His personal associates. Thus He turned the whole city of Vārāṇasī into another Navadvīpa [Nadīyā-nagara].
verses.purport:
PURPORT
Both Navadvīpa and Vārāṇasī were celebrated for their highly educational activities. At the present time these cities are still inhabited by great, learned scholars, but Vārāṇasī is especially a center for Māyāvādī
sannyāsīs
who are learned scholars. However, unlike Navadvīpa, there are hardly any devotees in Vārāṇasī. Consequently a discussion of
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
was very rare in Vārāṇasī. In Navadvīpa, such a discussion was quite ordinary. After Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu visited Vārāṇasī and turned Prakāśānanda Sarasvatī and his disciples into Vaiṣṇavas, Vārāṇasī became like Navadvīpa because so many devotees began discussing
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam.
Even at the present moment one can hear many discussions on
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
taking place on the banks of the Ganges. Many scholars and
sannyāsīs
gather there to hear
Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam
and perform
saṅkīrtana.

verses.devanagari: নিজগণ লঞা প্রভু কহে হাস্য করি’ । “ কাশীতে আমি আইলাঙ বেচিতে ভাবকালি । কাশীতে গ্রাহক নাহি, বস্তু না বিকায় । পুনরপি দেশে বহি’ লওয়া নাহি যায় ॥১৬৮॥
verses.transliteration: nija-gaṇa lañā prabhu kahe hāsya kari'\\nkāśīte āmi āilāṅa vecite bhāvakāli
verses.translation: Among His own associates, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu laughingly said, "I came here to sell My emotional ecstatic love.

verses.devanagari: কাশীতে গ্রাহক নাহি, বস্তু না বিকায় ।\\nপুনরপি দেশে বহি’ লওয়া নাহি যায় ॥১৬৯॥
verses.transliteration: kāśīte grāhaka nāhi, vastu nā vikāya\\npunarapi deśe vahi' laoyā nāhi yāya
verses.translation: "Although I came to Vārāṇasī to sell My goods, there were no customers, and it appeared necessary for Me to carry them back to My own country.

verses.devanagari: আমি বোঝা বহিমু, তোমা-সবার দুঃখ হৈল ।\\nতোমা-সবার ইচ্ছায় বিনামূল্যে বিলাইল ॥১৭০॥
verses.transliteration: āmi bojhā vahimu, tomā-sabāra duḥkha haila\\ntomā-sabāra icchāya vinā-mūlye bilāila
verses.translation: "All of you were feeling unhappy that no one was purchasing My goods and that I would have to carry them away. Therefore, by your will only, I have distributed them without charging."
verses.purport:
PURPORT
When we began distributing the message of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu in the Western countries, a similar thing happened. In the beginning we were very disappointed for at least one year because no one came forth to help this movement, but by the grace of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, some young boys joined this movement in 1966. Of course we distributed Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's message of the Hare Kṛṣṇa
mahā-mantra
without bargaining or selling. As a result, this movement has spread all over the world, with the assistance of European and American boys and girls. We therefore pray for all the blessings of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu upon all the devotees in the Western world who are spreading this movement.

verses.devanagari: সবে কহে, — “লোক তারিতে তোমার অবতার । ‘পূর্ব’ ‘দক্ষিণ’ ‘পশ্চিম’ করিলা নিস্তার । ‘এক’ বারাণসী ছিল তোমাতে বিমুখ । তাহা নিস্তারিয়া কৈলা আমা-সবার সুখ ।।” ॥১৭১॥
verses.transliteration: sabe kahe,-loka tārite tomāra avatāra\\n'pūrva' 'dakṣiṇa' 'paścima' karilā nistāra
verses.translation: All the Lord's devotees then said, "You have incarnated to deliver fallen souls. You have delivered them in the east and in the south, and now you are delivering them in the west.

verses.devanagari: ‘এক’ বারাণসী ছিল তোমাতে বিমুখ ।\\nতাহা নিস্তারিয়া কৈলা আমা-সবার সুখ ॥” ১৭২ ॥
verses.transliteration: 'eka' vārāṇasī chila tomāte vimukha\\ntāhā nistāriyā kailā āmā-sabāra sukha
verses.translation: "Only Vārāṇasī was left because the people there were against Your missionary activities. Now You have delivered them, and we are all very happy."

verses.devanagari: বারাণসী-গ্রামে যদি কোলাহল হৈল ।\\nশুনি’ গ্রামী দেশী লোক আসিতে লাগিল ॥১৭৩॥
verses.transliteration: vārāṇasī-grāme yadi kolāhala haila\\nśuni' grāmī deśī loka āsite lāgila
verses.translation: After the news of these events was broadcast, everyone from the surrounding neighborhoods began to pour in to see Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

verses.devanagari: লক্ষ কোটি লোক আইসে, নাহিক গণন ।\\nসঙ্কীর্ণ স্থানে প্রভুর না পায় দরশন ॥১৭৪॥
verses.transliteration: lakṣa koṭi loka āise, nāhika gaṇana\\nsaṅkīrṇa-sthāne prabhura nā pāya daraśana
verses.translation: Hundreds and thousands of people came to see Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. There was no counting the number. Because the Lord's residence was very small, not everyone could see Him.

verses.devanagari: প্রভু যবে স্নানে যান বিশ্বেশ্বর-দরশনে ।\\nদুইদিকে লোক করে প্রভু-বিলোকনে ॥১৭৫॥
verses.transliteration: prabhu yabe snāne yāna viśveśvara-daraśane\\ndui-dike loka kare prabhu-vilokane
verses.translation: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu went to take His bath in the Ganges and to see the temple of Viśveśvara, people would line up on both sides to see the Lord.

verses.devanagari: বাহু তুলি’ প্রভু কহে — বল ‘কৃষ্ণ’ ‘হরি’ ।\\nদণ্ডবৎ করে লোকে হরিধ্বনি করি’ ॥১৭৬॥
verses.transliteration: bāhu tuli' prabhu kahe-bala 'kṛṣṇa' 'hari'\\ndaṇḍavat kare loke hari-dhvani kari'
verses.translation: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu passed by the people, He would raise His arms and say, "Please chant Kṛṣṇa! Please chant Hari!" All the people received Him by chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa, and they offered their respects to Him by this chanting.

verses.devanagari: এইমত দিন পঞ্চ লোক নিস্তারিয়া ।\\nআর দিন চলিলা প্রভু উদ্বিগ্ন হঞা ॥১৭৭॥
verses.transliteration: ei-mata dina pañca loka nistāriyā\\nāra dina calilā prabhu udvigna hañā
verses.translation: In this way, for five days, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu delivered the people of Vārāṇasī. Finally, on the next day, He became very eager to leave.

verses.devanagari: রাত্রে উঠি’ প্রভু যদি করিলা গমন ।\\nপাছে লাগ্ লইলা তবে ভক্ত পঞ্চ জন ॥১৭৮॥
verses.transliteration: rātre uṭhi' prabhu yadi karilā gamana\\npāche lāg la-ilā tabe bhakta pañca jana
verses.translation: After rising very early on the sixth day, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu started to leave, and five devotees began to follow Him.

verses.devanagari: তপন মিশ্র, রঘুনাথ, মহারাষ্ট্রীয় ব্রাহ্মণ ।\\nচন্দ্রশেখর, কীর্তনীয়া-পরমানন্দ, — পঞ্চ জন ॥১৭৯॥
verses.transliteration: tapana miśra, raghunātha, mahārāṣṭrīya brāhmaṇa\\ncandraśekhara, kīrtanīyā-paramānanda,-pañca jana
verses.translation: These five devotees were Tapana Miśra, Raghunātha, the Mahārāṣṭrian brāhmaṇa, Candraśekhara and Paramānanda Kīrtanīyā.

verses.devanagari: সবে চাহে প্রভু-সঙ্গে নীলাচল যাইতে ।\\nসবারে বিদায় দিলা প্রভু যত্ন-সহিতে ॥১৮০॥
verses.transliteration: sabe cāhe prabhu-saṅge nīlācala yāite\\nsabāre vidāya dilā prabhu yatna-sahite
verses.translation: These five wanted to accompany Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu to Jagannātha Purī, but the Lord attentively bade them farewell.

verses.devanagari: “যাঁর ইচ্ছা, পাছে আইস আমারে দেখিতে ।\\nএবে আমি একা যামু ঝারিখণ্ড-পথে” ॥১৮১॥
verses.transliteration: "yāṅra icchā, pāche āisa āmāre dekhite\\nebe āmi ekā yāmu jhārikhaṇḍa-pathe"
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "If you want to see Me, you may come later, but for the time being I shall go alone through the Jhārikhaṇḍa forest."

verses.devanagari: সনাতনে কহিলা, — তুমি যাহ’ বৃন্দাবন । তোমার দুই ভাই তথা করিয়াছে গমন । কাঁথা-করঙ্গিয়া মোর কাঙ্গাল ভক্তগণ । বৃন্দাবনে আইলে তাঁদের করিহ পালন ॥১৮২॥
verses.transliteration: sanātane kahilā,-tumi yāha' vṛndāvana\\ntomāra dui bhāi tathā kariyāche gamana
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu advised Sanātana Gosvāmī to proceed toward Vṛndāvana, and He informed him that his two brothers had already gone there.

verses.devanagari: কাঁথা-করঙ্গিয়া মোর কাঙ্গাল ভক্তগণ ।\\nবৃন্দাবনে আইলে তাঁদের করিহ পালন ॥১৮৩॥
verses.transliteration: kāṅthā-karaṅgiyā mora kāṅgāla bhakta-gaṇa\\nvṛndāvane āile tāṅdera kariha pālana
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu told Sanātana Gosvāmī, "All My devotees who go to Vṛndāvana are generally very poor. They each have nothing with them but a torn quilt and a small waterpot. Therefore, Sanātana, you should give them shelter and maintain them."
verses.purport:
PURPORT
Following in the footsteps of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, we have constructed temples both in Vṛndāvana and Māyāpur, Navadvīpa, just to give shelter to the foreign devotees coming from Europe and America. Since the Hare Kṛṣṇa movement started, many Europeans and Americans have been visiting Vṛndāvana, but they have not been properly received by any
āśrama
or temple there. It is the purpose of the International Society for Krishna Consciousness to give them shelter and train them in devotional service. There are also many tourists eager to come to India to understand India's spiritual life, and the devotees in our temples both in Vṛndāvana and in Navadvīpa should make arrangements to accommodate them as far as possible.

verses.devanagari: এত বলি’ চলিলা প্রভু সবা আলিঙ্গিয়া ।\\nসবেই পড়িলা তথা মূর্চ্ছিত হঞা ॥১৮৪॥
verses.transliteration: eta bali' calilā prabhu sabā āliṅgiyā\\nsabei paḍilā tathā mūrcchita hañā
verses.translation: After saying this, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu embraced them all and began to proceed on His way, and they all fainted and fell down.

verses.devanagari: কতক্ষণে উঠি’ সবে দুঃখে ঘরে আইলা ।\\nসনাতন-গোসাঞি বৃন্দাবনেরে চলিলা ॥১৮৫॥
verses.transliteration: kata-kṣaṇe uṭhi' sabe duḥkhe ghare āilā\\nsanātana-gosāñi vṛndāvanere calilā
verses.translation: After some time, all the devotees got up and returned to their homes very much grief-stricken. Sanātana Gosvāmī proceeded toward Vṛndāvana alone.

verses.devanagari: এথা রূপ-গোসাঞি যবে মথুরা আইলা ।\\nধ্রুবঘাটে তাঁরে সুবুদ্ধিরায় মিলিলা ॥১৮৬॥
verses.transliteration: ethā rūpa-gosāñi yabe mathurā āilā\\ndhruva-ghāṭe tāṅre subuddhi-rāya mililā
verses.translation: When Rūpa Gosvāmī reached Mathurā, he met Subuddhi Rāya on the banks of the Yamunā at a place called Dhruva-ghāṭa.

verses.devanagari: পূর্বে যবে সুবুদ্ধি-রায় ছিলা গৌড়ে ‘অধিকারী’ ।\\nহুসেন-খাঁ ‘সৈয়দ’ করে তাহার চাকরী ॥১৮৭॥
verses.transliteration: pūrve yabe subuddhi-rāya chilā gauḍe 'adhikāri'\\nhusena-khāṅ 'saiyada' kare tāhāra cākarī
verses.translation: Formerly Subuddhi Rāya had been a big landholder in Gauḍa-deśa [Bengal]. Saiyada Hussain Khān was then a servant of Subuddhi Rāya.

verses.devanagari: দীঘি খোদাইতে তারে ‘মুন্সীফ’ কৈলা ।\\nছিদ্র পাঞা রায় তারে চাবুক মারিলা ॥১৮৮॥
verses.transliteration: dīghi khodāite tāre 'munsīpha' kailā\\nchidra pāñā rāya tāre cābuka mārilā
verses.translation: Subuddhi Rāya put Hussain Khān in charge of digging a big lake, but, once, finding fault with him, he struck him with a whip.

verses.devanagari: পাছে যবে হুসেন-খাঁ গৌড়ে ‘রাজা’ হইল ।\\nসুবুদ্ধি-রায়েরে তিঁহো বহু বাড়াইল ॥১৮৯॥
verses.transliteration: pāche yabe husena-khāṅ gauḍe 'rājā' ha-ila\\nsubuddhi-rāyere tiṅho bahu bāḍāila
verses.translation: Later Hussain Khān somehow or other was appointed Nawab by the central Mohammedan government. As a matter of obligation, he increased the opulences of Subuddhi Rāya.

verses.devanagari: তার স্ত্রী তার অঙ্গে দেখে মারণের চিহ্নে ।\\nসুবুদ্ধি-রায়েরে মারিতে কহে রাজা-স্থানে ॥১৯০॥
verses.transliteration: tāra strī tāra aṅge dekhe māraṇera cihne\\nsubuddhi-rāyere mārite kahe rājā-sthāne
verses.translation: Later, when the wife of Nawab Saiyada Hussain Khān saw the whip marks on his body, she requested him to kill Subuddhi Rāya.

verses.devanagari: রাজা কহে, — আমার পোষ্টা রায় হয় ‘পিতা’ ।\\nতাহারে মারিমু আমি, — ভাল নহে কথা ॥১৯১॥
verses.transliteration: rājā kahe,-āmāra poṣṭā rāya haya 'pitā'\\ntāhāre mārimu āmi,-bhāla nahe kathā
verses.translation: Hussain Khān replied, "Subuddhi Rāya has maintained me very carefully. He was just like a father to me," he said. "Now you are asking me to kill him. This is not a very good proposal."

verses.devanagari: স্ত্রী কহে, — জাতি লহ’, যদি প্রাণে না মারিবে ।\\nরাজা কহে, — জাতি নিলে ইঁহো নাহি জীবে ॥১৯২॥
verses.transliteration: strī kahe,-jāti laha', yadi prāṇe nā māribe\\nrājā kahe,-jāti nile iṅho nāhi jībe
verses.translation: As a last alternative, the wife suggested that the Nawab take away Subuddhi Rāya's caste and turn him into a Mohammedan, but Hussain Khān replied that if he did this, Subuddhi Rāya would not live.

verses.devanagari: স্ত্রী মরিতে চাহে, রাজা সঙ্কটে পড়িল ।\\nকরোঁয়ার পানি তার মুখে দেওয়াইল ॥১৯৩॥
verses.transliteration: strī marite cāhe, rājā saṅkaṭe paḍila\\nkaroṅyāra pāni tāra mukhe deoyāila
verses.translation: This became a perplexing problem for him because his wife kept requesting him to kill Subuddhi Rāya. Finally the Nawab sprinkled a little water on Subuddhi Rāya's head from a pitcher that had been used by a Mohammedan.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
More than five hundred years ago in India, the Hindus were so rigid and strict that if a Mohammedan would sprinkle a little water from his pitcher upon a Hindu, the Hindu would be immediately ostracized. Recently, in 1947, during the partition days, there was a big riot between Hindus and Muslims, especially in Bengal. The Hindus were forcibly made to eat cow's flesh, and consequently they began crying, thinking that they had become Mohammedans. Actually the Mohammedans in India did not come from the country of the Mohammedans, but Hindus instituted the custom that somehow or other if one contacted a Mohammedan, he became a Mohammedan. Rūpa and Sanātana Gosvāmī were born in a high
brāhmaṇa
family, but because they accepted employment under a Mohammedan government, they were considered Mohammedans. Subuddhi Rāya was sprinkled with water from the pitcher of a Mohammedan, and consequently he was condemned to have become a Mohammedan. Later, Aurangzeb, the Mohammedan emperor, introduced a tax especially meant for Hindus. Being oppressed in the Hindu community, many low-caste Hindus preferred to become Mohammedans. In this way the Mohammedan population increased. Later the British government made it a policy to divide the Hindus and the Muslims, and thus they maintained ill feelings between them. The result was that India was divided into Pakistan and Hindustan.
From early histories it appears that the entire earth was under one culture, Vedic culture, but gradually, due to religious and cultural divisions, the rule fragmented into many subdivisions. Now the earth is divided into many countries, religions and political parties. Despite these political and religious divisions, we advocate that everyone should unite again under one culture-Kṛṣṇa consciousness. People should accept one God, Kṛṣṇa; one scripture,
Bhagavad-gītā;
and one activity, devotional service to the Lord. Thus people may live happily upon this earth and combine to produce sufficient food. In such a society, there would be no question of scarcity, famine, or cultural or religious degradation. So-called caste systems and national divisions are artificial. According to our Vaiṣṇava philosophy, these are all external bodily designations. The Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement is not based upon bodily designations. It is a transcendental movement on the platform of spiritual understanding. If the people of the world understood that the basic principle of life is spiritual identification, they would understand that the business of the spirit soul is to serve the Supreme Spirit, Kṛṣṇa. As Lord Kṛṣṇa says in
Bhagavad-gītā
(Bg. 15.7),
mamaivāṁśo jīva-loke jīva-bhūtaḥ sanātanaḥ:
"The living entities in this conditioned world are My eternal, fragmental parts." All living entities in different life forms are sons of Kṛṣṇa. Therefore they are all meant to serve Kṛṣṇa, the original supreme father. If this philosophy is accepted, the failure of the United Nations to unite all nations will be sufficiently compensated all over the world by a great Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement. Recently we had talks with Christian leaders in Australia, including the Bishop of Australia, and everyone there was pleased with our philosophy of oneness in religious consciousness.

verses.devanagari: তবে সুবুদ্ধি-রায় সেই ‘ছদ্ম’ পাঞা ।\\nবারাণসী আইলা, সব বিষয় ছাড়িয়া ॥১৯৪॥
verses.transliteration: tabe subuddhi-rāya sei 'chadma' pāñā\\nvārāṇasī āilā, saba viṣaya chādiyā
verses.translation: Taking the Nawab's sprinkling water upon him as an opportunity, Subuddhi Rāya left his family and business affairs and went to Vārāṇasī.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
It appears that Subuddhi Rāya was a big landholder and a responsible, respectable gentleman. He could not, however, avoid the social misconception that one becomes a Mohammedan when water is sprinkled on one's face from a Mohammedan's pitcher. Actually he was planning to give up his material life and leave his family. Hindu culture recommends four divisions—
brahmacarya, gṛhastha, vānaprastha
and
sannyāsa.
Subuddhi Rāya was thinking of taking
sannyāsa,
and by the grace of Kṛṣṇa, he received this opportunity. He therefore left his family and went to Vārāṇasī. The system of
varṇāśrama-dharma
is very scientific. If one is directed by the
varṇāśrama
institution, he will naturally think of retiring from family life at the end of his life. Therefore
sannyāsa
is compulsory at the age of fifty.

verses.devanagari: প্রায়শ্চিত্ত পুছিলা তিঁহো পণ্ডিতের গণে ।\\nতাঁরা কহে, — তপ্ত-ঘৃত খাঞা ছাড়’ প্রাণে ॥১৯৫॥
verses.transliteration: prāyaścitta puchilā tiṅho paṇḍitera gaṇe\\ntāṅrā kahe,-tapta-ghṛta khāñā chāḍa' prāṇe
verses.translation: When Subuddhi Rāya consulted the learned brāhmaṇas at Vārāṇasī, asking them how his conversion to Mohammedanism could be counteracted, they advised him to drink hot ghee and give up his life.

verses.devanagari: কেহ কহে, — এই নহে, ‘অল্প’ দোষ হয় ।\\nশুনিয়া রহিলা রায় করিয়া সংশয় ॥১৯৬॥
verses.transliteration: keha kahe,-ei nahe, 'alpa' doṣa haya\\nśuniyā rahilā rāya kariyā saṁśaya
verses.translation: When Subuddhi Rāya consulted some other brāhmaṇa, they told him that he had not committed a grievous fault and that consequently he should not drink hot ghee and give up his life. As a result, Subuddhi Rāya was doubtful about what to do.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is another instance of Hindu custom. One
brāhmaṇa
would give advice condoning a particular fault, and another would give advice to the contrary. Typically, lawyers and physicians differ, giving one kind of instruction and then another. Due to the
brāhmaṇas'
different opinions, Subuddhi Rāya became further perplexed. He did not know what to do or what not to do.

verses.devanagari: তবে যদি মহাপ্রভু বারাণসী আইলা ।\\nতাঁরে মিলি’ রায় আপন-বৃত্তান্ত কহিলা ॥১৯৭॥
verses.transliteration: tabe yadi mahāprabhu vārāṇasī āilā\\ntāṅre mili' rāya āpana-vṛttānta kahilā
verses.translation: In his state of perplexity, Subuddhi Rāya met Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu when the Lord was at Vārāṇasī. Subuddhi Rāya explained his position and asked Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu what he should do.

verses.devanagari: প্রভু কহে, — ইহাঁ হৈতে যাহ’ বৃন্দাবন ।\\nনিরন্তর কর কৃষ্ণনামসংকীর্তন ॥১৯৮॥
verses.transliteration: prabhu kahe,-ihāṅ haite yāha' vṛndāvana\\nnirantara kara kṛṣṇa-nāma-saṅkīrtana
verses.translation: The Lord advised him, "Go to Vṛndāvana and chant the Hare Kṛṣṇa mantra constantly."
verses.purport:
PURPORT
This is a solution to all sinful activities. In this Age of Kali everyone is perplexed by so many inconveniences-social, political and religious-and naturally no one is happy. Due to the contamination of this age, everyone has a very short life. There are many fools and rascals who advise people to adopt this way of life or that way of life, but real liberation from life's perplexities means preparation for the next life.
Tathā dehāntara-prāptir dhīras tatra na muhyati.
One should be situated in his spiritual identity and return home, back to Godhead. The simplest method for this is recommended herein by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. We should constantly chant the holy names of the Lord, the Hare Kṛṣṇa
mahā-mantra.
Following in the footsteps of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, this Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement is recommending this process all over the world. We are saying, "Chant the Hare Kṛṣṇa
mahā-mantra,
be freed from all the complexities of life and realize Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Engage in His devotional service and perfect your life so that you can return home, back to Godhead."

verses.devanagari: এক ‘নামাভাসে’ তোমার পাপ-দোষ যাবে ।\\nআর ‘নাম’ লইতে কৃষ্ণচরণ পাইবে ॥১৯৯॥
verses.transliteration: eka 'nāmābhāse' tomāra pāpa-doṣa yābe\\nāra 'nāma' la-ite kṛṣṇa-caraṇa pāibe
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu further advised Subuddhi Rāya: "Begin chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa mantra, and when your chanting is almost pure, all your sinful reactions will go away. After you chant perfectly, you will get shelter at the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
The ten kinds of offenses should be considered. In the beginning, when one is initiated into the chanting of the Hare Kṛṣṇa
mahā-mantra,
there are naturally many offenses. However, the devotee should be very careful to avoid these offenses and chant purely. This does not mean that the Hare Kṛṣṇa
mahā-mantra
is sometimes pure and sometimes impure. Rather, the chanter is impure due to material contamination. He has to purify himself so that the holy names will be perfectly effective. Chanting the holy name of the Lord inoffensively will help one get immediate shelter at Kṛṣṇa's lotus feet. This means that by chanting purely, one will immediately be situated on the transcendental platform. We should note, however, that according to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's instructions, one should not wait to purify himself before chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa
mantra.
Whatever our condition may be, we should begin chanting immediately. By the power of the Hare Kṛṣṇa
mantra,
we will gradually be relieved from all material contamination and will get shelter at the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa, the ultimate goal of life.

verses.devanagari: আর কৃষ্ণনাম লৈতে কৃষ্ণস্থানে স্থিতি ।\\nমহাপাতকের হয় এই প্রায়শ্চিত্তি ॥২০০॥
verses.transliteration: āra kṛṣṇa-nāma laite kṛṣṇa-sthāne sthiti-\\nmahā-pātakera haya ei prāyaścitti
verses.translation: "When you are situated at the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa, no sinful reaction can touch you. This is the best solution to all sinful activity."

verses.devanagari: পাঞা আজ্ঞা রায় বৃন্দাবনেরে চলিলা ।\\nপ্রয়াগ, অযোধ্যা দিয়া নৈমিষারণ্যে আইলা ॥২০১॥
verses.transliteration: pāñā ājñā rāya vṛndāvanere calilā\\nprayāga, ayodhyā diyā naimiṣāraṇye āilā
verses.translation: Thus receiving the order from Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu to go to Vṛndāvana, Subuddhi Rāya left Vārāṇasī and went through Prayāga, Ayodhyā and Naimiṣāraṇya toward Vṛndāvana.

verses.devanagari: কতক দিবস রায় নৈমিষারণ্যে রহিলা ।\\nপ্রভু বৃন্দাবন হৈতে প্রয়াগ যাইলা ॥২০২॥
verses.transliteration: kataka divasa rāya naimiṣāraṇye rahilā\\nprabhu vṛndāvana haite prayāga yāilā
verses.translation: Subuddhi Rāya stayed for some time at Naimiṣāraṇya. During that time, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu went to Prayāga after visiting Vṛndāvana.

verses.devanagari: মথুরা আসিয়া রায় প্রভুবার্তা পাইল ।\\nপ্রভুর লাগ না পাঞা মনে বড় দুঃখ হৈল ॥২০৩॥
verses.transliteration: mathurā āsiyā rāya prabhu-vārtā pāila\\nprabhura lāga nā pāñā mane baḍa duḥkha haila
verses.translation: After reaching Mathurā, Subuddhi Rāya received information of the Lord's itinerary. He became very unhappy because he was not able to contact the Lord.

verses.devanagari: শুষ্ককাষ্ঠ আনি’ রায় বেচে মথুরাতে ।\\nপাঁচ ছয় পৈসা হয় এক এক বোঝাতে ॥২০৪॥
verses.transliteration: śuṣka-kāṣṭha āni' rāya vece mathurāte\\npāṅca chaya paisā haya eka eka bojhāte
verses.translation: Subuddhi Rāya would collect dry wood in the forest and take it to the city of Mathurā to sell. For each load he would receive five or six paise.

verses.devanagari: আপনে রহে এক পৈসার চানা চাবাইয়া ।\\nআর পৈসা বাণিয়া-স্থানে রাখেন ধরিয়া ॥২০৫॥
verses.transliteration: āpane rahe eka paisāra cānā cābāiyā\\nāra paisā bāṇiyā-sthāne rākhena dhariyā
verses.translation: Earning his livelihood by selling dry wood, Subuddhi Rāya would live on only one paise's worth of fried chick-peas, and he would deposit whatever other paises he had with some merchant.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
In those days there was no banking system like the one now found in Western countries. If one had excess money, he would deposit it with some merchant, usually a grocer. That was the banking system. Subuddhi Rāya would deposit his extra money with a mercantile man and spend it when necessary. When one is in the renounced order, saving money is not recommended. However, if one saves money for the service of the Lord or a Vaiṣṇava, that is accepted. These are the dealings of Subuddhi Rāya, who is one of the confidential devotees of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī also followed this principle by spending fifty percent of his money in order to serve Kṛṣṇa through
brāhmaṇas
and Vaiṣṇavas. He gave twenty-five percent of his money to relatives, and twenty-five percent he deposited in the custody of a merchant. These are the approved methods recommended in
Caitanya-caritāmṛta.
Whether in the renounced order or in the
gṛhastha
order, a Vaiṣṇava should follow these principles set forth by the previous
ācāryas.

verses.devanagari: দুঃখী বৈষ্ণব দেখি’ তাঁরে করান ভোজন ।\\nগৌড়ীয়া আইলে দধি, ভাত, তৈল-মর্দন ॥২০৬॥
verses.transliteration: duḥkhī vaiṣṇava dekhi' tāṅre karāna bhojana\\ngauḍīyā āile dadhi, bhāta, taila-mardana
verses.translation: Subuddhi Rāya used to spend his savings to supply yogurt to Bengali Vaiṣṇavas who came to Mathurā. He also gave them cooked rice and oil massages. When he saw a poverty-stricken Vaiṣṇava, he would use his money to feed him.
verses.purport:
PURPORT
There is a special reference for the maintenance of Bengali Vaiṣṇavas. A Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava is a Bengali Vaiṣṇava. Most of the devotees of Lord Caitanya at that time were Gauḍīyas and Oriyās, inhabitants of Bengal and Orissa. There are still many hundreds and thousands of disciples in Bengal and Orissa. Bengalis are habituated to eating cooked rice as their staple food. When they went to Mathurā in the North, they found that the people generally ate chapatis or
roṭi
made of wheat. The Bengalis could not digest this food because they were used to cooked rice. Therefore as soon as Subuddhi Rāya saw a Bengali Vaiṣṇava arriving in Mathurā, he would try to supply him with cooked rice. Bengalis are also accustomed to taking a massage with mustard oil. In any case, Subuddhi Rāya wanted to serve the Vaiṣṇavas according to their needs. Therefore he would supply yogurt to ease the digestion of food eaten in Mathurā, particularly the wheat-made chapatis and
roṭi.

verses.devanagari: রূপ-গোসাঞি, আইলে তাঁরে বহু প্রীতি কৈলা ।\\nআপন-সঙ্গে লঞা ‘দ্বাদশ বন’ দেখাইলা ॥২০৭॥
verses.transliteration: rūpa-gosāñi, āile tāṅre bahu prīti kailā\\nāpana-saṅge lañā 'dvādaśa vana' dekhāilā
verses.translation: When Rūpa Gosvāmī arrived at Mathurā, Subuddhi Rāya, out of love and affection for him, wanted to serve him in so many ways. He personally took Rūpa Gosvāmī to see all the twelve forests of Vṛndāvana.
verses.purport: PURPORT\nŚrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī had been a minister in the government of Hussain Shah, and Subuddhi Rāya was also known to Hussain Shah, because as a boy, he had been Subuddhi Rāya's servant. It appears that Subuddhi Rāya was elderly, yet while he was living in Mathurā he showed Rūpa Gosvāmī the twelve forests of Vṛndāvana.

verses.devanagari: মাসমাত্র রূপ-গোসাঞি রহিলা বৃন্দাবনে ।\\nশীঘ্র চলি’ আইলা সনাতনানুসন্ধানে ॥২০৮॥
verses.transliteration: māsa-mātra rūpa-gosāñi rahilā vṛndāvane\\nśīghra cali' āilā sanātanānusandhāne
verses.translation: Rūpa Gosvāmī remained in Mathurā and Vṛndāvana for one month in the association of Subuddhi Rāya. After that, he left Vṛndāvana to search for his elder brother, Sanātana Gosvāmī.

verses.devanagari: গঙ্গাতীর-পথে প্রভু প্রয়াগেরে আইলা ।\\nতাহা শুনি’ দুইভাই সে পথে চলিলা ॥২০৯॥
verses.transliteration: gaṅgā-tīra-pathe prabhu prayāgere āilā\\ntāhā śuni' dui-bhāi se pathe calilā
verses.translation: When Rūpa Gosvāmī heard that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu had gone to Prayāga on the road along the banks of the Ganges, both Rūpa and his brother Anupama went that way to meet the Lord.

verses.devanagari: এথা সনাতন গোসাঞি প্রয়াগে আসিয়া ।\\nমথুরা আইলা সরান রাজপথ দিয়া ॥২১০॥
verses.transliteration: ethā sanātana gosāñi prayāge āsiyā\\nmathurā āilā sarāna rāja-patha diyā
verses.translation: After reaching Prayāga, Sanātana Gosvāmī, following the order of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, went to Vṛndāvana along the public road.
verses.purport: PURPORT\nThis is especially significant because when Sanātana Gosvāmī went from Bengal to Benares, due to the political situation he did not go along the public road. After meeting Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu at Benares, however, he was ordered to proceed to Vṛndāvana along the public road leading to Mathurā. In other words, he was advised not to fear for his political situation.

verses.devanagari: মথুরাতে সুবুদ্ধি-রায় তাহারে মিলিলা ।\\nরূপ-অনুপম-কথা সকলি কহিলা ॥২১১॥
verses.transliteration: mathurāte subuddhi-rāya tāhāre mililā\\nrūpa-anupama-kathā sakali kahilā
verses.translation: When Sanātana Gosvāmī met Subuddhi Rāya at Mathurā, Subuddhi Rāya explained everything about his younger brothers Rūpa Gosvāmī and Anupama.

verses.devanagari: গঙ্গাপথে দুইভাই রাজপথে সনাতন ।\\nঅতএব তাঁহা সনে না হৈল মিলন ॥২১২॥
verses.transliteration: gaṅgā-pathe dui-bhāi rāja-pathe sanātana\\nataeva tāṅhā sane nā haila milana
verses.translation: Since Sanātana Gosvāmī went along the public road to Vṛndāvana and Rūpa Gosvāmī and Anupama went on the road along the Ganges banks, it was not possible for them to meet.

verses.devanagari: সুবুদ্ধি-রায় বহু স্নেহ করে সনাতনে ।\\nব্যবহার-স্নেহ সনাতন নাহি মানে ॥২১৩॥
verses.transliteration: subuddhi-rāya bahu sneha kare sanātane\\nvyavahāra-sneha sanātana nāhi māne
verses.translation: Subuddhi Rāya and Sanātana Gosvāmī knew one another before accepting the renounced order. Therefore Subuddhi Rāya showed much affection to Sanātana Gosvāmī, but Sanātana Gosvāmī hesitated to accept his sentiments and affections.

verses.devanagari: মহা-বিরক্ত সনাতন ভ্রমেণ বনে বনে ।\\nপ্রতিবৃক্ষে, প্রতিকুঞ্জে রহে রাত্রি-দিনে ॥২১৪॥
verses.transliteration: mahā-virakta sanātana bhramena vane vane\\nprati-vṛkṣe, prati-kuñje rahe rātri-dine
verses.translation: Being very advanced in the renounced order, Sanātana Gosvāmī used to wander from forest to forest, never taking shelter of any habitation built of stone. He used to live under trees or beneath bushes both day and night.

verses.devanagari: মথুরামাহাত্ম্য-শাস্ত্র সংগ্রহ করিয়া ।\\nলুপ্ততীর্থ প্রকট কৈলা বনেতে ভ্রমিয়া ॥২১৫॥
verses.transliteration: mathurā-māhātmya-śāstra saṅgraha kariyā\\nlupta-tīrtha prakaṭa kailā vanete bhramiyā
verses.translation: Śrīla Sanātana Gosvāmī collected some books about archaeological excavations in Mathurā, and, wandering in the forest, he sought to renovate all those holy places.

verses.devanagari: এইমত সনাতন বৃন্দাবনেতে রহিলা ।\\nরূপ-গোসাঞি দুইভাই কাশীতে আইলা ॥২১৬॥
verses.transliteration: ei-mata sanātana vṛndāvanete rahilā\\nrūpa-gosāñi dui-bhāi kāśīte āilā
verses.translation: Sanātana Gosvāmī remained in Vṛndāvana, and Rūpa Gosvāmī and Anupama returned to Vārāṇasī.

verses.devanagari: মহারাষ্ট্রীয় দ্বিজ, শেখর, মিশ্র-তপন ।\\nতিনজন সহ রূপ করিলা মিলন ॥২১৭॥
verses.transliteration: mahārāṣṭrīya dvija, śekhara, miśra-tapana\\ntina-jana saha rūpa karilā milana
verses.translation: When Rūpa Gosvāmī arrived at Vārāṇasī, he met the Mahārāṣṭrian brāhmaṇa, Candraśekhara and Tapana Miśra.

verses.devanagari: শেখরের ঘরে বাসা, মিশ্র-ঘরে ভিক্ষা ।\\nমিশ্রমুখে শুনে — সনাতনে প্রভুর ‘শিক্ষা’ ॥২১৮॥
verses.transliteration: śekharera ghare vāsā, miśra-ghare bhikṣā\\nmiśra-mukhe śune sanātane prabhura 'śikṣā'
verses.translation: While Rūpa Gosvāmī was staying at Vārāṇasī, he resided at the house of Candraśekhara and took prasāda at the house of Tapana Miśra. In this way he heard of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's instructions to Sanātana Gosvāmī in Vārāṇasī.

verses.devanagari: কাশীতে প্রভুর চরিত্র শুনি’ তিনের মুখে ।\\nসন্ন্যাসীরে কৃপা শুনি’ পাইলা বড় সুখে ॥২১৯॥
verses.transliteration: kāśīte prabhura caritra śuni' tinera mukhe\\nsannyāsīre kṛpā śuni' pāilā baḍa sukhe
verses.translation: While staying at Vārāṇasī, Rūpa Gosvāmī heard of all Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's activities. When he heard of His deliverance of the Māyāvādī sannyāsīs, he became very happy.

verses.devanagari: মহাপ্রভুর উপর লোকের প্রণতি দেখিয়া ।\\nসুখী হৈলা লোকমুখে কীর্তন শুনিয়া ॥২২০॥
verses.transliteration: mahāprabhura upara lokera praṇati dekhiyā\\nsukhī hailā loka-mukhe kīrtana śuniyā
verses.translation: When Rūpa Gosvāmī saw that all the people of Vārāṇasī respected Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, he became very happy. He even heard stories from the general populace.

verses.devanagari: দিন দশ রহি’ রূপ গৌড়ে যাত্রা কৈল ।\\nসনাতন-রূপের এই চরিত্র কহিল ॥২২১॥
verses.transliteration: dina daśa rahi' rūpa gauḍe yātrā kaila\\nsanātana-rūpera ei caritra kahila
verses.translation: After staying in Vārāṇasī for about ten days, Rūpa Gosvāmī returned to Bengal. In this way I have described the activities of Rūpa and Sanātana.

verses.devanagari: এথা মহাপ্রভু যদি নীলাদ্রি চলিলা ।\\nনির্জন বনপথে যাইতে মহা সুখ পাইলা ॥২২২॥
verses.transliteration: ethā mahāprabhu yadi nīlādri calilā\\nnirjana vana-pathe yāite mahā sukha pāilā
verses.translation: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu returned to Jagannātha Purī, He passed through the solitary forest, and He received great pleasure in doing so.

verses.devanagari: সুখে চলি’ আইসে প্রভু বলভদ্র-সঙ্গে ।\\nপূর্ববত্ মৃগাদি-সঙ্গে কৈলা নানারঙ্গে ॥২২৩॥
verses.transliteration: sukhe cali' āise prabhu balabhadra-saṅge\\npūrvavat mṛgādi-saṅge kailā nānā-raṅge
verses.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu happily returned to Jagannātha Purī in the company of His servant, Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya. As previously, the Lord performed many pleasing pastimes with the forest animals.

verses.devanagari: আঠারনালাতে আসি’ ভট্টাচার্য ব্রাহ্মণে ।\\nপাঠাঞা বোলাইলা নিজ-ভক্তগণে ॥২২৪॥
verses.transliteration: āṭhāranālāte āsi' bhaṭṭācārya brāhmaṇe\\npāṭhāñā bolāilā nija-bhakta-gaṇe
verses.translation: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu arrived at a place known as Āṭhāranālā near Jagannātha Purī, He sent Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya to call for His devotees.

verses.devanagari: শুনিয়া ভক্তের গণ যেন পুনরপি জীলা ।\\nদেহে প্রাণ আইলে, যেন ইন্দ্রিয় উঠিলা ॥২২৫॥
verses.transliteration: śuniyā bhaktera gaṇa yena punarapi jīlā\\ndehe prāṇa āile, yena indriya uṭhilā
verses.translation: Hearing news of the Lord's arrival from Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya, hordes of devotees became so happy that they seemed to be getting their lives back. It was as though their consciousness had returned to their bodies. Their senses also became agitated.

verses.devanagari: আনন্দে বিহ্বল ভক্তগণ ধাঞা আইলা ।\\nনরেন্দ্রে আসিয়া সবে প্রভুরে মিলিলা ॥২২৬॥
verses.transliteration: ānande vihvala bhakta-gaṇa dhāñā āilā\\nnarendre āsiyā sabe prabhure mililā
verses.translation: Being overwhelmed with great pleasure, all the devotees hastily went to see the Lord. They met Him on the banks of Narendra-sarovara, the celebrated lake.

verses.devanagari: পুরী-ভারতীর প্রভু বন্দিলেন চরণ ।\\nদোঁহে মহাপ্রভুরে কৈলা প্রেম-আলিঙ্গন ॥২২৭॥
verses.transliteration: purī-bhāratīra prabhu vandilena caraṇa\\ndoṅhe mahāprabhure kailā prema-āliṅgana
verses.translation: When Paramānanda Purī and Brahmānanda Bhāratī met Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the Lord offered them His respectful obeisances due to their being Godbrothers of His spiritual master. They both then embraced Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu in love and affection.

verses.devanagari: দামোদর-স্বরূপ, পণ্ডিত-গদাধর  ।\\nজগদানন্দ, কাশীশ্বর, গোবিন্দ, বক্রেশ্বর ॥২২৮॥
verses.transliteration: dāmodara-svarūpa, paṇḍita-gadādhara\\njagadānanda, kāśīśvara, govinda, vakreśvara
verses.translation: Devotees like Svarūpa Dāmodara, Gadādhara Paṇḍita, Jagadānanda, Kāśīśvara, Govinda and Vakreśvara all came to meet the Lord.

verses.devanagari: কাশী-মিশ্র, প্রদ্যুম্ন-মিশ্র, পণ্ডিত-দামোদর  ।\\nহরিদাস-ঠাকুর, আর পণ্ডিত-শঙ্কর ॥২২৯॥
verses.transliteration: kāśī-miśra, pradyumna-miśra, paṇḍita-dāmodara\\nharidāsa-ṭhākura, āra paṇḍita-śaṅkara
verses.translation: Kāśī Miśra, Pradyumna Miśra, Dāmodara Paṇḍita, Haridāsa Ṭhākura and Śaṅkara Paṇḍita also came there to meet the Lord.

verses.devanagari: আর সব ভক্ত প্রভুর চরণে পড়িলা  ।\\nসবা আলিঙ্গিয়া প্রভু প্রেমাবিষ্ট হৈলা ॥২৩০॥
verses.transliteration: āra saba bhakta prabhura caraṇe paḍilā\\nsabā āliṅgiyā prabhu premāviṣṭa hailā
verses.translation: All the other devotees also came and fell down at the Lord's lotus feet. In return, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu embraced them all with great ecstatic love.

verses.devanagari: আনন্দ-সমুদ্রে ভাসে সব ভক্তগণে ।\\nসবা লঞা চলে প্রভু জগন্নাথ-দরশনে ॥২৩১॥
verses.transliteration: ānanda-samudre bhāse saba bhakta-gaṇe\\nsabā lañā cale prabhu jagannātha-daraśane
verses.translation: Thus they all merged in the ocean of transcendental bliss. Then the Lord and all His devotees proceeded toward the temple of Jagannātha to see the Deity.

verses.devanagari: জগন্নাথ দেখি’ প্রভু প্রেমাবিষ্ট হৈলা ।\\nভক্ত-সঙ্গে বহুক্ষণ নৃত্য-গীত কৈলা ॥২৩২॥
verses.transliteration: jagannātha dekhi' prabhu premāviṣṭa hailā\\nbhakta-saṅge bahu-kṣaṇa nṛtya-gīta kailā
verses.translation: As soon as Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu saw Lord Jagannātha in the temple, He was immediately overwhelmed with love and affection. He chanted and danced with His devotees for a long time.

verses.devanagari: জগন্নাথ-সেবক আনি’ মালা-প্রসাদ দিলা ।\\nতুলসী পড়িছা আসি’ চরণ বন্দিলা ॥২৩৩॥
verses.transliteration: jagannātha-sevaka āni' mālā-prasāda dilā\\ntulasī paḍichā āsi' caraṇa vandilā
verses.translation: The priests immediately brought them flower garlands and prasāda. The temple's watchman, who was named Tulasī, also came and offered his obeisances to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

verses.devanagari: ‘মহাপ্রভু আইলা’ — গ্রামে কোলাহল হৈল ।\\nসার্বভৌম, রামানন্দ, বাণীনাথ মিলিল ॥২৩৪॥
verses.transliteration: 'mahāprabhu āilā'-grāme kolāhala haila\\nsārvabhauma, rāmānanda, vāṇīnātha milila
verses.translation: When the news spread that Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu had arrived at Jagannātha Purī, devotees like Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya, Rāmānanda Rāya and Vāṇīnātha Rāya all came to meet Him.

verses.devanagari: সবা সঙ্গে লঞা প্রভু মিশ্র-বাসা আইলা ।\\nসার্বভৌম, পণ্ডিত-গোসাঞি নিমন্ত্রণ কৈলা ॥২৩৫॥
verses.transliteration: sabā saṅge lañā prabhu miśra-vāsā āilā\\nsārvabhauma, paṇḍita-gosāñi nimantraṇa kailā
verses.translation: The Lord and all His devotees then went to the residence of Kāśī Miśra. Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya and Paṇḍita Gosāñi also invited the Lord to dine at their homes.

verses.devanagari: প্রভু কহে, — “মহাপ্রসাদ আন’ এই স্থানে ।\\nসবা-সঙ্গে ইহাঁ আজি করিমু ভোজনে ।।” ॥ ২৩৬ ॥
verses.transliteration: prabhu kahe,-"mahā-prasāda āna' ei sthāne\\nsabā-saṅge ihāṅ āji karimu bhojane"
verses.translation: Accepting their invitation, the Lord asked them to bring all the prasāda there so that He could eat it with His devotees.

verses.devanagari: তবে দুঁহে জগন্নাথপ্রসাদ আনিল ।\\nসবা-সঙ্গে মহাপ্রভু ভোজন করিল ॥২৩৭॥
verses.transliteration: tabe duṅhe jagannātha-prasāda ānila\\nsabā-saṅge mahāprabhu bhojana karila
verses.translation: Upon receiving Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's order, both Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya and Paṇḍita Gosāñi brought sufficient prasāda from the temple of Jagannātha. The Lord then dined with everyone at His own place.

verses.devanagari: এই ত’ কহিলুঁ, — প্রভু দেখি’ বৃন্দাবন ।\\nপুনঃ করিলেন যৈছে নীলাদ্রি গমন ॥২৩৮॥
verses.transliteration: ei ta' kahiluṅ,-prabhu dekhi' vṛndāvana\\npunaḥ karilena yaiche nīlādri gamana
verses.translation: Thus I have described how Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu returned to Jagannātha Purī from Vṛndāvana.

verses.devanagari: ইহা যেই শ্রদ্ধা করি’ করয়ে শ্রবণ ।\\nঅচিরাৎ পায় সেই চৈতন্য-চরণ ॥২৩৯॥
verses.transliteration: ihā yei śraddhā kari' karaye śravaṇa\\nacirāt pāya sei caitanya-caraṇa
verses.translation: Whoever hears Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's pastimes with faith and love very soon attains shelter at the Lord's lotus feet.

verses.devanagari: মধ্যলীলার করিলুঁ এই দিগ্দরশন ।\\nছয় বৎসর কৈলা যৈছে গমনাগমন ॥২৪০॥
verses.transliteration: madhya-līlāra kariluṅ ei dig-daraśana\\nchaya vatsara kailā yaiche gamanāgamana
verses.translation: I have thus given a summary of the Madhya-līlā, which is a special description of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's travels to and from Jagannātha Purī. Indeed, the Lord traveled to and fro continuously for six years.

verses.devanagari: শেষ অষ্টাদশ বৎসর নীলাচলে বাস ।\\nভক্তগণ-সঙ্গে করে কীর্তন-বিলাস ॥২৪১॥
verses.transliteration: śeṣa aṣṭādaśa vatsara nīlācale vāsa\\nbhakta-gaṇa-saṅge kare kīrtana-vilāsa
verses.translation: After taking sannyāsa at the age of twenty-four, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu lived another twenty-four years. For six of these years, He traveled extensively throughout India, sometimes going to Jagannātha Purī and sometimes leaving. After traveling for six years, the Lord fixed His residence at Jagannātha Purī and stayed there for the eighteen remaining years of His life. During these eighteen years He mainly chanted Hare Kṛṣṇa with His devotees.

verses.devanagari: মধ্যলীলার ক্রম এবে করি অনুবাদ ।\\nঅনুবাদ কৈলে হয় কথার আস্বাদ ॥২৪২॥
verses.transliteration: madhya-līlāra krama ebe kari anuvāda\\nanuvāda kaile haya kathāra āsvāda
verses.translation: I shall now chronologically reassess the chapters of Madhya-līlā so that one can relish the transcendental features of these topics.

verses.devanagari: প্রথম পরিচ্ছেদে — শেষলীলার সূত্রগণ ।\\nতথি-মধ্যে কোন ভাগের বিস্তার বর্ণন ॥২৪৩॥
verses.transliteration: prathama paricchede-śeṣa-līlāra sūtra-gaṇa\\ntathi-madhye kona bhāgera vistāra varṇana
verses.translation: In the First Chapter I have given a synopsis of the last pastimes [Antya-līlā]. Within this chapter is a vivid description of some of the pastimes of the Lord that took place toward the end of His life.

verses.devanagari: দ্বিতীয় পরিচ্ছেদে — প্রভুর প্রলাপ-বর্ণন ।\\nতথি-মধ্যে নানা-ভাবের দিগ্দরশন ॥২৪৪॥
verses.transliteration: dvitīya paricchede-prabhura pralāpa-varṇana\\ntathi-madhye nānā-bhāvera dig-daraśana
verses.translation: In the Second Chapter I have described Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's talking like a crazy man. Within this chapter it is indicated how Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu manifested His different emotional moods.

verses.devanagari: তৃতীয় পরিচ্ছেদে — প্রভুর কহিলুঁ সন্ন্যাস ।\\nআচার্যের ঘরে যৈছে করিলা বিলাস ॥২৪৫॥
verses.transliteration: tṛtīya paricchede-prabhura kahiluṅ sannyāsa\\nācāryera ghare yaiche karilā vilāsa
verses.translation: In the Third Chapter I have described the Lord's acceptance of the renounced order and how He enjoyed His pastimes in the house of Advaita Ācārya.

verses.devanagari: চতুর্থে — মাধব পুরীর চরিত্র-আস্বাদন ।\\nগোপাল স্থাপন, ক্ষীর-চুরির বর্ণন ॥২৪৬॥
verses.transliteration: caturthe-mādhava purīra caritra-āsvādana\\ngopāla sthāpana, kṣīra-curira varṇana
verses.translation: In the Fourth Chapter I have described Mādhavendra Purī's installation of the Gopāla Deity as well as Gopīnātha's stealing a pot of condensed milk at Remuṇā.

verses.devanagari: পঞ্চমে — সাক্ষিগোপাল-চরিত্র-বর্ণন ।\\nনিত্যানন্দ কহে, প্রভু করেন আস্বাদন ॥২৪৭॥
verses.transliteration: pañcame-sākṣi-gopāla-caritra-varṇana\\nnityānanda kahe, prabhu karena āsvādana
verses.translation: In the Fifth Chapter I have narrated the story of Sākṣi-gopāla. Lord Nityānanda Prabhu narrated this while Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu listened.

verses.devanagari: ষষ্ঠে — সার্বভৌমের করিলা উদ্ধার ।\\nসপ্তমে — তীর্থযাত্রা, বাসুদেব-নিস্তার ॥২৪৮॥
verses.transliteration: ṣaṣṭhe-sārvabhaumera karilā uddhāra\\nsaptame-tīrtha-yātrā, vāsudeva nistāra
verses.translation: In the Sixth Chapter I have told how Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya was delivered, and in the Seventh Chapter I have described the Lord's tour of different holy places and His deliverance of Vāsudeva.

verses.devanagari: অষ্টমে — রামানন্দ-সংবাদ বিস্তার ।\\nআপনে শুনিলা ‘সর্ব-সিদ্ধান্তের সার’ ॥২৪৯॥
verses.transliteration: aṣṭame-rāmānanda-saṁvāda vistāra\\nāpane śunilā 'sarva-siddhāntera sāra'
verses.translation: In the Eighth Chapter I have recorded the Lord's elaborate discussion with Rāmānanda Rāya. The Lord personally listened as Rāmānanda gave the conclusive essence of all Vedic literatures.

verses.devanagari: নবমে — কহিলুঁ দক্ষিণ-তীর্থ-ভ্রমণ ।\\nদশমে — কহিলুঁ সর্ব বৈষ্ণব-মিলন ॥২৫০॥
verses.transliteration: navame-kahiluṅ dakṣiṇa-tīrtha-bhramaṇa\\ndaśame-kahiluṅ sarva-vaiṣṇava-milana
verses.translation: In the Ninth Chapter I have described the Lord's tour of South India and the different places of pilgrimage. In the Tenth Chapter I have described the meeting of all the devotees of the Lord.

verses.devanagari: একাদশে — শ্রীমন্দিরে ‘বেড়া-সংকীর্তন’ ।\\nদ্বাদশে — গুণ্ডিচা-মন্দির-মার্জন-ক্ষালন ॥২৫১॥
verses.transliteration: ekādaśe-śrī-mandire 'beḍā-saṅkīrtana'\\ndvādaśe-guṇḍicā-mandira-mārjana-kṣālana
verses.translation: In the Eleventh Chapter I have described the great chanting of the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra that surrounded the Lord. In the Twelfth Chapter I have given a narration of the cleansing and washing of the Guṇḍicā temple.

verses.devanagari: ত্রয়োদশে — রথ-আগে প্রভুর নর্তন ।\\nচতুর্দশে — ‘হেরাপঞ্চমী’-যাত্রা-দরশন ॥২৫২॥
verses.transliteration: trayodaśe-ratha-āge prabhura nartana\\ncaturdaśe-'herā-pañcamī'-yātrā-daraśana
verses.translation: In the Thirteenth Chapter I have described Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's dancing before the chariot of Jagannātha. In the Fourteenth Chapter, there is an account of the Herā-pañcamī function.

verses.devanagari: তার মধ্যে ব্রজদেবীর ভাবের শ্রবণ ।\\nস্বরূপ কহিলা, প্রভু কৈলা আস্বাদন ॥২৫৩॥
verses.transliteration: tāra madhye vraja-devīra bhāvera śravaṇa\\nsvarūpa kahilā, prabhu kailā āsvādana
verses.translation: Also in the Fourteenth Chapter the emotional ecstasy of the gopīs was described by Svarūpa Dāmodara and tasted by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

verses.devanagari: পঞ্চদশে — ভক্তের গুণ শ্রীমুখে কহিল ।\\nসার্বভৌম-ঘরে ভিক্ষা, অমোঘ তারিল ॥২৫৪॥
verses.transliteration: pañcadaśe-bhaktera guṇa śrī-mukhe kahila\\nsārvabhauma-ghare bhikṣā, amogha tārila
verses.translation: In the Fifteenth Chapter Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu highly praised the qualities of His devotees and accepted lunch at the house of Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya. At that time, He delivered Amogha.

verses.devanagari: ষোড়শে — বৃন্দাবনযাত্রা গৌড়দেশ-পথে ।\\nপুনঃ নীলাচলে আইলা, নাটশালা হৈতে ॥২৫৫॥
verses.transliteration: ṣoḍaśe-vṛndāvana-yātrā gauḍa-deśa-pathe\\npunaḥ nīlācale āilā, nāṭaśālā haite
verses.translation: In the Sixteenth Chapter Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu departed for Vṛndāvana and journeyed through Bengal. He later returned to Jagannātha Purī from Kānāi Nāṭaśālā.
